First Official Cardinals-Broncos Injury Report Revealed
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Denver Broncos have revealed their first official injury reports for Week 7's clash at State Farm Stadium.
It's a loaded side for the Cardinals while Denver's is a bit lighter.
Reports for both teams on Wednesday:
The big topic of the Cardinals is Love, who is now at risk of missing a second consecutive game after being ruled out last week.
“Yes, he’s feeling better, but it kind of goes without saying. (We're) not going to put him out there until he feels 100%," LaFleur said on Love's ankle injury.
There's also an illness currently going around the team, which is something to monitor moving forward
“I guess I could cancel everything. I don’t know (Laughs)," LaFleur said. "No, I’m not a doctor. Drink some electrolytes and get some sleep. I don’t know. but it’s a good question. I don’t know.”
Surtain and Hufanga would be massive absences for Denver if they're unable to go at State Farm Stadium.
LaFleur had glowing reviews for Denver's defense, which is currently ran by former Arizona defensive coordinator Vance Joseph.
“Last few years. They’re very smart. They’re very well coached. I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them.
"You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it. They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. Yes, it’s the last two weeks, but it’s really been all year, and it’s been for a few years now. We have our hands full with this group, for sure.”
The Cardinals and Broncos will practice twice more before revealing official game statuses such as questionable, out or doubtful ahead of Week 7's tilt in Glendale.

title: Cardinals Claim Panthers OL Off Waivers
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have claimed former Carolina Panthers offensive tackle Albert Reese IV, the team officially announced.
More on Reese from the team's official press release:
"Reese (6-7, 325) entered the NFL with Carolina in May as an undrafted rookie free agent from Mississippi State and was inactive for each of the Panthers first five games this season. A native of Edmonton, Alberta, Reese played 49 games (22 starts) at tackle over five seasons (2021-25) at Mississippi State. He started all nine games played in 2025 and started all 12 games in 2024 and won the Kent Hull Trophy as the best offensive lineman in Mississippi."
Reese was just waived earlier this week. Panthers OL Taylor Morton returned from injury, which prompted the move.
The Cardinals are currently down two starting offensive linemen due to injury while illness is spreading through the team, which has impacted new backup tackle Jedrick Wills according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
Arizona plays the Denver Broncos this week.
The Cardinals believe they got their rushing attack sorted last week after Bam Knight rushed for 80 yards, a much needed sign of life after Arizona's unit upfront struggled. To pair, the Cardinals' line didn't allow a single sack on Jacoby Brissett in Week 6.
"I do think in some aspects our run game has grown from a variation standpoint in terms of what we’re doing schematically and then how those guys are executing, but there are still aspects of our run game we need to improve," LaFleur told reporters today.
"I think the operation’s the one that is the biggest. There's no yards that go with operation in terms of what you guys can see, but we know that when we’re operating at the level that we’re capable of it does lead to yards, which leads to points, which leads to obviously the result that we’re all hunting up, so I'd say those two aspects."

title: Cardinals Battling Injuries, Illness and Weather as Broncos Prep Begins
full_text:
ARIZONA — The weather is changing, and while your coworkers are fighting off the sickness around the office, so too are the Arizona Cardinals.
Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Budda Baker and Jedrick Wills would miss practice due to illness today while Jeremiyah Love, Walter Nolen and Andrew Wingard won't practice due to their respective injuries.
"Just get this out of the way for you guys. So Jeremiyah [Love], Walt [Nolen] and Dewey [Wingard] will all be not practicing today, and then [we] got a little bit of an illness going around from a player, coaches [perspective] too, but from a player perspective, Budda and Jedrick Wills will be out. We'll know more a little bit as we go throughout the week. So, going to take it day by day with those guys," said LaFleur.
The Cardinals are beginning Week 7 prep for the Denver Broncos.
Arizona also had to move up their practice time just to account for the weather. Storms and flood warnings are prevalent throughout the Valley, which forced the Cardinals to move their practice time up by an hour.
"They're good. I mean, it wasn't a huge adjustment. We got through all of our meetings. Nothing was rushed," LaFleur said of adjusting the practice schedule.
"The biggest thing is what I like about our schedule, not only from a meeting perspective, a lifting perspective, do all those things, is guys don't mind eating before walkthroughs. And then because obviously it's still just a walk-through, jog-through type deal, and then you give them that extra hour to let it digest a little bit more, if you will, and then you go practice. Well, we're going straight from walk-through to practice, so the biggest adjustment really was just making sure they got a little grub in them before their normal time I guess."
Arizona, sitting at 2-4, is hoping to string together consecutive wins for the first time all season with Denver making the trek to State Farm Stadium.
What does LaFleur have to combat the traveling illness? Not much.
"I guess I could cancel everything. I don't know. I'm not a doctor. I drink some electrolytes and get some sleep," LaFleur joked. "So I don't know. Yeah, but it's a good question. I don't know."
The Cardinals will reveal their first injury reports of Week 7 later today, so we'll see who exactly is impacted by the array of issues currently impacting the team.
Fans and players alike may be indulging in some chicken noodle soup tonight.

title: Cardinals Kicker Wins NFL Player of the Week Award
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland has won the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week after his performance in Week 6 against the Los Angeles Rams.
Ryland scored all 18 points in Arizona's upset victory at SoFi Stadium, booting home six field goals for the Cardinals' second win of the season. This is his first time winning the award and became the ninth kicker in Arizona history to take home such honors.
“I think our special teams has been really good all year," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said after the win. "I think they're an edge for us for sure in all units. I told the guys last night I didn't plan on using our punt team. We obviously had a few punts, but for the most part, did a pretty good job of controlling the ball.
"I never want to see six kicks again unless they're extra points. But if you're going to kick it, you might as well make it. I’m very happy for those guys.”
Ryland was brought back in free agency this past offseason and won an offseason battle with Josh Karty to be Arizona's kicker. After a handful of big kicks for the organization in 2024, Ryland saw some struggles in 2025.
However, Ryland's mostly come up big for the Cardinals this season, which included makes from 34, 30, 22, 38, 27 and 43 yards on the afternoon.
"He is the second Cardinals player to earn 'NFC Special Teams Player of the Week' honors this season after Simi Fehoko was selected following the Cardinals Week 1 win at the Chargers. It is the first time since 2015 that the Cardinals have had two different players each named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week (David Johnson, Chandler Catanzaro).
"Ryland accounted for all 18 points in Arizona’s 18-16 victory, connecting on all six field goal attempts. His final field goal of the day was a 43-yard game-winner as time expired in regulation. Ryland’s six field goals and 18 total points are both career highs.
"Only once in franchise history did a player make more field goals in a game than Ryland did on Sunday (7 by Jim Bakken on 9/24/67 at Pittsburgh). His six field goals in Los Angeles are the most in a single game in the NFL this season and the 43-yarder was his fifth career game-winner.
"He became the first NFL player to have 6+ field goals in a game since Houston’s Ka’imi Fairbairn on 1/4/2026 (6 FG) vs. Indianapolis. Ryland is tied for 3rd in the NFL in made FGs (14) and 4th in the NFL in total points (54) in 2026."

title: Buy or Sell: 5 Biggest Cardinals Storylines Entering Week 7
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 2-4 heading into Week 7 with plenty of chatter around the organization.
It's the middle of October and there are rumors galore — what's real, and what's not after six weeks of football?
Playing buy or sell with some major talking points around the desert:
Why we're buying it: Brissett continues to be heralded in the eyes of Mike LaFleur, and orchestrating a game-winning drive against the Rams only did Brissett more favors despite another very average performance. After another upset win, the Cardinals now have less pressure to make changes, which will start at quarterback whenever that time comes. It just won't be next week.
Why we're selling it: Rallis' defense looked renewed on Sunday after dialing up the pressure, which ultimately saw Arizona play their best defensive ball of the season. However, last Sunday shouldn't completely get Rallis off the hook. If the clock strikes midnight this weekend and Arizona's defense reverts back to a pumpkin against Denver, conversations will again arise on bigger-picture problems.
Why we're selling it: The Cardinals don't have the depth or luxury of time to do this. Yes, Bam Knight looked strong on Sunday, though a backfield of only Knight, Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull isn't inspiring. Love's ankle by no means appears serious, and if that were the case, he would have been placed on injured reserve last week. Love could miss multiple games, but completely ruling him out for four weeks during his rookie season when the Cardinals need him most isn't wise.
Why we're buying it : The Cardinals were justified to not trade Sweat at the beginning of the season. Now, times have changed. The more Sweat reverts back to his old self, the more teams are going to pony up for his services near the trade deadline, when his value will be highest. It's clear Sweat wants a pay raise and fresh start elsewhere, and if the Cardinals can see their top pass rusher continue getting to the quarterback, they might just have their price met.
Why we're buying it: It's a week-to-week league, as the Cardinals have now shown numerous times. Next up for Arizona is Denver, Dallas, Seattle and Los Angeles in the next four weeks. All four of these opponents are extremely beatable at this moment in time. Expected? Very much not, though it's conceivable the Cardinals, after downing the Rams, could walk away winners from multiple matchups within the next month.

title: 3 Cardinals Quietly Having a Strong 2026 Season
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 2-4 to start the 2026 season — which isn't something to write home about, though it's on par with what many were realistically expecting out of Mike LaFleur's first season in charge.
Stars are beginning to shine in the desert, though there's three Cardinals who are quietly building strong campaigns for Arizona:
So many were disappointed by Robinson's first two seasons in the league, and criticisms surrounding the former first-round pick were fair entering 2026. Robinson had lived nowhere near the level of hype that came with his arrival in 2024, and time was running out for his development to show on the field.
Robinson's steadily improved, and has gotten after the quarterback at much better rates — which might not be saying much compared to his prior outputs  — but we demanded improvement, and Robinson has done just that.
Robinson is tied with Josh Sweat with the team lead in pressures (7) with four quarterback knockdowns. He has 14 tackles and one sack through six games.
He may never live up to the billing of a first-round pick, though Robinson is building himself into a piece Arizona wants to stick around beyond his rookie deal.
Lopez made his return to the desert after a short stint with the Detroit Lions last season, though the Cardinals re-signed him in free agency hoping to revamp their defensive line alongside fellow free agent addition Andrew Billings.
Billings has mostly been inactive, though Lopez has managed to make a legitimate impact for Arizona in the trenches, totaling 20 tackles (3 for loss) with one sack and one pass batted down as well.
The Cardinals have struggled to stop the run in recent years. Lopez has been an energetic and effective presence for Arizona, one that's fair to call underrated.
Trey McBride commands most of the respect in Arizona's tight end room and overall offense. Rightfully so.
However, Elijah Higgins plays a massive role as the Cardinals' TE2. In an offense that uses plenty of multi-TE sets, especially 13 personnel, Higgins has carved out a strong role for himself to help his team far more than a typical backup tight end.
Higgins has caught all 11 targets thrown at him for 124 yards and one touchdown on the season. Perhaps equally as important, he's molded himself into a viable run-blocking tight end for Mike LaFleur to deploy as well.

title: What NFL Experts Say: Cardinals Surge in Week 7 Power Rankings
full_text:
Across the world of NFL power rankings, the Arizona Cardinals got some massive respect after their upset win over the Los Angeles Rams.
Just when many were ready to give up on Arizona, they managed to shock the world — and climbed practically every NFL power ranking list ahead of Week 7 in the process:
Conor Orr : "Nick Rallis joined the legion of defensive coordinators who have felt the absolute power and joy of blitzing with reckless abandon. This one happened to net the Cardinals one of the most shocking upsets of the season."
Josh Kendall/Chad Graff on Trey McBride : "The Cardinals tight end is in an unfamiliar spot, third at his position in fantasy scoring (17.2 ppg), but he’s still pacing an Arizona team that is pretty frustrating in every other aspect for fantasy managers. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love has been a disappointment so far (10.2 ppg), and Michael Wilson has yet to have a 100-yard receiving game."
Nick Shook : "Perhaps the Cardinals should just become the third tenant at SoFi Stadium. It’s where they play their best football. For a second time this season, Arizona rolled into Inglewood and punched the home team in the mouth, defeating the Rams despite not scoring a touchdown, playing without its starting running back and leaning on a receiving corps that no longer includes Marvin Harrison Jr. Arizona will remain a frustrating team for me to analyze on a weekly basis because of how games like these reveal its potential when I know it won’t perform at this level every week. When the Cardinals do, though, it’s a fun watch."
Josh Weinfuss : "Sunday's win amplified the Cardinals' red zone issues. They were 0-for-5 in the red zone and are now ranked 27th in red zone efficiency. It almost cost them in Los Angeles, but six field goals saved the day. After the game, quarterback Jacoby Brissett and coach Mike LaFleur each said they need to look at the film of Sunday's game to identify the issues. LaFleur alluded to a solution. 'I know where we could have been better,' he said."
Mike Florio : Maybe they should move to L.A.
Frank Schwab: "Nick Rallis was under heat after the first five games. He has been Arizona's defensive coordinator since 2023, survived a head coaching change, and none of his defenses have ranked better than 21st in yards allowed. A slow start to the season with new head coach Mike LaFleur had people wondering if Rallis was close to being replaced.
"Rallis bought himself some time. The Cardinals had a shocking win Sunday led by their defense, which held the Rams under 300 yards and to 16 points. The Cardinals kept the pressure on Matthew Stafford and forced him and the Rams' offense into a poor game. That relieves a lot of pressure, and provides hope this season."
Staff : "The Arizona Cardinals have looked like one of the league's worst teams over the past few weeks, but they stopped their four-game skid with an unexpected road win over the Los Angeles Rams.
"The fact that Arizona pulled off the upset without star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love and after trading away wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. should catch the attention of future opponents. The Cardinals might not be a great team overall, but they have a collection of offensive skill players that can at least keep games interesting."

title: Cardinals Stock Report: Three Players Rising, Two Falling After Week 6
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals shocked the world in their Week 6 upset victory over the Los Angeles Rams, a win that saw the Cardinals move to 2-4 on the season.
Three players who improved their stock — and two who didn't:
Knight made the final roster and has taken a backseat to Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier in Arizona's backfield. Entering Week 6, Love was injured and Allgeier (spoiler: more on him later) hasn't given the Cardinals quite the same impact as a bruising back.
Knight rose to the occasion this week, totaling 98 scrimmage yards which included a 31-yard gain — by far the biggest splash made by any Cardinals back this season.
“Not shocking. He’s a stud. He’s a tough dude. He’s a tough tackle. I’ve seen it in a green jersey over in New York and then got to see it obviously yesterday," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of Knight. "He ran hard. I thought the guys did great job. I thought everyone was connected."
Knight continues to impress in whatever opportunities granted to him.
Wilson was hoping to bounce back from a tough Week 5 where he caught four passes for 30 yards. Week 6 saw a slight improvement with four receptions for... 32 yards.
In fairness, his target share has practically been reduced in half. However, the freshly paid wideout was expected to step up after the Cardinals dealt Marvin Harrison Jr., and on a day where no Cardinals pass-catchers were having much success, the $75 million man couldn't emerge.
He's still an incredible player, and person, though Wilson's stock has undeniably taken a hit after this week.
Sweat is one of two defensive stars on this list, which feels odd to place in a rising section, but that's what a slow start does to you. After weeks of rumors around Sweat, his health and his overall desire to stay with Arizona, the edge rusher has seemingly found his form.
Sweat notched one sack (and another on a two-point conversion) to pair with four tackles (2 TFL) and two quarterback hits.
“Yes, it was cool. He was a force on the edge there and obviously had the production to boot with it, so it was good," LaFleur said of Sweat.
The Cardinals have been waiting for Sweat to emerge and produce. It looks like that's finally happening.
Allgeier is fine in short-yardage scenarios and is a strong back to have in pass protection, though he hasn't quite taken full advantage of his opportunities with the ball in his hands.
That was evident on Sunday, where he averaged just 2.1 yards per carry on 18 touches, his longest rush clocking in at just seven yards.
Yet Allgeier finds himself on this list mostly for his inability to capitalize off Love's injury, one that could have seen him take the lead-back role in the desert for however long the first-round pick is out. Instead, Knight stole the spotlight and Allgeier played second fiddle to yet another back in Arizona.
Baker's 2026 season has been extremely hot and cold, though Week 6 was undoubtedly his best piece of work. Baker poured in six tackles (2 TFL), two quarterback hits, one sack and one pass defensed. It was about as close to vintage Baker as fans remember seeing.
Baker, especially with injuries piling at the safety position, played some of his best football to date thanks to defensive coordinator Nick Rallis pushing the pedal to the floor and getting aggressive with his play-calling.
The Cardinals' defense needs Baker at his best. That's precisely what we saw in Los Angeles, and it was a fun sight to see.

title: Report Card: Grading Every Cardinals Position Group vs Rams
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals brewed the largest upset of Week 6 after defeating the Los Angeles Rams 18-16 at SoFi Stadium.
If you missed our coaching grades, you can check them out here .
Player grades from this Sunday:
Brissett turned the ball over on Arizona's first drive after staring down Trey McBride but managed to have an efficient day passing the ball after that, finishing with 24 completions on 35 attempts for 218 yards.
Brissett churned out another typical performance, though the red zone woes do partly fall on him. Five trips to the red zone with zero touchdowns can't happen if the Cardinals want to continue churning upsets.
Without Jeremiyah Love, the Cardinals' running back room ultimately proved to play above expectations thanks to the performance from Bam Knight, who had 80 yards on 15 attempts with a long of 31.
Tyler Allgeier churned out some tough yardage for the Cardinals and did well in pass protection, though his box score numbers aren't glamorous.
A very fine performance from this room on Sunday.
The Cardinals struggled to get much of anything going to their receivers, with Kendrick Bourne's 47 yards leading the group. In fairness, Arizona leaned more heavily on tight ends on Sunday, though drops from Bourne and Jalen Brooks (before his redeeming catch on the final drive) hurt.
Michael Wilson (four receptions for 32 yards) was on the back-burner for a second straight week after trading Marvin Harrison Jr. and nobody has really filled in that WR3 role consistently since.
Brooks' big grab on their final drive saved the day, but it was an overall average afternoon for this group.
Trey McBride did lead all Cardinals pass catchers with seven receptions for 53 yards, and Arizona's success between the 20s was thanks to an uptick in 12/13 personnel.
With that said, there was nothing glaring (good or bad) that stood out from this unit. It's one of the stronger positions on the team.
Missing two starters and facing a Rams front with Aaron Donald appeared to be a daunting task. Donald looked poised for a big game early, though Arizona's line took over the game and was a big part of their success.
They paved impressive rushing lanes for Knight and didn't allow Brissett to be sacked once on the day with just five quarterback hits on the afternoon.
All things considered, this might have been their best work of the season.
The Cardinals allowed 4.6 yards per carry on the ground, but looking beyond the box score guys such as Walter Nolen III came alive while Darius Robinson and Roy Lopez each had respective impacts as well.
Perhaps if L.J. Collier pitched the ball back on the two-point conversion this grade would increase.
Josh Sweat's performance is doing plenty of heavy lifting here, though that's simply the case for Arizona this season. The veteran pass rusher finally came alive with two sacks (one coming on a two-point conversion so it doesn't show on box scores) and four tackles.
Jordan Burch and Zaven Collins filled in nicely on the edges for stopping the run.
Production is the name of the game at inside linebacker, and the Cardinals had plenty of that on Sunday. Starters Mack Wilson and Jack Gibbens combined for 16 tackles (both No. 1 and 2 on the team individually) while backup Cody Simon forced a fumble in the second half.
Nothing over the top, but this was solid play from their corps of inside linebackers.
The Cardinals mostly kept Puka Nacua and Davante Adams bottled up for most of the afternoon, and corners such as Max Melton and Garrett Williams were heavily involved in the run game.
Sprinkle in Denzel Burke's fumble recovery and we've got ourselves an overall solid outing from a room that's missing Will Johnson for the rest of the season.
With Andrew Wingard out due to injury, the Cardinals needed a big game from Budda Baker — and that's what they got. Six tackles, one sack, two QB hits and a pass defensed was Baker's output, who filled rushing lanes nicely and was flying across the field.
Dadrion Taylor-Demerson didn't feature much on the day, though with Baker doing most of the heavy lifting he didn't need to.
Nacua's 43-yard catch was the only explosive play allowed on the day, which is something the Cardinals can live with.

title: Cardinals Promised Changes, And Delivered Their Best Defensive Performance Yet
full_text:
ARIZONA — What a difference a week can make in the National Football League.
At this point in time last week, Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur declined to make sweeping changes to his defensive staff, keeping coordinator Nick Rallis in his seat amid a four-game stretch where Arizona's defense allowed 30 points per game.
Fans, rightfully so, had grown impatient with the fourth-year play-caller, and entering Week 6's matchup against a highly potent Los Angeles Rams attack, another poor performance from Arizona's defense just might have been the final nail in Rallis' coffin.
LaFleur, defending Rallis at the podium, promised schematic changes to one of the league's worst statistical defensive units before Week 6. He wouldn't share what they were, but was confident in things turning around. Quickly. And he needed them to, not just for Rallis' sake, but for the organization's as well.
If the proof is in the pudding, LaFleur's eating it in heaping portions at the moment. The Cardinals put on one of their most impressive defensive displays in recent memory during their 18-16 win at SoFi Stadium, shocking the NFL and Los Angeles in one fell swoop.
Sean McVay teams have typically gotten the best of Arizona during his tenure with the Rams, though Sunday marked the first time in what's felt like forever where the Cardinals looked more than prepared. They weren't just ready for the test, they had the answers for it.
"I thought their play style was awesome. It looked to me like they had clear minds. I just saw clear minds. I saw 11 as one. I saw cleats in the ground, and I thought they were just working together in unison. It was really cool. It was reminiscent of what I felt like I saw in '24, maybe even in the early parts of last year, in terms of just something that did not look fun for the opposing offense," LaFleur shared with reporters on a victory Monday.
"... That's what it looked like to me. And hopefully we are even better than that."
The Cardinals limited Matthew Stafford to just 222 passing yards, though he did find two touchdowns through the air. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams respectively had quiet days while Los Angeles allowed three sacks and turned the ball over once. The Rams went 4-10 on third down and 0-2 on fourth down.
Rallis was once regarded as a potential head coaching candidate thanks to the work he did with previous iterations of a less talented Cardinals defense, most notably for his creative play-calling and willingness to send pressure.
That once coveted aggressiveness dwindled to extremely low points in recent weeks, and just when Rallis was potentially on the verge of packing his bags, he dialed up the pressure to new levels. According to Pro Football Focus, Arizona's 13 blitzes on Sunday were the most the Cardinals had all season. The Cardinals tallied seven quarterback hits on Stafford, who averaged just 2.57 seconds to throw on Sunday.
The aggressive gameplan worked, and it's been something fans and media alike have been pounding the table for since earlier in the season.
LaFleur also touched on playing smoother and more free. The Cardinals previously utilized a heavy Cover 6 usage, which is one of the more difficult coverages to play due to its complexity. That can often lead to miscommunications on the backend, which has prompted explosive plays on a weekly basis against Arizona.
Final data isn't out just yet on coverage shells for Week 6, though the Cardinals seemed to simplify their coverages and allowed their defenders to think just a bit less and play a tad faster.
"It was all productive," LaFleur said on last week's meetings to make defensive changes. "And that's their standard. They set the bar right there. That was a really good defensive performance.
"I just want to play great defense. I want hair on fire, hats to the ball, shots on the ball. 11 as one, and that's what I saw yesterday. The guys should be proud of that performance they put out there. It was real."
Budda Baker was flying around the front seven. Josh Sweat was getting to the quarterback and the Cardinals' defensive line was flying to whoever had the ball. Week 6 was, in many ways, what so many fans had hoped for Arizona's defense to become.
One game isn't enough to save jobs. Nobody believes the Cardinals have magically fixed all of their problems, and a 2-4 record is still not up to par. Yet perhaps more than anything, Sunday showed there just might be light at the end of the tunnel for Rallis and his defensive unit.
"I trust the human. I trust the worker. I know what the players think of him. We know this is a results-based business. We understand that, we know that. But I knew our defense had more than what we'd been putting out there, and we just had to unlock it some way, somehow," LaFleur said on his confidence in Rallis.
"And again, this was just one week, but it was a step in the right direction. I do believe we can grow from this one. I do believe we can start to build an identity off of this one. Each week's going to be a game of its own, and there's always going to be unique challenges, but I got a lot of faith in Nick. I got a lot of faith in the rest of the defensive staff. I think they're coaching their butt off. I think the details are improving. I think you could see that yesterday, particularly up front. I believe in the players that have to go out and execute it."

title: Falcons Bijan Robinson Shares What He Learned From 49ers Christian McCaffrey
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson has embraced his role as the centerpiece of Atlanta's offense, and his respect for San Francisco 49ers star Christian McCaffrey stems partly from their similar responsibilities.
The Falcons face the undefeated 49ers on Sunday, giving Robinson an opportunity to compete against a running back he spent a month working out with during the summer of 2025. Both players are trusted to carry the football, contribute as receivers and handle significant responsibilities within their respective offenses.
Robinson recently offered insight into his willingness to shoulder a heavy workload when discussing how he plays Madden.
"I play Madden how I would run the football in real life," Robinson said. "And people don't like playing Madden against me just because I'm gonna run it like 50 times. But it's just, you just can't stop it in the game."
While Robinson's actual workload depends on Atlanta's offensive game plan, this shows his confidence in carrying the ball repeatedly. Through six games in the 2026 season, Robinson has recorded 111 carries for 641 rushing yards, averaging 5.8 yards per attempt. He has also caught 20 passes for 144 yards and a touchdown.
His ability to contribute in multiple phases gives Atlanta flexibility in how it uses him. Whether running between the tackles, creating explosive plays outside or catching passes, Robinson remains a central component of the Falcons' offensive identity.
McCaffrey fills a comparable role in San Francisco, where his versatility allows the 49ers to keep him involved throughout games.
Through six games in 2026, McCaffrey has recorded 77 carries for 350 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns. He has also caught 28 passes for 190 yards, demonstrating his importance as both a runner and a receiving option.
Robinson has generated more rushing yards, while McCaffrey has scored more frequently. Both players give their teams versatile weapons capable of challenging defenses in different ways.
Robinson's willingness to embrace a heavy workload mirrors the importance McCaffrey holds within San Francisco's offense. Their ability to handle repeated touches while remaining dangerous in the passing game makes them difficult players to account for over four quarters.
Robinson spent a month working out with McCaffrey in California during the summer of 2025, allowing the two running backs to exchange knowledge and observe each other's preparation.
"He's very detailed in his work ethic and probably how he goes about his business," Robinson said to Terrin Waack.
"He's the ultimate competitor. You see he likes to be in the game as much as possible to make an impact as much as possible," Robinson added.
Robinson also praised McCaffrey's recovery routine, highlighting the importance of taking care of his body while preparing for the demands of an NFL season.
That lesson becomes especially relevant when considering the responsibilities both players carry for their teams. Maintaining effectiveness while handling substantial workloads requires preparation and consistency throughout the season.
Atlanta will need Robinson to be productive against a San Francisco team that has won every game entering the matchup. Establishing the run and finding ways to involve Robinson as a receiver could help the Falcons control the tempo.
Robinson understands the challenge ahead and emphasized the importance of execution.
"We have to match the urgency and we have to, for one play at a time, play at the highest level," Robinson said.
Against McCaffrey and the 49ers, Robinson will have an opportunity to demonstrate why he is such an important part of Atlanta's plans while facing a player whose preparation and competitive mentality he admires.

title: How Badly were Atlanta Falcons Punished in Latest NFL Power Rankings?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons ’ 2026 season has seen drastic ups and downs. The highs include two lopsided wins, but the lows have left fans scratching their heads.
The last two weeks have been particularly frustrating, with inconsistent performances holding this team back. Against the Ravens, the Falcons went flat in the fourth quarter and overtime after controlling the first three quarters. The opposite happened against the Bears, but both games ended in losses.
Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and the secondary struggled through most of the game, but they turned it around late to keep it close. Ultimately, the 31-7 fourth-quarter deficit proved too much to overcome.
Sunday brings a new challenge as the undefeated San Francisco 49ers head to Atlanta. If the Falcons want to get back on track, they will need a lot of things to get back on track, and quickly.
Elsewhere in the division, the Panthers topped a beat-up Eagles squad, the Buccaneers lost to the Steelers, and the Saints snapped a three-game losing streak with a win over the Giants. Falcons OnSI pulled the results from those sites and put them all in one place for fans. See below where the Falcons land compared with their division rivals.
Upcoming Opponent ( 49ers )
A common theme in these power rankings is criticism of quarterback play when pressure gets to Michael Penix Jr. Conor Orr joined them in highlighting the Falcons’ inability to handle the Bears’ pressure, saying they'll see a lot of this until they find a way to respond.
Elsewhere in the South, SI ranks the Panthers No. 13 (up seven spots), the Saints No. 25 (no change), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (down three spots). Orr has the 49ers at No. 1.
Pete Prisco dropped the Falcons one spot, calling their performance “terrible for most of the game”, a fair assessment of what they produced. He did give them credit for making a game of it, but that is no more than a moral victory.
Elsewhere in the South, CBS ranks the Panthers No. 14 (up six spots), the Saints No. 26 (no change), and the Buccaneers No. 29 (no change). Prisco has the 49ers at No. 1.
Nick Shook was high on the Falcons last week despite their late collapse against the Ravens, but he dropped them after Sunday’s result. He sees potential with this team, but says it's “difficult to explain who these Falcons are.” Some big tests loom for them over the next several weeks, and those answers will be clearer after that.
Elsewhere in the South, NFL.com ranks the Panthers No. 13 (up one spot), the Saints No. 20 (up seven spots), and the Buccaneers No. 27 (down four spots). Shook has the 49ers at No. 1.
ESPN hasn't been high on the Falcons this season, but they held steady after a second straight loss. Marc Raimondi noted how much this offense has struggled when Michael Penix Jr. faces pressure, citing his seventh-worst EPA/dropback and the second-worst completion percentage in those situations. The Bears sacked Penix five times on Sunday, and this will remain an issue until the quarterback finds his footing with defenses coming after him.
Elsewhere in the South, ESPN ranks the Panthers No. 15 (up three spots), the Saints No. 24 (up two spots), and the Buccaneers No. 28 (down one spot). ESPN has the 49ers at No. 1.

title: A.J. Terrell Jr. Takes Major Step Toward Return to Atlanta Falcons
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are potentially getting a major boost to their secondary, as cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. will practice Wednesday after spending the previous four games on injured reserve with a groin injury.
Terrell suffered the injury early in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Carolina Panthers, forcing him to miss several games during a critical stretch of the season. His return to practice gives the Falcons hope that one of their top defensive players could be available for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.
Terrell's return to practice also opens a 21-day window for Atlanta to activate him to its 53-man roster. The Falcons must make that move before the window expires. Otherwise, Terrell will revert to injured reserve and miss the remainder of the season.
Getting Terrell back would be a significant development for an Atlanta defense that has dealt with multiple injuries in its secondary over the past several weeks.
In Terrell's absence, C.J. Henderson stepped into the starting lineup at outside cornerback opposite Mike Hughes. Henderson provided Atlanta with another option on the outside before suffering his own groin injury in Week 5 against the Baltimore Ravens.
With Henderson unavailable for the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Chicago Bears, rookie Avieon Terrell, A.J.'s brother, stepped into a starting role at outside cornerback. Billy Bowman Jr. handled slot cornerback responsibilities.
However, Bowman exited the loss to Chicago early with an injury, leaving his availability for Week 7 uncertain. His status will be worth monitoring throughout the week as Atlanta prepares for a difficult matchup against San Francisco.
The injuries have forced the Falcons to adjust their secondary and rely on younger players to handle expanded responsibilities. Terrell's return would provide valuable experience and stability to a defensive backfield that has been forced to navigate several personnel changes.
The timing of Terrell's return to practice could not be much better for Atlanta. The Falcons are preparing to face an undefeated San Francisco team that presents a significant challenge on both sides of the ball.
Terrell has established himself as one of Atlanta's most important defensive players, and his presence would give the coaching staff another experienced option to deploy against the 49ers' passing attack.
Still, Wednesday's practice is only the first step toward a potential return. The Falcons will need to evaluate how Terrell responds as he works his way back from the groin injury before determining whether he is ready to play.
For now, the Falcons will continue monitoring the health of their defensive backs while hoping Terrell's return marks the beginning of a healthier stretch for the unit.

title: Falcons' Mike Hughes Struggles as Secondary Needs Reinforcements
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons were on the back foot from the opening kick on Sunday, quickly falling behind the Bears 14-0. The deficit quickly ballooned to 31-7 by the fourth and ultimately proved too much for the Falcons to overcome, despite their improbable late surge.
Plenty of blame goes around for Sunday’s woeful performance, but the secondary must find its footing, and fast.
Caleb Williams’ hamstring looked fine after missing the last several weeks, and the Bears’ quarterback made the Falcons look like the one that needed to shake off the rust.
Williams completed his first 12 passes and went 24-of-24 for 248 yards when he didn’t face pressure (the most attempts without an incompletion from a clean pocket since at least 2018, according to Next Gen Stats ). He finished his day 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a touchdown on his return.
The Falcons' secondary had a tough day, particularly Mike Hughes.
The veteran corner stepped in as the primary boundary corner due to injuries in the secondary and allowed 103 yards and a touchdown (QB rating of 158.3) on six catches (seven targets). Sunday’s performance isn't an isolated incident: Hughes has allowed a league-high 394 yards in coverage this season and is third-worst in the NFL in coverage EPA (+21.4).
He's in a difficult situation, playing out of his usual field position, and Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski reiterated his support for Hughes on Monday.
“We'll work through all those things this week. Obviously, Mike's a vet that we're counting on,” Stefanski said Monday. “These are tough matchups. We can always look at things that we can do better. Certainly, as we design the defense and those types of things, we'll always look at what we can do better. But the bottom line is we expect a lot from our corner position.”
Lately, those performances haven't been good enough, and that is on more than just Hughes.
Over six games, the Falcons have allowed 270 yards or more four times. Even in Week 5, when Atlanta held Baltimore below 270 passing yards, backup Tyler Huntley completed all 11 passes for 80 yards and accounted for two scores on the Ravens' final two drives, fueling a late comeback.
Atlanta has dropped to No. 20 in EPA/pass (-0.02) and No. 28 in passing yards per game allowed (252.0), but reinforcements could be coming soon.
Stefanski confirmed Monday that top cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. is “trending” toward an opened window to return from injured reserve, while his backup, C.J. Henderson, could also return this week after not participating in practices last week.
Both corners suffered groin injuries, with Terrell having missed the last four weeks. Henderson stepped in and played well in Terrell’s absence, earning praise from defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich , but the secondary’s already thin depth was tested when he couldn't play on Sunday.
Terrell's return could provide a much-needed boost, while Henderson would give Atlanta valuable depth at cornerback. With the undefeated 49ers coming to town, however, the Falcons need answers in the secondary quickly.

title: Atlanta Falcons Sign Linebacker after Kendal Daniels Injury
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons were busy this week trying to fill gaps in their roster as injuries have mounted, especially on the defensive side of the ball.
The move that grabbed the most attention this week was probably the signing of quarterback Andy Dalton and the release of quarterback Cooper Rush.
But the Falcons will probably get more help on the field from their defensive signings. They signed edge rusher Charles Snowden off of the Commanders' practice squad yesterday, and later they announced they added rookie linebacker TJ Quinn to the practice squad.
Quinn was signed to add some depth to the Falcons' linebacker room, which suffered injuries to both Divine Deablo and Kendal Daniels. The first injury report of the week will be out on Wednesday afternoon, but it would be a surprise to see Daniels in uniform, even though he appears to have avoided major injury .
Quinn is a native of Valdosta, Ga. and went to Lowndes High School. He spent four years at Louisville and had an extremely productive career. In 2025, he posted 95 tackles with 8 tackles for loss, 3 sacks, and 2 interceptions.
He had 82 tackles as a junior and 92 tackles as a sophomore.
He signed with the Green Bay Packers as an undrafted free agent, but didn't make the initial 53-man roster. At 6'0 and 225 pounds, Quinn had a good Pro Day with the Cardinals in the fall, clocking a 4.53 forty, but it wasn't enough to get him drafted.
The Falcons have had good luck with their rookie linebackers this season . Daniels was a fourth-round pick out of Oklahoma, and Harold Perkins Jr. was selected in the sixth round in April's NFL Draft. Both have shown long-term potential to man the inside in the future.
Deablo is the veteran, and he's had a relatively poor season. He missed some time in training camp with an ankle injury, and he's looked a step slow laterally. He's on the final year of a two-year deal, and at this rate, the Falcons likely wouldn't bring him back next season, preferring to hand the reins full-time to Daniels and Perkins.
The Falcons' linebackers have a tough matchup this week as they are understaffed with the San Francisco 49ers coming to Mercedes-Benz. Running back Christian McCaffrey, tight end George Kittle, and wide receiver Deebo Samuel are all players who will stress the second level of the defense.
Kickoff is at 1 p,m. EST on FOX.

title: Atlanta Falcons Poach Commanders Practice Squad for Former Raiders Starting Edge
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are taking a chance on a veteran, signing edge rusher Charles Snowden off the Washington Commanders’ practice squad to their 53-man roster, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport.
"The Falcons are signing edge Charles Snowden off the Commanders practice squad to their 53-man roster, source said. With Washington this year, Snowden was with the Raiders the last three seasons," Rapoport wrote on X .
Josh Kendall of The Athletic reported that edge rusher Bralen Trice was being released in a corresponding move. Trice had burned through his three practice squad elevations and was signed to the 53-man active roster prior to the Bears game. There's a good chance he ends up back on the practice squad and resets his three-game elevation eligibility after clearing waivers.
The move comes as Atlanta continues to deal with significant absences at edge rusher. With multiple players unavailable, the Falcons are searching for additional bodies who can contribute and add to this group.
Snowden spent the previous three seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders before joining Washington. He brings NFL experience to a position group that has been hit hard by injuries and suspensions, giving Atlanta another option as it tries to improve its pass rush.
However, Snowden also comes with off field concerns. He was arrested last month for DUI and suspended for three games after joining the Dallas Cowboys, making this another calculated risk for a Falcons team that needs help at a position of significant concern.
Atlanta’s edge rusher situation has become increasingly difficult to manage. Rookie Jalon Walker is sidelined for the season, while fellow first round pick James Pearce Jr. is serving an eight game suspension, with two games remaining.
The Falcons have also placed Yasir Abdullah on injured reserve, while Za’Darius Smith has missed 2 games. Those absences have left Atlanta searching for additional options to help fill the void.
The Falcons cannot afford to overlook opportunities to add depth. The lack of healthy and available edge rushers puts more responsibility on the remaining defensive linemen to get after the quarterback. Snowden could help ease some of that burden if he earns a role in the rotation.
Snowden, 28, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Virginia in 2021. He previously spent time with the Chicago Bears and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before establishing himself with the Raiders.
During his time in Las Vegas, Snowden appeared in 31 games across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, recording 67 tackles, 12 tackles for loss, and 4.5 sacks. He also recorded an interception during that stretch. He started nine games in each of the previous two years with the Raiders.
Those numbers give Atlanta a player with experience contributing at the NFL level, even if he is not a proven premier pass rusher.
The Falcons are clearly willing to take risks as they attempt to address their personnel problems. Snowden’s arrival is not a guaranteed solution, but it gives Atlanta another option at a position where reinforcements are needed.

title: 3 Things Atlanta Falcons Must Fix to Turn Their Season Around
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are running out of room for error after dropping back-to-back games, including Sunday's 31- 23 loss to the Chicago Bears at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
At 2-4, Atlanta still has time to get its season back on track, but the team must address several issues before its playoff hopes begin to slip away.
Here are three things the Falcons must fix to turn their season around.
The Falcons cannot continue putting themselves in early holes and expecting to rally in the second half.
Against Chicago, Atlanta fell behind 14- 0 before the Falcons even had a first down. The deficit eventually grew to 31-7 late in the third quarter before the Falcons mounted a fourth-quarter comeback that ultimately fell short.
Michael Penix Jr. finished the game completing 19 of 33 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns. Two of those touchdown passes went to Kyle Pitts Sr., but much of that production came after Atlanta had already put itself in a difficult position. He was 9 of 20 for 47 yards when the Falcons were behind 31-7.
The numbers show that the Falcons have the offensive talent to move the football. Through six games, Atlanta has recorded 2,066 total yards, including 897 rushing yards. The team is averaging approximately 149.3 rushing yards per game, giving it a strong foundation to build around.
The problem is turning that production into consistent scoring before games get out of hand. This team is built to run the ball and then work big plays off play-action. That doesn't work when the team is chasing a lead.
Atlanta must establish Bijan Robinson early, use play action to create opportunities downfield and avoid becoming too predictable when trailing. A balanced offense would also help take pressure off Penix and keep opposing defenses from focusing exclusively on the passing game.
If the Falcons can start faster and sustain drives throughout all four quarters, they will give themselves a much better chance to finish close games.
The Falcons cannot afford to keep giving opponents extra opportunities, especially when they are already struggling to find consistency. They are 31st in the NFL in turnover differential at -7.
Atlanta's biggest problem against Chicago was that it had to overcome mistakes while chasing a significant deficit. The Bears capitalized on their opportunities, while a late fumble by Penix Jr. helped Chicago close the door on Atlanta's comeback attempt.
Quarterback decision making must improve, but the responsibility does not fall on Penix alone. The entire offense must protect the football, while special teams must avoid mistakes that give opposing offenses favorable field position.
The Falcons also need to become more disciplined in critical situations. Penalties, missed assignments and turnovers can erase otherwise productive drives and put additional pressure on the defense.
Atlanta's defense has shown flashes of potential, particularly against the run, but the secondary must do a better job of slowing down opposing quarterbacks.
The Falcons entered their Week 6 matchup against Chicago allowing approximately 80.2 rushing yards per game, ranking fourth in the NFL at the time. That strength should give Atlanta a foundation to build upon, but the defense must also find ways to disrupt opposing passing attacks.
The Bears exposed that weakness on Sunday.
Caleb Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown in his return from a hamstring injury. He completed his first 12 passes for 142 yards and a touchdown, helping Chicago establish a 14 point lead before Atlanta could respond.
Allowing a quarterback to complete 83.3 percent of his passes is not a sustainable formula for winning football games.
Atlanta needs to generate more pressure, tighten its coverage, and force opposing quarterbacks into difficult decisions. The pass rush has shown promise, with defensive end Cam Thomas recording 11 quarterback hits and two sacks through the Bears game. The Falcons need that pressure to translate into disrupted drives, sacks, and turnovers.
The secondary must also communicate better and prevent easy completions early in games. Forcing opponents into third-and-long situations would allow the pass rush to attack more aggressively.
James Pearce Jr.'s impending return will help the pass rush, and the secondary should get a boost from the return of A.J. Terrell and CJ Henderson.
The Falcons are 2-4, but their season is not over. Atlanta has produced 897 rushing yards through six games and shown that it can score in bunches, including 45 points against New Orleans and 35 against Green Bay.
The challenge now is consistency. The Falcons must start games with urgency, stop giving away possessions and prevent opposing quarterbacks from getting comfortable early.
Their next opportunity comes Sunday, October 25, against the San Francisco 49ers, who enter undefeated at 6-0. It will be a significant test for a Falcons team that needs a response after two consecutive losses.

title: Atlanta Falcons 6-Week Report Card: Who Makes the Grade?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are 2-4 as they've passed through the one-third mark of the season. They've already experienced the roller coaster highs and lows of a team in two-game stretches. Going from a team looking like it was picking in the top 5, to playoff contenders, and then back to getting dominated at home.
With the inconsistencies, it's tough to put a grade on each unit, but we're going to give it a shot at the 6-week mark of the season.
If I were grading the unit as a whole, it would probably be a C- or D, with the first two games coming in at F- (helping to explain the 2-4 record). But Cooper Rush, who was released on Monday in favor of Andy Dalton, was never meant to play. An emergency starter who was unemployed in July looked just that: an emergency starter who was unemployed in July.
However, Michael Penix Jr. has now made four starts after missing the first two games, and there's been a lot of good, with some things that need to improve.
His accuracy on intermediate and deep passes has been among the best in the NFL. He's shown off his talented left arm, which made him a top-10 pick in 2024. His passer rating of 106.0 puts him fifth in the NFL among quarterbacks who have made at least four starts.
He needs to improve his pre-snap reads, finding the hot route when there's obvious pressure coming. The Chicago Bears blitzed him on 56% of his dropbacks, and he was 9/20 for 47 yards while the Bears built a 31-7 lead.
Being better against the blitz is a combination of Penix being more comfortable facing a rush, offensive coordinator Tommy Rees installing plays with easy hot routes, and the protection from his offensive line, tight ends, and linebackers.
Experience should go a long way towards helping Penix recognize and adjust plays pre-snap. He's shown plenty of potential; now it's about staying healthy and progressing.
Put whatever flavor of "A" you'd like on this: A or A+. Bijan Robinson is one of the best players in the NFL, and he got a three-game prime-time window to show off just how good he is.
The only way to slow him down is to keep him off the field. The Chicago Bears did just that on Sunday with a 2-1 advantage in time of possession. Robinson had just nine carries in the entire game.
Brian Robinson Jr. has been a capable No. 2 and provided power running and pile moving to replace the departed Tyler Allgeier.
Drake London is an A, and Jahan Dotson has looked like a solid option at No. 2 when he's gotten the opportunity. He only has 11 catches, but he's being asked to stretch the defense for bigger, lower-percentage plays. His 21.5 yards per catch leads the Falcons.
Olamide Zaccheaus has been a bit of a disappointment. He's not going to be high volume in this offense, but he still only has four catches on 11 targets in six games.
Zachariah Branch has 10 catches on 11 targets, but he's mostly been used as a gimmick receiver on screens and has just 55 yards. We got a reminder on Sunday that despite the potential, he's still a rookie with plenty of room to grow.
Penix has an elite arm and an elite No. 1 wide receiver. Drake London is going to hoover up most of the targets. Tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. would like to see a little bit better ball distribution. He's been really good when targeted. His 68.2% reception rate and three touchdowns both lead the team.
However, he's only been targeted 22 times in six games. To get the most out of Pitts and the investment the Falcons put in him , that number should be around 36.
Charlie Woerner has been an adequate blocker and Austin Hooper has done a decent job as a second receiving tight end option.
I think it's safe to say that Jack Matthews is having his worst season as a Falcon. He's not expected to keep improving at 34 years old, but he's been a liability in pass protection this season. If you put any stock in PFF grades, they have him at 53.1 this season. 69.8 was his previous low (last season), other than his rookie season more than a decade ago.
Jawaan Taylor is the only newcomer to the offensive line. He looked it on Sunday against the Bears. He's done an admirable job at right tackle and has been a clear upgrade over last year's starter, Eli Wilkinson, but he was overwhelmed by the Bears' blitz packages.
It's not so much a physical problem. He's been good when on task, but the confusion the Bears caused from the right side of the offensive line with multiple blitzes made Taylor a liability.
If we take quarterback off the table, offensive tackle becomes the biggest need for the Falcons in the 2027 NFL Draft.
The Falcons have two of the five highest-paid guards in the NFL. Matthew Bergeron comes in at No. 2 at $24.0 million per season, and Chris Lindstrom is No. 5 at $20.5 million.
They've looked like the highest-paid tandem for most of the season. The Falcons' run game has been excellent this season, giving Robinson enough room to be spectacular, and they've been good in protection. For the most part, any pass protection problems have come from overloads on the edges, not up the middle.
Ryan Neuzil is a free agent at the end of the season. He's making $6.2 million this year and should be in line for a raise when his contract expires.
The Falcons' rebuilt defensive line has been really good. Gervon Dexter Sr. and Brandon Dorlus form a fearsome interior pass rush. LaCale London and Maason Smith are solid in the rotation as well. Zach Harrison has made an impact after being cut by the team at the beginning of the season.
The Falcons' run defense is ranked No. 4 in the NFL at 83.2 yards per game.
Dexter got a contract extension already, and Brandon Dorlus is in line for one this offseason.
This is a room that is defined by who hasn't been there. Jalen Walker was lost for the season in training camp. James Pearce Jr. was suspended for the first eight games of the season. Za'Darius Smith missed the better part of three games after a concusson early in Week 4.
Cam Thomas has been better than expected, but he and Samson Ebukam are quality depth pieces forced into starting roles. Thomas has been good against the run, but sealing an edge has been a problem for this team in run defense.
Bears QB Caleb Williams doesn't escape the pocket and have eons of time and acres of space if it's Pearce or Walker chasing him instead of Thomas or one of the defensive linemen.
The Falcons lack speed on the edge right now. Mobile quarterbacks like Williams and Tyler Huntley of the Ravens exploited that in the last two weeks.
Pearce is scheduled to return after sitting out two more games.
If we're going against expectations, the grade would be higher. Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins have both played well... for rookies. There's a lot of excitement for their future, but if you want to see A-grade linebacker play, wait until Fred Warner comes to town with the 49ers next week.
Divine Deablo suffered an ankle injury in training camp that may have slowed him down, but there's no other way to put it right now: he's been poor. He's been out of position and has looked a step slow in space.
I thought he'd be in line for a contract extension over the summer. He's a free agent after the season, and the way he's playing, he won't be back in 2027.
The Falcons finally invested a second-round pick in the cornerback room, but Avieon Terrell wasn't going to fix years of neglect by himself. This room is thin on talent, and injuries have made it threadbare.
A.J. Terrell gets a lot of grief from Falcons fans, but it's painfully obvious when he's not out there. He's missed the last four weeks, but he's scheduled to return from the injured list this week. He may need some time to work his way back into shape after a four-week hamstring injury.
Mike Hughes is a useful No. 3 or No. 4 cornerback forced to be a No. 1 or No. 2. Billy Bowman Jr. has missed time recovering from an injury. CJ Henderson was on the practice squad last year, and then he was playing well this season in Terrell's spot before getting hurt.
If offensive tackle is the No. 1…

title: Atlanta Falcons Signing Veteran Quarterback Andy Dalton, per Report
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are adding another veteran quarterback to their roster, as Andy Dalton is signing with the team, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .
Dalton, 38, joins Atlanta after recently being released by the Philadelphia Eagles, giving the Falcons another experienced option in their quarterback room. The move comes as Atlanta continues to navigate uncertainty at the position and looks to maintain depth for the remainder of the season.
To make room for Dalton, the Falcons are releasing Cooper Rush, according to the reported roster move.
Dalton brings 16 seasons of NFL experience, having spent time with the Cincinnati Bengals, Dallas Cowboys, Chicago Bears, New Orleans Saints, and Carolina Panthers before joining Philadelphia earlier this year. He has thrown for more than 39,000 career yards and 254 touchdowns during his NFL career, making him one of the league's most experienced backup quarterbacks.
The Eagles acquired Dalton from the Panthers in March for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick. Philadelphia wanted an experienced presence behind starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, with Dalton competing against Tanner McKee for the backup position.
Dalton initially won that competition but struggled to hold onto the job. He appeared in one game for Philadelphia, completing none of his one pass attempts and throwing an interception during a Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears. He entered the game while Hurts underwent an evaluation for a possible head injury.
Philadelphia subsequently demoted Dalton behind McKee before releasing the veteran quarterback on Oct. 9. The Eagles determined that carrying four quarterbacks was no longer necessary, leaving Dalton available to sign elsewhere.
Although Philadelphia could have considered bringing Dalton back to its practice squad, his reported agreement with Atlanta gives him another opportunity to continue his NFL career.
Meanwhile, Rush's departure marks another change for Atlanta's quarterback depth chart. The Falcons signed Rush during training camp as insurance while Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa dealt with injuries. His experience made him a valuable option as Atlanta worked through uncertainty at the position.
Rush appeared in two games for the Falcons this season, completing 22 of 39 passes for 229 yards, one touchdown, and four interceptions. He finished with a 42.5 passer rating while also rushing twice for 20 yards. He's been the emergency third quarterback for the last four games.
Those numbers leave Atlanta looking for a different option behind its quarterbacks, and Dalton provides a veteran alternative with extensive starting experience.
The Falcons will hope Dalton's familiarity with multiple offensive systems and his experience in high pressure situations can help stabilize the position group as the season progresses.
For Atlanta, the signing represents an insurance move designed to provide additional experience and depth. With Dalton now headed to the Falcons and Rush being released, the team is making another adjustment to its quarterback room as it prepares for the remainder of the 2026 season.

title: Where Falcons Rookie Zachariah Branch Found Support after Costly Mistakes
full_text:
Zachariah Branch was one of the most talked-about Atlanta Falcons rookies during the offseason.
Coming out of USC and Georgia, his blazing speed and explosiveness as a wide receiver and return specialist had Atlanta fans excited for what’s to come out of the third-round NFL draft pick.
Through Branch’s first six NFL games, he’s primarily been the return man for the Falcons (2-4).
But in their Week 6 31-23 loss on Sunday to the Chicago Bears (4-2) , he faced his first adversity, fumbling two costly returns for the Falcons.
“Zachariah’s somebody that we’re going to be counting on. He’s a conscientious kid,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters postgame. “He has to take care of the football; he has done a good job up to date. He will learn from this.”
Down 14-7 with a little less than two minutes left in the second quarter, Atlanta was looking to turn the corner earlier in their failed fourth-quarter comeback effort.
Branch fielded a punt from Bears punter Tory Taylor, and muffed it as he was falling forward to the ground. Chicago’s Josh Blackwell recovered it, and running back D’Andre Swift scored on a two-yard rush to take a 21-7 halftime lead.
And then late in the third, after the Bears had taken a 28-7 lead, Branch had a chance to redeem himself on a kickoff.
After returning it for 26 yards, he fumbled it again, and the Bears recovered it, this time by Nick McCloud. Bears kicker Cairo Santos got a 50-yard field goal out of it.
As Branch walked sheepishly to the sideline, Stefanski spoke with him and tapped the rookie on his helmet.
Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson then pulled Branch aside.
“He’s a rookie,” Robinson said. “He needs a leader to be with him in that moment. And for me, it’s important to make sure that he’s alright because in this world that we live in, a lot of worldly things can get into his mind.”
Branch had slammed his helmet to the ground in frustration. But Robinson brought a calming presence to the frustrated first-year NFL player.
When the camera panned back over to the Falcons duo, they had their heads bowed.
“I just wanted to make sure that he was OK mentally and that his faith is high,” Robinson said of the exchange. “We prayed together, and I just wanted to make sure that he’s spiritually well. Because for a young guy, that’s the most important thing. Zach, he’s obviously a hell of a player, but I’ve always got to keep him in the game no matter what the situation is.”
Branch finished Sunday with one punt fielded and four kick returns for 86 yards. He also got involved with the offense during the late rally, making two catches for nine yards.
Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. completed a pass to Branch for a two-point conversion after Atlanta scored its first points in the fourth quarter after a scoreless third.
“He’ll be better for this,” Stefanski said of Branch.
Searching for their first home win of the season, the Falcons next host the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers (5-0) in Atlanta next Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. San Francisco will put their undefeated streak on the line against the Washington Commanders on Oct. 19’s edition of Monday Night Football.
Falcons-49ers kick off at 1 p.m. on FOX.

title: What The Ravens Can Realistically Afford At The NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens are pretty much all-in on 2026 as it stands.
Expecting much at this trade deadline, after general manager Eric DeCosta already overpaid for an expensive center w ho hasn’t even suited up for them yet, is fool’s gold. There are numerous indicators and market forces that are signaling this is about as good as it’s going to get from a roster standpoint, though there is potential to add a low-money item.
With a fungible salary cap and a motivated owner, there is always a way. The question, of course, is, with nearly $370M invested in this payroll already (top five in the NFL and way higher than Steve Bisciotti ever goes), and having just picked up a center making $17M a year who is a substantial injury risk, how much further he’s willing to go?
And the Ravens are already in a far more extreme cap bind than most teams. And DeCosta has already started mortgaging future drafts and he covets nothing more than draft lottery tickets and he’s going to have massive holes to fill on this roster in 2027, so the odds of him dealing any more substantial draft capital are slim.
But they also don’t have to sit on their hands entirely.
So the payroll is basically near it’s limit. As for the cap, well, per spotrac.com. they have the least cap space in the NFL , at under $3M. Again, you can create more, but Baltimore’s options are limited.
Most players are already running threadbare base salaries (like the $50M restructure they ran on Lamar Jackson to drop him to the vet minimum because they can never sign him to extension proactively like top front offices do all the time). Or they have big salaries but they aren’t very good anymore – like Roquan Smith and Marlon Humphrey – so you aren’t going to try to extend them or get cute to create additional space.
Nnamdi Madubuike has a salary of over $1M per game, but he also only has one additional year remaining on his contract which cuts down on your ability to prorate when you convert base salary to a bonus and spread over future years. They could play around with Trey Hendickson’s deal (three years remaining) to create a few more million in cap space.
So could they take on half a season of salary/cap for a player making $4M or so without having to do anything too dramatic? Yeah. But not much else unless they are shipping out salary in return in trade and that’s highly unlikely.
The Ravens want you to believe that kicker Tyler Loop is at the root of their issues , after backing him through the entire offseason. And maybe he is. But it also stands to reason that if Jake Moody, currently on the practice squad, gets the gig he is erratic and he is not a proven NFL starter, either.
So could they trade for All-Pro caliber Cameron Dicker from the failing Chargers? Yeah, they could, for the reasons explained here. If that’s too rich for their blood, Joey Slye is having a heck of a year for the Titans, who are tanking, and he is a pending free agent and only makes $2M. Or even Tampa’s Chase McLaughlin, who is making $3.8M this season and is also a pending free agent.
Outside of that, if the cornerback need becomes acute despite all the "talent" there, picking up a young veteran still on his rookie contract – someone they liked out of college who hasn’t broken through with his current team – is about the best they could try to swing. Teams are loathe to give up on such players who are young and cheap and play a premium position and had a quality college pedigree … but we have seen recent first-round pick QBs and WRs dealt, so trust me, DeCosta will be looking at those types of price points.

title: Ravens Head Coach Updates Lamar Jackson's Week 7 Status
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter, just six games into his career, continues to navigate complex injuries across his roster and particularly at quarterback.
To this point in his regime, there have been telltale signs about how this new staff would handle numerous key injuries – especially Lamar Jackson’s, which we told you would be at least two weeks despite rampant speculation to the contrary. And many of those indicators are flashing again this week as Minter tiptoes around Jackson's status once more. Minter has stuck to a “day-to-day” refrain about the two-time MVP, but the ankle situation has obviously been more serious than that.
Jackson did manage to practice Wednesday in a very limited basis, the coach said, ahead of a meeting with the Bengals ( and their new dominant defensive line ), and everything Minter has said and done to this point regarding every medical situation has been very cautious and judicious. The Ravens are also juggling trying to get new center Cam Jurgens – for whom general manager Eric DeCosta paid a prohibitive price – fully vested in a new offense with a new offensive line as he was fully cleared for practice Wednesday after missing two games in concussion protocol.
"Lamar was actually able to ge a little bit of limited work in, in preparation," Minter said Wednesday afternoon. "That's where that’s at … it's a day by day thing … and he was able to get a little bit of work in."
As one who parses words and writes words for a living, that's a lot of "little" in one response, and an "actually" that seems quite telling. Regardless, this was the first time Jackson got back on a field since the injury, although it does not sound like he tested much. Minter indicated it will take a consensus among player and medical team before Jackson starts a game.
"When it's ready for him to be able to play, from both sides," Minter said, "and we feel like that's the best thing to do, then that's what we'll do."
Minter has been very judicious with early-season injuries and while he has claimed for three weeks now that Jackson is day-to-day and gone out of his way indicate each of those weeks that the superstar could play in a game without practicing much that week … only to then rule him out on Friday. Such an outcome again this week would not come as a surprise.
To expect Jackson to return from an injury clearly this impactful, and one that has now wiped out this much practice time, without a full and vigorous practice tomorrow seems like a stretch. Despite calling it "day-to-day" they have been wary of aggravation. Either way, Thursday will be quite telling.
Jackson was performing at an MVP level prior to getting taken down by his lower leg from behind for a sack at the end of the first half of Week 4’s win over the Titans. He left that game, returned to the sidelines, began getting treatment on the sidelines and got an MRI the next day. The situation is complicated by the fact that Jackson is the rarest of elite QB who is playing out what amounts to the final year of his contract, as his 2027 deal has no guarantees and a ridiculous $85M cap charge that the Ravens cannot withstand.
Jackson has more leverage than any player in perhaps NFL history (NFL analyst Domonique Foxworth explained as such on “The Daily Flock Show” ) and top agent Mike McCartney, who negotiated multiple fully-guaranteed deals for Kirk Cousins (Jackson serves as his own agent) suggested Jackson can dictate at least $70M/year in 2027 from essentially any suitor he wants having achieved “virtual free agency,” due to a no-trade provision and a no-franchise tag provision.
Of course, situations like this are precisely while teams like the Chiefs (Patrick Mahomes) and Bills (Josh Allen) never allow those QBs to get within two years of free agency let alone the cusp of it. Then again, those QBs also never had to endure a collusion case ruling , or sit on the market on a non-exclusive franchise tag, either.
