title: Ravens Film Room: The Matchup That Will Mean Everything vs. Bengals Sunday
full_text:
Alas, this is finally the week Cam Jurgens will make his Ravens debut after general manager gave up a second-round pick while the struggling offensive lineman was still in concussion protocol.
But careful what you wish for.
Jurgens was getting whipped at guard for the Eagles – there is just no other way to put it - and his health is a major concern and people close to that team believe Jurgens was about to get benched in Philadelphia before Ravens GM Eric DeCosta panicked and gave up a bounty for him . And now Jurgens is on a path to fully practice and get cleared to play for Baltimore for the first time … just in time to face the most daunting group of defensive tackles in the NFL through the first third of the season led by signature offseason acquisition Dexter Lawrence, whom Cincy traded the 10th-overall pick for and who is living up to that price tag.
Oh, and Lamar Jackson is still very much a candidate to miss this game and he hasn’t had a full practice since injuring his ankle Week 4 and backup Snoop Huntley refuses to really lean into using his legs. And Baltimore lost its best blocking tight end for the season.
Jurgens has not been the same player since undergoing back and nerve surgery after helping the Eagles win the Super Bowl in 2024, and time will tell if he is indeed an upgrade over rookie guard Vega Ioane, who was curtailing the spate of A-gap pressure that was occurring before he was forced to move to center, while the run game remains hit-or-miss. Ioane held up quite well against dominating individuals like Jeffery Simmons, and while his snaps were sometimes erratic he showed significant promise and earned high praise in Owings Mills and around the NFL.
Jurgens allows him to shift back to his natural guard spot, but Eagles general manager Howie Roseman doesn’t lose a lot of trades. It’s hard not to look at a chart like this and express concern how Jurgens is going to hold up Sunday playing with a new line and a new quarterback for the first time, with the Bengals coming off a bye and sporting the only trio of defensive tackles in the NFL who each have at least two sacks (Lawrence, Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr.):
How often OGs are on an Island in Pass Blocking and their Successful Block rate on those plays pic.twitter.com/8wzdPIG8kf
Bengals owner Mike Brown went completely out of character with the Lawrence trade and he has devoted big resources to rebuilding his defense at the point of attack after years of failure on that side of the ball. They have a deep rotation up front with four tackles averaging at least 16 snaps per game and that does not include run-stuffer BJ Hill who was injured most of the year but played 33 snaps in his return in Week 5 and got to recover during the bye.
Lawrence is already fifth in NFL history in terms of career sacks among all players 350 pounds or heavier; the Bengals lead the NFL with eight sacks from defensive tackle already (in just five games). But let’s highlight Lawrence for a moment and where he ranks among DTs (again, having already had a bye):
Sacks : 3 (tied for 6th with Allen) Pressure Rate: 14% (3rd) Hurries: 13 (T-10th)
On the season the Bengals are allowing a passer rating of just 87.0 – identical to the vaunted Ravens secondary (that actually hasn’t been very good, especially in the second half ) – in large part due to the tackles. When Lawrence and Allen are on the field together they are collapsing the pocket and picking apart the space between the centers and the guards and producing these results for the Bengals defense:
Pressure Rate: 40.5% Sack Rate: 10% (11 on 111 dropbacks)
Passer Rating: 84.5 TD/INT: 3-2
Total D EPA w/Lawrence + Allen : 24.75 Total D EPA w/o both on field: 6.75
For an AFC North game this critical, knowing exactly how compromised the Ravens are in the interior offensive line (guard John Simpson looks highly overpaid at $10M and Ioane is switching positions, again), I would expect heavy volume from these two tackles but, again, they have maybe the deepest rotation here in the NFL.
Baltimore cannot really run the ball up the middle, and the Bengals have big issues against the run on the perimeter and their linebackers do not tackle well, so Derrick Henry is likely to attack there. Ravens rookie coordinator Declan Doyle needs to get Zay Flowers more involved from the backfield and more Justice Hill on sprint plays in pistol looks and more designed RPOs for Huntley and exploiting the horizontal plane, because vertical ain’t happening with the back-up QB.
If you were wondering where Ioane would look on a scatter chart at center, by the way, when he gets isolated, um, it looks a whole lot more inviting than the one for Jurgens:
How often Centers are on Islands in run blocking and their success blocking on those plays pic.twitter.com/6oVLS9mGgQ
Yeah, I have a hard time thinking Sunday is going to be a whole lot of fun for Jurgens and this offensive line, but we’ll see.

title: Ravens Report Card: Rookie Head Coach Jesse Minter After First 6 Games
full_text:
Jesse Minter couldn’t have asked for a much better schedule for his first six games as an NFL head coach.
The Ravens got a soft launch to his first season in the role, and they mostly took advantage with a 4-2 start. They have dealt with their fair share of injuries, for sure, and two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson might still have to miss another week with his ankle injury. Minter had to navigate a trip to Brazil and his offensive line has been in disrepair and he doesn’t seem very confident in his kicker anymore, either ( maybe they’ll consider a trade ?).
Oh, and he’s already blown three 10-point leads and ended up losing two of them. Nothing is every easy and boring around here, is it?
So what do we make of Minter through his first 1/3 of a season in charge? You’ll have to read the column to find out.
The Ravens showed a flawless execution in Brazil to win a game despite having only seven seconds to pull off that game-winning sequence. They rallied on the road with a back-up QB, after a rough first half, to win in Atlanta in the only game Minter wasn’t the favorite .
They won a game in which they had to cycle through three centers, landing on a rookie guard who then held down snapping duties. They dealt with the usual spate of penalties that come with start-up operations and largely overcame it. Minter made a ballsy call to take the ball in overtime of that game in Atlanta and it led to a seven-minute TD drive.
So at a macro level, given how new this is to him, and some of what’s been thrown at him, his feels appropriate to us.
These players like him and they respond to him. They start games well, and seem generally prepared. He knows how handle the media and convey what needs to be conveyed and he’s generally protective of his players.
He hasn’t tried to BS the fans about injuries and they have taken the long-view with a serious of injuries that should pay off down the road. I don’t have many real issues here. He hasn’t put his foot in his mouth, we haven’t seen any player have major discipline issues or fly off the handle in-game. I don’t have a lot of issues here.
Maybe I am holding him to too high of a standard. But he was a stud with the Chargers without having a top roster and his adjustments and in-game tactics were remarkably on point. So I expected as much here, with these players used to his concepts from their time in Mike Macdonald’s similar defense here.
This side of the ball got loaded with resources in the offseason. It was supposed to be plug-and-play and supposed to start winning on third down and with the pass rush and in coverage and, especially in the fourth quarter. Not so much . They have fallen apart after the half despite having games in hand time and time again, and the secondary has actually been the biggest underperformers on the team. It's gotten bad enough that corner might be the biggest need on the team.
Minter has to wear that. The corners and safeties don’t have an interception yet. These choke gene is alive and well and now it’s 16 times being DeCosta-ed (blowing a 10-point lead and losing) since 2019.
Expected the defensive coordinator thing to be his carrying trait and strength. Wearing all these hats all the time isn’t for everyone and it can take a while to figure it out and that’s an ongoing process for this coach who happens to be the rare first-timer who is replacing a potential Hall of Famer and has a team with Super Bowl expectations.

title: Ravens Week 6 Rookie Report: Pass Catchers Shine Despite Offensive Struggles
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's drag of a 13-10 road loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. They are in an AFC North division in which every team's record is above .500, and after falling to 4-2, they are now tied with the Pittsburgh Steelers for second place in the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. Fourth-round tight end Matthew Hibner was out with a hand injury, while the only rookies who were healthy scratches were fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt and undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano, who still suited up as an emergency No. 3 option. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his second week of eligibility and seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman made his third straight and final start at center since sliding over from right guard. While the offensive line as a whole struggled to hold up in pass protection and gain much traction in the ground game, Ioane was far from the problem and still managed to put some nice reps on tape of him clearing rushing lanes for star running back Derrick Henry.
The #Ravens successfully executing trap, trying to take advantage of the Browns playing downhill. Works well becuase Ioane clears out the 1T pic.twitter.com/QtUlimNkkv
The second-rounder continues to be a steady rotational presence for the Ravens on early downs, playing 25 defensive snaps against the Browns. He recorded a trio of total tackles for the third time this season, including an assisted takedown for a loss, two solos and his first career quarterback hit.
This is on the Zion young tape every week Putting his hand in the dirt and doing the dirty work in the muck. Fundamentally sound player. pic.twitter.com/RE0UiwIsjo
In his first game back from a four-week stint on injured reserve after suffering a fractured wrist in the season opener, the third-rounder made quite a strong impression and was on the field for over 50% of the offense's total snaps, with 31. Lane made the most of his opportunities by catching four of his five targets for 40 receiving yards and was the highest-graded offensive player on the team according to Pro Football Focus with an overall of 79.7. Each of his snags resulted in a first down, as he presented himself as a quarterback-friendly target for Huntley in the passing game in some key situations, three of which came on third down. Lane also showcased his skills as a downfield blocker in the run game as well.
Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane | 4 catches | 40 yards | 1.82 YPRR Lane made some tough catches into traffic this week, unphased by nearby defenders. Also showed great physicality through his routes, using his large frame to create separation by pushing off on one. pic.twitter.com/cQebyURg1L
"I thought Ja'Kobi did some really nice things," head coach Jesse Minter said. "I think there's parts of the game where [you can see] it's his second game, and it shows that it's his second game. Then you see what also created a lot of the energy and excitement around Ja'Kobi for how he did in training camp with his ability to pluck the ball out of the air and make tough catches and be a really physical receiver and use his body really well. I thought he had some really nice plays and some nice catches. He had a couple really nice blocks as well."
The fifth-rounder didn't see any playing time on defense for the first time since making his regular-season debut in Week 2, after the Ravens decided to deploy second-year pro Keyon Martin at the nickel spot over him. He did play 15 snaps on special teams for the second week in a row, tying his career high, which also ranked second-most among rookies.
The fifth-rounder saw an uptick in his playing time for the fourth week in a row, with 30 combined snaps between offense and special teams, including a season-high 23 on offense and seven on special teams. He was on the field early and often, playing 40.4 % of the team's total offensive snaps and recording career highs with four catches for five targets, 44 receiving yards and his first touchdown.
Rookie Josh Cuevas scores his first career TD! BALvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/s38V1mHPG9
Cuevas was the beneficiary of one of offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's most innovative play designs of the season thus far, where he essentially lined up at left guard before going on to record his longest career reception on a 29-yard catch-and-run.
This is sick: #Ravens OC Declan Doyle lined up TE Josh Cuevas at LG, then released him into a route for a 29-yard gain. Because Cuevas was off the line of scrimmage, he was eligible to go downfield. This is brilliant. pic.twitter.com/jN4icyVvEG
The sixth-round specialist impressed as a field-flipping weapon for the third week in a row, setting new career highs for punts in a game and punt yardage with seven for 346 yards. He pinned the Browns' offense inside their 20-yard line three times, including an excellent play where he joined forces with special teams ace Keondre Jackson to stop the ball at the Cleveland one-yard line. Eckley averaged 49.4 yards per punt with a new career-long of 62.
9 iron inside the 5 for @RyanEckley1 . ⛳️ Tune in on FOX. pic.twitter.com/V8ibXW474E
Even with the return of four-time Pro Bowl veteran edge rusher Trey Hendrickson from finger surgery, the undrafted free agent still got to see some playing time on defense, although it wasn't in the double digits, with seven and logged the fourth-most special teams snaps on the team with 18, which was also the most among rookies. During his limited playing time on defense, Burke came close to notching his second career regular-season sack twice. Both instances came with him rushing against the Browns' right tackle, and he narrowly missed Deshaun Watson before one of his teammates came in and finished the play.
Ravens UDFA Ethan Burke almost had 2 sacks Sunday pic.twitter.com/nvFNPoY1oQ

title: Ravens Biggest NFL Trade Deadline Need Is Painfully Obvious Yet Shocking
full_text:
The Ravens can’t get enough first round corners.
It’s been a fetish for middling general manager Eric DeCosta for years and they have struck out on quite a few – Jaire Alexander, anyone? – and overpaid a bunch ( Marlon Humphrey, anyone ?) and rarely a year goes by without using a first-round pick on a corner or safety.
The secondary is supposed to be the strength of the team and rookie head coach Jesse Minter is a coverage savant and all of the genius stuff he did with the Chargers defense was supposed to carry over here, where he'd have a “better roster” and with DeCosta pumping the preponderance of the offseason resources into this side of the ball.
Yet here we are a third of the way through the season and the Ravens have faced one of the easiest schedules of offensive opponents in the NFL ( that’s about to change in a major way ) and mostly bad quarterbacks and they can’t get any of their corners to be playmakers . Hell, they can’t get most of them not to be a liability in coverage when the game is on the line. It’s ridiculous and sad, but true.
And with Joe Burrow and Josh Allen and Trevor Lawrence and even Bryce Young and CJ Stroud coming up ahead, they are about to be tested in ways they just haven’t yet. And they haven’t met anything close to a No. 1 receiver who hasn’t carved them up already to this point, and Minter doesn’t seem to trust Chidobe Awuzie at all, leaving them short of depth and quality on the boundary and Humphrey is a shell of what he was a few years ago and Nate Wiggins has yet to take the leap and just might not be a guy who makes a lot of plays on the ball (206 times thrown on; four career picks).
So for a team that has already dealt a second-round pick to try to fix its offensive line and that brought in competition already for its kicker ( they could always trade for one of them too ) and that should be getting healthier overall on offense, cornerback looks like a bizarre need to me.
Perhaps the latest injury to young corner TJ Tampa, who the Ravens wanted fans to know was getting trade interest over the summer, is a bigger deal than we may have assumed. Corner is supposed to be their strength and he has been injured quite a bit. But now the depth and quality looks shaky.
Quarterbacks have been coming after Humphrey for years, he was a bottom 10 corner in the NFL in many categories last season , and that isn’t changing. The corners do not have an interception all season as a group, they have just six pass break ups in 86 attempts and, again. the caliber of QB is about to jump up several notches. Maybe the pass rush really gets going, which would help, but some of this is alarming.
Ravens corners are allowing a QB rating of 94.4; the QBs they have faced, for the season, collectively, have a passer rating of just 86.0 and have combined to throw 23 picks already between them. Those QBs are averaging just 6.5 yards/attempt – this has not been big-boy football by and large – but have fared better against the Ravens corners than the rest of the league they have faced.
Awuzie has played just 47 snaps in coverage all season and they seem loath to move Humphrey to the slot more because they don’t trust anyone outside. Problem is, the guys who are in the slot in the dime role – rookie Chandler Rivers til he got benched Sunday and now Keyon Martin – are both allowing a QB rating of 119 in the slot and a guy like Ja’Marr Chase, who already has three games of 190 yards or more against the Ravens, might eat them up in the slot.
For the season, here’s where the Ravens rank defending the slot (they have faced 58 passes there, seventh-most in the NFL):
Passer Rating: 117.7 (27th) Comp %: 74.1% (26th)    Y ards: 510 (27th) Yds/Att: 8.8 (23rd)
Lamar Jackson will eventually be back to save this offense – though perhaps not this week – but with each passing week this secondary gives me more pause.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: One Trade Deadline Move The Ravens Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
The Ravens are telling you they have a crisis of confidence with one position group above and beyond all else.
They want you to believe than an inconsistent second-year kicker – which is the norm and whom they refused to push with a veteran challenger all offseason long until right before final cuts – is what’s holding them back. Not the incompetent general manager who won a power struggle with John Harbaugh’s coaching staff and brought in a new one of his own choosing and still can’t fix the offensive line or pass rush or fourth-quarter defense or get the two-time MVP quarterback signed to a contract extension .
Nope, it's Tyler Loop who's the biggest issue.
It’s not that they have a collection of five-to-six of the worst, most-bloated contracts in the NFL, all of Eric DeCosta’s making . And now they want you to believe that DeCosta making a panic move to land a struggling guard who was in concussion protocol and couldn’t even play for two weeks is going to transform this OL . Okay, fine, three weeks from the trade deadline let’s play their game.
And when rookie head coach Jesse Minter refuses to really lean into his defense sucking in coverage  against bad QBs with 10-point leads week after week, but instead gives us a dissertation on a kicker who missed with the season on the line last year (yet no one did anything to push him and just talked him up all summer), we'll listen. We'll even take him at his word about what’s really holding this football team back as the Ravens opted to bring back Jake Moody, a failed journeyman kicker to this point , on the practice squad.
“There is a confidence level for how (Loop) prepares and how he practices and how he operates and how he strikes the ball, but at the same time, that position itself is completely results-driven,” Minter said Monday. “So, we'll continue to work with him and continue to try to put him in position, but we need to make second-half kicks. You could argue that second-half missed field goals are no different than turning the ball over in those situations. So, definitely something we want to keep striving to be better at."
He won’t say a bad word about the guys making $20M a year on his defense who never make a play, but Loop is the boogeyman. Okay, so do something about it then. because trying to sell Moody as some major upgrade is silly.
You want me to believe you are a kicker away? Go get this guy:
The Chargers are a joke at 0-6 and facing existential questions about Justin Herbert’s future there and Jim Harbaugh is no spring chicken and it’s this now a rebuild? Their owners are notoriously cheap and the expectation from other GMs is the Chargers start shedding salary during their bye week and reposition themselves by the deadline. They need help all over and will covert draft picks and kicker Cameron Dicker doesn’t make big money - so that’s not a big savings - but wouldn't he be worth much more to a contender?
How much is the best kicker in the NFL from 2024-2026 (91.5%) who is making just $4.25M with a manageable $5.7M cap figure (slash those totals in half if you got him midway through the season) worth to a team that fancies itself a Super Bowl contender? Go get one of the guys who knocked disgusting Justin Tucker off the mantle atop the kicking game and get him in his prime (well, he has missed two kicks this season).
But if you want to pretend Loop didn’t need competition then, and that Moody is maybe better than him now, then just go get the real thing. How much are game-winning kicks worth? Two years left on this deal, DeCosta’s old buddy Joe Hortiz is the GM with the Chargers (longtime Ravens exec) they hooked up on the Odafe Oweh deal a year ago. After what DeCosta just gave up for Cam Jurgens, trust me, Hortiz will listen.
Go get a legit kicker (maybe Chase McLaughlin from the fading Bucs). If this is a the big problem – of DeCosta’s creation, of course – then get real about fixing it.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The 5 Biggest Disappointments For The Ravens So Far
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens have played one of the easiest scheduled in the NFL, but that’s about to change.
They are going to need more consistent performances from all three phases of this football team if they are going to challenge for a Super Bowl. The first third of the season is complete, the time for growing pains and working out the kinks with a rookie coaching staff is over and they are about to be tested at a much higher level.
Oh, and it seems far certain that two-time MVP Lamar Jackson, who the highly-suspect general manager cant get signed to contract extension like everyone else with a top QB does, might not be back for Sunday's against the Bengals in another big divisional game. If that’s the case, then the individuals on this list of biggest disappointments so far are going to need to figure something out.
Last week we gave you the five biggest standouts from this roster thus far. This is the opposite end of the spectrum.
He’s been cooked for a long time and it’s been obvious to everyone except that cocky GM who wanted to prove some ridiculous point to former Ravens TE Isaiah Likely – who is a top three tight end in the NFL right now – and give Andrews a $13M/year contract extension last December despite Andrews being cooked.
Well, I don’t want to give too much away but you might be getting a hint for who is the leader in this list. Giving Andrews essentially $35M guaranteed from December of 2025 through the end of the 2027 season was ridiculous. He cost the Ravens 16 points in the Atlanta, game, he leads all NFL tight ends in drops, he averages less than eight yards per catch, he has all of one catch for four yards with the offense in desperate need of help Sunday.
When Matthew Hibner comes back from injury he needs to be seeing a whole lot more of the bench HYPER. Averaging two yards after the catch the past two years is ridiculous. He ranks 28th among TEs in Expected Points Added/Target (-.18) and is 67th in yards/target.
He was brought in for $30M a year because DeCosta got cold feet on a trade for Maxx Crosby -a dominate edge defender who does more than rush the passer. He bailed on that trade for injury concerns to sign an older pass rusher who has injury concerns; Crosby is playing 95% of the snaps and Hendrickson can’t stay healthy.
His hand/finger injury seem like a big deal and if anything Hendrickson is an opener – starting games quicky – who cant do anything in the fourth quarter (10.8% pressure rate). Baltimore remains a fourth-quarter failure, they already blew three more 10-point leads and inept against the pass in the fourth quarter despite facing most bad QBs and they have three total sacks in the fourth quarter despite facing the most dropbacks.
They rank 25th in fourth-quarter pressure rate. If this guy is limited with the hand issue for weeks to come, guys like Joe Burrow and Trevor Lawrence and Josh Allen and, yeah, Bryce Young, will cook them.
Lumping them together. Two of DeCosta’s favorites who he kept too long and paid too much. Remember when defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver vowed how both would be making people eat crow with comeback years in 2027? Um, notsomuch.
Smith carried a cap hit $14M higher than any middle linebacker in the NFL ($33M), but is fourth on the team in solo tackles and doesn’t make impact plays and isn’t a thumper around the line of scrimmage anymore and needs to be protected in coverage. He makes Fred Warner money and is often invisible for long stretches of games … for years now.
Humphrey is a liability in coverage who wants to take on top receivers but has a lot to do with why top receivers have shredded this secondary. Ravens corners and safeties do not have an INT. He is the 10th highest paid corner in the NFL at $19.3M and has the top cap hit. Not going so well. This is one of the worst second-half defenses in the NFL, and these two have plenty to do with that.
When do these guys make big plays? The defense goes as they go , and Week 1 looks like an outlier for them thus far.
We are going to give him some grace as a rookie head coach (we’re putting that on DeCosta, who wanted a novice head coach under his thumb), and he has a lot more on his plate than ever before.
But as a defensive coordinator – his forte and where he is a proven commodity, well, we’ve got issues. Continuing the fourth-quarter collapse thing is kind of unthinkable (we know its mostly the roster, but this had to be job No. 1 for him on that idea of the ball). Minter didn’t have star players with the Chargers by and large but he has a dominant pass defense and they eliminated big plays and won with scheme and were sound as heck.
So what happened? How do you explain this?
First Half          Second Half
Point Differential +52 (1st)           -35 (31st)
Opp Pt/Drive 1.47 (4th)          2.55 (24th)
Opp Pass Rt 71.8 (4th)          102.3 (22nd)
Opp Pass Yds 462 (5th)             780 (28th)
The best coordinators win the second half and tighten the screws at the half. Minter’s defense is consistently put in great positions in the first half and wilt when it counts on money downs (third-and-fourth down) against mediocre passers in the clutch. He might be spread too thin on game day and he might need to be willing to blitz more and play more man coverage and mix things up.
Every year he has the same overarching needs to fix and every year he fails.
His OL has been awful for years. He got the coaches pushed out and got the new ones he wanted, but his offensive line still stinks so bad he made a panic move for an injury risk who was probably getting benched despite being in the concussion protocol and missing two games. (In his defense, he comes from a personnel family tree that never blossoms) .
He has ceded all leverage to Jackson and repeatedly blew it with this contract situation. And put Jackson behind a bad line with only one proven downfield target – Zay Flowers – in a walk year despite running a $370M payroll (with a lot of the money blown on the other guys on this list).
Put the 16 blown double-digit leads for a loss since 2019 on him; put the franchise’s sick disease with the choke gene on the guy who keeps building the choking rosters. He’s the one constant – it’s cut across seven coordinator and two head coaches. No one, it seems, can overcome DeCosta.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: 10 Winners and 6 Losers From Ravens' Ugly Road Loss To Browns
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens had their win streak snapped in Week 6 of the 2026 regular season on Sunday by allowing the Cleveland Browns to rally in the second half and defeat them 13-10 on the road.
Despite franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson being out with an ankle injury yet again, they came into this game as favorites to come out on top but blew another double-digit lead instead . For the second time this season, they let an inferior opponent outplay them in multiple phases and are no longer in the top spot in the AFC North standings, with their second division game next week.
Here are several Ravens players and coaches who stepped up and showed out, and others who made some costly mistakes from coaching and execution standpoints.
In his first game back after missing the previous two while recovering from finger surgery, the four-time Pro Bowler and prized free agent addition of the Ravens looked every bit the elite disruptive force off the edge that they're paying him to be. Hendrickson gave Browns first-round left tackle Spencer Fano all he could handle and then some by recording his second sack of the season and eight pressures on 26 pass-rush snaps, according to NextGenStats .
With fellow rookie Matthew Hibner out with a hand injury, the fifth-rounder got a chance to use his more as a pass catcher. Cuevas set new career highs across the board by finishing second on the team with four catches on five targets for 44 receiving yards and his first career touchdown.
The two-time Pro Bowler continued to look like his old dominant self since returning from injury in this game, both as a run defender and interior pass rusher. Madubuike had several impressive run stuffs at the line of scrimmage for minimal to no gain, led all defensive linemen on the team with five total tackles, including four solos, recorded half a sack and two quarterback hits, one of which nearly resulted in a strip sack.
The third-round rookie also had an impressive return to the lineup for the Ravens after spending the last four games on injured reserve. Lane tied Cuevas for the second-most receptions and targets on the team and finished third with 40 receiving yards. He was a reliable chain-mover, especially in some high-leverage moments, with all four of his snags resulting in first downs.
The three-time All Pro had another stellar game, especially when it came to playing fast and physical downhill and making plays in the backfield. He finished with the second-most total tackles with seven, four of which were solos and three were for a loss. On his tackles behind the line of scrimmage, Hamilton snuffed out and blew up a wide receiver screen and well-timed his blitzes off the edge for the other two.
The six-time veteran had a strong game and joined elite all-time company for the second week in a row. With his first-quarter lunging sack of Watson, who was threatening to scramble, he became just the third player at 40 years old or older to record a sack since at least 1982. The other two were Hall of Famers Bruce Smith and Clay Matthews.
After playing one snap in the previous four games, the second-year pro was back in the regular rotation at the nickel spot for the first time since Week 1 and had an excellent game. Martin finished with three tackles, all of which were solo, including a clutch tackle for loss in the open field to chop down a running back behind the line of scrimmage on a checkdown. On the Browns' final drive of the first half, he recorded a pass breakup in tight coverage and his first sack of the season on back-to-back plays. Martin was unjustly and incorrectly called for defensive pass interference on a pivotal red zone play in the fourth quarter that wound up setting the Cleveland up for its only touchdown of the game.
The four-time Pro Bowler had an incredibly strong start to this game, ending the Browns' second drive with clutch back-to-back plays, with the first being his second sack of the season on a blitz and the second on a quarterback hit that was nearly his third. Smith finished with five total tackles, including three solos.
The third-year pro had a strong day, both playing in coverage and being physical in run support. He recorded a pair of solo tackles, a pass breakup and erased a couple of angles on outside runs that resulted in negative plays.
Even though he didn't record any splash plays like a sack, pass breakup or forcing a turnover, the fourth-year pro had another great all around performance. He tied for the team lead in total tackles with eight, including four solos and finished with the highest Pro Football Focus grade of any player on the team with a overall of 90.2.
A week after bulldozing the top-ranked defensive front against the run for a season-high 208 rushing yards, the same configuration struggled mightily to gain any consistent traction on the ground after the first quarter against what had been one of the worst run defenses in the league. The Ravens were held under 100 rushing yards as a team for the first time this season and just the second time in their last 16 games.
The second-year pro continued to struggle with second-half kicks in close games by going 1-of-2 on his attempts in this game, with his 49-yard miss in the third quarter looming large in a game where the Ravens lost on a walk-off chipshot attempt.
As bad and leaky as the blocking was in front of him over the final three quarters, the former Pro Bowler was inconsistent as a thrower, missing open targets and making bad decisions. He had a pair of passes late in the game that could've been intercepted, took three sacks and finished 19-of-31 for 161 passing yards and a touchdown and ran five times for 28 yards.
The first-year play-caller went from being in his bag and looking like an offensive mastermind to start the game to not having good enough answers for the adjustments the Browns made over the final three quarters. He kept calling the type of plays that Cleveland kept keying on and snuffing out, resulting in negative plays and little to no gains.
The five-time Pro Bowler and future Hall of Famer didn't have much running room after the first quarter, as he was met in the backfield by a host of Browns defenders far too often. He was held out of the end zone for the first time this season and finished with 17 carries for 58 rushing yards with a meager average of 3.4 yards per carry. While the poor blocking wasn't on him, he picked the worst possible time to have his first lost fumble of the season, as it set Cleveland up for its only red zone possession of the game that resulted in a game-tying touchdown eight plays later.
With the loss, the Ravens blew their 17th double-digit lead since 2018, which is the most in the league during that span. Just when it seems like they've kicked this recurring bad habit, it rears its ugly head again and reminds the players and fans alike that they continue to be their own worst enemy with the lead too often. If Jackson had been available for this game, they likely would've cruised to a lopsided victory, but no matter who they had under center, there's no reason they should've lost this game.

title: Ravens Are Addressing Their Kicking Situation After Another Miss From Tyler Loop Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens are once again tinkering with their kicking situation after youngster Tyler Loop missed a 49-yard kick Sunday.
Head coach Jesse Minter spoke cryptically of his Loop’s status at his Monday press conference and was critical of his consistency and, according to a league source, the Ravens are signing veteran kicker Jake Moody back to the practice squad. Baltimore originally signed Moody to the practice squad late in the summer when Loop was missing kicks in preseason games. Loop had a chance to put the Ravens up two scored Sunday and his miss loomed large in a 13-10 loss at Cleveland.
Minter was loathe to couch it as a kicking competition at the time, though general manager Eric DeCosta framed it more in that regard. Loop did not do anything to lose the job once Moody came on board, and he reached a career pinnacle in Week 3 making a game-winning kick in Brazil from 56 yards and he has also made a 60-yard kick after kicking from distance proved to be a problem in his rookie year.
Loop entered this offseason under scrutiny after missed a 48-yard kick in Pittsburgh in Week 18 which knocked the Ravens out of the postseason and gave the Steelers the AFC North title. Minter was staunchly behind the kicker even as he missed kicks at M&T Bank Stadium throughout the preseason, and Moody’s time here was brief as the practice-squad spot went to more needy positions after Loop’s fast start.
"I think like any position — you're always looking at ways of how to impact the roster, how to impact improvement,” Minter said Monday of the kicker position. “So, that one would be no different."
Moody has bounced around to three teams in his NFL career and was with Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle in Chicago last season. He finished last season strong and is a former second-round pick of the 49ers who has ties to Minter from their time together at the University of Michigan.
Loop’s issues this season are from 40-49 yards. He is just 2/5 on kicks of that distance and 10/13 overall on field goals, placing him outside the top 20 in the NFL. He has made all 16 extra points.
“Confronting issues and confronting problems is really what this whole thing's about,” Minter said, while also updating Lamar Jackson's injury status on Monday . “So, there have been a few times where it's not the end-of-a-game kick that everybody sees as a game winner, but there are kicks that take a lead from a two-score game to a three-score game a few games ago, or take that game from a one-score game to a two-score game, which, the way that game is going, is really, really critical.
“So, those are critical misses. There is a confidence level for how he prepares and how he practices and how he operates and how he strikes the ball, but at the same time, that position itself is completely results-driven.”

title: Bills Should Consider Adding $60 Million Titans' Cornerback Via Trade
full_text:
At the bye week, the Bills 2026 defense ranks poorly in just about every defensive category.
Leonhard has vowed to make changes to his defensive unit moving forward, and Bills ON SI recently suggested a few such switchups that Buffalo should consider during the current bye week .
One of those changes involved trading for another defensive playmaker. The upcoming trade deadline is less than three weeks away on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET.
And, apparently, the idea of defensive difference-makers being shipped around the league is a popular idea as ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler revealed that a player on trade watch is Tennessee Titans’ cornerback Alontae Taylor.
Taylor is a former No. 49 overall pick of the New Orleans Saints out of the University of Tennessee in 2022.
In 69 career games, which includes 58 starts, Taylor has been impactful, amassing:
That performance afforded Taylor the opportunity to test free agency inking a three-year deal with the Titans worth up to $60 million.
The switch from New Orleans to Tennessee, however, hasn’t been a warm “homecoming” for the former University of Tennessee Volunteer standout defender.  In Week 6, he was benched by Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh  due to continued poor play this season.
In fact, Taylor, who stands at 6-foot-1 and weighs 199 pounds, was a healthy scratch last Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts.
Might that mean he’s on the move in the coming weeks? Well, possibly . . . depending on what team can facilitate his hefty salary.
Could the Bills be one of those teams?
The cap space the team has to pull from isn’t very much, though, currently standing at $4.4 million in available space.
Given the team’s struggles in the secondary—both on the boundary and in the slot—the addition of another capable body to help Leonhard’s ailing defense makes plenty of sense .
Taylor's skill set appears much better suited for the nickel cornerback position, which is where he primarily played for the New Orleans Saints during his first four years in the league.
After signing with the Titans prior to this season, Tennessee suprisingly moved him to an outside corner role.  So it’s not hard to see why there might be a disconnect between the 27-year-old’s past success and his failures with his new AFC South squad.
At his stellar size, Taylor is a physical player who seems more comfortable playing closer to the quarterback and near the line of scrimmage where he can be an asset to a team in both the run and the pass game.
While it’s unclear whether or not the Titans would actually move on from their big free-agent signing after just six games, it’s a possibility seeing that Tennessee already benched him before the calendar has even turned to November.
Coupling that with the fact that Tennessee is now fighting for the No. 1 overall pick next April (battling the hapless Miami Dolphins), it would be smart for the Titans to acquire multiple draft picks to retool for 2027.
It’s never a good thing when a franchise i s thinking about the draft in the middle of October, but that’s exactly where Tennessee’s heads should be at.
Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane needs to pick up the phone and talk with the Titans’ brass.
The Bills' current nickelback Dee Alford Alford signed a 3 year, $15M contract with the Buffalo Bills before this season, but is struggling mightily in Leonard's new system.  The Bills can't wait and hope for things to work themselves out and need defensive help now.
At some point, something’s got to give with Leonhard and Co. on the defensive side of the ball, so nobody should be shocked to see Beane pull out all the stops to make sure that dreadful unit isn’t what holds Buffalo back in the playoffs once again.
Pass defense is the biggest area of concern for the Bills, so some sort of defensive back is the most logical move.
So, why not Taylor, Bills Mafia?

title: Bills' Stock Report: Ray Davis Rising, Maxwell Hairston Falling as Bye Week Arrives
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are in the midst of their bye week following a 5-1 start to Joe Brady's first season as a head coach.
While the Bills are the NFL's highest-scoring team (32.8), they are surrendering the fifth-most points per game (28.5) to opponents.
Although Brady and franchise quarterback Josh Allen have admitted that across-the-board improvement is needed , Buffalo enters Week 7 as the No. 2 seed in the AFC behind only the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0).
As for individual performers, we've singled out five players in our bye week stock report. Here are three players rising and two falling.
Don't look now, but Ray Davis is leading the NFL in kick return average (31.0) through the season's first six weeks.
After a slow start, the 2025 All-Pro has rebounded heading into the bye. In addition to huge opening kickoff returns that created points in back-to-back weeks, Davis has also seen a slight bump in offensive snaps .
"But the running back right now, I got to get Ray playing more," said Brady late last month . "He's too good of a player."
Davis, who averaged six offensive snaps per week over the first four outing, totaled 19 reps on offense over the past two games. He had a key 31-yard catch-and-run down to the 1 against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football.
Between the extracurricular nonsense and his subpar performances, the Bills needed to show safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson the door , yesterday.
Already on the decline, Gardner-Johnson's stock dropped like a rock in Week 6. After missing two tackles on Raiders' tight end Michael Mayer, he was ejected from the game due to spitting on tight end Brock Bowers .
It's just one distraction after another with Gardner-Johnson, who has shown to be a selfish player with little situational awareness. Following the Week 4 loss to the New England Patriots, he insulted wide receiver Efton Chism in his childish postgame comments.
During training camp, he violated the sanctity of the locker room by live streaming on social media. Even if he played like Ronnie Lott, he wouldn't be worth the excess baggage, and right now, he's not even playing as well as Damar Hamlin.
Keon Coleman was written off by everyone from the fans to the owner , but as Geno Smith once famously said, the Bills' wide receiver "ain't write back."
Instead Coleman has quietly done his job through the season's first six games, and he's done it well. With DJ Moore unavailable, Coleman has answered the bell .
“He's where he needs to be. He's handling everything like a pro," said Brady. "There's so much trust we have for him as the player, the development, and he continues to just make plays."
The 6-foot-3 wide receiver has touchdown receptions in each of his last three outings. For the season, he's averaging a robust 14.9 yards per reception while accounting for a 79.2 catch percentage.
The Bills' 2025 first-round pick earned the starting nod opposite Christian Benford in Week 1, but his struggles in coverage have resulted in a reduced role in Weeks 5 and 6.
He was not in the starting lineup against the Rams and the Raiders. During the two-game road swing, Hairston saw only 29 percent of defensive snaps.
Hairston has already allowed two touchdowns while opposing quarterbacks post a 96.2 rating when targeting the slightly-undersized defender. He also owns an alarming 21.4 percent missed tackle rate.
While he hasn't approached Kaiir Elam bust territory, Hairston is clearly falling out of favor due to his performance .
With Hairston's fall comes second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun's rise . The Ohio State product has earned back-to-back starts, playing with high effort and infectious energy.
According to PFF, Igbinosun has three pass break-ups playing man coverage to lead all rookies in that category. He has seven total break-ups to go with 27 tackles.
"I think what he's done the last couple weeks, he's definitely earned a high majority of the snaps at the corner position," said defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. "I know what I'm getting, play in and play out. I think he's stepped in and done a great job handling more volume in this defense."

title: Six Buffalo Bills' Bye-Week Superlatives Include James Cook, Davison Igbinosun
full_text:
As of right now, the Buffalo Bills are sitting pretty during their bye week with a 5-1 overall record and the current lead in the AFC East.
For the most part, it’s exactly the type of start to the season that Bills’ owner Terry Pegula and general manager Brandon Beane had probably hoped for this fall after the unexpected firing of longtime head coach Sean McDermott back in January.
And, the adventure to reach their current mark under the guidance of first-year head man Joe Brady has been nothing short of fascinating .
On one hand, the offense and quarterback Josh Allen are humming along at levels hardly seen before in the history of the league, as Allen and Co. are averaging the most points per game of any team aside from the Detroit Lions through six weeks of the season at a rate of 32.8 points per game.
On the other side of the coin, though, new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s unit has been one of the most disappointing groups in all of professional football midway through the month of October.
In short, describing the situation in Western New York as perplexing might be an understatement.
But, there have still been plenty of bright spots to highlight throughout the first several weeks of the 2026 campaign.
Here are Bill ON SI ’s six superlatives for Buffalo at the bye.
Honestly, is there any other player to consider here? I think not.
If it weren’t for ninth-year veteran quarterback Josh Allen, who currently leads the NFL in touchdowns scored through Week 6 with—fittingly, given his jersey number—a total of 17 trips across the goal line (9 passing, 8 rushing), then the Bills probably wouldn’t even be close to the top of the the AFC and the AFC East division at the current moment.
In fact, it wouldn’t be too hard to imagine Buffalo being 1-5 or even 0-6 if it weren’t for the incredible weekly play of Allen on offense.
The former 2024 MVP is on a roll to start the 2026 campaign, and there’s reason to believe that he could even earn another NFL Most Valuable Player award once the season is all said and done later on this winter.
In addition to his incredible touchdown output, the 6-foot-5, 237-pound gunslinger has also tallied 1,504 passing yards, 240 rushing yards, and just four interceptions.
So far, Allen has put the roster on his back, but it’s unclear if Buffalo’s current model for winning is sustainable.
In spite of his ongoing fumbling issues, outside of quarterback Josh Allen there’s no other player more important to Buffalo’s overall success than running back James Cook III .
The defending 2025 NFL rushing champion has seemingly picked up right where he left off last season as Cook’s (627 yards) currently ranked third in the league in rushing behind only Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson (641 yards) and Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker III (665 yards) through six weeks of the season.
Averaging 104.5 yards per contest at the moment, the former Georgia Bulldog is actually on pace to break his mark of 1,621 yards on the ground from one season ago as he’s currently on track to rack up 1,777 yards this season if he were to appear in every game and maintain this steady rate. Cook is also tied for second in the NFL in rushing touchdowns for running backs in 2026 with a total of six.
Simply put, the 5-foot-11, 190-pound tailback has been electric once again this season, and it’s clear he’s almost just as valuable to the offense as Allen is at this point in their careers.
It’s not quite the same, but Cook has continued to be an integral part of Joe Brady’s offensive attack, and rightfully so.
Honorable mention: WR Keon Coleman
Just as Cook III is on schedule to break his previous career-high, third-year wideout Keon Coleman is also currently en route to doing so this season for Buffalo.
The Bills have been without veteran D.J. Moore for the past two matchups, as well as during portions of other games this fall, but the unit still hasn’t missed a beat with the team’s former second-round pick out of Florida State getting the lion’s share of the load with Moore in and out of the lineup.
While it hasn’t been a massive amount of production, it’s certainly been a steady output as Coleman has recorded 19 receptions for 283 yards and three touchdowns, which sets him on pace for a solid stat line of 54 catches for 802 receiving yards and nine touchdowns.
If he can keep it up, then people might change their tune about a second contract being handed out to the 23-year-old Opelousas, Louisiana, native.
For that reason, Coleman needed to be listed as an honorable mention.
Much like with the aforementioned Coleman and Cook III, sixth-year veteran outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau is currently on a trajectory to shatter his previous career-highs in quarterback pressures, sacks, and tackles for loss.
Right now, the player nicknamed “Groot” seems to have gained an extra gear under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard despite almost every other player outside of Deone Walker struggling at this point of the season.
Rousseau has more quarterback pressures (39) than any other pass-rusher in the league according to Pro Football Focus , and he’s also second in the NFL in tackles for loss and sacks with a total of eight tackles for loss and six sacks, respectively, which is just two shy of his previous career-high of eight sacks.
The 6-foot-6, 266-pound former Miami Hurricane is on pace for a 2026 stat line of 60 total tackles, 54 quarterback hits, 22 tackles for loss, and 17 sacks.
And, astonishingly, given that Rousseau has those 39 previously mentioned quarterback pressures through six games, he’s also technically on pace for 111 total pressures this season, which is simply amazing.
Will he reach those lofty statistical levels? Probably not, but he’s still the Bills’ most dominant defender to date.
Veteran Tyler Bass had a rough stretch in 2025 due to a bout with multiple injuries pertaining to his left hip, groin, and pelvic areas, which ultimately required surgery to repair the ailments.
He missed the entirety of the season, and some fans and outside media members questioned if Bass would even be Buffalo’s starting kicker in 2026 after Matt Prater had a successful stint as the team’s placekicker last season.
In the end, however, that wasn’t the case as Buffalo didn’t bring in any competition for Bass this summer for training camp, and so far that bet has paid off.
The 29-year-old is a perfect 13-for-13 on his field-goal attempts through six games, and he’s missed just two extra points all year.
It’s been a nice developing story of redemption given Bass’ struggles with both his injuries and shaky past performances in big moments, so it’ll be interesting to see if his individual success continues moving forward after the bye week.
Although Davison “IGB” Igbinosun was a bit of a surprise pick by the Bills in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft this past April, the former Ohio State defensive back has been the team’s most consistent and promising rookie so far this season.
Now, that could all change moving forward given the possible incoming increased roles for fellow rookies Skyler Bell and Kaleb Elarms-Orr, but as of right now Igbinosun has been the best of the bunch from general manager Brandon Beane’s most recent draft class .
The 6-foot-2, 189-pound New Jersey native has started three games thus far, and he’s held his own for the most part as he’s recorded 27 total tackles and seven pass deflections.
And, given that he’s seemingly unseated fellow cornerback Maxwell Hairston at the starting position opposite Christian Benford, there’s no reason why Igbinosun shouldn’t be listed as the “Most Outstanding Rookie” for the Bills so far this season.
Surprisingly, through six games of Buffalo’s 2026 campaign, it’s been special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers—not the highly-touted up-and-comer Jim Leonhard or longtime NFL assistant Pete Carmichael Jr.—who’s been the best new assistant coach in Western New York so far this fall.
Rodgers has somehow helped revive the confidence…

title: Bills Land Ascending High-Motor Edge Rusher in New 2027 NFL Mock Draft
full_text:
For the past two seasons, Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane has been heavily focused on defense during the NFL draft. He kicked things off in 2025 with Kentucky cornerback Maxwell Hairston and used six of nine selections on defenders.
In 2026, his first selection was in Round 2, where he took Clemson EDGE T.J. Parker, followed by Ohio State cornerback Davison Igbinosun in the same round. Beane again used most of his selection on defense, taking six defenders with his 10 picks .
Despite all that attention, the defense remains problematic in Buffalo. New defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has had a rough start, but there's also still a strong need for depth. That's why SI.com' Gilberto Manzano sees the Bills looking for help on that side of the ball once again in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
Manzano has Buffalo selecting 27th overall, which is where they land UCLA's Sahir West , a player with a high motor who continues to get more attention every week for his play.
"West is getting more attention each week. Teams will likely fall in love with his intensity and motor. Even when he appears outmatched against a double team, he can break free because his energy is unmatched," Manzano wrote. "The 6'3, 279-pound pass rusher is the best player on UCLA’s dominant defense. West has 22 total tackles and two sacks this season.”
West spent two seasons with James Madison, breaking out in 2025 with 45 tackles, seven sacks, and four bass deflections. This year with UCLA, his numbers haven't been eye-popping, but he brings an infectious energy and is a disruptive force.
The real question is whether Buffalo can afford to spend a premium draft pick on the edge. While you can never have enough pass rushers, they have Greg Rousseau, Bradley Chubb, and Parker all under contract. That gives them plenty of options, and the same can't be said in the secondary.
Buffalo has been struggling in coverage both at the cornerback and safety position. West might be the best player on the board, but the Bills might need to allow their need to come into play with this selection. They've already benched Hairston this year and have struggled with injuries at cornerback as well. There's also a very slim chance C.J. Gardner-Johnson returns following his actions this past week, which led to a one-game suspension .
Manzano has the Bills taking Miami cornerback OJ Frederique Jr. at No. 61 in Round 2, but even then, they're going to be thin at safety.

title: Bills and Buccaneers Identified as Perfect Trade Partners With Buffalo's Secondary Need
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have a need at the safety position and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are a team they should have their sights set on for a possible trade.
The Bills are currently sporting a starting duo of C.J. Gardner-Johnson and Cole Bishop, but there's a few problems with that combo. Neither player has performed all that well in 2026 and Gardner-Johnson could self-destruct at any second, as we witnessed in Week 6 when he spit on a player and got both ejected and suspended for it .
If Buffalo loses either one of those players for an extended period of time for any reason, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard would be left with options that include Damar Hamlin and Jalon Kilgore.
Hamlin is not a starting-caliber player, and we can't say for sure if Kilgore is given his extremely limited sample size over the first six weeks of this season.
At the very least, the Bills could use more veteran depth, but we would like to see general manager Brandon Beane swing for the fences.
In an article naming "fairytale trades" for 10 teams , Pro Football Focus' Bradley Locker matched up the Bills and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with safety Antoine Winfield being the player he suggests Buffalo should trade for.
"It seems improbable that the Buccaneers would legitimately trade a defensive anchor in Winfield, who’s under contract through next season and would incur a $27.8 million dead cap hit if dealt," he said. "However, his work operating as a true free safety would fit excellently in Buffalo on a Bills team that lacks reliable difference-makers in its secondary."
The Buccaneers' willingness to trade Winfield depends on how they view the future of the team. Right now, that future doesn't look good.
The Bucs are a dreadful 1-5 after six games and it looks like they are going nowhere in 2026. One has to assume head coach Todd Bowles is on the hottest of hot seats, especially after last year's collapse, and it's conceivable Tampa Bay could consider hitting the reset button.
If so, trading Winfield makes sense, as he would be one of their most attractive trade chips and would garner the kind of return capable of greatly assisting a rebuild.
This is the kind of home-run swing Beane needs to take.
A two-time Pro Bowler, Winfield is one of the best and most versatile safeties in the NFL and would instantly provide an upgrade for Buffalo's defense.
Winfield can play in the box, where he's a stout run defender and plus pass-rusher when asked to blitz, but he really excels as a free safety, where he's an asset in coverage as the last line of defense.
Having Winfield would give the Bills a much deeper safeties room since it would push one of Bishop or Gardner-Johnson down the depth chart. Both players are capable of playing in the box and that would allow Winfield to take his spot back deep.
It might take a little extra to pry Winfield away from the Bucs, but as long as the price isn't egregious, Beane and the Bills should make the trade.

title: Another Bills Defender Suspended For Spitting After C.J. Gardner-Johnson Incident
full_text:
It looks like Buffalo Bills defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson wasn't the only player on the team spitting at an opponent on Sunday afternoon.
The NFL announced on Wednesday that Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. has been suspended for spitting during the Week 6 game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
"Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. has been suspended without pay for one game for an act of unsportsmanlike conduct during Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders," the NFL revealed.
The league noted that the incident occurred in the fourth quarter with 1:32 remaining, which is after Gardner-Johnson managed to get himself ejected for spitting at a Raiders player.
"With 1:32 remaining in the fourth quarter following Las Vegas' successful extra point atempt, Franklin Jr. spit at an opponent, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to 'any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."
As if spitting on someone in and of itself wasn't idiotic enough, the fact that Franklin did it after watching his teammate get ejected only makes it dumber.
According to Sal Capaccio of WGR 550 , Franklin is denying the allegation and will appeal.
"I'm told Franklin vehemently denies this ever happening and will be appealing," Capaccio reported .
It isn't clear if there's any video of Franklin spitting like there was with Gardner-Johnson. If not, that will certainly help his chances of winning the appeal.
Any appeal will be heard by and decided on by either Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera or James Thrash, all of whom are hearing officers jointly appointed by the NFL and NFLPA.
Franklin is in his seventh season in the NFL. He has spent five of those years with the Carolina Panthers and the last two with the Buffalo Bills. Over 23 games since 2025 in Buffalo, Frankin has posted 19 tackles.
In 2026, Franklin has only played on special teams, with 132 snaps in that area. He has recorded six tackles in those snaps.
Speaking of Gardner-Johnson, he has also been suspended one game, barring a successful appeal. However, that appeal is very unlikely to succeed if Gardner-Johnson goes through with one because he was caught on video and has since admitted his mistake .
"I want to take a moment to address my actions and sincerely apologize to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me," Gardner-Johnson said.
"My passing and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," Gardner-Johnson adds. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game."
While many fans called for the Bills to cut Gardner-Johnson, head coach Joe Brady has said the team does not plan on doing that.

title: Josh Allen's Basic Expectation for Buffalo Bills Following Bye Week
full_text:
Five wins and one loss may look good in the NFL standings, but for the Buffalo Bills , it's not good enough.
Despite being one of only four teams with at least five victories through the season's first six weeks, both the franchise quarterback and the head coach have acknowledged that across-the-board improvement is needed if the Bills are to get to where they want to be come February.
“I mean, 5-and-1's, it's really good. That's no secret. It's our goal to come out and be 1-and-0 each week. We feel like there's games that could have gone the other way, on both sides, so we have to continue to get better," said Allen.
According to the five-time NFL MVP finalist, there were multiple examples throughout Buffalo's final game prior to its Week 7 bye.
Although the Bills, who lead the league in scoring offense (32.8), put up 33 points in a road game, they weren't crisp in a couple of key situations. Buffalo twice settled for field goals in the red zone, including one possession that went from 1st-and goal at the 8 to 4th-and-goal at the 10.
"We can be better as an offense. We left a lot of points on the field. I don't think we were very good in the red zone tonight," said Allen.
The games will only get tougher as the season wears on, and the Bills, for the sake of their Super Bowl aspirations, have to be ready for the grind that begins with a November 1 game against the AFC rival Baltimore Ravens.
"Our best football has to be ahead of us," said head coach Joe Brady.
In order to help make that happen, the Bills have an opportunity to reset and recalibrate during the bye. It should also help that Buffalo projects to have a fully healthy 53-man roster come Week 8.
"I think that having this bye week where it is now, get away for a little bit, let guys kind of catch their breath and relax," said Allen.
For the Bills' franchise field general, it all comes down to reaching optimal performance as the season rolls on.
"When we come back, we got to play our best football," said Allen.
In their second game out of the bye, the Bills must visit the Minnesota Vikings, who are currently 5-0 with the NFL's second-ranked defense (259.8).
The Bills (5-1) trail the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) for the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Buffalo will host the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night for what promises to be an important Week 12 matchup.
It's quite clear that the toughest tests are yet to come, and the Bills will need to meet the moment.

title: Four Critical Changes That Bills Must Make During Bye Week
full_text:
At this point in the 2026 season, the Buffalo Bills are one of the most compelling teams in the National Football League.
Currently equipped with the league’s highest-scoring offense—along with the NFC’s Detroit Lions—that’s averaging 32.8 points per game through six weeks behind quarterback Josh Allen, the Bills certainly have the firepower on that side of the ball to make a trip all the way back to SoFi Stadium in Inglewood this upcoming February .
It’ll be up to Allen and Co . to stay the course and quit sounding the “smoke detectors” that have crept up and proved costly against the New England Patriots in Week 4: Buffalo’s only loss of the season so far.
On the opposite side of the operation, things look more bleak than ever before for the defense under first-year NFL coordinator Jim Leonhard , which is a unit that is currently surrendering 28.5 points per game.
Leonhard’s group, which is also allowing 386.8 yards per contest according to FOX Sports —the second most in the league, ironically, behind only Detroit, as well—has given up the second most touchdowns in the league to opposing offenses with a total of 21 trips across the goal line midway through October.
Any way someone tries to slice it, so to speak, the end results have been dicey.
The former University of Wisconsin defensive coordinator was thought to be a solution to Buffalo’s defensive woes over the past nine years under former head coach Sean McDermott , but that couldn’t be further from the truth thus far.
Something has to change, and it needs to happen quickly.
So, with the bye week upon us, here are four proposed solutions to figuring out those aforementioned miscues on both sides of the ball in order for the Bills to continue making noise later on this season . . . possibly even in February.
Although rookie defensive back Jalon Kilgore just made his NFL debut during the team’s victory on Monday Night Football over the Los Angeles Rams to end Week 5, the former University of South Carolina playmaker has shown fairly well in his first two professional outings.
Yes, there have been some ups and downs, but that’s to be expected with a 21-year-old getting his feet wet, especially for one who missed several training camp practices in August due to injury.
And, with that said, Kilgore’s rookie blunders will be much more palatable than fellow safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s continuous poor play and disturbing antics on and off the field. At this point in his career, Gardner-Johnson is all bark and no bite.
Now that he’s suspended for one week, if the Bills aren’t going to flat out release the verbose veteran, then It’s at least time for Buffalo to bench the soon-to-be 29-year-old defender in favor of its rookie fifth-round pick.
Gardner-Johnson was supposed to bring an edge to the defense in Western New York this year, however, the 5-foot-11, 208-pound trash talker has done none of that. As of now, the defense is about as edgy as a butter knife.
Keeping that in mind, Kilgore nearly had an interception of Kirk Cousins against the Las Vegas Raiders in the fourth quarter last week in limited action following Gardner-Johnson’s inexcusable ejection from the game, so there’s reason to believe that he can continue to develop and trend in a positive direction moving forward.
The former Gamecock had 178 total tackles, 21 pass breakups, eight interceptions, and four-and-a-half tackles for loss in three seasons as an undergraduate before being selected by the Bills at pick No. 167 this past April.
The cry for help at the second level of Buffalo’s defense this season is nothing new. Yet, nothing has been done about it to this point, and that’s not acceptable.
Old adage says that the definition of insanity is, “repeating the same thing over and over, and expecting different results,” and that’s exactly what the Bills seem to be doing on defense.
Jim Leonhard recently vowed that changes were on the way to his defense, but if any adjustments were made prior to the recent Raiders’ game, then they surely weren’t very apparent in terms of better results.
Yes, fourth-year linebacker Dorian Williams made his first career interception —a crucial game-changing one at that—to help the cause against Las Vegas, but fellow linebacker Terrel Bernard has been practically invisible all season in terms of being a real playmaker like he seemed to be during his first few seasons as a starter in Sean McDermott’s old defense.
Right now, Leonhard’s scheme doesn’t appear to be a fit for Bernard . . . for whatever reason.
So, while maybe it’s not necessarily time to pull the plug on Williams and Bernard as the starting tandem just yet, it wouldn’t hurt for Leonhard to consider tinkering with the lineup a little.
Elevating 12th-year veteran Shaq Thompson, who racked up 69 total tackles, eight tackles for loss, and one interception in six regular season starts and two playoff starts for the Bills last season, from the practice squad for the next three games should be the first order of business.
Unlike Gardner-Johnson this season, Thompson did provide the defense with some juice last season in his limited starting action, so there’s no reason to think he can’t do that once more despite being 32 years old.
Pairing him with rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr could be an intriguing idea moving forward in Leonhard’s 3-4 scheme, at least in certain packages or in some sort of rotation until the kinks are worked out.
There’s no other way to say it: wide receiver Joshua Palmer has been a bust of a free-agent signing for Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane so far.
Whether it be his battle with an exorbitant amount of injuries in his first year with the team last season, or his terrible struggle with drops and overall impact so far in 2026, Palmer doesn’t deserve to see many offensive snaps—if any—going forward after the bye week.
If and when D.J. Moore is fully healthy, then Buffalo’s top receivers should be Moore, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman , and rookie Skyler Bell , who has now appeared in two regular season games.
Bell hasn’t been allowed to see many snaps , though, because Palmer is still standing in the way for some reason.
At some point, the young fourth-round pick needs more opportunities between the white lines, and continuing to try and make it work with a fragmented free-agent signing from last spring doesn’t make much sense.
Buffalo should consider calling the Los Angeles Rams, who just announced a lengthy stay on the sideline for fellow receiver Davante Adams due to a hamstring injury on Monday, and see if the NFC West squad has any interest in Palmer’s services.
He did play at SoFi Stadium with the Los Angeles Chargers prior to coming to Western New York, so maybe he’d be happy for the “change” in scenery, as well.
While there are probably 20 more changes that could be made for Buffalo during the bye week, the fourth and final one on this list might be a bit of a stretch . . . but, the Bills should consider it.
Whether it be for a difference-maker in the deep secondary in lieu of the aforementioned Kilgore and Gardner-Johnson, another veteran cornerback to pair with Christian Benford instead of Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun, or taking another stab at trying to grab a fellow pass-rusher to better pair with outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau , Brandon Beane should be hitting the phones this week—and every week until the November 10 trade deadline—to try and consummate a deal for an outside defensive playmaker.
After all, the “Jimmys and Joes” are the ones that make the difference on the field. So, maybe it’s not all Jim Leonhard’s fault.
There were rumblings of some subtle disagreements between Beane and Sean McDermott last year over roster construction, and it seems like maybe McDermott was in the right.
Buffalo’s roster on defense isn’t all that great, even if it is considered the youngest unit in the National Football League in 2026.

title: Tre'Davious White Returns to Orchard Park, But This Old Bills' All-Pro Won't Be Back
full_text:
It's not like the Buffalo Bills couldn't use him just about right now .
Unfortunately, those hoping for another Jordan Poyer reunion are bound to be disappointed.
The Bills brought cornerback Tre'Davious White back into the fold on Monday, addressing a lack of depth at the position, but don't expect Poyer to follow despite the current need at safety.
The 35-year-old Poyer, who found his way back into the starting lineup after initially rejoining the Bills in a practice squad capacity last year, isn't ready to run it back one last time. Currently home in South Florida, the former All-Pro seems to be coming to terms with the reality that his playing days are likely over.
Appearing on the Buffalo Plus Podcast fewer than 24 hours after the White news broke, Poyer was put on the spot by co-host Mike Catalana.
"Jordan, when you signing with the Bills?" said Catalana.
Although Poyer, who earned 2021 All-Pro First Team honors for the Bills followed by a Pro Bowl nod in 2022, would undoubtedly like to suit up a few more times, the 13-year NFL veteran recognizes that such a wish is highly unrealistic at this point.
"I haven't officially called it [quits], and I don't know if it's because I hanging onto something," said Poyer. "Part of me knows, like, Po, there's no way you can go out there and hit nobody again. As much as I want to, and really feel like I could, deep down within, I'm like man, whatchu holding on to? At some point, I will announce my retirement. Who knows."
While his career as a player has seemingly reached its end, Poyer has no intention of leaving the football world.
"I think there's definitely coaching in the future for me. There's so much to give back to the game, and that's what I really think and feel where I can impact the game of football still," said Poyer.
In a sense, Poyer was a player/coach for Buffalo in 2025 , credited with helping young safety Cole Bishop's breakout.
Amazingly enough, Poyer was teammates with current Bills' defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard as members of the 2014 Cleveland Browns. One has to wonder if Poyer winds up on Leonhard's defensive staff at some point down the road.
Tre White is back, could Jordan Poyer be next? The former Bills safety join us on the @BuffaloPlus podcast with Micah Hyde and I asked Poyer about Buffalo #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/5QtKwbIFpp
When appearing on Mitch Morse's In Good Company Podcast on radio row at Super Bowl LX, Poyer teased the possibility of one more dance with the Bills.
"I do feel like I still have some [football left] in me. I found a little rhythm this last year that kind of got some more excitement to be like, 'okay, what if?'" said Poyer. "I'm taking one day at a time, enjoying my family right now, enjoying, being home, being here, hanging out."
While his heart may have been saying yes, it appears as if Poyer's mind told him his time has passed .
