title: Everything Chicago Bears Have to Fear About New England Patriots in Week 7
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are turning the page from Week 6 quickly as they prepare for a Thursday night showdown against the New England Patriots in Week 7.
The Bears are coming off a bounce-back performance with their win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday while the Patriots are looking for their fourth straight win after a 1-2 start.
The last time these two teams squared off was in 2024, when the Patriots beat then-rookie Caleb Williams and the Bears, 19-3. New England has had Chicago's number for years now, with the Pats winning six out of the last seven against the Bears.
Here's the three biggest concerns the Bears have when it comes to their Week 7 opponent.
The Patriots don't have an elite pass-rush with just 14 sacks, but they do have 12th-most pressures, the eighth-highest pressure percentage and the ninth-best pass-rush win rate , per ESPN, so New England is certainly formidable.
Christian Barmore and Milton Williams are two players to watch out for on Thursday. The interior duo has combined for 3.5 sacks and 21 pressures over six weeks and could be even more of a problem if the injured guard Jonah Jackson doesn't play.
The good news is, Caleb Williams has elite mobility, so he can negate the pressure New England is capable of bringing, but nothing is guaranteed on a snap-by-snap basis.
In terms of passing yards allowed per contest, the Pats are giving up the 11th-fewest in the NFL and have one of the better one-two punches at cornerback in the league with Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis, the latter of whom is on track to return from injury after being upgraded at practice on Tuesday .
New England also has Kevin Byard patrolling the back end and Bears fans know first hand how good of a ball-hawking safety Byard is.
Bears pass-catchers are going to have a stiff test on Thursday night.
The Patriots have been pretty stingy against the run in 2026, with New England sporting the ninth-lowest yards-per-game average. Mike Vrabel's defense is also giving up just 3.9 yards per carry.
That's particularly troubling for the Bears because they are likely to be without Kyle Monangai once again this week and instead Roschon Johnson will spell D'Andre Swift, which amounts to a downgrade for Chicago.
What's even worse about not having Monangai is the Bears have been leaning on Swift less and less in the second half of games to keep him for the entire season.
After a brutal start to the season, Maye has played much better of late and is looking more like the MVP candidate he was in 2025. In his last three games, Maye has thrown for 878 yards and 11 touchdowns to one pick.
Not only is Maye a major threat with his arm, but he is capable of taking off with the football to evade the pass-rush and pick up back-breaking gains with his legs.
Maye's outlook is even better now that A.J. Brown is back. Granted, Brown struggled mightily last week with some brutal drops in his first game back from injury, but he should be better this week now that he's had a chance to shake off some rust.
In years past, we would have been confident in Jaylon Johnson shutting Brown down, but Johnson has been a shell of that guy since last season, so there is major concern about the Bears' ability to keep Brown in check.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Bears Reload the Defensive Line in Latest 2027 NFL Mock Draft
full_text:
Entering the 2026 NFL season, the Chicago Bears' defensive line was expected to be its biggest weakness, and while it hasn't been perhaps as bad as expected, this unit could still use an infusion of talent. A fairytale trade scenario may be something the Bears consider, but it's more likely that they seek a boost to their pass rush in the 2027 NFL draft.
That's exactly what Gilberto Manzano, an NFL analyst for Sports Illustrated has the Bears doing in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft . In this two-round mock, Manzano has the Bears selecting EDGE defenders with their first and second round picks. They land Alabama's Yhonzae Pierre in Round 1 with the No. 28 pick, then select Oregon's Matayo Uiagalelei at No. 59 in Round 2.
Justifying the Pierre pick, Manzano writes, "Pierre tends to have quiet stretches, but he has plenty of upside due to his athleticism and size... with 3.5 sacks this season, [he] can put it all together at the next level."
As for Uiagalelei, Manzano noted, "The defense is what’s holding back coach Ben Johnson’s team. The 6'5", 270-pound Uiagalelei excels at setting the edge and consistently winning his matchups in passing situations."
I applaud Manzano's effort to reload Chicago's defensive line, given it's lack of star-power. In fact, they may choose to release what little talent they do have in the offseason. Montez Sweat, who recently got himself suspended for two games for violating NFL policy , will be on the last year of his contract in 2027, and the Bears could create $21 million in salary cap space by releasing him, according to Spotrac .
However, I'm not sure that the defensive line is their biggest problem anymore. The cornerback room has been a nightmare of inefficiency so far through 2026. Jaylon Johnson is allowing a 115.1 passer rating when targeted, according to Pro Football Focus , making him and his $76 million contract a cut candidate in 2027 . Tyrique Stevenson continues to run hot and cold. The only bright spot in that room is fourth-round rookie Malik Muhammad.
With that in mind, it might behoove the Bears to target a cornerback with their first-round pick next year. Georgia's Ellis Robinson IV would be a great fit for Dennis Allen's man-heavy defensive scheme, but he goes at No. 26 to the Cleveland Browns in Manzano's mock draft. In the second round, either Alabama's Zabien Brown or Mississippi State's Kelley Jones would also be good options.
At the end of the day, it's far too early in the season to take mock drafts too seriously. We still have no idea where the Bears could end up picking, and with the trade deadline still on the horizon, the Bears could make a splashy move that both addresses these roster concerns while relieving them of their top picks.
Two defensive linemen may be exactly what the Bears need in April, but one would hope that the significant investments they've already made at that position, namely Austin Booker, Dayo Odeyingbo, and Shemar Turner, would make that unnecessary. Especially since the cornerback room looks to be in rough shape.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Chicago Bears D-Line Will Have a Chance to Take Over the Game Against Patriots
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' defensive line was widely considered the team's most glaring weakness this offseason, and many were surprised they didn't make a more concerted effort to improve the unit.
However, they're currently tied for fifth in the league with 17 sacks. While a handful of those came from a few defensive backs ( *cough* Kyler Gordon ), the defensive line has played much better than expected thus far.
They've played a big role in all four of the team's victories, and are a major reason they boast the league's seventh-best defense (and ninth-best rush defense) through six games. A bit of misfortune on the Patriots' end could also allow them to have a massive impact on Thursday night's contest.
The Patriots already weren't in a great spot up front entering Sunday's game against the Jets. Three offensive linemen were already on Injured Reserve, including star guard Mike Onwenu.
Unfortunately, their injury luck worsened significantly against New York, as three more linemen went down in Week 6. Two of them, guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown, are already listed as doubtful for Thursday night's matchup. Meanwhile, right tackle Morgan Moses is considered questionable.
They might not be big names, but all three players have helped the unit rank fifth in pass-block win rate (56%) and eighth in run-block win rate (75%). Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has only been sacked twice over the past three weeks.
While New England has high hopes for backup tackle Caleb Lomu , whom they selected in the first round of this year's draft, if Moses can't go, they're in a much worse spot at guard. Third-year man Walter Rouse would be in line to make his first career start on one side, and veteran journeyman Matt Pryor would start on the other. That's not an ideal situation for a team hoping to establish offensive consistency.
The Bears also might not have their full complement of d-linemen ( they'll be without two key starters , Dayo Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat), but their previously maligned defensive interior will have a chance to quiet their doubters on Thursday night.
Grady Jarrett's stat line (11 tackles, 1 TFL) might not jump off the page through the first six games, but he's been far more disruptive this season than he was last year. He has a good chance to continue that trajectory against New England's injury-riddled offensive line.
Meanwhile, the rest of the rotation must bring their A-game to capitalize on the situation. Kentavius Street and James Lynch have both shown flashes, and they should get plenty of opportunities to build on them against the Patriots.
If Chicago's defensive line doesn't let the Patriots establish a rhythm, the Bears will have a good chance to come out of Thursday night with a victory.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears Connected to Elite 4-Time Pro Bowl Defensive Tackle in 'Fairytale' Trade Scenario
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have multiple needs along the defensive line ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, with one of those needs coming at defensive tackle.
The Bears sent Gervon Dexter packing in a trade with the Atlanta Falcons before the season started, and say what you want about Dexter being a poor fit in Dennis Allen's defense, the Bears still miss his pass-rushing skills .
As Dexter has racked up two sacks and 21 pressures over six games (the latter mark ranks fifth among interior defenders), Chicago has gotten half of that sack production out of its defensive tackles thus far.
The Bears' run defense up the gut hasn't been great, either, with Chicago giving up the ninth-most yards per carry and sporting a 27% run stop win rate , which ranks 28th, per ESPN.
In an ideal world, the Bears pull off a trade for an interior lineman who can provide a boost to the pass-rush and the run defense.
In an article dreaming up 10 fairytale trades ahead of next month's deadline, Pro Football Focus' Bradley Locker connects the Bears to star Tennessee Titans defensive tackle, Jeffery Simmons.
"While the Titans have floundered over the past two seasons — going a combined 4-19 in that span — that hasn’t deterred Simmons," Locker said. "His 90.0 overall PFF grade is the second-best among all defensive linemen since the start of 2025, and his 91.0 PFF pass-rush grade also leads the pack."
"The Bears’ defense has punched above its weight in 2026, sitting 12th in EPA per play," Locker added. "However, the team owns the third-worst overall PFF grade among interior defender units, with Chicago’s 9.5% pressure rate at the position tied for 30th."
Talk about exactly what the Bears need. Simmons checks both boxes the Bears must improve upfront.
Simmons is a top-notch interior pass-rusher, as evidenced by his four sacks and 21 pressures, which rank fourth and fifth among interior defensive linemen, according to PFF .
Simmons is also an elite run defender, with the four-time Pro Bowler tallying a 78.8 grade in that area, ranking fifth at his position.
The Titans are going nowhere once again this season, so the team selling off pieces at the deadline is possible. However, that doesn't mean Simmons will be one of them.
Chances are Simmons will have to force his way out of Nashville, and we could see that happening.
Simmons has reiterated time and time again he's sick of losing , something the Titans have done a lot of the last four years and stand to do again this season after a 1-5 start.
Simmons is the best of the best at the defensive tackle spot and just turned 29 years old, so he's going to be extremely expensive. It will probably take a first-round pick just to get the conversation started.
That's a lot, but it would be worth it for the massive upgrade that Simmons can bring to Chicago's defense. Further softening the blow is the fact that Simmons is under contract through 2030, which means there's no risk he'll leave anytime soon.
The Bears have just a few more years before Caleb Williams' salary balloons to a massive number, and combined with the fact that the Bears look like true contenders this season, now is the time for general manager Ryan Poles to make this kind of investment.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Kevin Byard Commands Attention of Caleb Williams and Bears Offense
full_text:
Oh yes, Caleb Williams went there.
The Bears quarterback brought up the age of 33-year-old Patriots safety Kevin Byard , his former Bears teammate .
“Being able to go versus him in practice for two years; I mean he's a super savvy vet," Williams said Tuesday after practice. "I know he's getting up there in age, but he's still fast."
Williams did say it with a smile while everyone laughed, a sure sign he was kidding his former teammate.
There is not animosity there and Williams even pointed out when the Bears and Patriots play Thursday his former teammate does have a bit of an advantage.
What a great play Sunday from #Patriots Kevin Byard to start the game and not allow the Jets 6 👏 pic.twitter.com/oNftKhObCJ
"I've seen him work, he studies film, he still moves extremely well and he knows the route concepts really well," Williams said. "Excited to go versus him. It's going to be a great challenge for us, a great challenge for me and the wide receivers to be able to go out there and execute and complete passes and keep being the offense and identity that we want to be.”
This will be a reunion game for the second straight week. The Bears fared well last week against former Bears defensive tackle Gervon Dexter and former Bears receiver Olamide Zaccheaus. Byard commands a little more respect as a top 100 player in the NFL.
Byard remains a player all the Bears talk of with reverence, whether player or even head coach Ben Johnson —  even if GM Ryan Poles and the coaching staff chose not to cough up $9 million in cap space the Patriots did to sign him in free agency, while spending it instead on younger free agent Coby Bryant.
No. 61 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Patriots S Kevin Byard! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/o8L2Lf6tGF
"KB, it’ll be great," wide receiver Rome Odunze said. "We’re on opposing teams so it’ll be a little bit of action there but I’m excited about it. He’s a tremendous player. I’m looking forward to going up against him and hopefully after the game, after the win, I’ll say my hellos."
Byard is already warning his teammates in the secondary not to get too comfortable at Soldier Field because they'll be facing an offense known for trickery.
"I know Ben," Byard told New England reporters. "Being Thursday night, he’s gonna have some stuff up his sleeve. It’s a primetime game. He’s gonna want to show off his expertise on Thursday night.”
Side-by-side of Kevin Byard and @terrellowens , 18 years apart, celebrating on the star at midfield in Dallas. 👀 @KB31_Era pic.twitter.com/d5FgFjVDUG
The signing of Bryant hasn't worked yet for the Bears, as he suffered a knee/leg injury in training camp and hasn't played this year. Sure, they could have used Byard for another year instead. Byard still has never missed a game in what is now an 11-year career.
"I love Kevin Byard and what he brings to the table," Johnson said. "You can tell he really fits their defense well in terms of the communication and what they're asking them to do."
How Patriots coach Mike Vrabel is using Byard is much like in their stint together with the Titans for 5 1/2 seasons. His passer rating against is an outstanding 76.8, better even than last year's 96.5 when he made All-Pro and the Pro Bowl for the Bears.
Former Bears S Kevin Byard says he already knows Ben Johnson is going to have tricks up his sleeve on Thursday Night Football: “I know Ben. Being Thursday night, he’s gonna have some stuff up his sleeve. It’s a primetime game. He’s gonna want to show off his expertise on…
What Byard isn't doing is getting beat for touchdowns this year. He hasn't allowed one yet, per Pro Football Reference. He gave up 10 in two seasons with the Bears and two the previous half season with Philadelphia after he left Tennessee.
Pro Football Focus' grading for Byard hasn't been so generous. They have him 78th of 98 NFL safeties overall, 80th of 98 in pass coverage and 68th stopping the run. They're blaming him for a lot more plays against the Patriots' secondary than PFR's Stathead does, giving him a 110.6 passer rating against.
If it's not Byard doing it, then someone is for the New England defense because they're 11th against the pass,. ninth against the run and sixth overall, and have allowed the fifth fewest points.
Why did the Bears let Kevin Byard walk to the Patriots in free agency in the offseason? Byard "was everything they could've asked him to be" in Chicago, @BradBiggs says before offering his best read on Byard leaving for New England. pic.twitter.com/kwvx9XOKy1
"(Cornerback) Christian Gonzalez on the outside just trying to figure out where he'll be and where he'll line up," Johnson said. "But all of those guys, they're fundamentally sound. They tackle really well. They shed blocks really well.
"And then schematically, they try to take away what you do best. And that's the challenge.”
It can't hurt having a wise old veteran in back directing it, one who always seems to answer the bell.
The Bears definitely have missed that this year as defensive coordinator Dennis Allen may be juggling his lineup again this week just as he has virtually every week since the season began without Bryant and also without Kyler Gordon, who is now back. Cam Lewis is at safety now after they cut Xavier Woods last week.
Rookie Dllon Thieneman continues to learn lessons each week in back.  There's a lot to be said for experience.
. @nyjets @Patriots @KevinByard one of the great FS to play this game...He isn't saving lives; but he is saving Touchdowns. #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/DqiLhyh7HH

title: Joe Burrow Reacts to Vice President JD Vance Attending Bengals Practice
full_text:
The Bengals hosted Vice President JD Vance during their practice session on Wednesday. A few members of the team got to meet the politician as Vance toured the Paycor Stadium facilities following Wednesday's outing.
Burrow discussed the visit during his weekly press conference just minutes after the fellow southern-Ohio native exited.

"We did not," Burrow said about having an interaction. "He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn't get to."

And that's everybody in the locker room. That's why we do what we do, whether it's on the TV, whether it's in person, whether it's on the practice field, that's what we do."
Burrow and the whole team are focused on a massive divisional game in Baltimore.

"It's a big game," Burrow said about the matchup to start his press conference. "There's a lot of football to be played after this, but anytime we play the Ravens with a place in the division on the line, it's going to be a big game. So we're treating it that way."

title: JD Vance Attends Bengals Practice After Cincinnati Visit
full_text:
Vice President JD Vance attended Bengals practice on Wednesday afternoon. Vance spent more than a half hour on the practice field.
The Bengals are preparing for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
After the practice visit, Vance's team walked through the locker room and the facilities. He grew up roughly 37 miles from Paycor Stadium in Middletown.
Vance was elected as Vice President in 2024 and was in town for a visit ahead of next month's midterm election.
Joe Burrow talked with Bengals owner Mike Brown ahead of Wednesday's session. It's easy to think that Brown was talking with Burrow about Vance's visit. Maybe not, but it's rare for Brown to talk to Burrow during practice—even while the star quarterback is warming up.
Vice President JD Vance arriving at Bengals practice today. @WLWT pic.twitter.com/fTCpZcsZM0
Vance hasn't been shy about weighing in on the Bengals in the past. Last year he discussed his fandom on the This Past Weekend Podcast With Theo Von.
Ironically, he made the case for signing Trey Hendrickson. The Bengals let Hendrickson walk in free agency and they'll face off on Sunday in Baltimore.
"Hendrickson is worth it, dude. He's a generational talent," Vance said . "It's very hard to get a guy like that. It's kind of crazy how, like, I'm a big football fan, but edge rushers have become ... It's almost like where left tackles were 10 or 15 years ago, where everybody just realized there's this really underpaid position that you gotta have. And so, yeah, I think we're [the Bengals] gonna have to pay Hendrickson.
"Here's what I'll say to Trey, if you're watching this show. If you're a Republican, I will show up to a Bengals game and take a photo with you if you sign on with the Bengals. And if you're a Democrat, I'll stay the hell away. Just sign with the Bengals because we got a chance, man. I say this every year, but with Burrow, with Ja'Marr Chase, if we get our defense and our offensive line, we could have a true championship run."

title: Zac Taylor Drops Latest Bengals Practice Statuses as Team Health Improves Entering Ravens Matchup
full_text:
It's all game weeks all the time for the Cincinnati Bengals moving forward in 2026. Zac Taylor's team is rolling into another practice today with pretty much every name on the active 53-man roster ready to row together and face the Ravens.
The only injury to monitor as of this writing is Kyle Dugger (quad), but he suited up for practice Wednesday and is on track to return. The backup safety was week-to-week and Taylor noted he made "great progress" over the team's bye week
Other than the injured reserve players, there are no other injuries for the Bengals. Taylor did say Andrei Iosivas is "making good progress" during his IR recovery from finger surgery.
Cincinnati is facing its second division opponent of the season, having already lost to the Steelers a few weeks ago. A 0-2 start in the division would be a tough hole to climb out of.
Colbie Young is slated to be right near 100% for this game as the young receiver tries to make an impact this season.
"He's looked as good as he's looked in a long time," Taylor said about Young on Monday. "I think last week he had a good week on what he could handle from a rehab perspective. So this week to get him back involved, he looked good running around. So I think it's good to finally get him back and feel like he's closer to 100% health."
They actually get to face the Ravens on the road outside of primetime this go-around and boast the league's easiest remaining schedule according to ESPN's FPI.
The early bye week could end up benefiting Cincinnati if they handle player workloads the right way over the next three months.
"Not necessarily in the games. No, I mean we're going to do everything we can to win," Taylor said about changing player workloads in an early bye week season. "Does it change the workload during practice? Potentially. I think we've done a good job of that so far during the season with some of the guys that are more veteran. So we're never shying away from helping guys during the week that maybe don't need the physical reps, and we need them healthy on Sunday.
"Obviously, strange weeks are coming forward at us, and so we'll do a great job just with the schedule and trying to keep it off those guys as best we can."
Cincinnati is gunning for a 4-2 record this weekend.

title: Lamar Jackson's Initial Practice Status Revealed as Bengals-Ravens Week Ramps up
full_text:
The Bengals are preparing to face Lamar Jackson (ankle) this week, but it may be Tyler Huntley time again for the Baltimore Ravens.
The team has gone 1-1 in the past two games without Jackson and he did not appear during the open portion of practice on Wednesday. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter was pretty vague about Jackson's status this week.
"I'd still put it in kind of the day-to-day thing," Minter said during Monday's press conference. "We'll know a lot more on Wednesday, I would say."
Wednesday is here and Jackson is not rolling out there, one other impactful player with murky injury status for Baltimore is center Cam Jurgens (concussion). His official status is getting confirmed later this afternoon on the injury report, but Minter sounded confident on Monday that he'd play.
UPDATE: Jackson did not appear in the open media portion but Minter noted "he got some work in" on Wednesday.
"We feel like it's come a long way over the weekend and that there's a real opportunity for him," Minter noted. "The final deal (exiting concussion protocol) may be today or tomorrow as we go, but we're excited to potentially get him in there this week."
Jackson has had a lot of success against Cincinnati in his career and could be even more effective with Jurgens snapping to him.
The electric quarterback is 11-3 all-time against Cincinnati and has won six of the past seven matchups.
"You know so much more about these teams, about these players," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about the matchup. "Obviously they got new schemes, but there's still a lot of similarities from from the past. They got great players, great coaching staff. It's exciting. I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get it fired up for every game, but every point in Baltimore in a divisional game, it's a fun one to get out for, and our guys will be up for it."
Jackson has two more chances to practice and likely needs to at least be limited on Friday to have a shot at getting a 12th win against Cincinnati.

title: Report: NFL Teams 'Tracking' Young Bengals Defender For Potential Trade
full_text:
One young Bengals piece could be a hot option for teams trying to add talent over the next three weeks. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported on Wednesday that Shemar Stewart is a name "teams are tracking" as the trade deadline approaches on Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.
Stewart has dealt with injuries in both his underwhelming Bengals seasons so far and hasn't broken into the main defensive line rotation yet.
Former Bengals safety Jessie Bates III also popped up as a name to watch from Fowler.
"One surprise name a few teams are tracking is Cincinnati edge rusher Shemar Stewart," Fowler wrote . "The 2025 first-round pick is not a factor in the team's rotation right now. He has played 17 defensive snaps, well behind the total for the fourth defensive end, Cedric Johnson (83). And rookie second-rounder Cashius Howell has been impressive.
"Cincinnati typically doesn't move its young draft picks, but it would be surprising if the Bengals haven't received inquiries on Stewart, whose upside remains high. Also, could a team pry safety Jessie Bates III out of Atlanta? He will be a free agent in 2027, and the Falcons are sitting at 2-4. I doubt Atlanta wants to trade him, but his value would be strong if that changes."
On the season, Stewart holds a 68.9 Pro Football Focus grade and has increased his snap diet from five and four snaps in his opening outings to eight against Miami, but he's clearly not a major factor for the defensive front right now.
It's hard to say the training camp knee injury is the reason. He hasn't been featured on many October injury reports, and that knee hyperextension was nearly three months ago .
"Well, we got a really good defensive end group, and all four of those guys played well. There are going to be moments when we get Shemar more involved. Yesterday just didn't work out that way and he's still in his ninth practice. Really started practicing three weeks ago. Happy with him. He's got a great effort, great attitude," Taylor said about Stewart after the loss to Pittsburgh last month. "And so there will be moments we're able to get him more plays. There'll be times where maybe he goes from a small number to 25-30 (snaps). You just never know. So he's had a good attitude about it."
Stewart did not play in that contest but had minor appearances in the following two games.

title: Referee Report: Bengals To End Longest White Hat Drought Sunday Vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals’ longest referee drought will come to an end Sunday in Baltimore.
For the first time in more than three years, Shawn Smith will work a Bengals game. The last time the league assigned him to work a Cincinnati game was Week 4, 2023, which was a 27-3 loss in Nashville.
The Bengals are just 1-4 with Smith as the referee, with the lone win coming in his third career game as a white hat, the memorable 37-36 win in Atlanta on A.J. Green’s late touchdown catch from Andy Dalton.
Smith also worked a pair of Bengals losses in 2020 – the 35-30 setback against the Cleveland Browns in Joe Burrow’s first career primetime game in Week 2, and the 20-9 defeat at Washinton a couple of months later when Burrow tore his ACL.
And Smith was the referee for the canceled game against Buffalo in wake of Damar Hamlin's medical emergency.
The longest Bengals referee drought after this weekend will be Shawn Hochuli, who hasn't worked one of the team's games since Week 13, 2024.
The Ravens are 7-4 with Smith as the referee.
Smith and his crew are averaging 13.33 penalties per game, which ranks 13th among the 17 referees.
However, his 43 flags against road teams rank fourth.
That falls in line with his 2025 numbers, when he ranked 13th in accepted penalties (11.56) and tied for fourth in flags against road teams (119).
Smith and his crew are averaging 4.33 offensive holding penalties per game this season, which is third most. Fifteen of those were against the home team, with 11 against the visitors.
The crew is tied for third in defensive holding penalties with 1.17 per game.
Smith is in his 12th season as an NFL official and ninth as a head referee.
He’s earned six consecutive postseason assignments, including his first Super Bowl last year when the Seattle Seahawks beat New England Patriots.
Smith had an NFC Divisional Round assignment in 2024, and he worked the 2023 AFC Championship Game in which the Kansas City Chiefs won at Baltimore.
In 2022, Smith did the memorable Wild-Card comeback by the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Los Angeles Chargers. And in 2020 and 2021, he worked AFC Wild-Card games.

Bengals 3-31; Washington 6-49

title: Bengals Get Encouraging Injury News on Key Playmaker Ahead of Ravens Game
full_text:
Every game is important in the NFL. However, the Cincinnati Bengals are preparing for a massive Week 7 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
The AFC North is one of the most competitive divisions in the league. A loss for the Bengals would move the team to 0-2 in the division and would also keep them in last place. It's all hands on deck for the Bengals this week, and it felt that way with Zac Taylor's comments to the media on Monday.
As the Bengals deal with a banged-up wide receiver room, Taylor revealed a positive update on rookie wide receiver Colbie Young, who could make an impact for the team on Sunday.
"He's looked as good as he's looked in a long time," Taylor said. "I think last week he had a good week on what he could handle from a rehab perspective. So this week to get him back involved, he looked good running around today. I think it's good to finally get him back and feel like he's closer to 100% health."
The 2026 fourth round pick suffered a knee injury in just his third game of his NFL career. In his short time on the field, Young has two receptions for the Bengals.
If Young is looking as good as Taylor says he is, the rookie wide receiver has a massive chance to stake his claim for the third option in a crowded room.
Andrei Iosivas is still dealing with a thumb injury, meaning Young could get a lot of snaps as the team's third option at wideout this Sunday.
The injury to Iosivas has been brutal for a receiver who is still looking to make his name for the Bengals. But after a strong camp from Young, it feels like Iosivas may soon run out of opportunities to make his name with the franchise.
The Week 7 matchup with the Ravens could be the one that leads to the Bengals finding another reliable offensive weapon.
Quarterback Joe Burrow and this Bengals offense aren't going to hide their strength. The pass game is going to be on full display. Can Young make his presence known?
It feels strange to say so early in his career, but if Young is ready to go, this could be a career-defining game for the young receiver.

title: Film Breakdown Reveals Why the Bengals Struggle to Stop This Type of Run
full_text:
The Bengals defense has improved when comparing this season to last year. They have gone from about 29 points per game to about 22 points per game. That takes them from 30th to about 14th so far this season. However, they have a very clear issue on defense and it’s something that has plagued them for a few years now. They struggle heavily against perimeter runs.
The Bengals run defense has generally been pretty good this season. They’re actually ranked 4th in FTN’s DVOA ranking for run defense. On all runs, the Bengals are allowing 4.5 yards per carry, a 38.5% success rate, 16.4% explosive play rate, and -0.04 EPA per play. However, all of those numbers spike when it comes to perimeter runs. Against perimeter runs, the Bengals are allowing 6.4 yards per carry, a 46.4% success rate, 32.1% explosive play rate, and +0.17 EPA per play.
These perimeter runs have also been a great way to attack the Bengals defense with Dexter Lawrence on the field. With Lawrence on the field, the Bengals run defense is allowing 3.7 yards per carry, a 34.2% success rate, 13.5% explosive play rate, and -0.06 EPA per play. Against perimeter runs those numbers once again sky rocket. The Bengals defense gives up 5.1 yards per carry, 37.5% success rate, 22.2% explosive play rate, and +0.08 EPA per play.
Not only are those numbers abysmal, but teams keep attempting more perimeter runs against the Bengals now that they can recognize this as a weakness.
In Weeks 1 and 2, the Bengals faced a combined eight perimeter runs. They faced six perimeter runs in both Week 3 and Week 4. They faced eight perimeter runs in Week 5. That’s 20 of the 28 perimeter runs in the last three games and there is no reason to think that it’s going to slow down any time soon.
There’s not a simple easy solution for these struggles and there’s also not just one finger to point. There are multiple issues for the Bengals when it comes to their struggles against the perimeter run game.
pic.twitter.com/XfEvCfP2SP
On this play alone, there are a plethora of issues present. The issues start with the play side end (Boye Mafe) who gets pinned by the Y. The next issue is that the nickel (Dax Hill) gets pinned and driven downfield by the F. The next problem comes from the 20 backer (Barrett Carter) who runs himself out of the play by going underneath the block from the center rather than fighting and getting over that block. With all 3 of those support players forced inside and underneath, the force from DJ Ivey is useless. The post safety (Jordan Battle) is the only player left who can make this stop.
Here is a comparison with a surprisingly good perimeter run defense in the Falcons.
pic.twitter.com/faOuFpZqsJ
The play side end fights to get over the block from the Y, the 40 backer flows over that block and takes out both the puller and the fullback, and the strong side safety avoids the block from the wide receiver before making the stop.
pic.twitter.com/lQmh8eyKhu
This time the Bengals are facing a reverse with a false pull. The first issue is that the playside end (Cashius Howell) does not get himself into position to make the play. Carter is in a 60 position over the Y and actually reads this out pretty quickly but he is physically manhandled by Aaron Brewer and pancaked.
Jordan Battle is the near safety on the play but he takes himself out of the play by going inside and underneath of the block from the backside guard. If he could fight over that block and force this further inside, then both Bryan Cook and Hill are in position to make the play. Cook still has an attempt but he is unable to bring down the ball carrier and the play ends up being an easy chunk play for the Dolphins.
Here is a comparison with one of the best perimeter run defenses in the league in the Texans:
pic.twitter.com/FdbCmIrljv
Watch how Will Anderson Jr. makes this play on his own as the playside end. Anderson has incredible processing to recognize this as an end around and he cuts it off by getting penetration.
pic.twitter.com/jiufBBy7Mm
This is just a jet sweep but the Bengals get caught in a nickel B gap blitz. This takes out one of the support players who could help make a stop here but there’s still unsound play from the other defenders. Both the playside end and the nickel could possibly make this play but the backer is unable to get over or defeat the block from the Texans X wide receiver. The corner then gives a very weak tackle which allows the ball carrier to pick up about seven additional yards.
The Bengals defense is going to need to be better against these runs. They need to play team football to do so. Working over the top of blocks won’t give a player stats but it will funnel the ball to his teammates. Right now a majority of the Bengals defenders try to go underneath those blocks to make a superhero play. They aren’t making that play and instead they’re stopping anyone from making that play. Additionally, all of the Bengals defensive ends need to do a better job. Whether that’s as the backside contain player for end arounds or the playside end on crack toss, they need to get themselves in position to make plays more difficult for opponents. Lastly, the nickel needs to be better against F tight end and slot wide receiver blocks. The best defenses in the league have a nickel who is willing to fight blocks. Through five weeks, the same cannot be said about this Bengals defense.
The good news is that these are all mental and technical issues which means they are fixable to some degree. It’s absolutely possible that they come out after the bye as a sound, team defense against these runs. The coaching staff is certainly going to make it a point of emphasis as they have alluded to the fact that they are struggling in this area. It has to improve on Sunday against the Ravens.

title: Bengals Should Buy Low, Trade For New York Giants Running Back to Enhance Offensive Depth
full_text:
The Bengals need to solidify their running back room entering the home stretch of the 2026 season, and a recently embattled young rusher could be the right answer.
Cincinnati may be able to trade for Giants running back Cam Skattebo after he seemingly entered head coach John Harbaugh's doghouse this month.
Skattebo has 81 carries for 291 yards and a score this season, but he played just six snaps on Sunday after being at 34-plus in every game this season.
"You can say, well, I don't like that. I don't like you divvying up the snaps between four backs. And I can tell you, I don't like it either," Harbaugh said about the snap drop for Skattebo on Sunday. "One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back.
"And none of those guys have done that yet. And when one of those guys steps up to be the back, then they'll be the back. That's your answer. And that's as honest as I can be about it. And they know that, too. And believe me, they're all hungry. They want to step up. One of those guys wants to step up. Somebody's going to step up and take that job. We're going to see who it is."
New York has three running backs (Najee Harris cut on Tuesday) vying for snaps on its roster right now and clearly isn't 100% bought in on Skattebo leading the room.
The 2025 fourth-round draft pick might be had for a low-value Day 3 pick in next year's draft, unlike some more expensive RB options out there, and he's flashed some great running before.
Skattebo has just a 55.4 Pro Football Focus grade this season and won't bring anything as a pass blocker (36 pass-blocking grade on 25 snaps this season), but he ran really well last year en route to an 80.5 overall grade.
The 24-year-old should have plenty of tread left on his tires and could spur Chase Brown to more impactful moments down the stretch of his contract season. Skattebo is under contract through the 2028 season and carries just a $1.79 million cap hit for the rest of this season and next.
Cincinnati should take a flier on Skattebo with one of its eight 2027 draft picks (one third-round compensation pick slated for them along with seven other normal picks).
Brown could bounce back and thrive in the final months of the season like he did last year, but it shouldn't cost much to get this insurance just in case that doesn't happen. Cincinnati has a few weeks to mull options before the trade deadline on Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

title: Browns’ Latest Injury Update Raises Concerns Ahead of Titans Matchup
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are missing several notable players from practice ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans . Camryn Justice of News 5 reported on six total players expected to be out for Wednesday practice:
#Browns players not expected to practice today due to injury: Kalia Davis (quad) Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) Elgton Jenkins (knee) Teven Jenkins (back) Carson Schwesinger (ankle)
Grant Delpit is one of the Browns' key defensive players and was injured after being accidentally struck by teammate Derek Barnett during a tackle attempt on Ravens running back Derrick Henry. Delpit is listed as having a shoulder injury as well as a concussion.
Grant Delpit Took A Hard Hit To The Head As He Was Going In For The Tackle. This Definitely Does Not Look Good. Hope He’s All Good. Scary Moment. 😬 pic.twitter.com/u3VMCaBu40
Delpit is the most uncertain name on the Browns' injury report, as he sustained the concussion during Sunday's matchup against Baltimore. The NFL's concussion protocol can be difficult to navigate, and his absence from Wednesday's practice raises questions about his availability this Sunday.
Delpit would be a big miss for the Browns, with one interception, one sack, and 25 combined tackles this year. Luckily for the Browns, they added depth at safety in the draft, and rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has started to emerge in recent weeks, with 24 tackles and just two receptions allowed this season. The Browns have some insurance at the position while Delpit works toward a return.
Carson Schwesinger has been a defensive star for the Browns this season. Unfortunately, Schwesinger has been dealing with an ankle injury in recent weeks. The injury kept him out of practice most of last week ahead of the Ravens matchup, and he was limited in Friday's final practice.
With Schwesinger missing Wednesday's practice, the Browns appear to be taking a similar approach this week. However, if his performance against the Ravens is any indication, Schwesinger should be available against the Titans.
Elgton Jenkins has anchored the Browns' offensive line at center this season and has been a bright spot for the position group. Jenkins was listed with a knee injury ahead of Wednesday's practice after playing every offensive snap against the Ravens in Week 6.
While his absence is worth monitoring, Jenkins' ability to play through last week's matchup is encouraging. For now, the Browns will hope the injury remains a practice concern rather than one that affects his availability on Sunday.
The Browns' injury report remains long, but it shows some encouraging signs compared to last week's report ahead of the Ravens matchup. Mason Graham and Quinshon Judkins, who both missed the Ravens game, returned to practice, with signs pointing to both potentially returning to action against the Titans.
#Browns DT Mason Graham continued practicing today as he aims to return this week from the MCL sprain and ankle sprain he sustained in Week 4. pic.twitter.com/fSpap4sJZ2
While Delpit's status is concerning, the team has some depth at safety to help offset a potential absence. Meanwhile, Schwesinger and Jenkins have shown they can play through injuries, giving Cleveland reason to be optimistic heading into Sunday's matchup.

title: How Many More Wins Can We Expect from the Browns after Week 6?
full_text:
So far in 2026, the Cleveland Browns have surprised many people. Quite frankly, even Browns fans themselves thought they were in for another 3-4-win season that sets them up for yet another high draft pick in 2027.
However, head coach Todd Monken has turned the team around in just his first season. Through six weeks, they have been winners four times already.
At this pace, the Browns can make the playoffs. But how far can the Browns really go? Let's take a look at the remainder of the season for Cleveland by breaking it down into three segments.
Starting with the Titans matchup, the Browns are set for three straight road games.
Realistically, the Browns need to try and win two out of three games here. Of course, it would be nice to win all three, winning in Pittsburgh has not been historically easy for the Browns.
As for the Titans and Saints matchups, these are two games the Browns need to make sure they win. Credit to New Orleans and Tennessee, but going into each matchup, the Browns are the better team.
Let's say the Browns hypothetically win two out of three. That would put their record at 6-3 before heading into the best part of their schedule.
After New Orleans, the Browns are set up for success being at home for five straight weeks.
Starting off against the Texans, this is a tough game. CJ Stroud is playing some of his best football and their defense is a top unit in the league. However, this is still weeks away, and you never know what will change by then.
After Week 10, the Browns got lucky with a later bye week this season. Coming out of it, you get the Raiders, Bengals, and Falcons.
Against Las Vegas, the Browns should be able to shut down the Raider offense and put some points on the board against their defense. While it may be close, this is one the Browns need to win.
Your first place 4-2 #Browns ' upcoming schedule: Week 7 @ Titans (1-5) Week 8 @ Steelers (4-2) Week 9 @ Saints (2-4) Week 10 vs. Texans (2-4) Week 11 BYE Week 12 vs. Raiders (3-3) #DawgPound
Following that game, the Bengals come to town for the first battle of Ohio in 2026. If they beat the Raiders, maybe some momentum can carry over to what will be a crucial divisional matchup.
Then, the game with the biggest storyline. The Atlanta Falcons, led by former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski, come to play in Week 14. Simply put, the Browns MUST win this one.
Going back to our hypotheticals, let's say the Browns go 2-2 in this stretch. 8-5 would most likely put them somewhere in contention for a wildcard spot, making the final four weeks the biggest yet.
Hopefully, the Browns learned what needs to change to win in MetLife Stadium. That's where they will play for the second time this season when they travel to take on the New York Giants.
Let's say the Browns can get a huge win in Week 15 against the Giants. That leads them straight into their second Ravens matchup the following week.
Something that is pretty clear with the AFC North is that home games give each team an incredible boost. The Browns will most likely struggle in both late divisional games against the Ravens and Bengals.
If the Browns drop one in Baltimore, they then play their final home game against the Colts. Who knows what the season will look like by then, but there could be a serious chance that with a win against Indianapolis, Week 18 in Cincinatti is a potential game for the division title.
Regardless of division, let's say the Browns once again go 2-2 dropping both AFC North matchups. Our hypothetical record is now 10-7, which may be enough to sneak into the playoffs.
Overall, the road to making the postseason for the first time since 2023 is not horrible on paper.
The important thing for Cleveland is to keep their focus on one game at a time, and keep stacking up wins.
For the NFL's second-youngest team, learning how to win going forward is what matters the most.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Browns Reveal Promising Update on Mason Graham Following Lower-Body Injury
full_text:
Even without Mason Graham, the Cleveland Browns' defense is elite.
And whenever he does ultimately return, there's a chance that the Browns get even better.
Fortunately, on Wednesday, Oct. 21, the Browns announced that Graham is getting healthier by the day. He is currently recovering from an ankle and knee injury he suffered in the Browns' Thursday Night Football clash with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
According to head coach Todd Monken, Graham wanted to play last weekend in the Browns' Week 6 clash with the Baltimore Ravens at home. However, he ultimately wasn't able to suit up.
He did share, though, that in the Browns' Sunday meeting with the Tennessee Titans , he should be ready to go.
"I think so. He wanted to go [vs. Baltimore]. He played for Jesse [Minter] at Michigan," Monken said. "He loves football. I think he's thankful and I am thankful it wasn't worse. Pretty good chance we will have him this week."
Browns coach Todd Monken said DT Mason Graham wanted to play last Sunday against the Ravens and his former coach at Michigan, Jesse Minter. "I think there's a pretty good chance we'll have him this week."
And it is obvious that the 23-year-old loves the game.
He made an incredible jump from his rookie campaign, becoming a much more impactful defender.
In his rookie season, he was named to the All-Rookie team by the Pro Football Writers of America , even though he only recorded 0.5 sacks, 49 tackles, seven for a loss and four quarterback hits.
This year, across the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season, he was one of the most dominant rushers in the league before injury. He totaled 15 combined tackles, seven of which were solo, and four sacks . His presence in the backfield led to 33 yards lost for opposing quarterbacks when he was credited with the sack.
That type of pressure and ability to back an offense up is incredibly important.
But even when he has been kept off the field, the Browns have had players step up to fill his void.
Maliek Collins is up to 3.5 sacks and five tackles for a loss this season, while Isaiah McGuire sits not far behind at 3.0 sacks and five tackles for a loss. Alongside Collins and McGuire, Adin Huntington, Sam Kamara and Mike Hall Jr. have put in the work, each totaling a sack or more as well.
In Sunday's win, the Browns' run defense had a 97th percentile EPA/rush allowed performance and a 98th percentile designed rushing success rate allowed performance. Their total Defense Impact Metric, according to Pro Football Focus, has them ranked within the Top 5 in the league.
They also rank first in tackles for a loss, fewest rushing touchdowns allowed and second in total sacks.
When Graham returns, that unit will be even better, with those who have filled his spot being warmed up now.
There are just a few more days for Graham to get cleared for this weekend, and even if he just plays on limited snaps, it will be a nice bump for the defense to try and lead the Browns to a 5-2 record.
The Browns and Titans will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium in Nashville this Sunday.

title: What I'm Buying and Selling About the Cleveland Browns After Week 6
full_text:
It’s hard not to feel good about the Cleveland Browns’ 4-2 start to the season, including wins over divisional rivals Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens so far in 2026.
After all, this is the team with the lowest winning percentage in all the NFL (.346) since it grew to 32 teams divided in eight divisions back in 2002, and the longest active drought without a division title league-wide (36 years and counting). Winning just isn’t a common occurrence here.
But even as the Browns face a very accessible schedule with just one remaining out of division foe with a winning mark, not everything has been smooth sailing for the franchise. Here are three things I’m buying and three things I’m selling from the Browns after Week 6 of the 2026 regular season.
The Browns began their regular season getting their teeth kicked in by the Jaguars on Opening Weekend. Since then, this unit has been one of the best in all the NFL. Cleveland is currently ranked second in the league in sacks in their first year without Myles Garrett and zero sacks by his nominal successor Jared Verse, and fourth in total quarterback pressures. Cleveland has also surrendered just one rushing touchdown all year long.
Granted, there are still some issues that need to be resolved, mainly in the secondary, but this unit is going places. Denzel Ward is enjoying one of his finest seasons as a pro, Carson Schwesinger is proving to be the real deal in his second season, and free agent addition Quincy Williams has been playing a very high level of football, too. The D-Line has been the team’s best group, nonetheless. Isaiah McGuire and Maliek Collins have been phenomenal, while Mason Graham has been living up to his billing when healthy. Sam Williams has also flashed on the edge, and Verse is getting the pressures, if not the sacks.
The Browns went all-in on Watson and, so far, there are reasons to be skeptical about his performance so far. His 4.0 percent touchdown percentage is his second worst as a pro, and his numbers across a few other metrics line up exactly to what he’s done before in Cleveland, very distant to what he did before in Houston, including QBR, success rate, yards per attempt, and sack percentage, while his 70.3 on target rate is his personal worst.
So no, Watson isn’t playing better under head coach Todd Monken than what he did under Kevin Stefanski, in any sense. He’s just being backed by a much better defense and has some top notch weapons at his disposal in the ground game, along with a trust-worthy placekicker in Andre Szmyt.
The Browns are winning despite Watson , and that means they can’t change quarterbacks now, but things are likely to get rocky at some point ahead.
Playing on an island on the left side is inherently more difficult than playing guard but make no mistake, Austin Barber has been as good if not better than Spencer Fano for the Browns. Either way, both are outplaying their respective counterparts in veteran left guard Zion Johnson and especially veteran right tackle Tytus Howard, so far.
There’s still a ton of improvement to be made here, and blocking for a quarterback that’s been responsible for a number of sacks is suboptimal, but expect these two to become cornerstones in Cleveland for the long run.
The team as a whole has been struggling mightily in the ground game , no doubt. But Judkins’ woes should come as no surprise when you take a good look at his rookie season.
He’s averaging 3.0 yards-per-rush this year, which is actually worse than his 3.5 yards-per-rush average from a year ago, and hasn’t been able to reach a 4.0 yard-per-carry average since Week 13 of last year, one of only four games all year long he was able to reach or surpass that number. And this year, he’s scored just once despite receiving the lion’s share in snaps on offense (60 percent, compared to 50 percent last year).
Run blocking has been a problem for the Browns, especially in terms of first contact for the backs, but Judkins’ numbers are worse off than last year’s underwhelming stats, neatly disguised by his seven rushing scores as a rookie.
If the rookie offensive linemen have been a hit for the Browns, the rookie wideouts have been even better.
KC Concepcion recovered from a concussion in time to play this past Sunday for the Browns, and he’s still leading the team with 22 catches for 186 yards. Meanwhile, Denzel Boston has 17 catches for 345 yards and a league-leading 20.3 yard per reception average to go along with his three scores.
Yes, the numbers for both could be better by this point, but they truly don’t have much to work with at the quarterback position. Even so, Boston should be seriously considered among the league favorites to take home the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award.
Currently, Cleveland is using play-action at a 18.5 percent rate -- 29th in the NFL -- down from 21.9 percent last year. The team’s EPA per pass attempt is at -0.04, meaning the Browns are faking handoffs at a very low rate, and are not a successful team at passing the ball when they do fake the handoff.
Again, the offensive line has had some protection issues and Watson is not playing good football right now, but a solid ground game would probably earn more respect from the defenses than what’s currently going on. Plus, play-action is known as a good countermeasure to pressure, which would be a good development for a team leading the league in sacks allowed .
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Could Browns’ Carson Schwesinger Enter the Defensive Player of the Year Race?
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year , Carson Schwesinger, continues to impress.
In the Browns' Week 6 matchup against division rival Baltimore, Carson Schwesinger was the X factor in the team's win. Despite entering the game listed as questionable with an ankle sprain, Schwesinger recorded 13 tackles. Most importantly, Schwesinger forced running back Derrick Henry to fumble , setting up Cleveland’s game-tying touchdown.
DROY Carson Schwesinger forces the fumble on Derrick Henry! BALvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TY9niNw746
The performance against the Ravens is not a one-off, either. Schwesinger has 56 total tackles through six games.  That averages 9.3 tackles per game, approximately matching Luke Kuechly’s career average. Maintaining that pace over a full 17-game season would put Schwesinger at roughly 159 tackles. Schwesinger has also added quarterback pressure, recording a strip-sack in the Browns’ Week 5 matchup against the Jets.
Carson FLYING in to knock it loose! #CLEvsNYJ on CBS pic.twitter.com/9HFah8X33w
While Schwesinger has been impressive throughout the 2026 season and has largely picked up where he left off in 2025 , his recent two-week stretch of 21 tackles, two forced fumbles, and a sack may strengthen his case for another individual honor.
Schwesinger already emerged in 2025 as one of the league's best defenders , but his recent production, despite injury, may put him in the Defensive Player of the Year conversation. Schwesinger has been nothing short of elite in the middle of the Browns’ defense over the last few weeks. If Schwesinger can keep playing at this level, even with a bad ankle, the illustrious Defensive Player of the Year award could be within reach.
History isn't exactly on Schwesinger's side, as pass rushers dominate the award.  Luke Kuechly was the last off-ball linebacker to win Defensive Player of the Year, earning the honor in 2013, when he played in all 16 games and recorded two sacks, four interceptions, and 156 combined tackles. Notably, Kuechly won the award in his second NFL season, the same stage of his career that Schwesinger has reached.
Jared Verse on Carson Schwesinger: “He has an old school linebacker mindset … He’s a hooper … He’s the most reliable person I know.” #browns pic.twitter.com/KoXZaGwh8H
Patrick Surtain II is the most recent non-edge defender to win the award, winning it in 2024 with 45 combined tackles, four interceptions, and 11 passes defended. Recent voting trends favor pass rushers like current betting favorite Will Anderson Jr., making it a tougher path for Schwesinger as an off-ball linebacker.
However, if Carson Schwesinger stays healthy and sustains his recent elite play, he could give the Luke Kuechly comparisons even more weight. Like Kuechly, Schwesinger could follow a Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign by claiming the NFL’s top defensive honor in his second season.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: Could Audric Estime Be the Answer? Browns Face RB Questions Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 NFL regular season, there weren't many concerns about the running back position.
After all, the front office spent all season focused on building up the offensive line, picking a starting quarterback and developing a young wide receiver room. Of all the positions, the running back room seemed to be the last thing on anyone's mind.
However, after the first six weeks of the campaign, it has jumped to the top of the priorities list.
Both starting running back Quinshon Judkins and backup Dylan Sampson ended up injured at the same time. Judkins missed a Week 6 win against the Baltimore Ravens due to an ankle injury, while Sampson was ruled out in Week 1. He unfortunately ended up on the injured list.
At this time, neither has been cleared for Week 7 when the Browns take on the Tennessee Titans on the road in Nashville.
In order to replace some of the lost depth, the Browns' front office went out and signed running back Audric Estime from the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad early last week.
Finding at least one body to pair with Jaleel McLaughlin, who was also thrust into a bigger role with Rahiem Sanders ending up on the injured list, was a big-time need for the Browns.
While Estime was somewhat of an unknown, having only rushed for 234 yards and three scores across his first two seasons in the NFL, he impressed in his debut with the Browns.
On nine carries, Estime recorded 19 yards and one touchdown, picking up two first downs as well. When the ball was in his hands, he had a 55.6% success rate . While his average yards per game was certainly down, his usage, especially in power-needed positions, led to this difference compared to his averages in 2024 and 2025.
But even then, the former Notre Dame standout was still able to find the end zone after just joining the franchise days before his debut.
“I just followed the blocker,” Estime said postgame when asked about what led to him finding six. “And the coaches trusted me. They said when we got down there that I was going to get in the end zone. I had confidence in myself. I didn’t know how it was going to look, but I really had confidence that I was going to get in the paint.”
With more time to get acclimated to the team both on the field and off, and more time for the coaches to get him more intertwined into the system, Estime could carve out a nice role for himself heading into Week 7.
At this point, the Browns are just trying to keep the run game afloat while they await the return of Sampson, Judkins and Sanders, and as long as McLaughlin can affect the game outside the hashes and Estime can get to work in the trenches, the Browns don't need to make a move at the deadline.
Instead, they can lean into the two they have on the roster now, with the hope that by the time Judkins and Sampson are fully good to go, the team is still playing competitive football.
Neither Sampson nor Judkins are supposed to be out for too long of a time period; however, any sort of leg injuries are going to slow running backs down. The Browns will want to play it safe, especially up the gut, so keeping Estime around is going to be important.
And at the end of the day, there is very little downside to letting a 23-year-old get another chance at establishing himself in the league.
“(Estime) shows up (at practice) on Wednesday and, heck, he’s taking meaningful snaps and scores a touchdown (a few days later),” Monken said about him in an article in The Athletic . “So that says a lot about the depth of our team and the expectations of the position, which you should have.
"You should have expectations of any player on your roster playing at a high level."
The Browns and Estime return to the gridiron Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium.

title: One Crucial Schedule Twist the Browns Need to Capitalize On Moving Forward
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are already one of teams making most waves through the first six weeks of the regular season thanks to a 4-2 record and the fact that they have already beaten the 4-2 Steelers and the 4-2 Ravens to claim the top spot in the AFC North, for now.
However, one glance at the remaining schedule for the Browns reveals an interesting quirk that head coach Todd Monken’s team will be looking to parlay into the team’s first postseason run since 2023.
Besides the four remaining AFC North games on Cleveland’s schedule -- a rematch against Pittsburgh, a rematch against Baltimore, and two contests against the 3-2 Bengals -- there is only one team currently holding a winning record among the games yet to be played.
The 3-2-1 New York Giants are the only team currently holding a winning record left on the Browns’ schedule. Besides the Giants, the Las Vegas Raiders at 3-3 are the only other team not holding a losing record. All other opponents left currently carry losing records: Titans, Saints, Texans, Falcons and Colts.
While the Browns would need at least two more wins to cover their win total odds of 5.5 from before the season started, winning all five games left against teams with losing records would ensure a winning season for the first time since 2023, and even then, playoffs might not be guaranteed. That’s why the way the Browns’ remaining schedule is lining up is so important for this team.
Life is hard within the league’s most competitive division. It’s not just the fact that back in 2023, it became the only division in league history with all four teams sporting winning records. It has to do with how hard it is to exert dominance over the other clubs.
Since 2002, the league’s probability at sweeping a divisional opponent sits at 42 percent, but in the AFC North, that number is roughly 34 percent. Likewise, the NFL has a league-wide probability of 3.8 percent of sweeping all three divisional opponents in any given year, but that number shrinks to 1.04 percent in the AFC North, where it’s happened just five times in its history -- the Steelers have done it three times, while the Bengals and Ravens just once, each. Cleveland has never swept the entire division since its inception.
Furthermore, since 2002, the Browns have only managed to sweep a single divisional rival three times in one season, all three against Cincinnati (2002, 2018 and 2020). Cleveland has never swept the Steelers while playing in the AFC North, and hasn’t done so generally speaking since 1988. The Browns have yet to sweep the Ravens in any instance.
With the Browns already handing losses to Pittsburgh and Baltimore, nobody says Cleveland can’t get a sweep over any one of those teams. It just hasn’t happened yet in the AFC North. And even thinking about sweeping Cincy is a complicated proposition, too. Moreover, we haven’t even begun to discuss how and why the team is winning despite Deshaun Watson’s poor performances , and without any sign of life from the ground game .
Yes, Cleveland is off to a phenomenal start to the season , but closing in on a postseason berth won’t be easy. That’s why the Browns need to take advantage of every single opportunity they get, including winning all their remaining matchups against non-winning teams.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost With Four Weeks Left
full_text:
The Browns are in first place after beating two divisional opponents in three weeks. The roster is filled with exciting young talent, with reinforcements on the way in next year’s draft.
The offense has not been pretty and the defense looks suffocating. In order to keep up the winning ways, Andrew Berry should take a look at these realistic targets at the November 10 trade deadline.
The Cardinals upgraded their running back room in the offseason, and Conner dropped to third on the depth chart. They are not going to win their division or compete for the wild card, so they may want to acquire assets for next year. Conner has been productive in the league, and the amount of carries he would get would be spread out with the other running backs. He would be obtainable for a very low pick.
Fant was a first-round pick in 2019 and has bounced around the league since. He is a backup in New Orleans and only has nine catches this season, but three of those went for touchdowns. The Browns have Harold Fannin Jr., but no real talent behind him. Deshaun Watson has not developed chemistry with Fannin Jr. this season and the offense needs production from the tight end position.
The pass-catching tight end can provide another outlet for Watson and a stagnant offense. He can be had for a late-round pick if the Saints continue to lose and see their contention chances slip.
Every team is seeking offensive line help at the trade deadline and the Browns could use some depth after a complete rehaul in the offseason. They have not played great in the early portion of the season and Penning can help down the stretch. He has only played in three games this season, but would not cost much capital to obtain.
It is no secret that the Browns’ offense has struggled to run the ball this season. Both running backs who played in Sunday’s game were not with the team at the beginning of the season and the offense could use a reliable back. Pollard is averaging four yards per carry and would immediately upgrade the positional group. He is on an expiring contract and the Titans sit in last place in their division.
Dylan Sampson is set to return at some point, but Quinshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders hit the injured list . Berry has three first fourth-round picks in next year’s draft and Pollard could be had for one of them.
The Chargers are in a tailspin at 0-6 and Mack is 35 years old. He signed a one-year, 18-million-dollar contract last offseason. He has three sacks and could bolster a surging defensive line. Due to his age and contract, the Browns would not have to give up too much to get him as a late-round pick should do it.
The downside would be that the compensation could get too high with other teams outbidding each other. The acquisition would also put the Browns over the salary cap.
The Browns’ roster has arrived early and Berry has some interesting options to upgrade the team right now. However, he has stacked draft picks for a deep draft next season and should not compromise good draft picks for the team this year.
