title: Two Browns' Players Who Have Earned More Snaps After Win Over Ravens
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns sitting at 4-2 and leading the AFC North Standings after six weeks has to be one of the feel-good stories over the first half of the season.
However, work is far from finished.
Head coach Todd Monken’s group must still navigate the remaining 11 games, including rematches against the also 4-2 Steelers and Ravens, two games versus the 3-2 Bengals, in addition to improving the team’s current struggles, primarily in the ground game and at the quarterback position.
Here are two players -- on on offense and one on defense -- who should see their snap count incremented over the next few weeks based on what they’ve shown so far, along with the players that could see their minutes reduced, as the Browns will attempt to close out the 2026 regular season as successfully as they have started it.
Listen, I realize this might be an overreaction, but there’s really nothing to lose.
Over the course of the last three weeks, McLaughlin ripped off a 28-yard touchdown run in his only carry versus the Steelers -- second carry all-season long -- and followed that with a nine-carry 41-yard effort on Sunday, with starter Quinshon Judkins out of the lineup .
Even with such a minuscule sample, McLaughin leads the team with a 6.5 yard-per-carry average, success rate (54.5) than Judkins (41.1) or Raheim Sanders (33.3), as defined by Pro Football Reference.
Maybe McLaughlin will earn more carries out of pure desperation, as Sanders also missed last Sunday’s game, while second-year pro Dylan Sampson has yet to log an offensive snap this season, but at least McLaughlin has earned a larger share of the workload based on what he’s shown on limited carries.
So far, McLaughlin has played on 17.65 percent of the team’s offensive snaps, compared to Judkins’ 49.73 percent and Sanders’ 27.01 percent. Newcomer Audric Estime has already seen 5.08 of the offense’s snaps after joining the team last week , wasting no time in scoring his first touchdown for the Browns.
But regardless of when Judkins, Sanders and Sampson are ready to reappear for the team -- “Hopefully we’ll get Samp back this week and we’ll get Q back. We’re hopeful to get two,” stated Monken after the win over the Ravens regarding his backfield -- and how much of a factor they can be coming back from their respective energy, McLaughlin has made a solid argument in favor of, at the very least, a running back by committee approach.
While Sanders’ could see some of his snaps taken away as the team’s primary backup, the Browns need to consider taking away snaps from Judkins in favor of McLaughlin.
“J. Mac ran hard, man. He ran hard. He ran with a passion and a mission,” said Monken about McLaughlin’s performance versus Baltimore.
McLaughlin won’t solve the Browns’ ground game issues by himself, but at least there’s a spark there. It would be a shame to see it go to waste.
Grant Delpit’s first quarter head injury sustained against the Ravens might be the catalyst for a change here. Before Week 6, Delpit had participated in 100 percent of the defensive snaps in four out of the five first games, while logging a 97.2 percent in Week 4 versus the Steelers.
Along with Delpit, Ronnie Hickman has also been on the field almost on every defensive play, including a 100 percent snap count in five matchups and a 95.4 percentage in Week 4 against the Bucs.
This had left McNeil-Warren playing around 32 percent of defensive snaps before he set a personal best of 94.7 against the Ravens in Delpit’s absence. Nonetheless, the rookie out of Toledo has been spectacular over the first six games of his pro career, and is currently graded as the top safety in the NFL by PFF.
Combine that with the fact that Delpit has been playing at a subpar level, and Hickman has had an up-and-down season, there’s no reason to keep McNeil-Warren on the sidelines even if Delpit makes it back fast from his concussion.
Now factor in how much slot cornerback Myles Harden has struggled at times, just like Mekhi Blackmon, and it’s obvious that McNeil-Warren needs more time on the field, even if it’s in big nickel formations along with Delpit and Hickman.
The second-rounder has been a little overshadowed by all the offensive rookies from this year’s draft, but McNeil-Warren’s been more than living up to those hefty expectations.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Biggest Need Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
So far this season, the Cleveland Browns have surprised many people with their game results.
However, there still is one big issue that the Browns need to address with the trade deadline coming up.
The Browns Offensive Line Cannot Hold Up To The Ravens Rush. Deshaun Watson Is Just Trying Not To Get Sacked. This Browns Team Has Looked Ridiculous The Last 5 Quarters. Total Collapse. 😬 pic.twitter.com/yHTaCozrS1
Let's put it plain and simple, the Browns offensive line is not good.
This season, Deshaun Watson is the most sacked quarterback in the NFL after being dropped 24 times through the first six games.
While some have been to the fault of Watson, the offensive line has not given him much help at all.
Clearly, there needs to be improvement made to the unit going forward.
This past week, Watson was only able to throw for 164 yards. Watching the film, he was never able to get comfortable in the pocket. Most plays, Watson was forced to flee and try and make the play himself.
Lots of credit to Watson for having the ability to make those plays, but thats not what the Browns need.
It is incredibly hard for a quarterback to build confidence when he is constantly under attack from four-man pass rushes.
Going forward, the Browns need to either make some changes internally or bring in some help to try and bolster the passing game. Some of the plays up Todd Monken's sleeve cannot be run at the moment because they do not have enough time to develop.
As much as the pass game has been weak, the worst part of the Browns' offense this year has been the run game, without a doubt.
Historically, Cleveland is always super strong on the ground, no matter the state of the team. In the current day, some critics are putting the blame on Quinshon Judkins .
However, if you go back and watch the film, the bigger holes needed for the bigger back in Judkins are not there like they were last season.
Sure, faster running backs like Jaleel McLaughlin are able to get through the initial holes slightly better, but film shows that the run blocking overall needs work.
Cleveland seriously needed to take some time at the trade deadline to look at their current line group.
Maybe, they first try and switch some guys around. All five of the starters are brand new in 2026, so while they are getting used to the new team maybe get them used to a new side of the line.
If not, maybe they turn to a rookie like Parker Brailsford .
If that won't work, turn to free agency. While they don't have an insane amount to work with, the $15 million dollars in cap space should be enough to go out and sign a veteran lineman. While some fans may not like it, Jack Conklin is available.
Lastly, of course you could go for a trade. The main issue there is what you would have to give up and for who. If there's a chance to go out and get a solid starter for years to come, maybe then they should use some draft capitol to make it work.
However, I don't like the idea of giving up draft picks for a temporary fix, especially when Cleveland has been able to hit on draft picks like Austin Barber.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Dallas Cowboys 3 Keys to Victory vs. Eagles in Week 7
full_text:
This week could be an important one for the Dallas Cowboys. At 2-4, they're still alive in the NFC East and can begin to make up some ground by securing a win against an ailing division rival .
The Philadelphia Eagles go into this one with Jalen Hurts, who is excpected to miss the remainder of the season with blood clots in his lungs. That scary injury has them leaning on Tanner McKee, who made just the third start of his career in Week 6.
For Dallas, they enter as the favorites but cannot take their opponent lightly. That said, here are three key areas they must focus on to make sure they leave Week 7 with a win.
Dallas was supposed to win in Week 5 when they were facing an 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers team with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starting under center. That wasn't how things went down as the Cowboys failed to get consistent pressure on the rookie and wound up losing 24-16 .
This week, they will face another backup in Tanner McKee, who was 26-of-45 for 215 yards with a touchdown pass in their Week 6 loss to the Carolina Panthers. He has more experience than Daniels and will be able to find success if he's given time. That's why Dallas has to find a way to get after him and keep McKee from gaining confidence. That's easier said than done with this defense, but they showed some positive signs in Week 6 as they recorded three sacks on Jordan Love.
Javonte Williams ran for 1,201 yards while averaging 4.8 per attempt in 2025. This year, he has just 317 yards while averaging 3.7 per attempt through six games. The lack of consistency in the ground game has been a major issue for Dallas, and that needs to change against the Eagles.
While Philadelphia has some disruptive defensive tackles, they're still just 19th in the league in run defense , which means there should be room for Williams to operate. If he takes advantage of that, it will keep the pressure off the shoulders of Dak Prescott, while also keeping their suspect defense on the bench. Williams is in the unique position of being able to help Dallas both offensively and defensively by running well.
Turnovers have been a killer for the Cowboys this season. In Week 3, Jake Ferguson coughed up the ball after catching a shovel pass, which killed a potential scoring drive against the Baltimore Ravens. Interceptions have also been a problem as of late, with Dak Prescott throwing four interceptions over the past two weeks.
Not all of those were on Prescott, with Ferguson allowing one pass to bounce off of his hands and land in the arms of a Tampa Bay defender, ending their potential comeback in Week 5. Regardless of whose fault it is, the Cowboys need to protect the ball in Week 7. Due to injuries in Philadelphia, Dallas is the superior team right now and can't afford to lose. Ensuring they protect the ball will be a major key for them as they simply can't afford to make anything easy on the Eagles.

title: Jerry Jones Weighs in on Cowboys Legend Troy Aikman’s NFL Front Office Future
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys legend Troy Aikman has been in the news quite a bit lately. Aikman's current deal with ESPN is up after the season and he has yet to sign a new contract.
He's also been honest about the fact that he's not sure exactly what the future will hold, which has led to plenty of speculation about him moving into an NFL front office role. Aikman has expressed interest in working with an NFL team , and was even hired as a consultant by the Miami Dolphins this offseason.
Of course, any time the possibility of Aikman serving in an operation role is mentioned, his former team is mentioned as a possibility. That might be a pipedream, however, since Jerry Jones prefers to keep family members in the key jobs in Dallas. That doesn't mean Jones doesn't think highly of Aikman, as he said on Wednesday that there's no job Aikman couldn't do that he wouldn't excel at.
"No, I think when I say no, Troy is very capable. And he's so really relatively speaking, he's in his youth, as careers go. And he's very capable of doing any one of a number of things, certainly anything to do with football. I don't know of any area short of getting back out on the field. I don't know of any area that Troy Aikman wouldn't be qualified and competent to go into," Jones said.
Jerry Jones says he has been following former Cowboys QB Troy Aikman’s comments on expiring broadcast deal. When asked about the possibility of Troy shifting to front office work, Jerry expressed confident in his ability to succeed there: pic.twitter.com/IweklsQ8HV
One thing that Aikman has proven during his time as a broadcaster is that he understands the game as well as anyone. He also knows what it takes to win, having led the Cowboys to three Super Bowls during his 12-year career.
That knowledge could be exactly what this Dallas front office needs as they continue to look for a way to get over their 30-year Super Bowl drought.
Hiring Aikman wouldn't guarantee success for the Cowboys, but it would bring in a new voice and a much-needed change of direction. He could also be the one to finally look for a coach with the right resume, rather than one who the Jones family believes will fit their current vision.
It's clear the Cowboys need a massive facelift and Aikman would provide that. We just shouldn't get our hopes up since Jones doesn't seem to realize their current structure is the problem. That means if Aikman truly hangs up the microphone and gets into an executive role, his knowledge will benefit some other team rather than the one in his own backyard.

title: Dallas Cowboys Great and Super Bowl Champion Dies at 86
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are mourning the death of one of their franchise legends on Wednesday.
The Cowboys announced that Cornell Green , who is widely viewed as one of the greatest defensive backs in franchise history, has died at the age of 86.
"We are sad to share news of the passing of Cowboys Legend Cornell Green this morning. Cornell was a true trailblazer having never played football in college, yet becoming a multi-time Pro Bowler, All Pro and NFL Super Bowl Champion with the Cowboys playing defensive back from 1962 to 1974. He was a member of the 25th Anniversary Cowboys Team as well. Cornell remarkably never missed a game in 13 seasons, becoming one of the best and most dependable teammates to ever wear the star," the Cowboys said in a statement .
"Our thoughts and prayers are with his family."
Green began his career with the Cowboys in 1962, but his road to the league was unconventional, to say the least, as he didn't play football in college. His football experience consisted of playing high school ball in his junior year.
"We purposely looked for players with speed," legendary talent evaluator Gil Brandt once said. "We brought the fast guys in and then some played on defense and some played on offense."
"We had a lot of those guys that played for the Cowboys," Cowboys legend Randy White said in the Deep Blue documentary Dirty Dozen . "A lot of them that Gil Brandt found were basketball players and ended up being great. Cornell Green, a bunch of them ended up being great football players."
Before joining the Cowboys, Green initially planned on going to the NBA and was even drafted by the Chicago Zephyrs in 1962
Green was a key member of the legendary Doomsday Defense and was part of the team's 1972 Super Bowl championship.
Over his 13-year career, he was a five-time Pro Bowler and four-time All-Pro, with two of those All-Pro nods being first-team selections.
He was also remarkably durable, with Green never missing a single game over his extensive career in Dallas.
Green hung up his cleats after the 1974 season. Despite not having played in over 50 years, Green still ranks tied for fifth in franchise history with his 34 interceptions.

title: Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones Hints at Aggressive Trade Deadline Approach
full_text:
Suddenly over the past two seasons, Jerry Jones has reverted to his gambler ways. The Dallas Cowboys owner traded away star pass rusher Micah Parsons and began to use his draft picks to bring in veteran talent.
The list of players added via trade since 2025 include George Pickens, Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams , Broderick Jones, Rashan Gary, Dee Winters, and Joey Porter Jr. Jones was also trying to land Maxx Crosby in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders, but he was traded to the Baltimore Ravens instead. Of course, that move was never completed when Crosby failed a physical in Baltimore.
Despite his moves, Dallas enters Week 7 with a record of 2-4 and they're searching for answers on both sides of the ball. The silver lining for them is that the NFC East is a mess , so they're still within range of first place. That being the case, Jones says the Cowboys could be active at the NFL trade deadline.
“I’ll be real clear, I could see being active at the trade deadline if it was something that could help the team this year," Jones said via NFL insider Albert Breet.
Jones was also asked if that meant they could be "sellers," which is often the case for struggling teams, but he shut that down quickly.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones: “I’ll be real clear, I could see being active at the trade deadline if it was something that could help the team this year.” Asked if he could see the team being a seller, he quickly said, “No.”
The NFL trade deadline is on Nov. 10 and the Cowboys could decide to use some of their future assets to improve this year, which is what they did last season when they added Williams to their defensive line.
The biggest name to watch remains Maxx Crosby. Dallas didn't go back to the negotiation table with Las Vegas after the trade to Baltimore was called off, but their interest has reportedly not changed . Crosby has looked fully healthy and has 14 tackles and two sacks. The Raiders are better than expected at 3-3, but if they don't feel as though they're true contenders, they could look to unload Crosby for a first-round pick (or more).
Another name to watch is Josh Sweat of the Arizona Cardinals. They're currently 2-4 and could be sellers at the deadline. Sweat, who has experience working with Christian Parker while with the Philadelphia Eagles, has 14 tackles and two sacks. He wouldn't be as costly as Crosby, but he's also not as disruptive a force.
Miami defensive tackle Zach Sieler was also named , but at this point, someone who can bring the heat off the edge feels like the most logical spot for Jones to target.

title: Cowboys Trade Rumor Casts Doubt on Dallas' Willingness to Make Deadline Deal
full_text:
If the Dallas Cowboys can't fix their defense with what they have in-house, the expectation has been that owner Jerry Jones will make another move.
However, one NFL insider, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , is pumping the brakes on that notion with what he's hearing.
Fowler is hearing from a source that a trade is "not a front-burner issue" for the Cowboys right now and the team could decide to not give up more draft capital than it already has in its quest to improve the defense.
"We talked about Dallas earlier. A source told me a trade to aid the Cowboys defense is not a front-burner issue at the moment," he reported. "So, Dallas will always explore a potential move, but it's quite possible the franchise holds onto whatever 2027 draft capital it has left (just three picks in the first six rounds)."
When it comes to draft capital, the Cowboys are in rough shape. After the Joey Porter Jr. trade, Dallas has just four picks in 2027, including one selection apiece in the first, second, fourth and seventh rounds.
Things aren't great in 2028, either, as the Cowboys don't have their second- or seventh-round picks.
Of course, it's possible Dallas could pick up more selections via comp picks next offseason, but it's hard to forecast that.
Jerry Jones has said several times that's he not opposed to doing more because he has faith in this team, but it's conceivable that might have changed after six weeks.
The Cowboys' willingness to make a trade is partly dependent on who is actually out there. The Cowboys need a difference-maker at edge rusher, for example, but those guys don't become available very often.
Another part of the equation is the Cowboys actually having faith in a trade making a big impact on the defense and right now they just can't possibly feel confident in that.
This defense is much more than one player away with all of its issues that include players underperforming and bad coaching from defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
If the Cowboys give up another premium draft pick and it doesn't change their fortunes, that would be a catastrophic scenario.
The right approach for the Cowboys is to gauge how things go between now and the Nov. 10 trade deadline. That gives the Cowboys a little under three weeks.
If things are looking as completely dysfunctional and hopeless as they currently do, the Cowboys would be wise to just wave the white flag and save what picks they have left.

title: New Cowboys 2027 Mock Draft Lands Explosive Interior Defensive Lineman
full_text:
Despite focusing heavily on defense this offseason, the Dallas Cowboys remain one of the league’s worst defenses . Through the first six games of the season, they’re 30th in yards surrendered and 25th in points.
First-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker has been unable to find any answers and the Cowboys recently brought in Mike Pettine as a senior assistant aimed at helping Parker improve. The hope is that Pettine can help turn things around as they look to catch up in a shockingly bad NFC East .
While there’s a chance Pettine could help, this defense still needs more talent. That’s why SI.com’s Gilberto Manzano has them targeting a massive interior lineman with their first pick in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
With the 27th pick in his mock, Manzano has the Cowboys bringing in Oregon’s A’Mauri Washington. The 6-foot-3, 319-pounder would be able to slide in as a starter next to Quinnen Williams, giving the Cowboys a powerful defensive front. In addition to his strength, Washington is praised by Manzano for the way he explodes off the snap, something this D-line desperately needs more of.
“The Cowboys need better edge rushers, but the defense can’t afford to take on more project players. It needs immediate results. Washington can do that playing next to Quinnen Williams,” Manzano wrote. “The best defenses lately have had plenty of interior defensive line depth. Not many players of Washington’s stature (6'3", 319 pounds) can explode the way he does once the ball is snapped.”
Washington has appeared in 43 games for the Ducks and has 65 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss, and 1.5 sacks. He might not be the flashiest player, but he’s a plug-and-play starter who has a high floor.
One move the Cowboys made in 2025 that’s been heavily criticized was their decision to give the New York Jets the better of their two picks in Round 1 as part of the Quinnen Williams trade.
Perhaps Jerry Jones felt the Cowboys and Packers would both be in playoff contention, so it wouldn’t matter too much, but that hasn’t been the case.
As Cowboys On SI’s Josh Sanchez wrote, the Cowboys paid a massive price for Williams with their projected draft slot being No. 6 overall entering Week 7. Compare that to pick 27 (where the Packers are slotted) and the criticism feels justified.

title: NFL QB Rankings Feature Dak Prescott Downfall After Struggling in Consecutive Losses
full_text:
Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys entered the season with a lot of hype after returning all 11 starters on offense. Unfortunately, a lack of creativity from head coach Brian Schottenheimer has made the offense stagnant, and production has dipped.
The uninspiring offense is holding Prescott back and the entire unit has regressed.
Over the past weeks, Prescott has thrown for just two touchdowns and four interceptions, with quarterback ratings of 69.1 and 65.2. As a result of the dip in production, Prescott has four spots in the latest quarterback rankings from PFF, and now sits at No. 10, and could be in danger of slipping out of the top 10 with another down week.
Sure, it doesn't all fall on Prescott's shoulders. His receivers have been plagued by drops, and Schottenheimer is clearly a problem, so hopefully, facing the struggling Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7 will give the team an opportunity to bounce back.
"Prescott is coming off his lowest-graded game of the season against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday night. He went 34-for-54 for 258 yards, and for just the second time this season, compiled more turnover-worthy plays than big-time throws," PFF writes.
"Over the past two weeks, we have seen Prescott produce a 13.3 percent and 15.4 percent negatively graded play rate, his worst performances of the year in that regard."
Prescott is sandwiched between New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and Chicago Bears star Caleb Williams.
Despite his recent struggles, Prescott is still performing well throughout the season. He ranks fourth in passing yards (1,639), 12th in passing touchdowns (10), and sixth in total QBR (75.4). Let's just hope that he breaks out of his recent slump.
"You're trying to go fast. You're trying to keep the defense on their heels . You're trying to extend the game for as long as you can and get as many ops as possible, because you don't know what's going to happen," Schottenheimer said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News . "So that's the No. 1 thing. When you shift in motion, obviously the play clock and the game clock go down, and so that limits your ops."
Let's hope that the defense can finally find its groove, so the Cowboys are afforded more flexibiltiy on offense moving forward.

title: Cowboys Trade Buzz From ESPN insider Links Dallas to Super Bowl-Winning Edge Rusher
full_text:
As the Nov. 10 trade deadline rapidly approaches, we're going to see the Dallas Cowboys connected to a lot of players who could become available.
There's a few reasons for that. One of them has to do with the fact that we've heard owner Jerry Jones say on numerous occasions that he's still open for business , even after a flurry of moves this past offseason and the blockbuster trade for Joey Porter Jr .
Another reason is the fact that the Cowboys' defense stinks. The offseason overhaul on that side of the ball that gave fans hope has not panned out at all, so the Cowboys can either sit back and hope it gets better (it won't) or try and make another big move or two and hope that will make a difference.
We suspect Jerry is going to take the latter approach, assuming a game-changing trade or two is actually available to him.
One of the many topics broached by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano in their weekly intel column was the trade deadline and possible candidates.
Fowler specifically mentions Arizona Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat as someone who at least one unnamed team executive is connecting to the Cowboys.
"As one team exec pointed out to me Tuesday, Josh Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense," Fowler said. "He fits Dallas' profile, and the Cowboys need edge-rush help. Sweat's Cardinals won Sunday, but they are not contention-adjacent just yet."
Fowler points out how Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort has been steadfast in his desire to keep Sweat, but that's probably just posturing because it makes all the sense in the world for the Cardinals to trade him.
Arizona isn't going anywhere this year. The Cardinals are in the midst of a rebuild and it's going to be a few years before they're competitive again, which is why trading a player who will turn 30 next year is a logical decision.
The Cardinals need draft capital badly to help boost the process of remaking their roster and trading an edge rusher with a history of strong production is a fantastic way to go about getting more.
Sweat could garner as much as a third-round pick if the market is robust enough, which we suspect it will be because of the premium there is on quality edge rushers.
The Cowboys' pass-rush has been inadequate this season, and that has only exposed the issues in the secondary even more.
Through six contests, the Cowboys have just eight sacks, and 2.5 of those have come from edge rushers, with Malachi Lawrence  and Rashan Gary having one and Donovan Ezeiruaku having 0.5.
Sweat is actually off to a slow start this season, but his two sacks are almost more than Dallas' entire edge rushers room combined.
Sweat, who won a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, has a lengthy history of production with a pair of double-digit sack seasons and four campaigns with 7.5 or more.
When it comes to improving their edge rushers room, Dallas needs to swing big. Sweat could very well be the biggest fish available and Jerry should do whatever he can to land him.

The Dallas Cowboys landed an extra first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft as part of the massive haul the team received from the Green Bay Packers for star pass rusher Micah Parsons. However, the team quickly flipped one of those picks for All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams .

title: Joey Porter Jr.'s Unreal Coverage Stats Justifying Cowboys' Trade With Steelers
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys took a big swing on Joey Porter Jr. last month in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers and that deal is looking very good for Dallas thus far.
While Porter hasn't been able to play a full complement of snaps yet, he has made the most of his limited opportunities.
According to Pro Football Focus , in the 61 snaps Porter has played over his two games with the Cowboys, he has been targeted just four times, which shows the level of respect opponents have for his coverage skills.
In those four targets, Porter has three forced incompletions, a pair of passes defensed and he has given up a miniscule passer rating of 39.6. That shows exactly why teams don't throw at him often.
Given the Cowboys' struggles in coverage this season, Porter's ability to shut down one side of the field is a breath of fresh air. Safe to say, the trade with Pittsburgh is justified so far.
Porter's snaps have been limited thus far for a few reasons. When he made his debut in Week 4, Porter was playing his first game of the season, so he needed to be worked in slowly.
After sitting out in Week 5 due to an illness, Porter returned in Week 6 but was dealing with an ankle injury that Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted kept him limited again.
If only the Cowboys could get anything remotely close to Porter's level of play on the other side of the field, they would really be in business.
Unfortunately, Dallas has gotten some of the worst cornerback play in the NFL at the other boundary spot, as DaRon Bland has struggled mightily once again this season.
The Cowboys are hoping Cobie Durant can make it back this week after missing four games in a row due to a hamstring injury Durant came down with in Week 2.
The veteran cornerback was easily the Cowboys' best cornerback throughout the offseason and he should provide a boost.
It would also be nice to see better play from the edge rushers, which would take a lot of pressure off the secondary. Dallas' edge rushers have tallied just 2.5 of the team's eight sacks. Neither one of those numbers are acceptable and much more is needed.
Cowboys beat writer Ed Werder reported Porter rolled his ankle in practice in the lead up to the loss to the Green Bay Packers.
Schottenheimer noted that Porter re-aggravated the injury during the game, as we saw when Porter was getting treatment on his ankle during the contest before returning to action.
"Brian Schottenheimer said today that Joey Porter Jr.’s limited availability was due to his ankle for what it’s worth," The Dallas Morning News' Joseph Hoyt said. "He said he tolled his ankle again during the game. Otherwise, he played very well."
Porter's injury is going to be something to watch this week as Dallas prepares for a showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles.
The Cowboys will release their first injury report of the week on Thursday, so we'll know more about Porter's ankle then.

title: First Week 7 Injury Report Offers Encouragement to Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are getting healthier ahead of their Week 7 road trip to face the Arizona Cardinals.
The team released its first injury report following Wednesday's practice, on which cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss were listed as limited and full participants, respectively.
Moss returned from his rib injury last week, but Surtain has been sidelined with an ankle issue he suffered in Week 4. The perennial All-Pro avoided short-term injured reserve and figures to have a chance to play against the Cardinals — though Week 8 versus Kansas City remains his likeliest target date.
Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was considered limited due to an apparent chest injury he picked up amid last Thursday's win over the Seahawks, during which he exited to the locker room. Waddle seems in little danger of missing Week 7.
Running back Jonah Coleman, as previously reported , logged a full session after being designated to return from injured reserve. Coleman is expected to be activated to the 53-man roster and play at Arizona.
Coleman's services will be required (alongside J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey) with backup RB Tyler Badie nursing a thumb injury, which held him out of Wednesday's practice. Badie will need at least limited sessions on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at playing.
Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) also did not practice and are unlikely to go Sunday. Elliss is a candidate for IR, though he's anticipated back at some point this season.
“He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," Payton told reporters on Wednesday.
Although some players, such as Hufanga and wide receiver Pat Bryant (IR), are still unavailable due to injury, the Broncos are beginning to round out into shape at an advantageous time — sitting at 4-2 and having completed the toughest portion of their schedule.
Veteran Taylor Rapp filled in admirably for Hufanga last week and figures to do so again. Coleman's reinsertion into the lineup will more than make up for the loss of Badie. Elliss' injury is offset by the reinstatement of incumbent starting OLB Jonathon Cooper, who missed the first six games while on the Commissioner's Exempt list.
“You never know how it’s going to unfold, but that’s a positive relative to our team. We’ll see how this week goes," Payton said regarding Cooper.
All of this, in preparation for a game the Broncos are favored to win by nearly five points. It's been a rollercoaster in the Mile High City thus far, but there's hope that things will soon stabilize.

title: Bo Nix Gets Real About What's Behind His Early Struggles
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 4-2, and that's something to celebrate , especially given the initial six-game gauntlet this team faced.
Alas, the full sweetness of the 4-2 feat has been soured by Bo Nix's ongoing slump. The third-year quarterback simply hasn't looked like himself, leading many to speculate on whether he's truly recovered from his ankle injury.
Nix suffered a fractured ankle in the Broncos' 33-30 overtime win over the Buffalo Bills in the divisional round of the playoffs, which required two surgeries. Both he and the Broncos have been adamant that his ankle is fine, but that doesn't necessarily mean that his psyche has yet to fully recover.
Amid the speculation about the true status of Nix's overall bill of health, the beleaguered signal-caller acknowledged that his ankle injury has played some role in his overall performance this season.
“I’d be lying if I said no," Nix said on Wednesday. "I think that’s just what happens. I think you come back, and every day is a progression. I’m not necessarily doing physical therapy treatment, but I’m out there on the practice field getting rep after rep, trying to get back in super great shape so my carries can go up, so I’m ready when my number’s called and when I can run."
Recovery from severe injury is a process — that, we know. And whether you're an average Joe or a multi-million-dollar pro athlete, the recovery process not only requires the physical injury itself to heal, but also the psyche to trust that it has. The physical and mental healing timetables don't always align perfectly.
Again, Nix emphasized that his ankle is fine. He's healthy, but he was candid in admitting that his recovery has played a role in his relative failure to launch, though he wouldn't say he's been on a "downslope." Perhaps that's because his No. 1 job as a quarterback is to win games, and he's certainly done that.
There may be some lingering mental side effects of his ankle recovery, but Nix was adamant in declaring that he's not afraid. He's not scared to play on his ankle and do his job.
"I’m not scared. I’m not physically worried," Nix said. "I just think there’s something to the sport. I think all guys, when they come back from an injury, just doing it one day at a time. I think that’s just part of the game. That’s part of the process. I had surgery probably six months ago. It takes a while for things to fully reengage."
Recovery is a process, and the time it takes to fully happen is contingent on many variables. According to NFL insider James Palmer , the Broncos have been "concerned" about Nix's performance, but they're standing behind him, fully confident that he's going to turn a corner and get back to the quarterback fans came to know and love over his first two years in the league.
Nix is confident that'll happen, too. And all it could take is one big game for the floodgates to open.
"I feel good physically. I think it’s going to be there," Nix said. "It’s just in football, you have to get that one (game) that just gets you going. I think we’ve been playing some really good teams thus far and haven’t gotten that one, but we’re searching for that one game that sort of just puts us right back where we were.”
Nix has always been a bit of a slow starter. That applies to individual games and seasons as a whole.
It seems to be baked into his DNA as a quarterback. At the same time, though, Nix is a bona fide gamer. And he's one of the NFL's best clutch-time quarterbacks. If we're talking football DNA, he definitely has the clutch gene.
Nix likened his recovery to a mountain. You climb, you climb, and then you finally peak. He wants to be peaking in December and January, rather than, say, September, as we've seen several quarterbacks do throughout NFL history, including this season.
"I don't want to be peaking until the playoffs. I don't want to be peaking at my best because you can't hold it the whole entire season," Nix said. "If you look at a training block, if you look at physical preparation, the guys that can build and grow and get to the peak, which is the playoffs, December, January, February, if you can get to that point and you can hold it, you'll feel really good."
We certainly saw that from Nix last year. He peaked at the best possible time, only to suffer a heartbreaking injury when he'd put the Broncos on the doorstep of the Super Bowl.
Hearkening back to the Peyton Manning days, some Broncos fans may say to themselves, "Well, gee. Can't we have good quarterback play in September, October, November, December, January, and February?"
Touche. But remember, Broncos Country wasn't around for Manning's early-career trial-and-error learning curve. He was an Indianapolis Colt for 14 years first.
Manning is a Hall-of-Famer, as is John Elway. The two have much in common, including multiple World Championships and records, but they also had to bump their heads a bit as young quarterbacks. Neither was a quarterback of legend out of the box, despite both being the No. 1 pick in the NFL draft.
Nix is still in the early developmental years of his NFL career. And yet, he's already accomplished so much. He's got a .700 career winning percentage and is 18-3 in his last 21 starts.
This is why the Broncos' confidence in Nix hasn't been shaken. And despite the funk and the incessant questions about his health, he's still confident he'll get back to playing the brand of football we saw before his ankle injury.
"I'm confident in myself," Nix said. "I know I'm going to get back and be exactly what I was, if not better, because as I get older, that's how it's been. But I do think it's just one game at a time. My training is going like this, and at the end of the day, it's all about getting better."
Getting the run game going would help Nix in his endeavors to improve. Sean Payton is very focused on doing just that entering Week 7's tilt against the Arizona Cardinals.
With rookie running back Jonah Coleman designated to return from injured reserve , the Broncos' ground attack is getting some reinforcements. It can only help Nix get back on his feet and return to playing championship-caliber football.
Nix is looking for that one big game. It could be the Cardinals this week on the road — a place where the Broncos have excelled in recent years.

title: Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman
full_text:
As expected , the Denver Broncos have officially designated rookie running back Jonah Coleman to return from short-term injured reserve—potentially as early as Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
Coleman, placed on IR with an ankle injury following Week 2, was listed as a full practice participant on the team's initial Week 7 status report, along with cornerback Riley Moss (ribs).
The Broncos now have 21 days to activate Coleman to the 53-man roster, for which they'll need to make a corresponding transaction.
The 108th overall pick of this year's draft, Coleman impressed during his limited appearances earlier this season, converting 10 carries into 39 yards and a touchdown. He also caught three passes for 19 yards prior to going down amid Denver's Sept. 20 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars.
“He played well," head coach Sean Payton said after the Jaguars game. "Then the very end, that last carry was… We work on four-minute [situations], but that certainly didn’t feel like a rookie series, if you will. He came up big, and we needed it. You carry three [running backs] on gameday like everyone else. We were down to two and the fullback. Those guys did a good job, and then we found a couple schemes that we liked and stayed with it. His play right at the end, staying in bounds, that was something you cover, but maybe he doesn’t get those same reps in practice. He did a good job.”
To say there's concern about the Broncos' barely-there rushing attack would be a massive understatement.
Veteran starter J.K. Dobbins has been utterly ineffective , posting a career-worst 3.3 yards per carry across the first six games of the year. RJ Harvey is a dependable pass-catcher out of the backfield, but hardly a workhorse runner. Tyler Badie did not practice Wednesday due to a thumb issue.
As a collective, the Broncos rank 26th in rushing offense, averaging a meager 84.2 yards per game.
Enter Coleman, who should suit up in Arizona and immediately contribute to what could be a ground-oriented game plan versus a susceptible defense, mixing in with (and potentially usurping) Dobbins on early downs before giving way to Harvey in passing situations.
"We think it's a deep room, a talented room," Payton said Wednesday regarding Coleman's return. "So all those things are a positive."

title: Broncos Trade Deadline: 5 Veterans Most Likely to Be Dealt
full_text:
At 4-2, the Denver Broncos are far more likely to be buyers than sellers ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline .
The Broncos weathered their initial six-game gauntlet as well as anyone could have expected, and now the schedule really opens up, though it's not without its challenges. All of the Broncos' goals are still on the table, which, again, points to the front office being in more of a buyer's mindset.
However, the Broncos do have a handful of potential trade pieces who could draw interest around the NFL. Most of these players are in a contract year, and the Broncos have viable replacement options behind them, in the event of a trade.
Today, we're ranking the players the Broncos would be most likely to trade away. Again, though, the odds of an outbound trade seem pretty slim, as the Broncos are looking to compete for a shot at the Super Bowl.
That being said, you never know. If a team made the Broncos an offer they couldn't refuse, all bets are off. These players will be ranked in order of most to least likely to be traded. Let's dive in.
Moss is in a contract year, and he's poised to command upwards of $20 million per year on his next deal. The Broncos opted not to extend him in the summer, which suggests that the front office is unconvinced on the subject, but it's still possible he could garner an in-season extension at the Week 10 bye.
Moss's rib injury has complicated a potential extension. He originally suffered it in the Broncos' second preseason game , falling on a fumble, but against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 4, he reaggravated it, and missed much of that game, all of Week 5, and only saw 10 snaps in Week 6's win over the Seattle Seahawks.
Meanwhile, Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Daine have played well in the absence of Moss and Patrick Surtain II. Both young cornerbacks have looked starting-caliber , which could clarify the Moss issue for the Broncos.
Barron was a 2025 first-round pick with three more years of cost control on his contract, while Abrams-Draine still has two more years left on his fifth-rounder deal. The Broncos have invested heavily at cornerback for a reason, and in each of the past two seasons, they've had to rely on that depth, which is why I doubt the team looks to trade Moss.
But if the phone rang, GM George Paton will always listen. It would take the right offer to get Moss of Denver's hands, though, especially given that, if they let him depart in free agency in 2027, they could receive a compensatory draft pick as high as a third-rounder.
Moss was a 2023 third-round pick, so if a team wanted him — remember, he's one of the best No. 2 cornerbacks in the NFL — the conversation would likely have to start with a Round 3 pick. Otherwise, there's no upside in Denver losing Moss during the season, although getting a third-round comp pick for him would be the best-case scenario.
Stidham has an $8 million cap number this year , and he just turned 30. He believes he's a starting-caliber quarterback, and despite Nix's slump this season, Stidham is never going to get that opportunity in Denver, especially given how poorly he played in the AFC championship game.
Stidham is also in the final year of his contract. In his training camp battle with Sam Ehlinger , Stidham wasn't the obvious winner, though the Broncos opted to retain him as Bo Nix's primary backup.
I believe the Broncos expect Stidham to leave in 2027 , in hopes of finding a starting opportunity somewhere. The best-case scenario for a comp pick would be a seventh-rounder, so the Broncos could likely be persuaded to part with Stidham with the right offer.
The Broncos have kept Ehlinger around for a reason, and while he's also playing on an expiring contract, I think the team plans on rolling with him as Nix's backup in 2027, while drafting a developmental option in the later rounds.
Mims hasn't looked like himself in his contract year. He changed agents during the offseason in hopes of perhaps getting the Broncos to offer him an extension, and he may have been trending in that direction before a leg injury sidelined him a week into training camp.
Mims missed most of camp and August, but he was able to recover in time to play in the preseason finale. Alas, early in that game, he went up high for a pass near the sideline and came down awkwardly on foot.
In Week 1, Mims didn't look quite right or comfortable, then he missed Week 2 and Week 3. Since his return in Week 4, though, he's been ineffective as a punt returner — his speciality — and a relative non-factor in the passing game.
While Mims was injured, the Broncos elevated undrafted rookie Kolbe Katsis from the practice squad against the Los Angeles Rams, and he turned in a record debut as a returner . The Broncos believe they have something potentially special in Katsis, which is another factor in the cooling of their heels on Mims.
If the Broncos let the chips fall, and Mims departs in free agency next year, depending on the contract he gets from his next team, he could yield a fourth- or fifth-round comp pick. Maybe higher, if some team overpays for him.
Mims was the first draft pick of the Sean Payton era, drafted in Round 2 back in 2023, and he's a two-time Pro Bowl and All-Pro returner. Because Katsis is waiting in the wings, if the right offer came in, I could see the Broncos moving Mims, but given the comp pick the team will receive if it doesn't extend or trade Mims, such an offer would have to be irresistible.
Uwazurike is in a contract year and has not played up to expectations. He's been a key cog in the Broncos' defensive line rotation, but he has failed to build on the progress he showed last year.
Were it not for the emergence of Malcolm Roach , the Broncos' defense wouldn't be weathering the loss of John Franklin-Myers nearly as well as it has. Uwazurike was one of the reasons the Broncos didn't even make an offer to JFM.
Uwazurike was a 2022 fourth-round pick, but he spent the 2023 season suspended for violating the NFL's gambling policy. Otherwise, he would have been a free agent this past spring.
Uwazurike hasn't looked nearly as good against the run and the pass-rush component has been inconsistent. Meanwhile, the Broncos have depth behind him, with a pair of former third-rounders waiting in the wings.
Sai'vion Jones has been getting more playing time this season, and he's looked good as a pass rusher. Meanwhile, rookie Tyler Onyedim has been a healthy scratch all year, while Jones and veteran Jordan Jackson have been getting the game-day nods.
At this stage, I geniunely don't believe the Broncos plan on re-signing Uwazurike. Now, he could turn things around, and change that conversation, but with Roach, Zach Allen, and D.J. Jones balling out, the Broncos have a top-tier starting D-line.
That implies Denver doesn't think Onyedim is ready. But if an interesting offer came in for Uwazurike, you know what they say: necessity is the mother of invention. If Uwazurike walked out the door, the Broncos would have no hesitation in dressing Onyedim.
Losing Uwazurike would weaken them, but at the right price, I could see a deal getting done. However, he's listed second-to-last for a reason: of all the names on this list, his would likely draw the least interest around the league ahead of the deadline.
Sutton is on pace for a career-low season . Much of that is due to Nix's slump and the insane caliber of opponents the Broncos have faced on a weekly basis this season, but Sutton shoulders his share of the blame , too.
Sutton isn't getting off the line of scrimmage well and creating separation consistently. Throw in the absence of his typical intensity at the catch point — turning 50/50 balls into 70/30s — and he's another veteran who simply hasn't looked like himself this season.
At 31, Sutton's best days are behind him, but he's coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons and he made the Pro Bowl last year. His $23.5 million cap number is pretty fair for an aging No. 1 receiver, even if his…

title: Broncos' First Six Games Raise Contract Questions for 5 Veterans
full_text:
Along with decisions on unrestricted and restricted free agents , the Denver Broncos may re-evaluate the contract status of certain players under contract for 2027. There's plenty of time left, but the first six games of the 2026 season may have raised questions about a handful of veterans.
In some cases, these players have little or no guaranteed money left in their deals after this season, while in others, they have option bonuses that the Broncos may exercise to treat as a signing bonus. If they're not exercised, they'd count as base salary.
The Broncos will make these decisions as they figure out their salary cap position. As things currently stand, the Broncos are projected to have about $30.5 million in cap space in 2027, but that's with 38 players under contract and only if the team exercises all of its option bonuses.
Let's examine the Broncos at the top of the list.
The Broncos chose not to exercise Sutton's 2026 option bonus , meaning the $17.5 million he's due will be paid as base salary. In 2027, $10 million of his $19.325 million base salary is injury-only guaranteed, becoming fully guaranteed if he's on the roster on March 17, 2027.
Sutton hasn't had his best start to the 2026 season, with just 9.5 yards per reception. He might be asked to renegotiate his base salary to convert some of it into incentives in exchange for more fully guaranteed money.
If push comes to shove, the Broncos could get out of the deal by cutting Sutton with a post-June 1 designation, which would save $20 million in space with a $6 million dead-money charge. However, it wouldn't be a surprise if the Broncos first try the renegotiation tactic.
Hufanga will be entering the final year of the three-year deal he signed back in 2024. The final year of his contract includes an option bonus of $14.74 million. He also has multiple void years for cap purposes.
Hufanga has played well this season, even though he'll miss a few games with an ankle injury. But if he returns and keeps playing at a high level, the Broncos may want to keep him for the long term.
Thus, the Broncos might choose to extend Hufanga for multiple seasons, which means the option bonus likely becomes an actual signing bonus, and the new years in the contract cover the void years.
If necessary, the Broncos could choose not to exercise the option to reduce dead-money charges when his contract voids. But an extension is in play here.
Jones will enter the final year of the three-year deal he signed in 2024. He's due a $12.235 million base salary and a $765K per-game roster bonus, and none of the money is guaranteed.
Jones has done some good things this season, but he'll be 32 years old. The Broncos could approach him about converting some base salary into incentives in exchange for making the remainder of his salary fully guaranteed.
The Broncos do have the option of cutting Jones, which would free $9.8 million in cap space with a $4.8 million dead-money charge. But the Broncos would likely attempt a contract renegotiation before they'd ever consider cutting him.
Wattenberg had a slow start to the 2025 season, but played better down the stretch, which prompted the Broncos to extend him. This season, he's not off to a good start.
It's possible Wattenberg's play will improve, but if it doesn't, the Broncos will have to decide whether it's worth exercising the option bonus in his contract. He has two such options, one for $3.5 million and another for $7.24 million, that would lower his cap number but come at the cost of pushing his biggest cap hits into future seasons.
Wattenberg's 2027 salary is fully guaranteed, so if he continues to struggle, he can't be cut without significant cap ramifications, and a trade would be unlikely. However, the Broncos could choose not to exercise his option bonuses, which would give them greater flexibility to cut him in 2028 when he'll have no more fully guaranteed money.
Dobbins is averaging just 3.3 yards per carry through six games . He can still break out for a long gain, but he's been slower to hit the hole.
If Dobbins's play doesn't improve in the weeks to come, the Broncos may be prepared to move on next season. That's particularly true if Jonah Coleman impresses once he returns from injured reserve .
Dobbins is due $7 million in base salary and a $1 million per-game roster bonus that aren't guaranteed in 2027. Cutting him would free $8 million in cap space with $2 million in dead money.
If Dobbins doesn't get back on track and the Broncos are content with Coleman and RJ Harvey as the top backs, they may decide to cut Dobbins and not bother with a renegotiated salary.

title: Insider Reveals Troubling Root Cause of Bo Nix's Struggles
full_text:
Bo Nix hasn't looked right since the 2026 season began.
The Denver Broncos' third-year quarterback has looked hesitant , as if he's either unsure of what he's seeing or afraid of getting hit. Turns out, fear has played a big role in Nix's funk, and much of it stems from his ankle injury.
Based on what NFL insider James Palmer posted on X this week , that fear is twofold. Palmer has deep connections to the Broncos front office, and his long X post offered quite a few gleanings into what the team believes is going on with Nix.
Let's examine what Palmer had to say, starting with the root cause of Nix's slump: the fear factor.
Nix seems to be afraid of getting hit and turning the ball over. It's easy to see that he's still carrying some anxiety over his ankle, but instead of that play-to-win mindset that helped him win 24 games in his first two seasons as a starter, he now seems to be focusing too much on playing not to lose.
"My understanding is there is a difference with Nix in 2026, where Nix is focused on not losing the game more than winning the game. Don't turn the ball over," Palmer wrote. "Don't be the reason why we lose the game. That's kind of manifested in his mind to the point that the conservative approach has become an issue on the field."
Despite having a Pro Bowl wide receiver — Courtland Sutton — who Nix has targeted 287 times since 2024, a two-time Pro Bowl tight end — Evan Engram — and a dynamic new weapon the Broncos paid dearly to acquire — Jaylen Waddle — the young quarterback leads the NFL in passes behind the line of scrimmage. That's great for PPR fantasy owners who drafted running back RJ Harvey, but it's bad news for the Broncos' offense.
Nix won't push the ball vertically, nor will he target the middle of the field. As Warren Sharp noted on X , 63% of Nix's passes have been outside the numbers, the most in the NFL, but his 6.0 yards per attempt on those throws rank 32nd in the NFL.
Fear is a powerul motivator. But you miss 100% of the shots you don't take. Pardon the cliche.
All opponents have to do is keep the two-high shell to dissuade Nix from throwing deep, swarm the boundary, and they can bottle up the Broncos' offense. Clearly, he's hesitant to throw inside, and that's allowing opponents to easily predict what he'll do.
Middle-of-the-field avoidance has been a flaw in Nix's game since he entered the league, but he's taken it to a whole new level this season. It's a big reason why Sutton is on pace for a career-low year and why Waddle has just 228 receiving yards thus far.
Palmer reports that Nix's ankle is "fine," and while the Broncos understand that recovering from a serious injury can take time, they want to see him take a big hit so he can get back to his feet and realize that he's okay. That could also help Nix be more assertive with his legs.
"The Broncos want Nix to run it more and they're seeing a player that is a bit gun-shy right now," Palmer wrote. "If you look at the runs that Denver has dialed up, a lot of them he's looking for the sidelines and he's looking for a way to get down as soon as possible. He's not looking for the extra yards or the needed yards in key situations. It's been frustrating."
Nix has definitely looked far more reluctant to use his legs this season. But his mobility has always been a big part of his game and the threat he presents to defenses, and his newfound timidity has removed that from the equation this season.
When it comes to off-schedule throws, Nix has never been on a Patrick Mahomes level, but it's always been one of his strong suits — until this season. This season, when Nix breaks the pocket, he's looked anxious and unpoised, leading to fewer rushing yards and fewer big off-schedule completions.
Nix looks uncomfortable, even when the Broncos' offensive line gives him clean pockets. He's bailing on pockets way early, which not only sabatoges the routes in the play-call, but it puts him on the move where, as we just discussed, he's not playing with poise and seeing the field.
It sounds like the Broncos are frustrated with Nix's reluctance to use his legs. And per Palmer, that fear his injury created has much to do with his sketchy pocket presence.
"This plays a part in the drifting or escaping out of clean pockets, I'm told. This has always been an issue with him his whole career, but this year it's more exaggerated and impacting a passing game where WRs are open," Palmer wrote. "Nix oftentimes is on the move before even the first read gets to the top of their route. The play designs have some longer development downfield, so this is a bad combination right now."
Nix isn't giving his receivers the time they need to run the route and get open. He's bailing on clean pockets, and while he's called it "hero-ball," it basically cuts the field in half and reduces the Broncos' offense to a slapdash backyard football exercise.
Sean Payton and the Broncos' coaches are working to coax Nix out of this shell. Following the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, Payton said at the podium that he wants Nix to " let 'er rip ."
Nix took that to mean "trust what you see." But we didn't see a change in his performance on Thursday night.
Against the Seattle Seahawks four days later, we saw Nix uncork two downfield passes, neither of which were complete, although one of them drew a defensive pass interference penalty that set the Broncos up on the 1-yard line. From there, though, the Seahawks just kept deploying the two-high shell over the top, and dared Nix to throw underneath; when he did, they'd swarm and tackle.
The Broncos went 3-of-14 on third down against Seattle because of this and an inability to get the run game going. It has all dovetailed into a world of suck for the Broncos' offense.
If Nix can get back to trusting his eyes and O-line, everything becomes possible. Per Palmer, Nix is too spooked out there.
"Nix is seeing ghosts at times," Palmer wrote.
Payton made it clear on Monday that the Broncos aren't considering making a change at quarterback. Nix is 18-3 in his last 21 starts. No team benches a quarterback with a .700 winning percentage.
But Palmer reports that the Broncos are "concerned." That being said, based on Nix's 30-game sample size as an NFL starter, the Broncos believe they have plenty to draw on to help get him back on the horse.
That brutal six-game schedule has played a much bigger role in Nix's failure to launch this year than most people realize. Now that the Broncos are through it — navigating that gauntlet with a 4-2 record — I think we're going to start seeing Nix loosen up a little bit.
This is a guy who's always at his best when the chips are down and the pressure is the highest. All it might take is one big game to shake the cobwebs off and get Nix back to playing like his pre-injury self.
The schedule opens up now, starting with this week's road trip to take on the Arizona Cardinals. There's a lot of season left to be played, and Nix has proven to be one of the NFL's best finishers.
He may not have started on the right foot, but if past outcomes are the best predictor of future outcomes, I fully expect Nix to finish strong.

title: Broncos Trade Deadline Big Board: Best Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is on November 10, and given Sean Payton’s aggressiveness, the 4-2 Denver Broncos could be buyers this year.
The Broncos weathered the initial six-game storm largely because of their defense, with Bo Nix and company barely scraping by, so if they do buy, it’ll likely be on offense to find a piece or two to help jump-start the unit.
While there are some intriguing defenders who could be available out there, it makes less sense for the Broncos to go buying on that side of the ball, unless they suffer injuries between now and the deadline, so knock on wood that they don’t.
The Broncos could use help at running back, tight end, left guard, center, and right tackle, as the players at these positions have underperformed, and they'd be the easiest to upgrade. Looking around the NFL, not many trade rumors are circulating yet, but there are some.
Any of these players could make sense, depending on the compensation it would take for Denver to acquire them. Today, we're unveiling our Broncos trade deadline big board, ranked from most to least likely.
Note: At this time, all players listed below are on teams with no more than two wins through six weeks.
The Titans are having a terrible season, and their offense is falling apart, with Cam Ward not looking like a legitimate starting quarterback. There have been rumors that Pollard is available, even going back to before last year's trade deadline.
He's mostly been linked with the Seattle Seahawks, but with the Broncos' running-game issues, they could look his way given J.K. Dobbins's struggles. It's unlikely Pollard would cost in a trade, maybe an early third-round pick in 2027 or 2028, with Denver getting him and a pick a round or two later back in return.
With the Colts firing GM Chris Ballard , many believe a fire sale is coming, but they made it clear they still have high expectations. However, if the Colts lose two of their next three games, that could change.
Nelson is playing on an expiring deal, and the Colts don’t have a first-round pick in 2027. Rumors suggest Indy may be willing to move Nelson to add to its Day 2 war chest in 2027. I could see Payton convincing Broncos GM George Paton to pull the trigger on Nelson amid Ben Powers’s struggles, though he hasn’t been the weakest link on the offensive line.
Taylor is a great running back, but his down-to-down consistency has struggled this year, with a success rate barely better than Dobbins’s. But Taylor does have a higher explosive run rate.
Teams aren’t selling out to stop Taylor, as he is facing only a slightly higher rate of stacked boxes than Denver, with both below the league average. The Colts will likely ask a lot for him , and the cost could be the sticking point.
There's also the fit issue. Taylor is better when the quarterback is under center, and Nix is one of the worst quarterbacks in that department, so it's not something the Broncos do much. If Denver wanted to pay for reputation, then giving up an early-round pick for Taylor is possible.
Still, his current level of play and the running-game analytics suggest a third- or fourth-round pick instead of a first- or second-rounder.
Luke Wattenberg has been a mess, and the Broncos are stuck with him through the 2027 season due to the extension he signed last year, unless they can trade him. Payton is familiar with McCoy, who can also play left guard if Denver wanted to look his way to improve over Powers.
McCoy is better at center, though, and his contract wouldn't be an obstacle in a trade. He should cost only a third- or fourth-round pick if the Saints want to move on from him. The Saints may need to suffer one or two more losses before they'd be willing to sell off some players.
The Texans' offense hasn’t been the issue amid their struggles; their defense has. Moreau has had a good year, and the Texans will likely look to offload either Brevin Jordan or Moreau, but the former's injury history and play should stay Denver's hand.
The Broncos should target Moreau, who has legit Y-tight end upside and could raise the floor, but would two Day 3 picks spread over the next two years be enough?
The Cowboys are underachieving, but they like Spann-Ford for his Y-tight end ability as a blocker and receiver, though he is limited as a pass-catcher. The Cowboys just signed him to a three-year extension, and he's a coach's favorite, but Jerry Jones likes to send messages to coaches when the team is underperforming, and that could lead to Spann-Ford being moved.
There haven’t been any rumors, but an earlier Day 3 pick could probably get it done if the Cowboys had interest in moving him.
This would be a dream get for the Broncos, as Parkinson is one of the better true Y-tight ends in the NFL. He is one of the best blocking tight ends and is more than enough of a receiving threat to be a game-changer for defenses.
However, Sean McVay loves Parkinson, and the Rams love their 13 personnel, which works because of him. Parkinson is still young and could be worth a slight overpay to get the Rams to make the trade, but they’re more likely to be buyers than sellers at this time in what could be Matthew Stafford's last ride.
Still, like multiple other players, a few more losses could change things in L.A.
Unlike Taylor, Williams does his best work in shotgun rather than the center, though he is more than capable at both. He isn’t afraid to open up to the media about topics his team would rather keep behind closed doors, and that's something Payton would take issue with.
Williams is a key player in the Rams' running game, and they're unlikely to move on from him unless they are offered a great deal, but as with Parkinson, two more losses could lead to a massive shift in the Rams' goals for this season.
The Bucs are another underperforming team likely to clean house, as questions arise about whether Todd Bowles will even finish the season as head coach. The Bucs could look to sell some players and kick-start a slight rebuild, so maybe Denver could convince them to move on from their starting right tackle.
Heck, the Broncos could even give them one back in McGlinchey, along with picks to get Goedeke. Probably not, though, given McGlinchey's low quality of play and his contract.
Teams don’t like to sell off offensive linemen who are playing well, even if the Bucs decide to be sellers. It's hard to build a quality offensive line in this league.
This is the dream . The Cardinals are wasting McBride’s prime, and they're still multiple years away from being a threat. It would undoubtedly take a first-round pick just to open the conversation, because he is one of the best tight ends in the NFL.
The Cardinals could be willing to trade away McBride at the right price, though. A couple more losses would likely have to happen first, and the Broncos could help with that by defeating them this week.
While McBride isn’t overly realistic, rumors over the past couple of years suggest Denver has been interested in him ahead of the trade deadline. Never say never.

title: Broncos' IR Watch: Who's Eligible to Return and What They Bring
full_text:
Help could be on the way to the 4-2 Denver Broncos.
Those first six games were brutal, but the Broncos weathered the storm. As the schedule begins to ease up, a handful of Broncos are eligible to return from injured reserve.
Keep in mind that just because they're eligible to return doesn't mean they're healthy enough , nor that the Broncos are ready to activate them.
Let's take a look at the three Broncos eligible to return from IR, starting with the one most fans have been pining for since Week 2.
Coleman suffered an ankle injury in Week 2, though he finished the game and was a big reason the Broncos were able to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Broncos placed him on IR a few days after that game, and he's missed the four mandatory games to be eligible for return.
Activating Coleman is a no-brainer, but the exact timing of when the Broncos do so could be tied to what happens with Tyler Badie. Badie suffered a thumb injury last week against the Seattle Seahawks, and if his recovery is longer than a couple of weeks, he could end up on IR.
The Broncos started the season with four running backs on the 53-man roster, but they only ever dress three, plus fullback Adam Prentice. Coleman's return would put them back at four, but since the rookie hit IR, other demands may have affected the roster math, which is why we may not see news of Coleman's return until later in the week.
The fourth-round rookie out of Washington plays with tremendous vision and burst, which are two elements the Broncos' ground attack is sorely missing right now. Suffice it to say, this offense could really use him, given that J.K. Dobbins is averaging a career-low 3.3 yards per carry this season.
Crum suffered a knee injury in the preseason, and he's eligible to return, if he's healthy enough. We don't know that he is healthy, though, and it's not a subject Sean Payton tends to open up about.
One big question worth asking here is whether the Broncos need Crum. My answer would be no, unless there were an injury to Mike McGlinchey, at which point, Alex Palzcewski would step in at right tackle, and the Broncos could use Crum.
He's a super smart, athletic freak, but I wouldn't expect to see Crum back any time soon.
After an impressive showing at the Broncos' rookie minicamp, we haven't seen hide nor hair of Lohner. He went under the knife right before OTAs began for a "routine" clean-up procedure that wasn't supposed to impact his training camp availability.
Alas, it did. The Broncos put him on IR designated to return. Given that Denver has already rostered one tight end it hasn't needed yet — rookie Dallen Bentley, who is yet to dress for a single game — I doubt the Broncos are urgently looking to get Lohner activated.
Then again, Payton seems to love Lohner, so that could change the thinking here. But I doubt it.
Gargiuolo suffered a torn ACL in the preseason of 2025. Alas, given that we didn't see him this past summer at training camp, I can only assume his recovery has been slow-going, or he experienced a setback.
The Broncos have some quality interior offensive line depth, so there is zero urgency to push Gargiulo back onto the field. And since we haven't seen the former seventh-round pick for 14 months, odds are he's on ice until 2027.
Bryant went down with an ankle injury in Week 4 , and with two games in the rearview since then, he has two more to go before he's eligible to return. Week 9's road game against the Carolina Panthers will be the soonest he can return, health-willing.
It was a shame to see Bryant get hurt because he was building up some nice momentum, and clearly has a connection with Bo Nix. The injury bug is no respector of persons, though.
Just when Bryant starts rolling, he gets hurt. That's been the theme through his first two NFL seasons; let's hope it's not a permanent one.

title: Broncos Stock Report: 4 Risers, 4 Fallers Entering Week 7
full_text:
The Denver Broncos weathered the storm of their first six-game stretch, getting out to a 4-2 start, which is about as good as anyone could have expected.
The Broncos' overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks afforded them a three-day "mini-bye," a needed breather to rest up before preparing for the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. The last few weeks have seen several players rise in relief of injured players, especially on defense.
Coming out of this mini-bye, let's break down the Broncos' biggest risers and fallers.
Barron has helped keep the Broncos' passing defense afloat while Patrick Surtain II has missed the past two-plus games. While he's given up completions, Barron has been physical and sticky in coverage, competing hard at the catch point.
Throw in his reliability as a tackler this season — which is huge, given that Denver co-leads the NFL in missed tackles — and it's safe to say the Broncos have a real player on their hands. All that summertime "bust" talk should be thrown completely out the window.
This former first-rounder has been playing up to his draft pedigree.
Like Barron, Abrams-Draine has been relied upon to help cover for the absence of Riley Moss. Although Moss dressed and even played 20 snaps last week, Abrams-Draine saw the lion's share of the snaps, tasked with covering Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.
Abrams-Draine's fourth-quarter interception against Seattle was huge, and it illustrated the confidence this kid is playing with as a cover corner. I'd like to see his tackling improve drastically, but he's never been the most physical defensive back.
The NFL's biggest talking point over the past four days has been Nix's slump and whether the Broncos should bench him. However, at 4-2, head coach Sean Payton made it clear on Monday that Nix's job as the starter is still secure.
That doesn't mean the Broncos are blind to Nix's struggles, though. The buzz out of Broncos HQ is that Nix is still quite bothered and affected by his ankle, which he fractured in the playoffs last season.
The Broncos say the ankle is healed, so it sounds like Nix is still struggling with the mental recovery. But now that the worst of the initial schedule is behind them, the third-year quarterback could be poised to get back on the horse, and give fans more than a glimpse of the dynamic player he was before his January injury.
Robinson is on a roll, and the Broncos are going to need him to stay on it. He co-led the team last week against Seattle with six QB pressures, notching his second sack of the season.
With Jonathon Cooper returning and Jonah Elliss dealing with what could be a severe leg injury , Robinson's role should be unchanged moving forward. Robinson has been one of the Broncos' best surprise players of 2026.
Dobbins looks indecisive and lacks burst. The Broncos have fed him over the past several weeks, but it hasn't led to much production.
Dobbins did score his first and second touchdowns of the season over the past two weeks, but he's otherwise been ineffective overall as a between-the-tackles runner. He seems to believe that the schedule had a lot to do with his lack of success early on, and if that's true, we should see him take some measurable steps forward.
Sutton is in line for a career-worst season. Granted, much of that has to do with Nix's slump and the Broncos' disjointed passing offense, but Sutton isn't blameless.
The veteran wideout isn't fighting for the ball at the catch point as we're used to seeing, and he's struggling to create separation as a route-runner, leading some to wonder whether Father Time has caught up to the ninth-year pro. Sutton needs to step it up.
Although he's still on the practice squad, Rapp came in handy last week against the Seahawks with Talanoa Hufanga sidelined with an injury. Rapp played 65 of the 85 total defensive snaps last week, and he was very good for the Broncos, helping to limit JSN and Kupp.
Rapp totaled six tackles and seemed perfectly comfortable and natural playing next to Jones. The Broncos have found their No. 3 safety, it would seem, but when Hufanga comes back, they're going to have to promote Rapp to the 53-man roster eventually, which will mean parting ways with JL Skinner or Tycen Anderson, in all likelihood.
I get it. Wide receiver is a quarterback-dependent position, but Waddle's impact could already be much greater than it's been.
He's dropped to many passes and I don't like the body language I'm starting to see from him. Right now, the Broncos need to fall in line and close ranks around the beleaguered Nix, and for guys like Waddle, when his number is called, he has to answer the bell.
Look for Payton to start opening up this offense moving forward. That should benefit Waddle.
