title: Broncos Have Several 2027 Restricted Free Agents—Only One Is a No-Brainer
full_text:
The Denver Broncos sit at 4-2 , with several players set to be unrestricted free agents in 2027. We've updated the outlook for each of those players six games into the season, and now it's time to examine the Broncos' 2027 restricted free agents.
Restricted free agents are eligible for a first-, second-, or original-round tender, which represents the draft-pick compensation the Broncos would receive if an outside team signed the player to an offer sheet. If it's an original-round tender and the player was undrafted, the team that loses the RFA doesn't get a draft pick as compensation.
The Broncos have five players set to become restricted free agents in 2027. We'll look at what the future likely holds for each after six games of the 2026 season, along with an early prediction.
Tillman has excelled as a depth and rotational player on the Denver defense. He has 28 pressures and nine sacks in his career, with four pressures in five games this season.
This will be an easy decision for the Broncos. Tillman needs to get a second-round tender so the Broncos can keep him for another year. The estimated $6.261 million salary is worth it.
Verdict : Second-round tender.
Jackson hasn't seen a lot of playing time the past couple of seasons. The Broncos mainly kept him for depth purposes, but other players have surpassed him on the depth chart.
Jackson won't be tendered, but there's a small chance that the Broncos will re-sign him to a one-year deal. However, that depends on how much the Broncos like players such as Sai'vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim.
Verdict : No tender, might not re-sign.
Key excels at special teams ( first-team All-Pro last year ), and he's shown he can do some good things on defense. He played a significant number of defensive snaps against the Seattle Seahawks because Talanoa Hufanga was out with an ankle injury, though Taylor Rapp received more.
There's a chance the Broncos will give the second-round tender to Key, even if they re-sign Brandon Jones. Another option is a two-year deal, like what the Broncos gave to offensive guard Alex Palczewski this past offseason.
Verdict : Second-round tender or re-sign to a short-term deal.
Badie has stuck around on the depth chart because of what he brings to special teams. He's shown he can be a productive back when called into action, but he's not somebody you want to rely on as a top option.
Badie isn't worth tendering. However, the Broncos like what he brings to special teams, so they could re-sign him to a one-year deal at the veteran minimum to compete for a roster spot.
Verdict : No tender, likely to re-sign.
Crum was the swing tackle and sixth offensive lineman last season after Matt Peart's season was cut short because of injury, and Palczewski stepped in at left guard for multiple games.
Crum did some good things last year, but he struggled in the preseason and is currently on injured reserve. He's unlikely to be tendered, but the Broncos might be willing to give him a one-year deal to let him compete for a roster spot.
Verdict : No tender, likely to re-sign.

title: Detroit Lions TE Sam LaPorta Is Biggest Loser In Tone-Deaf Interview
full_text:
That is all Detroit sports fans are asking these local athletes to do. Nobody is burying their heads in the sand, oblivious to the fact these athletes are playing a kids game for a significant amount of money.
Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta quickly learned that fans in Detroit are not going to sit back and watch him proclaim that he can get paid elsewhere.
Lately, each professional team in Detroit has had one player make their contract situation very awkward and uncomfortable.
LaPorta, a former second-round who is playing on the last year of his rookie contract, went on the "Pardon My Take" podcast and was likely a little too comfortable when he answered the question about playing in 2026 without having a new contract extension.
The Red Wings are dealing with Dylan Larkin, whose demand to be traded went public. The Tigers eventually dealt pitcher Tarik Skubal, but not before he spent a couple of years proclaiming his love for the City and wanting to be a Tigers, yet hired a powerful agent to get him to a team that could possibly pay him a lucrative contract. Jalen Duren of the Pistons caught the wrath of fans for how his saga played out with the Pistons.
How did that trip to Sacramento go Jalen? Nobody believed seriously that he was interested in joining an irrelevant NBA franchise. It was all a negotiation ploy.
LaPorta failed to realize his comments came across to regular fans as tone-deaf and selfish. Everybody understands he wants to be paid a contract that is similar to or exceeds what the top players at his position earn.
He may have even been low-balled by general manager Brad Holmes.
What turned many people off is the flippant answer that came across that he did not care. much if his playing days were in Detroit or somewhere else.
Fans have been asked to weather raising ticket prices, a team that has regressed and witnessing one of the worst defenses in NFL history.
The last thing they were interested in hearing was a star player talking about taking his ball and going somewhere else.
Yes, we like players to join podcasts and be honest. But the 25-year-old could have answered the question much, much differently.
Do the Lions even have a P.R. staff? It appeared the staffer assigned to LaPorta might have just taken the week off or didn't care he was going to appear on one of the biggest sports podcast of all-time.
Maybe the Lions public relations department were updating their files that week? Who knows.
He could have mentioned his frustrations and why. The part of the answer that frustrated people the most was, 'If I don’t get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good. I’ll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever.'
Really showing that appreciation for the fans that pay high ticket prices to watch the Lions each and every week.
In an economy where many are struggling financially, those type of comments should have been reserved for his agent of his friends. Maybe the backlash will wake up more players to the idea that many fans care more about the logo on the front than the name on the back.
If LaPorta leaves, Detroit will simply draft another solid tight end and it will still be all good. So, whatever.
LaPorta should have read the room better and maybe taken a page out of the playbook of Jack Campbell, who masterfully handled his contract talks and eventual extension.

title: One Trade Deadline Move the Lions Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
It's no secret that the Detroit Lions have a glaring need on their roster ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
With one of the league's worst pass defenses and little in the way of reinforcements, Detroit would benefit greatly from being active on the trade market and adding a cornerback to the mix.
Fortunately for Detroit, there are some teams with intriguing options who have struggled out of. the gate and as a result could be enticed to make a deal. One team worth watching at the deadline is the winless Los Angeles Chargers, who have fallen to 0-6 with a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6.
Los Angeles has a trio of intriguing cornerbacks who could draw some trade interest, with the top option being third-year option Tarheeb Still. The former fifth-round pick is on his rookie contract through the end of next season, and as a result fits Detroit's current financial situation in addition to having plenty of upside.
Still has been fairly productive through the first six games of the season. While he hasn't logged an interception this season, the Maryland product has notched an overall defensive grade of 71.6 and a coverage grade of 76.6 via Pro Football Focus.
He has allowed an opposing passer rating of 93.6 according to PFF, which is lower than Detroit's three highest-utilized cornerbacks in D.J. Reed (124.2), Roger McCreary (111.6) and Rock Ya-Sin (96.7).
Reed, in particular, has been underwhelming . The veteran was signed last offseason with the expectation of being the top cornerback, but hasn't lived up to that billing early in his tenure.
Ennis Rakestraw, the team's second-round pick in 2024, has been intriguing but hasn't had the level of consistent reps that would cement him as a top option.
The Lions need to find a consistent option to provide them with a boost for the second half of the season, as the assembly they've had early in the year hasn't been satisfactory. Detroit has been fortunate to get enough offensive production throughout the 3-2 start, but these secondary issues could haunt them in pivotal games.
Still has the ability to help right the ship, and may not carry a hefty asking price. As a former fifth-round pick, perhaps the Lions could swing a deal providing the Chargers with a fourth-round pick to give the Chargers more draft value than what they used on him.
With four career interceptions, Still has some proven ball production. He could be a difference-making addition, and as a young player could have plenty of room to grow in Detroit's scheme. Ultimately, making this move would be a win for general manager Brad Holmes, and would give the team another intriguing young option along with Rakestraw.

title: 3 Lions Impacted Most by Brian Branch's Return from Injury
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are getting a big playmaker back for their defense in safety Brian Branch.
Assuming all goes to plan for the remainder of this week, Branch is expected to suit up for the first time this season when the Lions take on the Green Bay Packers Sunday at Ford Field. He could be one of two big returns the Lions get from injury, as center Cade Mays is also trending toward playing.
If Branch is able to go, it adds a significant level of production to Detroit's defense heading into a pivotal stretch that starts with back-to-back division games at home. There will be a ripple effect felt throughout Detroit's defense, as his return will cause some shuffling in the secondary.
Here are three players who will feel the impact of Branch's return from injury.
Clark is a veteran who inked a one-year deal with Detroit heading into the season. He was expected to fill in for depth purposes until Branch returns, but based on how things have shaken out he could still find himself in the starting lineup next to Branch moving forward.
Avonte Maddox, who was the team's other starter at safety to open the year, is out for the season after an injury against Buffalo in Week 2. Christian Izien is another option , but his role has diminished after a decent start to the season. Meanwhile, Thomas Harper is also on injured reserve.
With Branch likely returning in a significant role, Clark appears to be the best option to play alongside him at this stage of the season. He could fill the void left by Kerby Joseph for the time being, as Joseph remains sidelined with a knee injury.
Izien was signed with the thought of playing multiple positions in Detroit's secondary. However, that hasn't quite materialized due to a number of factors throughout the early part of the season. He missed the season opener with an injury, and has shuffled between nickel and safety.
In their win over the Arizona Cardinals, Izien did not play one defensive snap as Detroit turned to Keith Abney to play the safety spot alongside Clark. Injuries could always open up an opportunity down the line, but for the time being it appears Izien may be limited to special teams.
One avenue the Lions could explore with him is playing the nickel spot, though that wasn't an option for him in Arizona. If he's going to get snaps defensively with Branch back in the mix, nickel may be the best spot for him to do
Week 5 was a big one for the rookie out of Arizona State. Abney recorded his first-career interception , and had a huge role playing the safety spot in Detroit's defense for the first time. While it wasn't a perfect debut, Abney showed that he is capable of contributing and earned a longer look.
It's tough to say when that look may come if Branch returns to full health and is able to play a big role right away. He could still spell his veteran counterpart so as not to rush him back too quickly, but the Lions will want Branch on the field whenever possible.
As a result, the Lions could experiment with playing Abney more on the boundary in place of one of their struggling cornerbacks, or align him in the nickel spot more often. He's proven to be deserving of another opportunity, but Branch's return complicates exactly when and how he'll line up moving forward for the Lions' defense.

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Week 7 Estimated Wednesday Injury Report
full_text:
The Detroit Lions released their first Week 7 injury report, ahead of the teams first divisional contest at Ford Field against the Green Bay Packers.
Last week, the team had a bye, so the scheduled players day off was Wednesday this week, resulting in an estimated injury report.
Veteran defensive back Rock Ya-Sin was listed as a limited participant , while Cade Mays and Brian Branch, who are both expected to suit up against Green Bay, were listed as full participants.
Head coach Dan Campbell has expressed respect for the Packers and their ability to force takeaways.
"I know I mentioned some of this yesterday, but they're playing really good football right now," said Campbell. "Two of their best games have been these back-to-back games. Plus-six in the turnover ratio the last two weeks, it was seven takeaways on defense, man. It's an opportunistic defense. They fly around the football. They disguise well and create issues. (Packers Head Coach) Matt (LaFleur)’s doing a hell of a job. They have, they've gotten better every week, man. They've settled some things in in that O-line. (Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan) Gannon's doing a hell of a job with that defense too."
Campbell added further, "They've just steadily gotten better and better and they're playing at a very high level right now. Offensively (Jordan) Love, man, he makes it go. He is the secret sauce. And (Christian) Watson and (Matthew) Golden, man, they're dangerous threats down the field and he's going to give them opportunities that shows up every week. (Tucker) Kraft has come off the injury nicely. He's gotten better every week. He's playing good football right now."
The Packers arrive with a record of 4-2, having defeated the Dallas Cowboys last week.
"This team's playing at a high level," said Campbell. "They're big, physical and special teams, man, they play hard. So, this will be an outstanding test for us. Hell of an opponent, first division game of the season at home. We're looking forward to it, but this is a real good team right now playing good football.”
CB Rock Ya-Sin -- Hamstring (LP) Safety Brian Branch -- Achilles (FP) OL Cade Mays -- Wrist (FP)

title: Sam LaPorta Reveals Extreme Frustrations: I Break My F'''ing Back For Lions
full_text:
Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta sounded off about his contract frustrations during a recent episode of the "Pardon My Take" NFL podcast.
Recently, reports surfaced that indicated LaPorta's camp and the Lions have tabled contract negotiations during the regular season.
The former second-round pick understands part of the reason the Lions' running game has been so successful has been his efforts blocking. He has made previous references to the challenges of blocking defensive ends who are much larger than he is.
“I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport we play, it sucks. It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta explained on the popular sports podcast. "Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f***ing back for this team. And then I’m going out there this year, and I’m ballin. And maybe they’re just not showing the love.”
Detroit has the option of using the franchise tag on LaPorta for the upcoming 2027 NFL season. General manager Brad Holmes has not chosen to use this salary-cap leverage, but may be forced to.
If LaPorta continues to play at a high level, he could command north of $20 million annually.
Detroit does have the salary-cap space, but may be forced to ink a cornerback to a hefty contract and there is still the matter of what to allocate for safety Brian Branch.
LaPorta indicated he still plans to play at a high level, and if that means he is wearing a new uniform next season, that will just have to be how it is.
As LaPorta explained, “So I’m going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months if I don’t get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good . I’ll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever."
The highest-paid tight ends in the NFL are George Kittle (19.1 million), Trey McBride (19 million) and Tucker Kraft (18.75 million).
Kraft visits Ford Field this weekend for the matchup against the Lions in Week 7.

title: Pros and Cons of Detroit Lions Signing RB Najee Harris
full_text:
There's no question the Detroit Lions have had an elite offense through the first six weeks of the 2026 campaign. In fact, Dan Campbell's squad has averaged 32.8 points per game, the second-highest total in the NFL.
Yet, the Lions haven't exactly found a running back to spell do-it-all runner Jahmyr Gibbs. Through five games, Sione Vaki is Detroit's second-leading rusher with 51 yards to his name, while signal-caller Jared Goff trails Vaki with 16 total rushing yards.
Basically there's been no semblance of a backup back in Motown thus far this season, and that could become problematic as the season progresses and Gibbs continues to accumulate carries.
The superstar back has amassed 105 of Detroit's 130 total rush attempts in 2026, equating to roughly 81 percent of the team's carries.
As much as the Lions want Gibbs to receive touches as often as possible (and rightfully so), that just doesn't seem like a sustainable percentage. And there is the fear that Campbell & Co. could run him into the ground, limiting his effectiveness down the stretch of the season.
No Lions fan or member of the organization wants that to happen. Consequently, Detroit should look into adding a competent No. 2 back. Enter veteran runner Najee Harris, who was cut on Tuesday by the N.Y. Giants.
Harris, a Pro Bowler in his rookie campaign with the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2021, had a highly inefficient, short-lived stint with the Giants. In five games with John Harbaugh's team, he compiled 31 carries for 99 yards and failed to reach the end zone.
Additionally, he received the start over Cam Skattebo on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, and proceeded to rush for a measly two yards on four carries.
The final straw for Harris in the Meadowlands, though, was his criticism of how he was deployed as part of a running back-by-committee.
“It's hard to get into a rhythm with one or two runs,” Harris told reporters Sunday. “The first couple runs you'll be like: 'OK, how are they playing me?' And then the next ones will be like: This is how you attack it. But if you're getting a play here and you get taken out for a series, there's nothing you can do. That's why I'm saying I don't know. I've never been through this before.”
Harris, who is 28, has been productive in his career. He produced four consecutive seasons with 1,000-plus yards and six-or-more touchdowns in his tenure in Pittsburgh. He also notably never missed a single game with the Steelers.
However, he has battled ineffectiveness and the injury bug since, tearing his left Achilles tendon with the L.A. Chargers early on in the 2025 season. He proceeded to suit up for just three games with the Chargers, notching 61 yards and zero scores on 15 carries.
He fought his way back from the ailment to be ready for the ‘26 campaign. However, he now finds himself unemployed after a failed stint in New York.
Although his best days could be behind him, he still could be just what the doctor ordered for the Lions. Harris is certainly a more capable, proven back than Vaki, and he could slide right into the No. 2 role in Detroit's backfield.
Subsequently, if I were Brad Holmes, I'd definitely consider inking Harris to a contract for the remainder of the season .

title: Why Lions Like Center Cade Mays Over Juice Scruggs Against Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will have a new center when the team takes the field against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field.
Speaking with 97.1. The Ticket during his weekly radio interview, head coach Dan Campbell explained he was impressed with what he saw from Cade Mays at practice on Tuesday afternoon.
As a result, the Lions will make the switch from Juice Scruggs to Mays, who inked a lucrative three-year contract in free agency this past offseason.
“We really worked the heck out of Cade yesterday. He got some quality reps, and we would like to give him a go here. We’d like to just rip this band-aid off of Cade," said Campbell. "I thought he had some good work yesterday. I thought he looked pretty good.”
Earlier in the week, the former NFL tight floated idea of potentially having a center rotation, but that was largely out of respect for how well Scruggs played the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season.
Additional NFL Insider Analysis: Despite Flaws, Lions Move Up in Week 7 Power Rankings
“I don’t see us doing that. You go around and around, and all these questions come in. It’s different than a guard. Jon, you know that. A guard and a center is totally different," Campbell explained. "That guy’s touching the ball. The snap count is different. Everything: the snap, the timing, the calls, the quarterback’s comfort with one guy over and over.”
Quarterback Jared Goff shared with reporters this week what it has been like to have Mays return at practice.
“Yeah, Cade's been great. He's been on top of it through his time off and his rehab and I bet he'd say he's even stronger now than he was before the injury with all the workouts he's been doing," said Goff. "Yeah, it's exciting and he's done a good job."
The 32-year-old signal-caller does not see much of a drop off, as he did take many snaps with the former Panthers center during offseason workouts and training camp, before Mays injured his wrist.
“No, I had a lot of snaps with Cade from April until about a month and a half ago and then I had a lot of snaps with Juice from that point.”
Goff also noted that the success of the 2026 team will be determined by how well the offensive line gels and performs the remaining 12 games of the regular season.
"We can't do anything without those guys," said Goff. "We do have a really good skill group here, but they know and we know as an offense and as a team, we only go where they go. And so when they're playing well, we can do some pretty special things and they know that.”

title: Kerby Joseph Posts Intense Workout: Will Safety Play in 2026?
full_text:
Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph excited supporters when he posted on social media a workout at the teams Allen Park Performance Center.
In the early morning hours, Joseph shared an intense workout that highlighted his speed, ability to cut and to change directions.
It has been over a calendar year since the All-Pro safety played, fueling speculation his career could be in jeopardy.
He has been seen at the practice facility in a jovial mood, but still remains on the Physically Unable to Perform List.
Head coach Dan Campbell, speaking to local reporters prior to practice on Tuesday offered an encouraging update, when asked about the former third-round pick.
“He's doing well. I'll leave it at that. He really is. He's doing a good job. I'm not going to give you a timetable, but I've been pleased with where he's at," Campbell said. "He's in a good head space right now, which is great because that's hard. You're coming off this, you're wanting to go and you're working at it, and at some point it's time for football. We all know that and recognize it, but we'll take it one day at a time.”
When asked directly if he expects Joseph to play this year, Campbell replied, "I do."

“Yeah. I mean, that's tough. You don't want to do this roller coaster. It can get frustrating. And inevitably, if we really want to be the team we need to be, that we need to be, we want to be, you've got to win back-to-back games. And you’ve got to do it more than once a year," said Campbell. title: Lions Biggest Need Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is growing closer, and as a result the Detroit Lions should be looking for ways to upgrade their roster.
Sitting at 3-2, the Lions are in position to make another push for a division title and playoff appearance after missing the postseason last year. However, their roster doesn't appear to be complete enough to make that push quite yet.
For general manager Brad Holmes, adding a player or two at the deadline would come with obvious benefits. In particular, Holmes should look to add talent in the secondary for the remainder of the season in an attempt to fortify the team's biggest area of weakness.
Detroit currently ranks last in the league in passing yards allowed per game, and have the fourth-worst passer rating against at 106.3. This has been the case despite the defense also ranking first in the league in sacks with 20.
For years, pass-rush was considered a major weakness for Detroit. However, through five games it has been one of their biggest strengths on defense. Now, the Lions need to find another option or two to help solidify their coverage attack.
Earlier in the year, the Lions were linked to Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. after he missed the start of the season amidst a contract dispute. However, they were outbid and ultimately missed the opportunity as Porter was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys.
There are several intriguing options who are expected to be available based on the start of the season across the league. In particular, the Indianapolis Colts, Los Angeles Chargers and Philadelphia Eagles are all off to slow starts and could theoretically be sellers come the Nov. 10 deadline.
Each of these teams has some intriguing options, including Los Angeles' Tarheeb Still, Cam Hart and Donte Jackson. Philadelphia has Riq Woolen, while the Colts could be open to a potential deal involving Sauce Gardner amidst their change in leadership after Chris Ballard was ousted as general manager.
The Lions need to add some depth to the cornerback room at the very least. D.J. Reed has not been the player that Detroit hoped he would be when they signed him to a three-year deal last offseason, as he has struggled against opposing team's top options.
Veteran Rock Ya-Sin entered the season as the second starter after the release of Terrion Arnold, but has lost his starting spot in favor of Roger McCreary. Ennis Rakestraw has also received some opportunities, but this area is Detroit's biggest detracting factor in their pursuit of the postseason.
Because of that, the Lions need to be active at the deadline and acquire an experienced option who fits their style and can give them consistency on the outside. Detroit could also look to add safety depth if Kerby Joseph isn't nearing a return by the time the deadline rolls around.
However, Detroit's safety room will get a big boost potentially as soon as this week with Brian Branch returning from an Achilles injury. If the Lions feel that one move is what they need, their efforts should be focused on adding a cornerback.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Detroit Lions Bring Back Rookie DL, Cut DL Chris Smith
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced a pair of practice squad roster moves early in the week ahead of their first divisional contest of the 2026 NFL regular season.
After visiting for a workout earlier this week, defensive lineman Aidan Keanaaina was brought back to the practice squad. In a corresponding move, defensive tackle Chris Smith was cut.
Keanaaina played collegiately at Notre Dame and for the California Golden Bears. In his last two years,  he secured101 tackles, 2.5 sacks and five tackles for loss.
He went undrafted and landed in Motown for his first NFL training camp. Unfortunately, he suffered an undisclosed injury and was waived in the middle of August with an injury settlement.
Lions team reporter Tim Twentyman expressed excitement about observing the 6'3, 320-pound defensive lineman during training camp, prior to his injury and subsequent release.
"One player I'm looking forward to watching a little closer once the pads come on Monday is rookie defensive lineman Aidan Keanaaina out of California," Twentyman wrote. "He's had some nice interior rushes early in camp and has worked his way into some second-team reps. Detroit's looking for depth and playmakers along the interior, especially at nose tackle. He had 101 tackles his last two years at Cal in that role. That's a lot of tackle production from the position."

title: Here’s Everything Josh Jacobs Said About Return to Packers, Re-Evaluating Life
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – For the first time since the Memorial Day Weekend incident that led to missing the first six games of the season, Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs talked to reporters about the arrest, punishment and return to the team he had captained the previous two seasons.
“Obviously, you never want to be in this situation, but just me being honest, for my life, it was probably one of the best things to ever happen to me,” Jacobs said outside the locker room at Lambeau Field on Wednesday afternoon.
“I say that because it gave me a chance to sit down and re-evaluate what’s important and what I want my life to look like, and what do I want people to know me for. When they think of me, what are they going to say? Another thing that it showed me was the people that were in my corner. A lot of people I didn’t even know or even expect to be in my corner, they showed up. So that was huge for me. It just gave me more appreciation, more love honestly for this organization and this team.”
It was his most powerful statement of the day. Since the NFL is continuing to investigate, Jacobs was limited in what he could say. So, there was no explanation of what happened on May 23.
But he expressed remorse for putting the team through the ordeal, gratitude for the team for standing by him and an eagerness to return to the football field.
Throughout the 9-plus minutes with reporters, he spoke nervously. His lips quivered at times and he frequently rubbed his chest.
Here are the highlights of what he said.
Jacobs did not speak from notes or read a statement. Instead, he spoke for 1 minute, 23 seconds to open the conversation.
“First, I’m excited to be back with the team, with the guys. I want to say thank you to the organization, really, for supporting me throughout this whole process and how everything played out. With that being said, I can’t get into a lot of things like specifics of things but, obviously, man, I’m remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation.
“Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a 4-second, 3-second decision can alter your life, honestly. But with that being said, still a human being, man, still trying to learn, still trying to grow from the whole process. Actually learned a lot throughout this process legally and just personally. But going forward, man, I just try to be better.
“I know for some people this might be a stain on me and my character. I feel like I don’t have to really speak on my character. A lot of people that know me in this locker room or that’s been around me, I’ll let them do that. But for me, man, I’m just trying to come back in here and play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward.”
Jacobs said he wasn’t “overly concerned” about his career being over because “in my heart, I know what happened and what didn’t happen.”
Jacobs spent the first six games of the season on the exempt list, meaning he could not practice or play with the team but could attend meetings and workout.
“I think six games was a lot, honestly, but that’s not really up to me to decide,” he said. “I’m grateful to be playing, so that’s not even something that I’m like arguing or petitioning with. I’m just happy to be back on the team.”
The NFL is continuing its investigation. A suspension is the expectation; the question is whether it will sideline him for more games.
“Honestly, I thought it would be sooner,” he said. “I thought it’d be sooner. I thought I’d be playing sooner. But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I’m just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn’t want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I’m just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing.”
Josh Jacobs on the possibility of not playing again. pic.twitter.com/ErkJELwnNt
Jacobs was arrested over Memorial Day Weekend and addressed the team shortly thereafter.
“I was just apologizing to the guys because I know a lot of guys look up to me, a lot of guys come to me about real-life issues and things that go on in their lives. And so for me, being that guy for a lot of people, it’s weird when you take that fall. For me, it’s just trying to show everybody like, you know, I’m not better than the next person. I still deal with my own personal things.
“But, at the end of the day, just know that I’m still be here, I’m still show up and I’m still be the same guy. But really the main story was for me, when we had that meeting, was me being apologetic for the attention that it’s brought to this team having the guys have to answer or watch what they say when it comes to that, so that’s just something I had to take accountability for.”
For Jacobs, his focus has been on the team – the players, coaches and front office – and not about winning over fans who turned on him following whatever happened almost five months ago, which concluded legally with him pleading no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property.
“No, I don’t think I had to earn respect back from the guys because I’m the same person every day. Like I said, at the end of the day, we human. We all make mistakes. It’s just different for me because I’m in the public eye.
“Like I said, I’ll let other people speak to my character and who I am and who I consistently have been. When it comes to earning the respect for the fans, I mean, for me, it’s more of a thing of not trying to put this organization in a position where it looks negative in any type of way. At the end of the day, people are always going to have they opinion. People are going to believe what they believe, and it’s not really my job to try to explain or discount certain things. All I can try to do is control what I can control and move on from there.”
Later, he made the same point about the fans, who have formed their opinion based on the facts made public and are unlikely to be persuaded one way or the other.
“I’m not trying to win nobody back, and that’s just me being all the way honest because, at the end of the day, like I said, I know what happened and if you feel some type of way – obviously, I feel bad because it’s still a situation occurred and it should’ve never even happened, so that’s something that I still will understand if people feel some type of way about it.
“But, like I said, all I can do is keep showing up and being who I am, being a leader for this team, being a leader in this community and that’s really all I can control.”
Jacobs will practice this week before a determination is made about his availability for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions. While he hasn’t been practicing with the team, he’s been in meetings and has been working out.
“I’ve been actually practicing with my helmet and shoulder pads, so it’s not like it’s like overly different,” he said. “But just trying to get back to the flow of the guys, simple stuff like being in the huddle, listening to the play call and going out there and executing within that 5-second, 6-second span.
“And also just getting back in the flow of the guys. We’ve got guys even up front that I’ve never played with. That’s another thing. But we’re going to see how it goes. I don’t know where we’re going to be at this week, or if I’m actually going to play or not. All I’m trying to do is get prepared to play if they let me.”
Jacobs isn’t sure if he’ll play, but that’s his goal.
“If it’s up to me,” he said, “I’m going to play.”

title: Packers-Lions Wednesday Injury Report: Here’s What Jordan Love Said About Sore Back
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Jordan Love has taken a beating at times this season. For the first time, it’s shown on the injury report.
The Green Bay Packers’ star quarterback, who has carried the load for most of the team’s 4-2 start, was deemed limited participation on Wednesday, the first day of on-the-field work before Sunday’s NFC North showdown at the Detroit Lions.
He said “no” when asked if he was concerned that he will not be in the lineup against Detroit.
Coming off a Sunday night game and with a Thursday night game looming against the Panthers, coach Matt LaFleur conducted a “jog-through” practice on Wednesday but will put the team in pads for a “really good” practice on Thursday.
That was welcome news for Love. After two games of strong pass protection in wins over Tampa Bay and Chicago, it was another painful week for Love in the win over Dallas.
“It’s just dealing with a sore back from the game,” he said. “Just some lingering effects from that. One of those things, we’ll just take it day by day but, obviously, it was nice to have a jog-through day, a little bit more mental day, and just recover.”
By the official stats, Love and Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson have absorbed a league-high 45 hits through Week 6.
He was hit eight times and sacked on three against the Cowboys.
“Obviously, just with the back, I don’t know exactly what play it happened on, when it happened,” Love said. “We talk about all the time: You want to, obviously, limit me taking hits in the pocket. That’s something that we’ve talked about, we harp on, and there’s been some better efforts to do better and protect better. I think guys are responding to that. It’s one of those things, yeah, you want to be able to limit as many hits as I take.”
Only one player, receiver Bo Melton (back), would not have practiced. Nine players were limited, including Love and receivers Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Christian Watson (ankle).
Running back Josh Jacobs, who is returning after six weeks on the exempt list, is not on the injury report.
“I’ve been actually practicing with my helmet and shoulder pads, so it’s not like it’s overly different,” Jacobs said. “I don’t know where we’re going to be at this week, or if I’m actually going to play or not. All I’m trying to do is get prepared to play if they let me.”
Fortunately for the Packers, while they have a long injury report, just about everyone practiced, which will help the team get ready for the deafening environment at Ford Field.
“It pretty much is you try to simulate that crowd noise as best as possible but that place is usually rocking pretty good and it’s hard to [communicate],” LaFleur said. “Good thing is we’ve had a couple road games where we’ve had to deal with that. So, you get some practice with that. That’s something that we train all offseason. We have days where we go on the silent count and all that. So, I think our guys will be ready for it.”
The Lions are coming off their bye. Every player on the roster practiced, including safety Brian Branch, who is set to return from last year’s torn Achilles.
“Here's what's great about getting BB back,” Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters. “BB gives you the flexibility – is what do you want to do with anybody else? Because there are things you're going to want to do with BB high, let him play top-down, and then there are things you want him to play underneath. And that doesn't require somebody else playing off of him necessarily. He'll make it right.“

Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows.

title: Jordan Love Getting Crushed by Drops; Why Aren’t Packers Crushing Panic Button?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers are dropping the ball on what should be a blockbuster season for quarterback Jordan Love.
With Week 7 of the NFL season on the horizon, Love has been victimized by a league-high 19 dropped passes, according to Pro Football Focus. No other quarterback has had more than 11 passes dropped. The six quarterbacks who’ve played for the other NFC North teams have had 15 passes dropped.
According to Next Gen Stats, which has counted 18 drops, Love is second in passing yards lost due to drops.
Most pass yards lost due to drops this season, per @NextGenStats : 1. Drake Maye – 161 2. Jordan Love – 158 3. Justin Herbert – 127 4. Trevor Lawrence – 111 5. Aaron Rodgers - 106 6. Joe Burrow - 103 7. Bo Nix - 101 8. Geno Smith - 100
New England’s Drake Maye has lost 161 yards with Love next at 158. Those are air yards only and don’t include potential yards after the catch.
Love enters Sunday’s game at the Lions ranked third in the league with 1,684 passing yards, behind only the Rams’ Matthew Stafford (1,794) and the Texans’ C.J. Stroud (1,714). If you add the drop yardage to Love’s tally, he would lead the league with 1,842 passing yards.
Using the numbers from Fantasy Points Data and understanding that drops sometimes are in the eyes of the beholder, Love has been plagued by a drop rate of 8.0 percent, which is the fourth-highest among quarterbacks who’ve thrown more than 50 passes. New England’s Drake Maybe has lost 206 yards to drops with Love fifth with 128.
According to Pro Football Focus, Love has had a league-worst 12.2 percent of his passes dropped; Tampa Bay’s Baker Mayfield (10.3. percent) is the only other player at more than 9.2 percent.
“What do you want us to do to address the drops?” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday. “It happens. It’s football. It happens. As long as guys are using the right mechanics and attacking the football, they happen.”
Among the 32-or-so quarterbacks with at least 275 dropbacks in a season during his tenure as the starter, Love was 18th in drop percentage in 2025 (5.8 percent), fifth in 2024 (8.2 percent) and 19th in 2023 (6.1 percent).
Using the numbers at Stathead, 46 quarterbacks have thrown at least 400 passes since Love took over as the starter, He has been victimized by the third-highest drop percentage, 6.0. Only Patrick Mahomes (98) has had more passes dropped than Love (96).
So, while Green Bay’s receivers have never been particularly sure-handed, this season is at a whole other level on a butterfingers scale. According to PFF, he had 24 passes dropped in 2023, 24 passes dropped in 2024 and 18 passes dropped in 2025. With 19 this season, he’s on pace for 54.
“The one thing is you’ve just got to trust yourself,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday. “Things like this happen. There’s been other guys – (Dontayvion) Wicks a couple years ago sticks out where he had the case of some drops. But the one thing is you’ve got to work hard, keep working on the JUGS, keep catching ball and just trust your hands and trust yourself, and he’ll keep making those spectacular plays.”
According to PFF, Matthew Golden leads the NFL with seven dropped passes. Of the 68 receivers have been targeted at least 20 times, Golden has the second-highest drop rate at 18.9 percent; former Packers receiver Romeo Doubs is first at 22.2 percent. Christian Watson, who has three drops, is tied for 15th at 9.4 percent.
At tight end, 27 players have been targeted at least 20 times. Tucker Kraft has the third-highest drop rate at 10.7 percent. He’s dropped three passes; Baltimore’s Mark Andrews leads in both categories with four drops and a 14.8 percent drop rate.
Green Bay’s backs have combined for four drops: two for MarShawn Lloyd (16.7 percent), one for Chris Brooks (25.0 percent) and one for Pierre Strong (11.1 percent).
Golden’s drops are dumbfounding. He caught everything in sight during his two training camps but has been plagued by big ones this season.
“No, no, I’m not concerned, just because I know the type of player that he is,” Stenavich said. “Again, just one of those things that you can’t lose trust in yourself. You got here for a reason. You are the player who you are for a reason. We all trust him. Jordan trusts him. I know he’s going to make those plays. The ball’s going to keep coming his way, so it’s just one of those things. You just got to work through it, trust yourself and keep your confidence.”
Love had five passes dropped last week against Dallas, according to PFF. Fantasy Data Points had Love losing 60 passing yards.
Love took it in stride as much as possible. Among 33 quarterbacks who’ve dropped back 100 times, Love is 28th in completion percentage. With drops turned into completions, he’s still only 28th. But it’s the big plays such as touchdowns that must be rectified before they cost the team in big moments in big games.
“It’s tough,” Love said after the game. “It’s football. I want to see us make every play. I want to make every throw. I want these guys to make every catch. That’s the expectation. Stuff happens. Drops happen.
“Obviously, I want those guys to make those plays, and we’re capable of making those plays. But for me, it’s got to be the next play mindset. You’ve got to move on. You’ve got to try and fight back and continue to make good plays. Yeah, it sucks and is something we’ve got to continue to get better at.”
Added together, the Packers somehow are 4-2 with a three-game winning streak with inconsistent pass protection, a penchant for penalties and far too many drops.
From his perspective, LaFleur understands that his receivers have missed too many opportunities. He also believes his players are doing things the right way, so there’s no sense of panic.
“Do we want them to happen? No,” LaFleur said. “If they’re using poor fundamentals, letting the ball get in their body, letting the ball cross their eyes, then, yeah, you work on that stuff. But it’s the same stuff we do every day. We go out there and we hammer fundamentals. Sometimes we make plays and sometimes we don’t. But I think that’s everybody in the league.
“I have a lot of confidence in our guys that when called upon, they’re going to make the plays. If they drop the ball, you know what I want them to do? I want them to reset and go play the next play.”

title: Packers Have Roughing-the-Passer Problem And It Goes Back Years
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – According to NFL Penalties , the league average for roughing-the-passer penalties this season is 1.38 per team. The Green Bay Packers have been guilty of a league-high six.
Meanwhile, eight teams have not had their quarterback on the receiving end of a roughing-the-passer penalty. The Packers are one of those teams.
Added together, the Packers are down 6-0 on roughing penalties. No other team is worse than minus-3 in net roughing calls. Either the Packers’ defense is filled with a bunch of cheap-shotting jerks or their opponents are leading with their halos rather than the crown of their helmets when they hit Jordan Love.
After Sunday night’s victory over the Dallas Cowboys, when the Packers were guilty of three roughing-the-passer penalties, coach Matt LaFleur said he left Lambeau Field “a lot later” than he wanted. Part of burning the midnight oil was looking at the infractions.
“I think just in regards to all that stuff, at the end of the day, you just want it to be called both ways,” LaFleur said. “So, if they’re going to call it one way, it should be called for the other team, as well, and I feel like there’s been a lot of times when Jordan’s taken some close to potential roughing calls, and he’s not getting the calls.”
It was quite the diplomatic choice of words by LaFleur as he walked the fine line of trying to make a point while not trying to lighten his wallet.
“I think (Love) needs to be more of an a-hole to the officials and lobby for some of those calls,” LaFleur said, somewhat lightheartedly. “You see some guys do it, and it works.”
But what about LaFleur? NBA coaches are famous for working the referees, especially during a playoff series, when a perceived lack of calls in one game is harped on after and between games in hopes of getting the calls the next game.
“You saying I’m not working them good enough?” LaFleur said to that example.
Only LaFleur would know how much he lobbies the officials during the game or the league during the week. With a contract extension, he probably can afford the fine for criticizing the officials for letting Love get blasted after the throw.
“I’m going to tell them next week, I’ll say, ‘Bill Huber told me that I need to get on you guys.’”
All joking aside, it’s wild that the Packers have been flagged six times compared to zero for their opponents. The Packers have been flagged for some legit fouls. Others, such as Lukas Van Ness’ two-handed shove of Dak Prescott, looked incredibly weak – even for this era of protecting the passer at all costs.
“We can only control our actions out there, and there were a couple hits like you cannot go high on a quarterback,” LaFleur said. “You’ve got to make sure that you’re going in the strike zone and then, obviously, if you do have him wrapped up, you’ve got to make sure you don’t land on him with your body weight.”
LaFleur said opinion among the coaches was split on Karl Brooks’ body-weight foul on Prescott, though he seemed to agree that was the right call.
“As far as some of those other calls,” he continued, “I thought Van Ness’ wasn’t. You get a step before you have to hit the quarterback, and I didn’t think it was a forceful hit to the quarterback.”
Part of the weekly postmortem is sending in clips to the league to question or gain clarity on penalties that were called or not called. Shots on the quarterback probably have been a theme.
“We’ll see what they say,” LaFleur said. “And then I obviously can’t tell you guys about what they say, but it helps us educate our players and at the end of the day that’s our job. We got to educate them on what they can and cannot do and make sure that we try to coach them up and they got to control themselves in the moment.”
No team has reached double-digits for roughing penalties since the Jets were flagged 14 times in 2020. The Packers, who have been guilty of 14 percent of the league total through six games, are well on their way.
“We can’t foul,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said, choosing to stay out of the public fray. “I always say, like it’s continuing to educate, continuing to talk technique and then decision-making. We got to make sure that we’re making correct decisions in real time, which I know is not easy to do, but good defenses don’t beat themselves.”
Using data from Sumer Sports, the Packers were flagged only once for roughing while opponents were penalized four times, so Green Bay was plus-3. In both 2023 and 2024, Green Bay was flagged three times and its opponents once.
That means during the three-plus seasons with Love at the controls, officials have called six roughing penalties against Green Bay’s opponents. The Cowboys’ opponents have been flagged 20 times during that span, three more than any other team. The Bills have been the second-largest beneficiary with 17.
The Chargers’ opponents have been flagged six times this season alone.
In the NFC North, Green Bay’s division rivals have been flagged for roughing one time apiece this season.
Due largely to this year’s 6-0 disparity, the Packers are minus-7 on roughing calls during the Love era. Only the Eagles at minus-8 have seen more lopsided officiating. For Green Bay during that span, only four teams have been flagged more for roughing the passer and only two teams (the Rams and Texans) have benefited from fewer roughing penalties.
Dallas is a staggering plus-13. Buffalo (plus-11) and Cleveland (plus-10) are the only teams that are double-digits positive.

title: Packers-Lions Matchups: Just One Advantage, But It’s Huge
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers have won three games in a row. As fictional manager Lou Brown from Major League II once said, that’s called a winning streak.
Can the Packers extend their streak to four? They will face a big challenge in Detroit against the Lions at 3:25 p.m. Sunday. It will be the first of five consecutive games against teams that would qualify for the playoffs if the season were to end today.
The Packers swept the Lions last season, including a 31-24 in Detroit on Thanksgiving. The teams are different now. Some key players are back. Others are on the shelf due to injuries. The Lions are coming off their bye week, while the Packers played Dallas on Sunday night.
While the Lions have the rest advantage, who has the advantage on the field? We go through that in our weekly matchups.
The talking point last week was that the Packers were playing well on defense but that they had not faced a real quarterback.
Now they have, and the Packers beat up Dak Prescott on Sunday night. This week? They’ll face another high-powered offense with a quarterback who has been mostly flawless this season.
Jared Goff does not get the league-wide respect that he deserves, but he’s been nothing short of excellent since coming to Detroit.
This year has been no different. He has completed 67 percent of his passes. His passer rating is 111.3. He’s thrown 12 touchdown passes and has yet to be picked off.
Perhaps Detroit’s offense was summed up best by Green Bay defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon.
“They’ve scored 30 any time they’ve touched the grass,” Gannon said on Tuesday .
Four out of five games but, with a second-ranked 32.8 points per game, close enough. Detroit’s offense is dangerous. They’re loaded with weapons. Receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams and tight end Sam LaPorta can all hurt the defense in different ways.
Last week, the Packers handled their matchup against George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb well. This group is deeper, and more dangerous.
The key to slowing down the Lions is pressuring Goff. The Packers beat him up last year at Lambeau Field and held the Lions to 13 points.
Can the Packers get enough pressure? Will Gannon have another masterclass up his sleeve?
As good as Green Bay’s defense has played early in the season, this matchup is closer than you would think at first glance.
Jonathan Gannon was asked what makes Jahmyr Gibbs, Jahmyr Gibbs. He sighed, before saying, “Woah.”
Gibbs is the fastest player on the field every week that he steps on it. He’s a dominant force in a Detroit ground game that remains its identity even with the loss of some of the personnel that made it such a powerful unit in 2024.
Green Bay’s run defense has truly only struggled once this season. The problem? That came against the Falcons, who employ a back with a similar running style to that of Gibbs. There’s an argument to be made that Gibbs is a better running back than Bijan Robinson, but it’s those two at the top of the league with everyone else fighting for a seat at the table.
Either way, Gibbs makes this group go.
The Packers did a good job against him last year. Gibbs was held to 19 yards on nine carries at Lambeau Field. He added 10 catches for 31 yards. If the Packers can hold him to 50 yards on 19 touches, they’d be thrilled.
In the rematch at Ford Field, Gibbs was more productive, but not up to his usual standard. He touched the ball 20 times for 86 yards. The Packers held him in check, but will be missing both linebackers from those games. Quay Walker is playing in Las Vegas while Edgerrin Cooper is rehabbing a torn Achilles.
Regardless, Gibbs’ excellence and the Packers’ recent history against a back of his caliber gives the nod to Detroit.
The Lions can make things difficult with their pass rush. Their front boasts two really good players in defensive tackle Alim McNeil and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. D.J. Wonnum is sixth in the lead with five sacks. Hutchinson has four and McNeill has 3.5.
Added together, the Lions lead the league in sacks – even while playing one less game than most teams.
So, why does their defense stink?
Once the ball goes in the air, the Lions have had significant problems. Their defensive backfield was in flux before the season even began. Their once elite safety tandem of Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph have missed the entirety of the season with injuries. Following last year’s torn ACL,, Branch is likely to return this week, which should give them a boost.
The cornerback spot has been an issue. D.J. Reed has not worked out as a free agent signing, and they’ve been struggling to find someone to give them consistency. Keith Abney is the only cornerback with an interception.
The Lions are allowing 297.4 passing yards per game. That’s the worst in the NFL this season and on track to be one of the worst in NFL history. The Lions are on track to allow 5,056 passing yards over 17 games. The 2011 Packers allowed the most passing yards of all-time with 4,796 yards over 16 games. That’s 299.8 per game.
They are 29th in opponent passer rating (106.3) and opponent completion percentage (68.1).
That’s good news for the Packers as they come in rolling. Jordan Love’s stats won’t show how well he played on Sunday against the Cowboys, but he was three drops away from throwing four touchdown passes.
Matthew Golden has back-to-back 100-yard receiving games, the first for the Packers since Davante Adams, and is turning into a star. Will the Packers be able to protect Love long enough to exploit a leaky pass defense? That’s the million-dollar question.
With the advantages Green Bay has, especially at quarterback, where Love has thrived almost regardless of the situation, the nod here goes to the visiting team.
Green Bay’s run game stinks. If there was any doubt about that, Sunday’s results against the Cowboys, who were 32nd in the league against the run, should have answered any remaining questions.
As has been the case all season, the Packers were terrible on the ground. Their leading rusher was Pierre Strong. He had 28 yards on 11 carries. Their starting running back was MarShawn Lloyd. He had negative yards rushing at halftime and finished with 10 yards on eight carries.
Their most efficient runner was Savion Williams, and those runs were on plays in which Jordan Love threw the ball behind the line of scrimmage.
They could be getting a boost this week. Josh Jacobs is off the commissioner’s exempt list, and looks to be on track to play this Sunday. How much can he play? He can help, but how much?  Those are questions we don’t know the answers to yet.
Until we know, it’s impossible to give the Packers the edge, against any opponent, let alone one that has been a decent 13th in rushing yards allowed per game and 12th in yards per carry.
From a special teams perspective, the Lions have some stability at kicker and punter. Jake Bates has been perfect on field goals this season and Jack Fox is averaging 47.2 yards per punt.
There is a slight transition in their return game with Tom Kennedy taking over for Kalif Raymond, who joined Ben Johnson in Chicago.
Green Bay’s special teams entered the Dallas game struggling. Trey Smack missed three kicks against Chicago and Skyy Moore is missing from their return game due to a high-ankle sprain that landed him on injured reserve.
Coleman Owen was elevated from the practice squad last week to return punts in Moore’s place while J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton returned kickoffs. Neither did much to stand out, but they protected the football. Matt LaFleur noted that he thought Owen did a nice job returning punts other than calling for a fair catch inside the 10. He will likely be elevated again this week.
Smack shook off some struggles against Chicago with a 5-for-5 night against the Cowboys. This game is in a dome, which should remove the degree of difficulty for kickers to some degree. Having said that, two of the worst games of Mason Crosby’s career came at Ford Field.

title: Coordinators Detail Huge Challenge Packers Will Face at Lions
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have gotten their season back on track. They will take a three-game winning streak into Sunday’s game at the Detroit Lions.
It will be one of their biggest tests of the season.
The Lions, who were the back-to-back NFC North champions in 2023 and 2024, are 3-2. They are 2-0 in home games this season and 20-7 at Ford Field dating to the start of the 2023 campaign. They are coming off their bye week, giving them a tremendous scheduling advantage . Home teams coming out of a bye are 53-34 since the start of the 2021 season.
And then, there’s the talent. The Lions have as much top-end talent as any team in the league. Especially on offense.
Here’s a closer look through the words of Green Bay’s three coordinators.
A week after Jonathan Gannon’s defense shut down the high-powered Cowboys on Sunday night, his unit will face an even bigger challenge against the Lions. Like Dallas, the Cowboys have a great quarterback (Jared Goff), great receivers (Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams), an impact tight end (Sam LaPorta) and a strong offensive line.
Unlike the Cowboys, the Lions have a cream-of-the-crop running back in Jahmyr Gibbs.
“Woo,” Gannon said when asked about Gibbs.
“He’s faster than everybody,” Gannon said. Plus, he can cut – especially at Ford Field – and he’s got “really good contact balance” and he “breaks a lot of tackles.”
Gibbs trails only the Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker with 149.4 scrimmage yards per game. He has three games of more than 160 total yards and he’s scored in every game.
As usual, Goff ranks among the league leaders in passer rating. He’s second at 111.3 on the strength of 12 touchdowns, zero interceptions and 67.0 percent accuracy.
Even while playing one fewer game than most players, St. Brown is seventh with 37 receptions and tied for third with five touchdowns. Williams has elite speed, making him a game-breaking threat.
Detroit’s offensive coordinator is Drew Petzing, who was Arizona’s coordinator under Gannon the previous three seasons.
“There's no tendencies,” Gannon said. “He's creative as all get out. He uses his playmakers in a way to showcase their talents. The quarterback does an excellent job of getting them in the right place to put you as a defense at a disadvantage. When you want to be aggressive, he burns you. When you want to be safe, he burns you.”
A calling card of Gannon’s defense has been its swarming play style. The Lions will match their intensity.
“They play hard,” Gannon continued. “They are tough, they play hard, they’re physical. That comes from the head coach and then the coordinator and then the position coaches. Hank Fraley, their O-line coach/run-game coordinator, this O-line is souped up now. They’ve got good players, they collectively play well together, they communicate, they never bust, their protection scheme is on point. And then they can run it to win and they can throw it to win.”
When Gannon said the Lions have scored 30 points “every time they’ve touched the grass,” he is only slightly wrong. They scored at least 31 points in four games (and 26 in the other).
They enter Week 7 ranked fourth in total offense and second in scoring, even though they are a woeful 22nd on third down.
On the other hand, Detroit’s defense is horrendous. It ranks 30th in points allowed per game, just 0.1 points per game better than the Cardinals and Saints. They are last in total defense and passing defense, and 30th or worse in third down, fourth down, red zone and goal-to-go.
However, they do rush the passer with D.J. Wonnum (five sacks) and superstar Aidan Hutchinson (four). Detroit’s front will challenge Green Bay’s biggest weakness, which has been its offensive line.
Plus, star Lions safety Brian Branch is expected to make his season debut following last year’s torn Achilles.
Embattled Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard remains on the job. He will have had the bye week to find some answers.
“The one thing about these guys is we’ve got to be ready for everything,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. “They bring a lot of different fronts. They bring a lot of different pressures. I think their D-line is really good. Obviously, Hutchinson and [defensive tackle Alim] McNeill are excellent players, Wonnum’s got a lot of sacks, so they’re playing really well up front. Their linebackers are athletic and aggressive.
“So that’s one thing, their front’s salty so we’ve got to make sure we do a nice job of handling those guys because it’s going to be a tall task for sure.”
Detroit’s is going to make life difficult for a Packers return game that lost its excellent returner, Skyy Moore, to an ankle injury.
Punter Jack Fox ranks ninth with a 43.3-yard net average this season and led the league in 2024.
“He’s very, very talented,” Achord said. “I think he’s got one of the bigger legs in the league, high, high hang times, and that allows the coverage units to get down there. Anytime you’re putting the ball 4.8s, 4.7s up there plus, it allows the gunners outside to factor.”
Plus, their interior players are tough. Added together, the Lions are 11th in punt coverage and seventh in kickoff coverage. They are one of six teams in the top 11 in both categories.
“They’re playing physical, they’re strong,” Achord said. “They do a really good job condensing it and squeezing to the ball. Our guys have to do a good job standing up to their size and physical presence out there.
“So, it’s going to be a great challenge. They are one of the top teams in coverage, in both phases, so I think it’s a really good challenge for our guys, and it’s something we’ll look forward to this week, being able to stand up to those guys.”

title: Consensus NFL Power Rankings for Week 7: Packers’ Astounding Rise Continues
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – After a blowout loss to the Falcons and uninspiring victory over the Buccaneers, the Green Bay Packers fell all the way to 24th in the Packers On SI Consensus NFL Power Rankings.
What a difference two weeks make.
First, what are our Consensus Power Rankings? We take eight sets of national power rankings and turn them into one more-powerful-than-a-locomotive power ranking.
After beating the Bears, the Packers rose to 14th . Now, after a convincing win over the Cowboys on Sunday night, they’ve moved up to 12th.
Here’s a closer look, with more extensive analysis and the full rankings available at the links.
Conor Orr could hardly be more bullish on the Packers as he moved them up eight spots from No. 12.
“With Micah Parsons en route at some point and the defense having posted back-to-back weeks of all-out swarming, the mood has shifted demonstrably in Green Bay,” Orr said. “The Jordan Love MVP conversation will soon round into shape. “
The Packers are up two spots in Mike Florio’s rankings. As he wrote, “They’re getting Josh Jacobs back at a perfect time.”
The Packers are up three spots in ESPN’s rankings , which are selected by its team beat writers.
This week’s theme is the ineffective running game, which is the worst in the league by a wide margin. As noted by Rob Demovsky, “MarShawn Lloyd, who missed most of the past two seasons because of injuries, is finally healthy but has averaged just 1.27 yards after contact -- 42nd among 43 qualified running backs. Kaleb Johnson has Green Bay's longest run of the season at 31 yards, but he has fumbled twice and barely played the past two weeks.”
Pete Prisco inched the Packers up two spots in his rankings.
“We knew the offense will get it going with the explosive passing game,” he wrote, “but it's the improved defense that has turned their season around. That unit will be tested on the road this week against the Lions.”
The Packers moved up one spot by Chad Graff and Josh Kendall in their rankings.
This week’s theme is fantasy football. They chose receiver Matthew Golden, noting: “Golden has been over 20 points in three of the last four games, and since Week 3, he is seventh in the league in receiving yards (348), just 2 shy of teammate Christian Watson. All three of Golden’s career 100-yard games have come in the last month.”
The Packers zoomed up eight spots from No. 22 in Ralph Vacchiano’s rankings.
He noted how coach Matt LaFleur was perhaps on the hot seat after a 1-2 start. Now, they’ve won three in a row.
“Jordan Love and the offense has clicked in that span, and the defense has been excellent, too,” he wrote. “So, why are they ranked this low? Because they barely beat the Bucs, they beat the Bears without Caleb Williams and then beat the reeling Cowboys. They can’t do anything about the schedule, but let’s see how it goes at Detroit, vs. Carolina, at New England and vs. Minnesota in the month leading into their bye week before I put my cheesehead on.”
The Packers moved up four spots in Frank Schwab’s rankings. He mentioned the Packers as one of the teams that are “impossible” to rank or figure out based on their performances during the first four games compared to their last two.
“Then the last two weeks, the Packers blew out the Bears and Cowboys, and are suddenly 4-2 and on a roll,” he said. “Had you just watched the last two games and nothing else, you'd think the Packers might be a top-five team at worst. But the first four weeks did happen too. The Packers still struggle mightily to run the ball and to protect Love, though the QB was masterful against pressure on Sunday night. Green Bay, like many other teams this season, is hard to figure out.”
The Packers gained one spot in Nick Shook’s rankings. The Packers’ defensive success against Chicago wasn’t a fluke, Shook said.
“Green Bay shut down Dallas’ explosive offense, making life miserable for Dak Prescott and Co., while Jordan Love and the offense did enough early to cruise to a victory. There are still kinks to work out offensively (which could be solved quickly if Josh Jacobs can get off to a fast start upon returning), but it’s time to start taking this team seriously.”
The Lions will host the Packers at noon Sunday at Ford Field. They are our 13th ranked team, or just one spot behind Green Bay, with individual rankings ranging from No. 9 at The Athletic to No. 18 at Pro Football Talk.
Sports Illustrated’s Conor Orr has them at No. 11.
“The Packers and Vikings are next on Detroit’s post-bye schedule. We’ll find out immediately if the defense was fixed, has the potential to be fixed, or if Jared Goff is going to continue needing to score 30-plus a week to keep the Lions in the conversation.”
Fox’s Ralph Vacchiano was surprised the Lions didn’t change defensive coordinators during their bye. They are giving up 404.4 yards per game, almost 20 yards worse than any other team. Opponents have eclipsed 440 yards and 30 points in three games.
“It’s a shame, really, because the Lions offense can run up the score on any team in the league, but the defense is going to kill them,” Vacchiano wrote. “Teams rarely last in the NFL when their only hope is to win 41-38 while praying they get the ball last.”
Sportsbook odds aren’t part of our rankings, but they do provide another useful perspective on how teams are viewed. In Packers-related odds at FanDuel Sportsbook :
The Packers, who were +2000 to win the Super Bowl before Week 1, plunged to +6000 after losing to the Falcons and stayed there after beating Tampa Bay and Chicago. Now, they’re +3000, though that still ranks only 15th.
Among NFC North teams, the Bears are +1400 and the Lions and Vikings +2000.
Green Bay opened the season ranked seventh in the NFC playoff odds at -112, fell to as low as 12th at +250 after the win at Tampa Bay, but are back to -118. They rank seventh in the NFC and last among the NFC North teams (Minnesota is -500, Chicago is -230 and Detroit is -188).
Quarterback Jordan Love opened at +2200 to win NFL MVP. He bottomed out at +10000 but is right back in the thick of the race, with his +3300 ranking ninth. Buffalo’s Josh Allen (+175) and San Francisco’s Brock Purdy (+250) are the clear front-runners.
In the NFC North odds at DraftKings, the Packers are still considered the long shots. Minnesota is +105, followed by Detroit and Chicago at +350 and Green Bay at +530.

title: No. 8 Is Coming Back; Eight Reasons Why Josh Jacobs Must Save Run Game
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs will get a “full week of practice” this week and could play at the Detroit Lions on Sunday, coach Matt LaFleur said on Monday.
Goodness knows, they need him.
Jacobs spent the first six games of the season on the exempt list following an off-the-field incident with a female over Memorial Day Weekend. He was removed from the exempt list on Monday but isn’t necessarily in the clear.
While Jacobs hasn’t practiced since the end of training camp, he’s been working out with the training staff and participating in team meetings, so he shouldn’t need a ramp-up like a player coming off a significant injury.
“Well, that’s to be determined,” LaFleur said of Jacobs’ readiness. “We feel like he’s in a pretty good spot. He’s been training, but he’s missed the exposure to football.”
The Packers don’t just need Jacobs. They desperately need him. Just look at the numbers.
Green Bay’s rushing attack is the worst in the NFL by a considerable margin. Here are eight statistics that show the complete ineptitude.
One: The Packers are 32nd in the NFL with 59.8 rushing yards per game and 2.87 yards per carry. They are last in both categories by considerable margins: 16.2 yards per game behind Dallas and 0.14 yards per carry behind the Raiders.
The Chargers in 2000 averaged a record-low 66.4 rushing yards per game.
Two: The Packers’ best rushing day this season was their 86 yards against Tampa Bay in Week 4. There have been 45 individual games of more than 86 rushing yards this season.
The Packers’ best rushing day in terms of efficiency was their 3.5 yards per carry against the Jets in Week 2. That best day would rank 30th in the NFL over the course of the season.
Three: On first-down running plays, the Packers are averaging a worst-in-the-league 2.25 yards per carry. The Raiders are 31st with a 2.81-yard average. A total of 26 teams are averaging at least one more yard per carry. Against Dallas, the Packers’ first-down average plunged to 1.47 yards per carry.
Four: Yards before contact can be an offensive line stat, but it obviously can be swayed by a player’s ability to get through a hole or make someone miss. According to Stathead, the Packers have a league-low 239 yards before contact. Their 1.9-yard average is 31st.
With Jacobs, the Packers were 26th with 2.2 yards before contact per carry in 2025 and 17th with 2.4 yards before contact per carry in 2024.
Five: Yards after contact is almost totally a running back stat, though speed through a hole and getting to the second level with the offensive line matters. The Packers are last with 120 yards after contact and 31st with 1.0 yards after contract per carry, according to Stathead.
With Jacobs, the Packers were 13th with 1.9 yards after contact per carry in 2025 and third with 2.4 yards after contact per carry in 2024.
Six: Green Bay’s rushing success this season is 34.3 percent, which ranks 30th. A “successful” play gains at least 40 percent of the required yards on first down (a 4-yard run on first-and-10 would be a success), 60 percent of the required yards on second down and 100 percent of the required yards on third and fourth down. Jacobs had individual success rates of 52.2 percent in 2024 and 49.1 percent in 2025.
Seven: A “stuff” is a run that gains 0 yards or worse. The Packers are 31st in stuff percentage, with a drive-killing 29.0 percent of their runs failing to gain yardage. With Jacobs, the Packers ranked second in stuff percentage in 2024 (17.6) and 12th in 2025 (19.3).
Eight: MarShawn Lloyd leads the Packers with 122 rushing yards. That’s a 17-game pace of 346 yards. That projected total would rank 16th in the league through Week 6.
Lloyd is averaging 2.54 yards per carry. It would require him to carry the ball 394 times to reach 1,000 yards. That would be the seventh-most rushing attempts in NFL history.
So, Jacobs could be a season-changing addition. The Packers have won three games in a row with no running game whatsoever.
“Well, I think he’s an elite-level back,” LaFleur said. “He’s certainly not going to hurt it. I think he can provide a spark.”
Is it the backs? Is it the blocking? LaFleur deflected the blame when asked about the running game on Monday, instead choosing to credit the Cowboys, who had the worst run defense in the NFL entering Week 6 but were coming off their mini-bye.
“I think there were some moments where it was good and then there were some moments where it wasn’t as good,” he said. “And then there were some moments where, quite frankly, the concepts had no chance based on different front structures they were presenting to us.
“They did a good job. I think any time that you go into a game and the opposition has a little longer to prepare for that, I think there’s some unscouted looks that can come up. Certainly, they caught us in a couple of those looks, where we didn’t have good plays for what they were showing.”
The Packers will play at the Lions on Sunday. They rank 20th in rushing yards allowed per attempt and 15th in rushing yards allowed per game. Then, they’ll host the Panthers, who are last in the league in yards allowed per attempt. Back-to-back games against the Patriots and Vikings, who boast top-10 run defenses, will follow.
Jacobs, even if it’s turning runs blocked for 1 yard into gains of 3 yards, could be a season-changing addition, perhaps as soon as Sunday.
“Yeah, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Jacobs can hit the ground running. “I think that’s possible but we’ve got to go through the week and see where he’s at.”
