title: New Packers Defensive Tackle Will Have Micah Parsons’ Seal of Approval
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – There might be nobody happier about the Green Bay Packers’ decision to sign Mazi Smith to the practice squad on Monday than his former-turned-current teammate, Micah Parsons.
As reported by ESPN.com’s Rob Demovsky , the Packers signed Smith to the practice squad following a Monday workout.
“Let’s go!” Parsons screamed when the Cowboys drafted Smith in the first round in 2023.
Parsons with the Packers has been the hype man for Lukas Van Ness, among others. He was the same way with Smith during their time together. More on that in a moment.
“NO MORE QB SNEAKS AJ!” @MicahhParsons11 told Cowboys DC Dan Quinn to pick Michigan's Mazi Smith earlier today and IT HAPPENED 😂 pic.twitter.com/nGm62CAnDK
Smith was a bust for the Cowboys and represents a Hail Mary of sorts for the Packers on a talented player who could fill a need. The Packers have been hammered by injuries at defensive tackle, with Warren Brinson, Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford on injured reserve. They beat the Cowboys with only four defensive tackles on the active roster. Plus, they have only one player on the practice squad, undrafted rookie David Blay Jr.
So, maybe the Packers will catch lightning in a bottle with Smith, who was the 26th pick of the 2023 draft.
"It's like Christmas," then-Cowboys coach Mike McCarthy said after Smith was selected. “When you look at all the work that goes into it, going back to his 30 visit, and just what a great fit he is for us … I just want him to be himself. He is a great fit for us.”
During the predraft process, Smith gained a big supporter in Parsons. He even texted his defensive coordinator at the time, Dan Quinn, hoping the Cowboys would draft Smith.
“It’s not what I think he can be, it’s what Mazi has to be,” Parsons said at the start of training camp in 2024 . “When you get to this business, there is no more of a choice or a can, it’s either you will or you won’t. They usually try to find someone else to do it if you can’t. It’s what Mazi has to be. He has to be dominant. He has to be a force. He has to be that guy for us.
“That’s why they drafted him in the first round. You’re not getting drafted in the first round not to be a productive talent, not to be on the sidelines. We drafted him to be in the game and that’s how much confidence you have (to have). I don’t expect Mazi to do anything. It’s what Mazi has to do at this point.
“That’s why I’m in his corner, I’m rooting for him and hoping to get him better every day. Pushing his conditioning, pushing his limits, because we need Mazi to be strong. We need Mazi to be that great force. He can be a dominant player, it’s just a will and mindset. That’s why we’re all here.”
Responded Smith : “I don’t really set goals. Everybody want to be an All-Pro, everybody wants to be a top five. I want to be the best me I can be and I know what that can get me. It’s got to this point so, I ain’t worried about accolades or that type.”
Smith played in 17 games with three starts as a rookie and started all 17 games in 2024, when he set career highs with 41 tackles and four tackles for losses.
“You can see it in his face that he loves ball, he loves everything about it,” Cowboys executive vice president and director of player personnel Stephen Jones said. “All the coaches that met with him agree that he'd be a great fit in this organization, and for him to fall down there to us and for us to have the opportunity to pick him, I feel like Mike. I feel like it's Christmas."
Last year, the Cowboys traded him to the Jets in the midseason blockbuster for Quinnen Williams, so he played in a total of eight games between the teams. He failed to make the Jets’ roster in training camp this year and signed to the Dolphins’ practice squad. He played in one game with Miami and was released last week.
Added together, Smith is in his fourth season. He’s played in 43 games with 20 starts. He has 57 tackles, including two sacks and seven for losses.
“I'm excited to get pointed in the right direction," he said after he was drafted, a quote that perhaps fits today. “To climb this big ole' mountain, they'll tell me where to start. I'm excited to get into the heavy duty [part] of things. I'm ready to put this work in and feel what my first offensive lineman feels like in the NFL.”
The native of Grand Rapids, Mich., was a consensus first-team all-Big Ten selection at Michigan in 2022, when he was the Wolverines’ defensive player of the year with 48 tackles in 14 games.
He was the No. 1 player on Bruce Feldman’s prestigious Freaks List before the 2022 season. He measured 6-foot-3 and 323 pounds at the 2023 Scouting Combine. He skipped most of the testing but put up 34 reps on the 225-pound bench press.
“A dog. A big dog, you know what I’m saying, he said after he was drafted. “A big fella; a big, physical guy. I’ve never been afraid of contact. I’ve never been afraid to ball. A guy that’s going to get in somebody’s face. A guy that isn’t going to make it easy.”
He used that size in college to be a premier run-stopping tackle.
“Man, I’m like 325 pounds. I’ve got real power in my hands. I’ve been strong my whole life. I came out of the womb looking like I did pushups. I was doing pushups in there, so I’ve just been strong my whole life. I’ve figured out how to use it on the field, figured out the right techniques, figured out the right stance to get into and just started striking blocks and making sure they went backwards.”
Parsons hoped that would improve Dallas’ run defense. It did not, but maybe that from-the-womb strength will be an asset with Parsons in Green Bay.
“You got to give him attention,” Parsons said after the 2023 draft . “He’s going to push guys back. He’s powerful. He’s strong. He’s going to get under people’s pads. And he’s great in the run and we’re going to develop him in the pass.”

title: Three Overreactions After Packers Beat Cowboys: Collapse Like House of Cards?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – A win is a win. The Green Bay Packers earned a big one against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. It was a surprisingly easy victory considering the number of self-inflicted wounds that prevented the Packers from winning by30.
Here are this week’s Overreactions
If ever there were a chance for Green Bay’s slumbering running game to at least crack open its eyes, yawn, stretch and shift positions, it was this game.
On offense, the Packers entered the game ranked last in the NFL with 60.4 rushing yards per game – almost 20 yards worse than any other team – and next-to-last with 3.05 yards per carry. On defense, the Cowboys entered the game ranked last with 168.4 rushing yards allowed per game and 29th with 5.10 yards allowed per carry.
Instead, the Cowboys looked like the Tom Landra-era Doomsday Defense and the Packers looked, well, exactly like they have all season.
The Packers ran the ball 26 times for 57 yards. Even with Jordan Love’s 13-yard run putting some cologne on a swine, they averaged 2.2 yards per carry. The 20 handoffs to running backs generated 36 yards, or 1.8 yards per carry.
The offensive line didn’t provide many openings. When there was a crack of daylight, the backs acted as if they were blindfolded in a cave trying to find a lost black sock.
The Packers’ run game almost impossibly went from worst to more worst – the intentional butchering of the English language a perfect fit for the butchering of the building block of offensive football. Green Bay is down to 59.8 rushing yards per game (Dallas is next with 76.0) and 2.87 yards per carry (Las Vegas is next with 3.03).
The 2000 Chargers set the dubious NFL record with 66.4 rushing yards per game. Over the past 70 seasons, only the 1994 Patriots’ 2.79 average was worse.
The Packers have 359 rushing yards in six games. Thirteen individuals have more rushing yards.
“Certainly, there’s some stuff that we can clean up where we’re maybe not winning a block or whatever it is, or we miss a cut,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “But we got to keep hammering it because it is critical in today’s football to be able to run the football at a decent level.”
A “decent level.” What a damning statement. Not a top-10 level. Not a winning level. The Packers, who are so far down the rankings that they have to reach up to touch bottom, would settle for decent.
A decent running game would open a world of possibilities. Against Chicago last week, Love in the play-action game was 12-of-14 passing for 245 yards and one touchdown. Against Dallas, those play-action fakes elicited giggles, with Love going 1-of-6 for 7 yards and getting pressured four times.
Maybe the vision and power of Josh Jacobs will be the salvation. If nothing else, he’ll fight for a gain of 3 yards rather than running sideways for a loss of 3.
MarShawn Lloyd think he's got 4.30 speed and he's going against some West Coast college's defense. He does not have 4.30 speed and this is not a college defense. pic.twitter.com/hOrNm6DC8Z
“I think that definitely hurts a little bit, especially when we’re trying to sell run action and they’re just sitting there waiting for you to do the passes off of it,” LaFleur said. “You’ve got to get the run game going.”
The Cowboys showed the rest of the league how to beat the Packers. Blow off the play-action game and attack the quarterback. The Packers had better figure it out fast, or the offense will fall like a house off cards.
The big reason why I predicted the Packers would finish 8-9 is that I didn’t think they had a snowball’s chance in a broiler to earn a win or two against the likes of the Bears, Cowboys and Lions without Micah Parsons.
The Packers beat the Bears, but they didn’t have Caleb Williams at quarterback. So, whatever. The game against Dallas would be an infinitely more difficult challenge. Dak Prescott is an elite quarterback. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens might be the best receiver duo in the NFL. Jake Ferguson is a quality tight end and Javonte Williams is a quality running back.
Without Parsons to protect the secondary, how on earth would the Packers be able to beat teams with real quarterbacks?
That, to me, was the season-defining question. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon delivered an emphatic answer on Sunday.
It’s a shame a phantom roughing-the-passer penalty on Lukas Van Ness led to the Packers giving up a meaningless touchdown in the final minute, because they entered the final drive having given up seven points and less than 200 yards. It was a defensive masterpiece for a team that entered the season with suspect cornerback and a suspect pass rush.
Green Bay’s cornerbacks helped limit Lamb and Pickens to a combined 4.9 yards per target. The traditional four-man rush was feeble, but Gannon created enough of a pass rush to make Prescott uneasy. The confusion created by Gannon led to two more interceptions.
“I was really happy just overall with our whole defensive performance, especially against that offense,” LaFleur said. “If you told me going into this game that you’re going to score 23 points, I was like, ‘Ah, we need to score 30-plus.’”
As it turns out, the 17 points in the first half were more than enough.
Through six games, LaFleur’s hiring of Gannon looks genius. The problem with hiring a good coordinator is he eventually becomes a head coach, as was the case with Jeff Hafley. Gannon bombed in his three-year run of coach of the Cardinals, but any team needing a coach at the end of this season should be smart enough to acknowledge that his tenure was torpedoed by the lack of a quarterback.
“I definitely think he’s doing a good job mixing it up,” said safety Xavier McKinney. “Putting guys in different positions, placing guys in different spots on the field, whether that’s deep zone, whether that’s in the half, blitzing, so it’s kind of mixing everything up. It’s hard for the opponents when they’re watching film and trying to figure who’s going to be doing what. So, I think it’s been a good mix of all of us kind of doing different things.”
The Packers are showing signs of being a pretty good team. But this is unsustainable.
The Packers have been penalized a league-high 57 times for a league-high 465 yards. They are first with six roughing-the-passer penalties, tied for second with four unnecessary roughness and tied for third with 10 offensive holding.
The Packers are No. 1 in dropped passes. According to Pro Football Focus, Jordan Love has had 19 passes dropped; no other quarterback has more than 11. All of the other NFC North quarterbacks have had 15 passes dropped.
They cleaned up their act against the Cowboys, but they’re still tied for the second-most fumbles per game.
They seemingly had cleaned up their act in terms of pass protection, but Love faced pressure on 45.5 percent of his dropbacks against Dallas – the fourth-highest of his career, according to Next Gen Stats.
The Packers have the second-highest stuff rate, with 29.0 percent of their running plays gaining 0 yards or worse. Their first-down rushing average is 2.25 yards – more than a half-yard worse than any other team. It was an even more feeble 1.47 yards against Dallas.
Green Bay’s offense is almost fully dependent on Love. It’s up to Love to navigate dirty pockets. It’s up to Love to make the offense work without a running game. It’s up to Love to follow up a perfect pass that was dropped with another perfect pass. It’s up to Love to pick up the slack by the first-down ineptitude.
Love has been tremendous for most of the season. It’s true for almost every team, obviously, that the season will go only as far as the quarterback can take it. It’s especially true for the Packers because of all the surrounding problems that continue to fester.

title: Texans' First Injury Report vs. Giants Features Several Concerns for Week 7
full_text:
The Houston Texans have dropped their first injury report of the week heading into their upcoming matchup against the New York Giants .
And after their first practice, there's a good chunk of players on the roster listed as either a DNP or a limited participant.
Let's break down everything to know about the Texans' Wednesday injury report:
LB Azeez Al-Shaair (knee) S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) RB David Montgomery (groin) OT Blake Fisher (thumb) OT Trent Brown (wrist) TE Dalton Schultz (calf)
WR Nico Collins (rest) LB Henry To'oTo'o (shoulder) DE Will Anderson Jr. (rest) DE Jadeveon Clowney (knee) DE Logan Hall (knee)
The Texans have been dealing with injuries to both running back David Montgomery and defensive back Jalen Pitre since their Week 5 game against the Tennessee Titans. Both of them missed the trip to London against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and they've both now missed their first of three practices heading into this weekend against New York. Both of them were considered week-to-week upon the announcement of their injuries a couple of weeks ago, and thus could provide a bit of optimism for their availability vs. the Giants. However, don't be surprised if either or both are due to miss another game.
As mentioned by DeMeco Ryans earlier this week, veteran safety Reed Blankenship is in concussion protocol , and therefore didn't practice with the team on Wednesday. It also seems as if he's dealing with a hand injury that's limiting him as well. So if things continue to trend in this direction for Blankenship, he could be forced out for Week 7, and instead return after the Texans' bye in Week 9. If that's the case, expect M.J. Stewart to be the next man up to start at safety next to Calen Bullock.
One noteworthy name to keep an eye on within the Texans' injury report heading deeper into the week is tight end Dalton Schultz, who seemed to suffer a calf injury in the middle of their trip to London against Jacksonville, but wound up finishing the game anyways. Given that he did finish the game out against the Jaguars, that tends to be a good sign that he'll be able to play this coming weekend. But in any event, he is forced to miss time; keep an eye on Foster Moreau, fresh off of his two-touchdown day.
Tank Dell is officially set to make his return to the NFL field this weekend. He's now logged multiple full practices over the past three weeks and will be designated for return from injured reserve for his first game in over 650 days. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans spoke about Dell's pending return earlier this weekend: "I expect Tank just to be himself, and just play the offense the right way," Ryans said. "No huge expectations for what he needs to do. We're all just going to be excited... I'm just thankful, grateful for him to have this opportunity to return." "I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there. And that's the only thing that matters."

title: Texans' DeMeco Ryans Shrugs Off Giants' Decision to Start J.J. McCarthy
full_text:
Heading into the Houston Texans' Week 7 matchup against the New York Giants , the opposition has made an eye-catching shake-up at their quarterback position.
The Giants have been rolling out Jameis Winston as their starting quarterback ever since Jaxson Dart went down with a knee injury in Week 2. However, New York head coach John Harbaugh announced Wednesday that J.J. McCarthy would start under center against Houston.
McCarthy had previously made an appearance at the end of the Giants' Week 6 game against the New Orleans Saints, in which he performed relatively well in the reps he was given: he completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards with a touchdown, an interception, and had two rushing attempts for 26 yards.
So now, the Giants have seen enough out of the 23-year-old quarterback from that showing to warrant another start in Week 7 on the road against Houston.
However, heading into that Week 7 duel against the Giants, it doesn't seem like Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans is too concerned about who's starting at quarterback for New York.
Ryans was asked during his Wednesday presser about his thoughts on the Giants starting J.J. McCarthy for their Week 7 matchup against Houston.
But overall, the focus remained more upon the Texans' defense being better prepared for the week ahead, no matter who the opposing quarterback is.
"For us, it really doesn't matter who plays quarterback," Ryans said of the Giants' quarterback decision. "For us, defensively, it's been about our process, and how do we do things that we do the right way, and do them well."
"So, whoever's at quarterback doesn't really dictate what we're going to do defensively. It's about us. We got to play better defensively, because it wasn't good enough in our last outing."
Of course, Ryans and the Texans won't be heading into this game without doing their due diligence scouting and studying film on McCarthy.
Knowing that he will be the guy under center could make Houston's preparation a little bit easier by having a bit more clarity on how New York's offense will look. Or, perhaps that pre-game prep can be a little more challenging without having as vast of a sample size with McCarthy as the Giants' starting quarterback.
But no matter what the Giants' quarterback looks like, that's not where Ryans head is sitting at a few days out from their Week 7 matchup. More than anything, Ryans clearly wasn't too satisfied with the output his defense showcased last week against the Jaguars –– and he wants those lapses ironed out ASAP.
In Week 6, Houston allowed Jacksonville to become the third team to score 30-plus points on them in a single game on the year. For reference, that feat only happened once over the course of the 2025 season in their Week 18 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts .
So rather than putting a ton of focus on the external factors in terms of who the Giants will have under center, Ryans is taking a different approach. He's more locked in on how he and his team can take the necessary steps forward to be the elite defense that they proved to be capable of all of last season.
Maybe this game can present a get-right opportunity for the Texans' defense and their hopes of lifting back to that elite level they stood at all of last season. But if it isn't, the conversations around exactly what's happened to this side of the ball in Houston will only continue to get louder.

title: Texans OL Emerging as Trade Candidate to Watch Before Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is a little less than three weeks away.
That means a few players around the league are due to find their way into some interesting trade rumors over the coming days––and that certainly doesn't exclude the Texans, who have already made a couple of acquisitions over the past couple of months in the case of Kayshon Boutte and Marvin Harrison Jr.
However, some of the latest buzz around the Texans seems to hint that there's one player on the roster on the verge of getting shipped out between now and the deadline: and that's none other than two-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Wyatt Teller.
According to ESPN' s Dan Graziano , Teller has been seen as "potentially available" in the weeks leading up to the NFL trade deadline as someone who's not working out in his new situation in Houston.
"Sometimes, circumstances change or things don't work out as expected, so teams will pivot if the terms are favorable," Graziano wrote. "A couple of other 2026 free agent signings who stand out as potentially available due to their situations not working out include Texans offensive lineman Wyatt Teller and Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen."
While the return for Teller might not be too grand of a package for the Texans, seeing Teller on his way out in the next few weeks certainly wouldn't be the most shocking outcome.
Teller, who was signed earlier this offseason, was brought into Houston with the intent of being able to compete for the Texans' starting left guard spot . He was inked to a two-year, $16 million deal, with most preseason expectations settling on Teller being the favorite to eventually claim that starting spot.
However, as the season got closer and closer to kicking off, it became clear that Teller was not going to be within the interior starting offensive line unit. Instead, the Texans were bound to start rookie Keylan Rutledge at left guard , Evan Brown at center, and Ed Ingram at right guard.
Teller did get two starts for the Texans in Weeks 2 and 3 at right guard as Ingram was sidelined with a groin injury. Though once he returned, he would settle back into his regular reserve spot— a role which he hasn't exactly been in routinely throughout what's been a relatively successful pro career.
So instead of letting Teller essentially rot on the bench for the next several weeks of the regular season as an unsuccessful free agent signing, the Texans could instead look to trade him.
Houston would be able to get some type of return on their previous investment, Teller could get a fresh start elsewhere with the hope that he can find a starting spot, and both sides can walk away wiping their hands clean.
So will the move actually wind up happening for Teller? It likely depends on whether or not the Texans can get the right package in return for him.
Given that Teller's in the back-nine of his career as is, and hasn't performed well enough to be a starter on Houston's up-and-down offensive line, there are no guarantees that the front office would be able to net much of an appealing package for him, even from an offensive line-needy team.
Yet, for a day three pick or similar value? That might just be enough for this front office to have interest in pulling the trigger. Time will tell if Houston winds up receiving that, but don't be surprised if we're entering the final days of Teller's brief time as a Texan.

title: Texans Stock Report: 4 Risers, 4 Fallers Heading Into Week 7
full_text:
The Houston Texans are now six weeks deep into their 2026 campaign, and have had several players around the roster see their stock shift both up and down since the start of the season.
Heading into Week 7 against the New York Giants , the Texans as a whole are certainly trending up from where they stood this time two weeks ago. At 0-4, it felt like the sky was falling in Houston.
However, a few standout playmakers from the past two weeks have been able to flip the script for a much-better-looking pair of performances for Houston to claim back-to-back wins. In the case of a few others, their struggles have lingered in one way or another, and their standing on this roster moving forward tends to look a bit different because of it.
With all of that in mind, let's sort through a batch of four players whose stock is on the rise heading into Week 7, along with four others who are on the opposite side of the equation:
Even if the wins haven't been flowing from start to finish of the Texans' first six weeks, things have looked extremely stout on C.J. Stroud's part, who's come out of the gates playing some of the best football of his NFL career thus far. Through six games, Stroud is averaging his highest passing yards (285.7), completion percentage (65.3%), TD-to-INT ratio (9-1), and passer rating (100.9) since being drafted back in 2023.
WHAT A THROW FROM CJ STROUD. HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Z8LUxZceAl
If there were a team MVP award to hand out at the six-week mark of the season, Will Anderson's certainly made a great case for himself as the current frontrunner for DPOY. Still, I might lean towards Stroud being the more deserving recipient.
The Texans have been without their lead running back, David Montgomery, for the past game and a half due to a groin injury he suffered in Week 5. But as Montgomery has stepped aside, Woody Marks has finally begun to deliver for this struggling Houston run game. The Texans nearly put up their highest rushing total on the season against Jacksonville with 114 total yards on the ground, largely thanks to the impact that Marks provided as an explosive playmaker in the backfield. Expect to see him continuously featured on the offensive end moving forward, with or without Montgomery in the mix.
It's become pretty hard to ignore Jaylin Noel's production over the past three weeks. Even if Noel hasn't exactly found his way to securing a super high volume of offensive snaps, he's made the most of the opportunities he's had, combining for 12 receptions, 233 yards, and a touchdown––coming in Houston's latest game against the Jaguars in London. Seeing Noel's stock rise even further in the weeks ahead could be a lot easier said than done, knowing guys like Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell will only continue to get more involved in the passing game. But if Noel continues making plays as he has been, it'll be really tough for the Texans to keep him off the field.
The Texans' ball-hawking safety has had a pretty quiet start to the season thus far, having recorded zero turnovers through the first five weeks of action. But in Week 6, Bullock finally saw those turnover numbers shift in his direction as he found his way to a Trevor Lawrence interception against Jacksonville in Week 6.
Calen Bullock picks it off in the end zone for the @HoustonTexans ! HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3EBfQmbmWr
Considering the Texans' turnover numbers through this point in the season have looked pretty bleak, it'd be a massive boost for the defense if Bullock can continue having a nose for the football moving forward.
Montgomery has been dealing with an injury over the past couple of weeks, which isn't exactly his fault. However, it's hard to look away from the fact that Houston's run game looked a whole lot better against the Jaguars than it has since Week 1, which came in a game in which Montgomery wasn't suited up for. He's been inefficient, ineffective, and is due to see some snaps taken away from him in the weeks ahead if his individual production can't turn around . Otherwise, Woody Marks could be the leader in this backfield in no time.
It's been a rocky start to Marlin Klein's rookie season. Over the first three weeks of the year, Klein had totaled just 22 combined offensive snaps, turning those in for just one reception taken for 16 yards. Since Week 4, he's been a healthy scratch, as the coaching staff has been looking for him to be a better impact player on special teams. For a player that was selected as high as Klein was in this past offseason's draft, you'd expect him to be a bit more involved at this point in the season. Six weeks in, though, and we have no sign on when he'll be elevated to the gameday roster, let alone being an impact player offensively .
For the time that Henry To'oTo'o was on injured reserve due to a shoulder injury , it was Jake Hansen who stepped up as someone who could play and start alongside Azeez Al-Shaair at linebacker–– or in the case of Week 4, alongside practice squad elevation Kenneth Murray–– and he held things down pretty serviceably. But now that To'oTo'o is back to full health, and Al-Shaair is trending towards playing in Week 7 after another groin injury scare this past weekend, it'll be much harder for Hansen to have a consistent role on defense.
It's been an up-and-down start to the season for Reed Blankenship, who was brought into Houston to provide stability at the safety position, but has been anything but that over the first six weeks he's played. He's clearly struggled adjusting to the Texans' defensive scheme, has allowed multiple big play opportunities, and is now dealing with a concussion that could sideline him for Week 7 against the New York Giants. If M.J. Stewart can enter the starting lineup and hold things down more effectively, the conversations will get a bit more interesting after the bye.

title: Texans' David Montgomery Problem Is Getting Hard to Ignore
full_text:
In the midst of the Houston Texans' Week 6 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars , this offense wound up having a lot more success running the ball than they've been accustomed to over the past several weeks.
Behind the duo of Woody Marks and Jawhar Jordan in the backfield, the Texans combined for 114 rushing yards, had over 4.5 yards per carry, and thus came out to their most productive game on the ground so far this year in terms of numbers.
And such a result came as a bit of a surprise for the Texans, all things considered. Houston was going up against statistically the best run defense in the entire NFL in Jacksonville heading into the week, and oddly saw things click in that area of their offense after consistently struggling beforehand.
The most noteworthy part of it all? Houston made it happen without the presence of their starting running back, David Montgomery, on the field, who was sidelined with a groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans.
And so such a performance from the Texans' run game begs one key question: is this run game better off without Montgomery leading the way in snaps?
Through the first five games of Montgomery's debut season in Houston, things haven't quite panned out as highly expected, especially following up from his Week 1 breakout with a three-touchdown performance.
He's logged 52 carries for 138 yards (2.7 yards per carry), coming out to under 30 yards on the ground per game, and has paired that with under 2.0 yards before and after contact for only the second time in his career. Receiving-wise, he hasn't been much of a factor, with just seven catches for 67 yards.
And based on the initial investment the Texans made in Montgomery earlier this offseason, the results are quite the disappointment. Montgomery was brought in to be a stabilizer for Houston's run game as a power back and complement to Woody Marks . But outside of his debut against the Buffalo Bills, he's been anything but that.
Montgomery hasn't looked anywhere close to the most explosive back in the backfield, has lacked any sense of efficiency in the opportunities he's gotten, and is now dealing with a groin injury that could continue to sideline him for another week, depending on how this coming week of practice goes.
Now, the offensive line certainly hasn't done Montgomery any favors when he's been on the field. But we've seen just as recently as last week that the Texans are capable of having effective days on the ground, even against one of the most challenging run defenses around the NFL in Jacksonville.
Woody Marks, on the other hand, has put together 205 total yards on the ground with an average of 3.5 yards per carry, and is now only one touchdown away from matching Montgomery's season total of three. He's looked explosive, has contributed in the passing game, and is now coming off his best game of the season thus far from Houston's overseason trip to London.
Woody Marks is wide open and gets the @HoustonTexans just inside field goal range... HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kIkn1kIptN
Jawhar Jordan, the Texans' practice squad elevation from this past week, took advantage of his opportunities against Jacksonville as well. He went for six carries and 43 yards with a touchdown, and has certainly made a good case to jump onto the 53-man roster, especially if Houston wants to steer away from incorporating Montgomery as a key piece of their game plan.
So should the Texans decide to turn away from Montgomery as the leader in the backfield once he's back? That's certainly not out of the question, but it still might be a little too early.
Maybe it's only a matter of time before Montgomery gets uprooted from his spot atop the Texans' running back depth chart. If things continue to trend like they looked in Week 6, Houston will have no choice but to keep handing Marks (and maybe even Jordan) more opportunities.
But that time might not be now––at least not until Montgomery is fully healthy from the injury that's kept him out of the lineup for the past week. Once he's back to 100%, whenever that might be, he can try to re-establish his footing as the veteran power back the Texans tried to add to their offense in the first place.
However, if there's any event that the Texans' run game continues to keep flowing at its best for another week if Montgomery is sidelined, or if things simply look groggy in the run game once he returns, the conversation's going to get a whole lot more interesting.
And if that's the case, that move the Texans made to first bring in Montgomery for a fourth-round pick and Juice Scruggs will only look uglier than it looks now. So the Texans are certainly hoping their veteran back can turn a positive corner once he's off the injury report.

title: Texans Week 7 Consensus Power Rankings: Things Trending Up in Houston
full_text:
The Houston Texans seem like they could be set to go on a run here over the next few games after a clutch Week 6 victory in London over the Jacksonville Jaguars .
From a gloomy 0-4 record after their first four to now having a bit more life with back-to-back wins in the books, the consensus is starting to turn around when it comes to how the league views this Texans team moving forward this season.
With that in mind, let's sort through a new batch of consensus power rankings to see just where the Texans stack up as they roll into Week 7 against the New York Giants .
Sports Illustrated 's Conor Orr kept the Texans steady at their 14th spot from last week. However, he certainly didn't hold back when breaking down how the team should approach the trade deadline as big-time buyers for one star running back.
"Forget about the defense. The narrative heading into the trade deadline should be: How much more help can Houston provide C.J. Stroud, who is playing at a top-10 level over the course of the last month and seeing the field better than he has in two years. My take? Call Philadelphia and see what Saquon Barkley has left in the tank."
Nick Shook gave the Texans a whole lot more respect in his rankings this week; largely because of how C.J. Stroud has taken on the past few weeks as a near-MVP candidate.
"Don’t look now, but the Texans are clawing their way back into relevance! Houston’s defense isn’t the shutdown unit it was in years past, but the talent-laden group has inched itself closer to familiarity since DeMeco Ryans took the play-calling reins. Most importantly, C.J. Stroud is playing some of the best football of his career. His performance in London was simply exquisite (save for his late interception in the end zone), and if the Texans can sustain their turnaround, he’ll force his way into the MVP conversation."
ESPN 's writers bumped the Texans up a few spots from where they stood last week, to now sit in the middle of the pack at 16th. D.J. Bien-Aime was tasked with highlighting the biggest concern on the offensive side of the ball, where he noted Houston's "lack of a run game."
"The Texans' passing attack is humming, as quarterback C.J. Stroud ranks second leaguewide in passing yards (1,712), but an effective run game would take this offense to the top tier. They're averaging 84.8 rushing yards per game (25th) and have 32 rushing first downs on the season (tied for 22nd). Running back David Montgomery, who was acquired via trade in March, is averaging a career-low 2.7 yards per carry and missed Week 6 because of a groin injury."
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff gave their flowers to Stroud for how he's taken on the first six weeks of the season––and even point out the interesting contract discussions that Houston is now set to have with their quarterback this coming offseason.
"Houston’s slow start was not the fault of its quarterback. Stroud, who is in the fourth year of his rookie deal and is headed toward interesting contract negotiations with the Texans, is 16th in the league in fantasy scoring (112.2) and on pace for the best passer rating (100.9) and EPA per dropback (0.15) numbers of his career. The Texans have won two in a row after Sunday’s victory in London."
Pete Prisco found a spot for the Texans in his top 15 this week. However, he still sees some holes on the defensive side of the ball, where Houston allowed 31 points to Jacksonville this past weekend.
"That was a big-time victory in London over the Jaguars. C.J. Stroud is really playing at a high level, but the defense has to pick it up."
Ralph Vacchiano is a whole lot more optimistic about the Texans compared to where they stood two weeks ago. And if this team can keep up the momentum they've built up through the past couple of wins, he sees a playoff appearance more than capable of being in their future.
"They’re baaaaaack! Everyone thought the Texans were dead at 0-4. … OK, I thought they were dead, but I wasn’t the only one. But they got right two weeks ago against the awful Titans and stayed right with a terrific 34-31 win in London against the Jaguars. C.J. Stroud finally looks like the franchise QB he was supposed to be. He has plenty of weapons, with the addition of WR Marvin Harrison Jr. But what happened to DeMeco Ryans’ defense? It’s not nearly as dominant as it once was. If the Texans can fix it, they’re a good bet to become the second-ever team to start 0-4 and make the playoffs."

title: Texans Injury Update: Another Starting DB Banged Up Before Week 7
full_text:
The Houston Texans were already dealing with a couple of key injuries heading into their Week 6 battle against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
On the offensive side of the ball, Houston was forced to go without running back David Montgomery with a groin injury he suffered back in Week 5 . Defensively, they were without their versatile nickel/safety Jalen Pitre, who suffered a shoulder injury in that same game .
And it turns out, after the events of the Texans' Week 6 game in London against Jacksonville, the secondary is dealing with another injury that could lead to an absence this weekend facing the New York Giants.
According to DeMeco Ryans in his Monday press conference, Texans safety Reed Blankenship is in the concussion protocol after leaving in the middle of Houston's Week 6 game against the Jaguars.
Ryans did also have some good news on the status of Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, who left in the middle of the game with a groin injury, but would eventually return and be described as "fine" heading into Week 7.
Being without Blankenship, though, is a notable loss for this Texans defense, who signed the veteran safety to be a weekly starter in the back-end of their secondary, and he's continued to fill that role since the season started.
While Blankenship's play has been up-and-down overall, he's combined for 45 tackles, three passes defended, one tackle for loss, and one interception in the six games he's played this season. And if without him in the secondary for any stretch of time, Houston will be forced to make another pivot for their starting defense as they already had to do last weekend without Pitre.
We won't know for certain if this Texans secondary will be without Blankenship heading into Week 7, though the concussion protocol for any player can tend to result in at least a one-game absence. So his status will be one to monitor over the course of this week at practice.
If Blankenship is forced to miss a game, the most obvious fill-in Houston could call up as their second safety next to Calen Bullock is veteran safety M.J. Stewart.
The 32-year-old is officially healthy after missing the first four games of the season due to a quad injury, but has appeared in the Texans' last two games with three total tackles. games with three total tackles.
Stewart was a frequent starter for the Texans in 2025 before he went down with what would be a season-ending quad injury, ultimately playing in nine games while starting in four of them for 25 tackles and two passes defended.
We'll certainly know more about the defensive plans for Houston once we get closer to Week 7's kickoff against the Giants. However, don't be surprised if the Texans are forced to be without both Blankenship and Pitre in their secondary as they were down the stretch in their last game against Jacksonville .

title: What to Expect From Texans WR Tank Dell in His Return vs. Giants
full_text:
The Houston Texans made a major announcement heading into their Week 7 matchup against the New York Giants, revealing that wide receiver Tank Dell would be making his return to the field for the first time in over 650 days since suffering his devastating knee injury in 2024.
It's been a long time coming for both Dell and Texans fans . The fan-favorite wideout first suffered his knee injury back in Week 15 of the 2024 NFL season against the Kansas City Chiefs, and has been diligently rehabbing and working back from it ever since.
Now, he'll finally get to see his hard work pay off this weekend in a key matchup for the Texans that could take them to their third win in a row.
But what exactly could Dell's first game back with the Texans look like? How often will he be able to get onto the field, and how involved in the offensive game plan will he be?
It probably goes without saying, but it'd be hard to expect Dell to get back into the mix for the Texans as an every-down receiver who's on the field for a lion's share of their offensive looks.
And those likely limited snaps come for two reasons: one being the obvious in that Dell hasn't played in a live, in-game setting since 2024. While he has been busy in team practice with pads on, playing in an NFL game with tackling and heavy contact is a different animal .
Houston, in all likelihood, will give Dell a few weeks of limited snaps for the first couple of games that he's back in the action, rather than simply throwing him into the fire, then continue to ramp up his workload the longer he's on the field.
Head coach DeMeco Ryans made it clear during his Monday press conference that he won't have any huge expectations for Dell in his first game back, and simply just wants to see him back out there and "be himself."
"I expect Tank just to be himself, and just play the offense the right way," Ryans said. "No huge expectations for what he needs to do. We're all just going to be excited... I'm just thankful, grateful for him to have this opportunity to return."
"I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there. And that's the only thing that matters."
The Texans also don't have to feel an overwhelming need to get Dell quickly adjusted because of the talent they already have around him in the wide receiver room.
Of course, having Dell on the field and at 100% makes this passing attack even more potent than it already looked last week. But when he's also surrounded by other pass-catchers like Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, and Jaylin Noel among others, the Texans can instead deploy Dell situationally and allow for an overall smoother transition to be a higher-usage player down the line.
And based on what DeMeco Ryans has seen in practice the past two weeks, he's confident that Dell can still be the explosive, playmaking talent he was when he was last on the field for the Texans.
"Tank is an explosive player. Still quick as ever. Ask our defenders who's been covering him the past couple of weeks," Ryans said. "He's been putting us in some tough matchups in practice the past two weeks. So I expect him to go out on Sunday and do the same thing; really stress defenders."
"And you add him in the mix with all the other guys we have, we just have a really good group of guys; a lot of guys who are capable of making big-time, explosive plays for us."
If there were a snap count projection to place on Dell heading into Week 7 against the Giants, think around 10-15 looks on the offense throughout the day.
We just saw last weekend against the Jacksonville Jaguars how the Texans wanted to limit Marvin Harrison Jr.'s integration into the offense in his first game back, where he was held to just 11 total offensive looks, though he saw four targets in the time he was out there.
Harrison Jr. and Dell are in two vastly different situations, sure: Harrison Jr. is getting integrated into a brand-new offense, while Dell has been in the building for the past three seasons and is just getting back on the field for the first time in nearly two years.
But in terms of how the Texans might deploy those two in their first games of the season, the results could be relatively similar: get Dell slowly integrated with a limited snap share, get him involved when he's out there for three to four targets, and both numbers will continue to increase with each passing week.

title: 3 Texans Players Most Impacted By Tank Dell's Return From Injury
full_text:
The Houston Texans announced on Monday afternoon that fan-favorite wide receiver Tank Dell would be making his long-awaited return to the field for Week 7's game against the New York Giants.
And that's undoubtedly massive news for the Texans' offense. Dell has been busy rehabbing his devastating knee injury ever since first suffering it in December of 2024, and will now be set to play in his first NFL game in over 650 days.
But upon Dell's return, his presence will certainly have a domino effect on a few surrounding players on the Texans' roster for one way or another.
On one hand, Dell's standout playmaking and explosiveness have a chance to take this rising Texans offense to another gear, if truly back to 100%. On the other hand, though, bringing in another pass-catcher for this scoring attack will inevitably take some critical reps away from others.
So with all of that in mind, let's take a look at three players in the Texans' offense who will be most affected by the return of Tank Dell, starting as soon as Week 7 back at home against the G-Men:
Of course, one primary beneificary of Dell getting back into the lineup is his quarterback, C.J. Stroud. Because the last time Dell was healthy and catching passes in this offense, he was one of his favorite targets as a potent and explosive downfield option.
And while there will be some heavy competition for Dell to get targets with the talent Houston has around him at wide receiver, it feels like a safe bet to assume that Stroud will ensure to get Dell involved in the offensive game plan for whatever extent he winds up playing.
We just saw an example this past week against the Jacksonville Jaguars of Stroud making it an emphasis to get new target Marvin Harrison Jr. involved in the limited reps he saw, having four targets on just 11 total offensive snaps that were converted into three catches for 34 yards.
It wouldn't be too surprising for Dell to have a similar role from the jump as he gets back to game speed. And from Stroud's perspective, it's hard to be against getting another weapon in what might now be his deepest wide receiver room since first arriving in Houston in 2023.
While the addition of Dell might impact Stroud's stock for the better moving forward, the same might not be able to be said for Kayshon Boutte, who now feels primed to see his opportunities in this offense dry up a bit further from what he's seen over the past six weeks of the season.
And based Boutte's last appearance against Jacksonville, there's a chance that downtick in opportunties has already started.
As Boutte was competing with Marvin Harrison Jr. for similar snaps at receiver, Boutte saw his offensive snap share drop from an average of 61.1% to a much lower 41.3% in Week 6. And now that Dell is entering as yet another target for the offense to get involved, Boutte might be forced to make some sacrifices.
It was less than two months ago when the Texans first made their move to pick up Boutte and help provide depth to a position group that needed it after Jayden Higgins' preseason injury. But in a short amount of time, Boutte has gone from being viewed as a WR2/3 in this offense to now potentially being as low as WR6.
Another name in the Texans' offense who feels due to make some more sacrifices than he's already made thus far: fourth-year wideout Xavier Hutchinson.
And it's really not an indictment on what Hutchinson is or isn't doing. His past three weeks have resulted in some pretty solid production, as he's combined for nine receptions on 13 targets for 121 yards while playing just over 40% of the offensive snaps.
Instead, the other names around Hutchinson in the receiver room simply might just be a bigger priority to get involved in the game plan.
Nico Collins is going to remain WR1 as he has for the past three seasons. Marvin Harrison Jr.'s workload is only going to continue going up. Jaylin Noel has shown no reason to see his snaps on the decline through the past several weeks, and when you add Dell into the equation, he's going to get his share of targets as well.
So where does Hutchinson land in all of this? Well, he certainly won't be disappearing from the Texans' game plan entirely . He's played too well in the reps he's gotten so far this season, and he's a plus contributor as a blocker. Just don't expect him to see much more than four targets a week now that Houston's receiver room looks even deeper than it was before.

title: Texans Set to Welcome WR Tank Dell Back After Lengthy Injury Absence
full_text:
The time has finally come for Tank Dell to get back into the fold for the Houston Texans.
According to an update from Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans on Monday afternoon, Dell will officially be set to be activated from injured reserve for Houston's Week 7 game against the New York Giants.
Texans coach DeMeco Ryans announced WR Tank Dell will play Sunday against the Giants — Dell’s first game since a major leg injury in 2024.
The return for Dell marks the first time the wide receiver has gotten on the field for an NFL game since December of 2024.
Dell went down with a severe knee injury during the Texans' Week 15 of the 2024 season against the Kansas City Chiefs, where he would suffer damage to his ACL, MCL, LCL, meniscus, and kneecap, which has left him rehabbing for the past 22 months.
Dell missed the entire 2025 season as he was recovering from the injury, and has been on injured reserve for the past six weeks of the 2026 season.
The Texans activated Dell's 21-day practice window from injured reserve after their Week 4 game against the Dallas Cowboys, which did provide a bit of a hint that Dell was on the brink of making his long-awaited return to this offense as one of C.J. Stroud's favorite targets.
And now, after the events of the Texans' Week 6 win against the Jacksonville Jaguars , it turns out Dell is officially ready to go and be activated for this coming weekend at home against the Giants.
Upon revealing that Dell would finally be back in the mix against the Giants, Ryan explained that he's simply looking for the Texans' wideout to "be himself" with no "huge expectations" for his long-awaited return.
"I just expect Tank to be himself, no huge expectations, all just excited to see him out there for first time in over two years," Ryans said on Monday. "Thankful, grateful to him. I don't have any expectations, just happy to see him out there."
"We all know Tank is an explosive player, still quick as ever, ask our defenders covering him past two weeks. I expect him to really stress defenders.'
The last time Dell was on the field for the Texans back in 2023 and 2024, he was an extremely potent downfield weapon that quickly developed some strong chemistry with Stroud as one of his favorite targets.
Through the first two years of his career, Dell played in a total of 25 games for 98 receptions, 1,376 yards, and 10 touchdowns, and set the Texans rookie record for touchdown receptions back in 2023 with seven.
Now, Dell will look to try and reclaim that status as a dangerous pass-catcher in the Texans’ offense, surrounded by what now looks to be a pretty deep and talented wide receiver room.
Dell will pair alongside existing targets in Nico Collins, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte, and will also get a chance to play next to the Texans' latest addition to the position in Marvn Harrison Jr., who was brought in via trade with the Arizona Cardinals around this time last week.
It remains to be seen how many snaps Dell will see upon his return , or just what his role will look like in a Texans offense that looks a whole lot different from the form he last saw it as.
However, to see Dell will finally be back on the field for his first in-game appearance in over 600 days, it's sure to be a welcomed sight to behold for not only Texans fans, but for the NFL world as a whole.
