title: Steelers Release Veteran Safety Before Paris Trip
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers shook up their defensive roster ahead of their Week 7 contest against the New Orleans Saints. As the team prepares for an international flight to Paris, France, one of the veteran defenders was informed that he won't be on the flight or on the active roster moving forward.
The Steelers cut safety Rayshawn Jenkins. The 32-year-old former Los Angeles Chargers draft pick played in the first six games of the season during his first season in Pittsburgh.
By releasing Jenkins, the Steelers opened up a vacant spot on their active roster, and there are a few options for how they could fill it. Steelers On SI publisher Noah Strackbein hinted at one potential outcome for Week 7.
#Steelers release Rayshawn Jenkins. Gotta think that could mean DeShon Elliott is coming back
The most optimistic take from this update is that the Steelers might be getting one of their most important members of the secondary back for their international matchup. Starting safety DeShon Elliott hasn't played in the regular season in nearly a year due to a lower-body injury he suffered against the Green Bay Packers last season.
Heading into this season, things were trending in a positive direction for Elliott's injury. But after he appeared in one preseason contest, he was placed on IR to begin the regular season schedule. In the weeks since, he's been quietly making progress, but the team has been quite vague. Ahead of their Week 7 contest, head coach Mike McCarthy said this about Elliott's status, via Alan Saunders of Steelers Now.
"I hope so," he stated. "We have a practice plan for him. He’s doing really well. He’s chomping at the bit, so we’ll see how it goes this week."
#Steelers HC Mike McCarthy on the potential for SS DeShon Elliott to return this week: “I hope so. We have a practice plan for him. He’s doing really well. He’s chomping at the bit, so we’ll see how it goes this week. … We’ll see how today goes.” https://t.co/5QtLC83eQs https://t.co/EcA2qqUnJW
He's the best-case scenario for the Steelers to replace Jenkins. Elliott has plenty of starting experience and playmaking ability to bring the defense to the next level. In five 2025 contests before his injury, he recorded 38 total tackles, a forced fumble, an interception and a sack. He was all over the field, producing splash plays across each level of the defense.
That's exactly the type of player the Steelers need back in the secondary. They've received solid play from players like Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette. Veteran Jalen Ramsey is on another level as the season inches towards the midway point. Adding Elliott could put this group over the top.
If Elliott can't return. the Steelers will have to rely even more on the three safeties they currently have on the roster. In addition to Ramsey, Jaquan Brisker has played a significant amount of snaps with mixed results. Rookie Robert Spears-Jennings has impressed to begin his career, but it's uncertain how much they trust the seventh-round draft choice.
If they look to the practice squad to fill the final roster spot for Week 7, they have a few players to pick from.
Sebastian Castro has NFL experience with both the Steelers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Undrafted out of the University of Iowa, he's a special teams standout who could earn more playing time if given the opportunity.
Darius Rush is a slightly older option who might have a better shot at getting on the field for gameday. The 26-year-old has six games of NFL experience.
Lastly, the Steelers could promote Car'Lin Vigers. An undrafted defensive back out of Louisiana-Monroe, he's extremely athletic and has the ideal size of a NFL DB. He's yet to make an appearance in an NFL regular season contest.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: 3 WRs Steelers Can Trade Day 3 Draft Picks For
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Even after the addition of Marquez Valdes-Scantling, the Pittsburgh Steelers haven't solved their issues at wide receiver.
Some senior voices on the Steelers' beat are convinced that another move is coming. Others feel assured that MVS was this team's big swing to improve the offense.
If the Steelers sit pat, they risk this offense not having what it takes to finally end their playoff win drought. Simultaneously, this team is trying to maintain as many assets as possible so they can target another top player in the 2027 NFL Draft. That leaves them with their Day 3 picks in the draft to gamble.
Luckily for the Steelers, these three wide receivers can easily be acquired for a late-round draft picks and would help solve this team's depth problems before the NFL Trade Deadline.
If the Steelers believe the top of their depth chart is secured, then finding that true wide receiver three or four is paramount. Enter Kendrick Bourne, the 31-year-old Arizona Cardinals pass-catcher with 133 games played and 351 receptions under his belt.
So far in 2026, he's performed very well. He has 22 receptions on 31 targets for 225 yards. His numbers are eerily close to what rookie Germie Bernard has posted so far, and that's exactly what this team needs production-wise.
Bourne also doesn't command a top receiver's share of the passing attempts like some other players out there. He could fill in for a few weeks, and then fall down the depth chart as the receiver room becomes healthier down the stretch.
Bourne brings experience and a history of productivity, but he isn't quite the speedster that the Steelers might be looking for. Right now, they have two strong, yards-after-the-catch pass-catchers in Bernard and DK Metcalf. A speedy, deep-ball threat would complement their current corps, and Bourne isn't quite that type of receiver.
The Philadelphia Eagles are in firesale mode, and that means many of their offensive names are on the table for trade. Two options could intrigue the Steelers, but provided his recent injury scare is nothing serious, Dontayvion Wicks is a perfect solution for the problems in Pittsburgh.
Wicks is a former draft pick of the Green Bay Packers, and he's been seen as a deep-ball threat on the outside for his entire four-year career.
So far with the Eagles, he's found success as the team flounders. He's hauled in 19 receptions in six games for 284 yards and a touchdown. Before the 2026 season began, the Eagles gave up a fifth and a seventh for Wicks, but they will likely part with him for any asset in return.
I honestly have no reason to suggest the Steelers avoid this trade. Wicks is speedy. He lines up out wide a majority of the time, but can play in the slot if needed. He's under contract through 2027 and comes with a $4 million cap hit for next year.
If I'm Omar Khan, I'm making a deal with the cross-state rivals immediately.
Speed is the name of the game with Los Angeles Chargers weapon Quentin Johnston. The former first-round pick in 2023 has posted multiple 700-yard campaigns, and he also brings that size to match Metcalf, coming in at 6'3" and nearly 220 pounds.
Johnston is an outside receiver who can go in motion or try to beat coverage over the top. He's battled injuries, something the Steelers have to be very careful in navigating more of, but if he's healthy he's the best fit for the offense on the market.
The Steelers have two receivers on Injured Reserve, another who is missing time, and they are running out of time and options.
Is it in their best interest to go after another player with an injury history and concern? That's the gamble for the Steelers, and it's possible this one wouldn't pay off.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Must Avoid This Veteran WR Trade Target
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers might not be done adding to their wide receiver room. No one knows for sure at this point, as the team recently added veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad.
It's a foregone conclusion that the Steelers will elevate MVS to the active roster soon, and it's only a matter of time before he's catching a small number of passes from Aaron Rodgers. But is that really it? Some, like Pat McAfee Show correspondent Mark Kaboly and Pittsburgh Post Gazette writer Ray Fittipaldo, believe another trade is coming.
Nationally, that sentiment is shared. In a recent article for CBS Sports , Carter Bahns wrote about why Tampa Bay Buccaneers receiver Chris Godwin would be a perfect fit for the offensively-needy Steelers. In a perfect world , that would be a quality addition. But the Steelers don' t live in that world, and Godwin is absolutely a player to avoid as the franchise navigates the final weeks before the NFL Trade Deadline.
The biggest issue with this idea has nothing to do with the player's production or abilities. Instead, the obstacle in the way is Godwin's contract. The 30-year-old signed a deal before the 2025 season that runs through 2027, and it is a costly one.
Godwin carries an absurd cap hit for this year and next, coming in at just over and under $30 million for 2026 and 2027. There is a potential out after the 2027 campaign, according to information rom Spotrac, but it comes with a dead cap hit of $16.2 million.
Simply put, Godwin is too expensive to bring on right now. Unless Tampa wants to absord a large portion of that deal, there is no trade to be made between the Steelers and Bucs.
I am a big fan of Godwin. He's a Penn State product with over 120 games in the NFL. He's exceed 1,000 yards in a season four times, and there was a time when he was a bonafide number two receiver.
The last few seasons, however, that's not the case. Injuries have taken its toll on his career, and he played in just 16 games total over the 2024 and 2025 campaigns. Bahns tries to make the case that he is healthy currently, and that's enough for Pittsburgh.
"He is healthy now, though, and that is what matters to the Steelers," he writes. "Plus, he should be a tremendous fit next to Metcalf. Godwin spent every year prior to this one on the other side of a towering No. 1 target in Mike Evans, so he would be right at home in the same lineup as a similarly sizable go-to weapon like Metcalf."
Sure, he's healthy now, playing in all six games this season. But he's not guaranteed to remain on the field for the rest of the schedule. That's true for every player in the NFL, admittedly, but if you are trying to address a position of need that has been ravaged by injuries. adding another player with a history of injuries defeats that entire purpose.
A few years ago, Godwin would have solved nearly every issue on offense. Nowadays, he's a player that comes with an expensive salary and significant risks. It's not the player the Steelers need moving forward, and it's a great idea to avoid this idea altogether.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Can Shut Down This Trade Idea
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need to continue making a few changes to this team. They alreays went out and grabbed a wide receiver for their practice squad who may replace their two call-ups, and they have a veteran linebacker waiting on the p-squad for his opportunity.
One that may be needed sooner rather than later.
But the one position we're still talking about that we probably shouldn't be is cornerback. Right now, this team has their starters, and have a rookie backup they're very impressed with. It's not time to adjust anything, and as the trade deadline approaches, it's not worth risking the future for a move now.
Jamel Dean doesn't need any justification. His interception against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers said everything it needed to that he can be CB1 for the Steelers and be the primary outside cornerback for the 2026 season, even if he wasn't expected to be coming into it.
Asante Samuel Jr. didn't start off too hot and certainly struggled at times this season, but the last two games have been very different. Through six games, Samuel Jr. allowed just 42.1% of passes thrown his direction to be completed, with seven pass deflections and a QBR of 74.1.
Outside of two touchdowns given up, he's become a very reliable outside cornerback for the Steelers in recent weeks.
Add third-round rookie Daylen Everette off the bench, and Jalen Ramsey in the slot, and the team looks pretty good at cornerback.
The Steelers should consider improving some areas of their team during the trade deadline. They're banged up at wide receiver and could use an insurance plan there because Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are on Injured Reserve.
Inside linebacker has been tough to watch, and it looks like Patrick Queen is either hurt or not playing well enough to keep his role. If Elandon Roberts isn't the answer, maybe someone on another team is.
Safety has been a toss-up all season because of the DeShon Elliott injury and Rayshawn Jenkins not playing well.
But trades for those positions solve a problem that may kill the Steelers' chances to win the AFC North and go on a playoff run. Cornerback is simply to add talent.
With the upcoming NFL Draft still looking like there will be a few quarterbacks worth first-round picks, Pittsburgh needs to stay the course. Omar Khan has said numerous times that until this team finds its next long-term starter at QB, they can't do anything too drastic with their picks.
Keeping them is the safe move. And Samuel Jr.'s improvement should reduce concerns about upgrading the cornerback position.
Trades should happen for the Steelers this season. Just not for a cornerback.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: Aaron Rodgers Check-In: Steelers Getting Enough From QB?
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers , after a comeback win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, have now started 4-2 for a fourth-straight season.
They made the playoffs in each of those prior three instances, which bodes well for the Steelers and Aaron Rodgers to make it back there in the future Hall of Famer's final season of his career.
Rodgers, who looked like he was on his way out of Pittsburgh once Mike Tomlin stepped down in January, opted to return for one last run once the organization hired Mike McCarthy, his former head coach for over a decade from 2006 to 2018 with the Green Bay Packers.
Now that the season is a third of the way finished, let's put together a report card for Rodgers and dive into how he's performed for the Steelers thus far in 2026.
Rodgers has thrown five interceptions (tied for seventh-most in the NFL) through six contests and is on pace for roughly 14, assuming he plays in all 17 of Pittsburgh's regular season games.
That would be quite the jump from the seven he threw for the Steelers in 2025, and it would also represent his career-high in a single year.
Rodgers has always done a great job of protecting the ball, and it's easy to assume that his decision-making or ability to process defenses has dropped at 42 years old based on his interception total up to this point.
That simply isn't the case, however. Three of Rodgers' five picks have deflected off the hands of a Pittsburgh receiver, with the first example coming on a screen to Germie Bernard in Week 2, the second on an in-breaker to Roman Wilson in Week 3 and the third on a screen to Darnell Washington in Week 6.
Additionally, one of Rodgers' two interceptions against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 was on a last-ditch throw downfield while trailing by three points with 10 seconds left in the game, so it's hard to blame him too much for that play.
Rodgers unquestionably has his limitations given his age. There are times where he steps into sacks, he does hold onto the ball too long sometimes, and his lack of mobility does hold back Pittsburgh's offense in the modern NFL.
At the same time, Rodgers has played about as well as the Steelers could've realistically hoped upon reuniting with McCarthy.
Though he's tied for the third-most sacks taken of any quarterback in the league with 19 (per Next Gen Stats ) and has had to play behind an offensive line that, at best, has been inconsistent in pass protection, Rodgers has still operated well from the pocket.
With 1,487 yards (eighth-most in the NFL) and 12 touchdowns (tied for fourth-most) through six weeks, Rodgers is on pace for 4,213 yards and 34 touchdowns this season.
If he reaches those numbers, it would be his most yards in a single year since 2020 and his most touchdowns since 2021. That touchdown total would also tie Ben Roethlisberger (2018) for the most in a season in franchise history.
Considering Rodgers won MVP in both 2020 and 2021 with the Packers, that's a good omen for both him and Pittsburgh moving forward.
It is worth pointing out, though, that Rodgers has not been overly efficient. His 61.4 completion percentage is the 11th-worst among qualified passers (per Next Gen Stats ) and a pass EPA of -48.9 is the third-lowest mark under the same criteria.
Rodgers, and the Steelers' offense as a whole, must clean some things up if they want to remain in playoff contention and make noise should they get there.
Again, Rodgers hasn't been perfect, but that never should've been the expectation. He's playing at a similar level to what he showcased in 2025 and has arguably even improved with a better infrastructure around him in McCarthy's system.
As long as he keeps up his current level of play and production, Pittsburgh should feel pretty good about its chances of making it back to the postseason for a fourth straight year, and that's really all it can ask for out of Rodgers.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Have Obvious Solution to Third Down Struggles
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- After earning their first road victory of the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers have the chance to set the schedule on fire. Two straight wins improved their record to 4-2, and an international trip to Paris, France, can help them earn their fifth win of the 2026 campaign.
In order to get the victory, the Steelers have to improve in several key areas. No area is more important than getting better results on third down. Head coach Mike McCarthy said so himself during his weekly press conference. After his offense has started the season converting on just 25 of 76 third-down opportunities, McCarthy discussed the team's struggles to extend drives.
"Boy, we left some out there," he admitted. "We have to convert on third downs. I think it puts us in a different level offensively. You know, you have about four, five sets of downs that we left out there yesterday and still had a lot of opportunities."
As McCarthy continues to establish this offense's identity, he has to rely on his best players on third down. That means a switch in play calling and a focus on running back Jaylen Warren on any third down with less than six yards to gain.
McCarthy has been consistent with one message over the past few weeks, and that's his belief in running back Jaylen Warren. In back-to-back weeks, he's referred to Warren as the offense's "featured player" and "one of the hottest" backs in the NFL right now.
But Warren wasn't a featured player when third down arrived. In the first half of Week 6, the Steelers attempted to get him the ball once on third down. That attempt was an incomplete pass to Warren on a third-and-short.
In the second half, the Steelers finally found Warren on a third down, and it was a successful play. Warren picked up 16 yards on the dump-off pass from Aaron Rodgers, putting the Steelers in the red zone and helping them put three more points on the board in their fourth quarter comeback.
Moving forward, running the ball in that scenario is a focus.
"Definitely want to get the ball ran more," McCarthy said. "That's clearly a focus. But, yeah, third down - it's happened numerous weeks. And so we've got to do a better job there."
One situation where the Steelers absolutely have to run the ball on third down is near the goal line. The Steelers had a golden opportunity after cornerback Jamel Dean intercepted Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels and returned it inside the 5-yard line.
The Steelers passed twice in three plays, separated by a handoff to Warren that went for two yards. That was their only positive play of that series.
On third down, with one yard to gain for the score, Rodgers opted for a low-probability pass attempt to DK Metcalf. The pass was incomplete, stopping the clock and giving the Bucs a chance to tie the game in the final moments.
The Steelers should have given the ball to Warren on third down and trusted their best back and offensive player to get the job done.
And that, in a nutshell, is what McCarthy needs to do more. In those tough third down play calls, he has to rely on Warren and see what happens. How else are they going to improve their frustrating third down results?
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Continue to Look Like Winners With Najee Harris Decision
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to move on from Najee Harris and commit to Jaylen Warren continues to look better by the day.
Harris, who signed a one-year deal with the New York Giants in August, was released following the team's Week 5 loss to the New Orleans Saints.
Coming off a torn Achilles he suffered as a member of the Los Angeles Chargers in 2025, Harris recorded just 99 yards on 31 carries for the Giants before being let go.
Warren, on the other hand, has emerged as one of the NFL's top running backs now that he's landed an opportunity to be the Steelers' featured back . He has 460 yards and a touchdown on 84 carries over six games, along with 258 yards and a score on 21 receptions.
A first-round pick out of Alabama in the 2021 NFL Draft, Harris was supposed to be a workhorse and star-level running back for the Steelers.
To a certain extent, that came true. Harris finished his rookie season with 1,667 yards from scrimmage and 10 touchdowns.
The issue for Harris, though, has always been his lack of true explosiveness, and that was never more evident than when Warren entered the picture.
As an undrafted rookie in 2022, Warren finished with 379 yards and a touchdown on 77 carries (4.9 yards per attempt), while Harris had 1,034 yards on 272 carries (3.8 yards per attempt) with seven scores.
Then, during the 2023 campaign, Warren rushed for 784 yards and four touchdowns on 149 carries (5.3 yards per attempt). Harris, meanwhile, logged 1,035 yards and eight touchdowns across 255 carries (4.1 yards per attempt).
Pittsburgh did not pick up Harris' fifth-year option before the 2024 season, yet he remained ahead of Warren in the pecking order despite the latter being far more efficient and dynamic, both on the ground and through the air during their time sharing the backfield up to that point.
Harris posted 1,043 yards on 263 carries (4.0 yards per attempt) with six touchdowns in 2024, while Warren had 511 yards and one score on 120 carries (4.3 yards per attempt).
From there, Harris hit free agency and joined the Chargers while Warren signed a two-year, $11.904 million extension ahead of the 2025 campaign that looks like one of the biggest bargains in the league.
It's not surprising that Warren was far more efficient than Harris during their overlapping stints with the Steelers, given that the former had a smaller workload and was a prototypical change-of-pace back at 5-foot-8, while the latter fit the mold of an old-school, physical back at 6-foot-1 and a little over 230 pounds who thrived in short-yardage situations while being fed a boatload of carries.
Still, just based on the numbers and the film, it became clear very early on in Warren's career that he was the higher-upside option for Pittsburgh and offered far more dynamism than Harris ever could, both on the ground and through the air.
Harris filled his role in a viable manner, but the Steelers' opting to prioritize him so heavily over Warren, particularly in the running game, held back the offense as a whole for several years.
Pittsburgh did pivot from Harris at the right time, though, and Warren has now proven to be an elite running back.
He was excellent in 2025 with 1,291 yards and eight touchdowns from scrimmage despite Kenneth Gainwell eating into his workload quite significantly, and he's set to exceed that total by a good amount in 2026.
Over 17 games, Warren is on pace for 1,303 rushing yards and 731 receiving yards, which would come out to 2,034 yards from scrimmage.
Those numbers are a bit inflated since Rico Dowdle missed three games with a toe injury before returning in the Steelers' Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, though Warren still finished that contest with 16 touches and should command a vast majority of the workload moving forward.
If Warren does exceed 2,000 yards from scrimmage, he'd become just the third player in franchise history to accomplish that feat, joining Le'Veon Bell (2,215 in 2014) and Barry Foster (2,034 in 1992).
We're still a ways away from that becoming a reality, but it speaks to just how dominant Warren has been and further hammers home the point that Pittsburgh made the right choice to move on from Harris.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: What Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid Said About Seahawks Confirms Game Plan
full_text:
The stage is set for the No. 1 defense in the NFL to face off against the No. 1 offense in the NFL. The Seattle Seahawks will host the Kansas City Chiefs in the ultimate battle between the best offense and the best defense.
Both teams have a great amount of respect for the other, and it's clear that the Chiefs know what they're getting into.
“They’re the best in the business right now,” Reid told reporters . “Mike [Macdonald] does a nice job with the defense, and they have a good scheme; then they fly around. They believe in it, and they fly around. They aren’t a lot of hiccups on the back end. You see some teams where something goes on, and suddenly someone is popping free. You don’t see that with these guys.”
The key to holding the Chiefs' offense at bay is containing quarterback Patrick Mahomes and making sure he doesn't have the opportunity to make an explosive play.
“They’re good at every single level of the defense,” Mahomes said in a press conference. “Defensive line, linebackers, secondary, everybody, and they have a great scheme. They’re going to make you earn it every single drive, and it’s not always going to be pretty, but you have to be consistent and not push it too far, but push it enough to make plays happen.”
Mahomes recalled his past matchups against the Baltimore Ravens when Macdonald was the defensive coordinator there in 2022 and 2023. Macdonald's final game with the Ravens came in the AFC Championship, where they lost to the Chiefs.
During that game, the Ravens held the Chiefs to just 17 points, but it wasn't enough as Baltimore's offense mustered only 10 points themselves. Mahomes was able to flush the ball out of the pocket quickly to combat the quickness of the pass rushers, and that should be part of Kansas City's strategy against Seattle on Sunday Night Football.
With that previous experience, the Seahawks defense has to match the speed of the Chiefs and lock down the passing routes to ensure Mahomes throws the ball away or keeps it in his hands long enough to draw a sack.
Kickoff between the Chiefs and Seahawks is scheduled for Sunday at 5:20 p.m. PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on NBC or stream it on Peacock.

title: Why Seahawks Won't Trade for Colts Star Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are a team to keep an eye on during the weeks leading up to the NFL trade deadline on November 10, but it is very difficult to pull off a midseason deal.
While the Seahawks could be in the market for an upgrade at the running back position and Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor could be an option, the two sides are unlikely to consummate a trade.
The Colts made a bold move earlier this week by firing general manager Chris Ballard after nine seasons with the team. Ballard's departure is a sign of what could be coming down the line for the Colts as they encounter an organizational reset. They could set the future general manager up nicely by acquiring draft picks for some of their top players, including Taylor.
Their 2-4 start, including a Week 6 loss at home to the winless Tennessee Titans, suggests that Indianapolis is not ready for a deep playoff run. At the very least, they should be listening to calls for Taylor, who has been one of the best backs in the league since he made his debut in 2020.
So far this season, Taylor has 122 carries for 492 yards and seven touchdowns. He ranks sixth in rushing yards behind Jahmyr Gibbs, Derrick Henry, James Cook, Bijan Robinson and Kenneth Walker. He ranks first among all running backs in touchdowns.
If the Colts sell high, they could get a premium pick or two for Taylor if they find the right suitor.
Taylor's contract is ultimately the reason why the Seahawks are unlikely to acquire him in a trade. He has a $16.1 million cap hit this season and is under contract for the next two seasons for $44 million. The team could cut him in the offseason and save up to $11 million, but the Seahawks aren't going to trade for someone just to move on from him a few months later.
If the Seahawks weren't willing to pay Walker the three-year, $43 million contract the Chiefs offered him in the offseason, they likely won't do the same for Taylor, especially for just half a season.
For now, the Seahawks need to find a cheaper option on the running back market if they are interested in an upgrade, or they need to count on Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price to get healthier sooner rather than later.

title: Seahawks Get Positive Injury News on Zach Charbonnet From Wednesday Report
full_text:
The vibes around the Seattle Seahawks right now aren’t particularly good, but every week is an opportunity to flip the narrative and get things going again. This week starts with the injury report, and there’s at least some good stuff there. So let’s take a look, then also see what’s up with the Kansas City Chiefs as we get started preparing for week 7.
The highlight of today’s report was definitely Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting a full participation note. We were told in previous days that Zach would have a full week of practice , so it’s not earth-shattering, but it shows that there have been no setbacks. I still wouldn’t say it guarantees he plays, but it does make it much more likely. We’re going in the right direction.
Anthony Bradford (knee) was limited, although the coaches sounded far more certain about him playing against the Chiefs. Tyrice Knight (oblique) was limited too, and given Drake Thomas’s issues this would not be a good time for him to get hurt. Drew Lock (right elbow), Rashid Shaheed (hip), and Beau Stephens (knee) rounded out the limited list.
As for the players who didn’t practice at all, DeMarcus Lawrence got a rest day. Connor O’Toole (hamstring), who played one defensive snap against Denver last week, sat out too. Chazz Surratt (calf) is still working through his issues on the sideline. But the big issue now is Drake Thomas (ankle), who has now missed four straight practices .
The Chiefs don’t seem to have a lot to worry about right now either. Cyrus Allen (knee), Chamarri Conner (knee), Patrick Mahomes (knee), and Trey Smith (hip) all practiced in full, so there’s little doubt of their availability. Conner missed the first month of the season before returning two games ago, so his injury is largely left over from September.
They also got good news on Travis Kelce (ankle), who got banged up against the Chargers but was limited today. Same for L’Jarius Sneed (knee). Cooper McDonald (knee), a backup linebacker who plays sparingly, got the limited status as well. Look for all three to be ready for Sunday. That just leaves a few question marks throughout the week, but they’re significant.
Josh Simmons is out of practice with a personal matter that isn’t injury related, so I wouldn’t pay much mind to that. Jaylon Moore (concussion), starting right tackle, is a big deal and he has an uphill battle to get through protocol this week. Finally, Rashee Rice (hamstring, knee) has dubious availability with no practice today, having missed the Chargers game last week.

title: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald Weighs in on Facing 'Tremendous' Kenneth Walker
full_text:
Former Seattle Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III will return to Lumen Field on Sunday for the first time since joining the Kansas City Chiefs this past offseason.
Walker won Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks last season before signing a three-year, $43.05 million deal with the Chiefs, and he's been the best rusher in the league through six weeks. The former Seahawks second-round pick leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards and six touchdowns on 106 carries.
“He’s off to a tremendous start,” Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said on Wednesday. “The stats back it up; tape definitely backs it up. He’s playing great football.”
The Seahawks are allowing 3.9 yards per carry this season , which ranks 15th in the NFL. Walker alone is averaging 6.3 yards per carry. Something will have to give on Sunday night when the two sides clash.
Macdonald was asked about his thoughts on facing his former running back, particularly on how they hope to stop Walker.
“I love Ken. I thoroughly enjoyed him being on our football team,” Macdonald said. “We’ve had some great one-on-one [conversations]; I feel like we have a great relationship. I respect the heck out of him. Happy for him. Obviously, we have to do a great job of stopping him this week. I think there’s mixed emotions in terms of, like, you’re happy for him, but also, hey, we’re trying to figure out ways to stop this guy, too, because he’s playing at a really high level.”
The Athletic's Michael-Shawn Dugar reported on Wednesday that the Seahawks did not make an offer to Walker before free agency began. He then quickly signed with the Chiefs once the negotiating window opened. It appears Seattle didn't aggressively pursue him, maybe expecting to have more leverage.
Macdonald was asked if he wished things had worked out differently. As expected, he wasn't dwelling on it, as the Seahawks are focused on learning how to stop him.
“We appreciate the heck out of him,” Macdonald said. “He got a Super Bowl MVP, helped us win a championship. These things happen, you know? We have to move forward now, but got nothing but great things and great memories of Ken.”
The Chiefs are currently 5-0 and setting up for yet another postseason run if their success continues. Seattle, on the other hand, is hoping to avoid dropping to 3-4 after losing three of its last four games.

title: Seahawks Have Perfect Opportunity to Cut Ties With Sam Darnold in 2027
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have to be honest with themselves moving forward. While the team won a Super Bowl title with quarterback Sam Darnold, they did it under the miraculous performance of Darnold being himself while turning the ball over. The Seahawks could handle an occasional turnover from Darnold, but it has become a point where the turnovers have cost them three wins while the defense has played great.
​ Seattle might have to move on from Darnold after the 2026 NFL Season if he continues to struggle significantly. The good news is that general manager John Schneider prepared for a potential out this next offseason, which is something the team would’ve never thought was possible before this season.
​The Seahawks got Darnold to sign a three-year, $100.5 million deal shortly after offseason free agency began in March 2025. He turned the ball over 20 times, but still played at a Pro-Bowl level and was a huge reason for the Super Bowl title.
​Fast forward to this season and Darnold has regressed significantly. His QBR ranks 26th in the league at 41.9, just ahead of Minnesota’s Kyler Murray, New York Giants’ Jameis Winston and Tennessee’s Cam Ward. Darnold completed 60.4% of his passes for 1,033 yards, seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 14 times in four full games and on the opening drive of the Week 1 win versus the New England Patriots.
​It isn’t just that Darnold is turning the ball over; he is doing it in the middle or late in the fourth quarter . His turnovers have cost the Seahawks potential wins in Week 3 at the Washington Commanders, the Week 5 home game over the San Francisco 49ers and the Week 6 Thursday Night Football road game versus the Denver Broncos. It has become a point where Darnold’s bad decision-making and regression outweigh the great attributes he shows each game.
​If Darnold continues to play as he has in the last four games, the front office and the coaching staff might decide to move on. The front office created a potential next offseason where they wouldn’t take so much damage in the salary cap. Seattle would have Darnold getting a total of $41.9 million. There is a $10 million roster bonus on Mar. 16, 2027, five days after the new league year begins. ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that his 2027 contract and the bonus aren’t guaranteed .
​The Seahawks will have to hit in the salary cap in some way if they move on from Darnold. If the Seahawks cut or trade him before June 1 , the team would have a $19.2 million dead cap hit, but they would save $22.7 million. If they cut or trade him on or after June 1, the Seahawks only pay a $6.4 million dead cap in 2027, but pay $12.8 million in dead cap for the 2028 season. Seattle, however, would save $35.5 million in salary cap space.
​There are 11 games for Darnold to turn it around and show he deserves to be the starting quarterback of a Super Bowl contender like the Seahawks . The critical and game-altering mistakes he makes that causes to fall short of a victory, the more it is going to be difficult to trust and earn a wealthy contract. Darnold isn’t the only reason why the offense is failing, which includes poor play from the offensive line and a lack of an explosive run game, but he isn’t helping with his turnovers.

title: Will Zach Charbonnet Play vs. Chiefs? Seahawks RB Gets Injury Update
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet could be making his long-awaited season debut in Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald explained where Charbonnet is in his recovery process.
"Zach is going to have a full week's worth of reps, so that's exciting, and there's a possibility that you could see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that's exciting," Macdonald said via the team's website.
Charbonnet is eight months removed from surgery on his torn ACL, which would make for a quick turnaround given the history of other injuries of the same sort. He's making a true push to get back on the field as quickly as possible.
"It's remarkable," Macdonald said via the team's website.
"I know he's had a certain date in mind, which is a really ambitious date. Those who have tried to come back from a significant knee surgery understand the undertaking that it takes. Zach's a beast. He looks great. It's not easy to say, 'All right, let's go.' So for him to have that courage to say that and work through the things he's worked through, you can't do anything but tip your cap to him."
The Seahawks rank 18th in the league in rushing yards per game at just 107.2. There has not been enough consistency in the run game, and they average one fumble per contest. With six fumbles, the Seahawks lead the league in that unfortunate statistic.
Charbonnet has not lost a single fumble in his first three seasons in the league, so Seattle will be more inclined to hand him the football.
Between rookie Jadarian Price, free-agent acquisition Emanuel Wilson and third-stringer George Holani, the Seahawks haven't found a consistent rushing attack. Bringing Charbonnet on board will open up the entire offense.
Logistically speaking, Charbonnet will be added to the 53-man roster this week ahead of the game against the Chiefs. He doesn't have to play, but he will have to be on the roster. There is a chance that he will be inactive for the game, but he is officially coming off the Physically Unable to Perform list.
Charbonnet and the Seahawks are set to kick off against the Chiefs on Sunday at 5:20 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on NBC or stream it on Peacock.

title: How the Seahawks Are Serious About the Offense's Changes for Week 7
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (3-3) are taking this mini bye week seriously and utilizing the rest of the week to properly prepare for the Kansas City Chiefs (6-0) . The Seahawks showed how vulnerable the offense was with their lack of a run game, inconsistencies at the offensive line and the mental regression of quarterback Sam Darnold. Seattle has lost three of the last four games due to the serious imbalance of problems on the offensive side of the ball.
​This is a problem the Seahawks needed to address during the ten days in between the 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos and the Week 7 matchup versus the Chiefs. There is still hope the Seahawks can turn this rough stretch around, especially after the attention to the problems that was focused on.
​Head coach Mike Macdonald said after the loss to the Broncos, he’ll be at the front of the offensive meetings to indicate what the biggest concerns of the offense are . He has faith in his coaching staff and leaders to turn the tide of the offensive inefficiencies, but three losses in four games should be a cause for concern. Macdonald has also stated that he is not planning on making the change at the first-string quarterback, but his answer didn’t shut down the fact that the option is on the table.
​In terms of the actual changes to the offense, the Seahawks signed two players before full practices for Week 7. Seattle signed veteran tight end Josiah Deguara and rookie fullback Jackson Acker. They may not be household names, but they could have huge implications for how they impact the offense and how the team implements its philosophy.
​Acker is a full-time fullback with lots of starting experience at fullback and running back while in college. Acker’s signing comes as second-string fullback Brady Russell has been taking fewer reps at the position. Tight end AJ Barner has been playing a lot of the fullback position in the backfield and less as a pass-catcher at the line of scrimmage. If Acker is capable of playing and starting, he could be a reliable blocker in the run and passing game while Barner goes back to a traditional tight end.
​Deguara’s signing comes after second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo was placed on IR for the shoulder injury he suffered in the loss to Denver. In seven years in the league, Deguara has caught 53 receptions for 471 yards and three touchdowns. He could be a player the Seahawks could call up for emergencies, or he could rise up to the number three tight end behind Barner and Eric Saubert.

title: Seahawks Urged to Pursue Eagles RB Saquon Barkley in NFL Trade Deadline Move
full_text:
Through the first six games of the season , it’s been very easy to see where the Seattle Seahawks are falling short . In 2025, they were a top-10 rushing team in the NFL with 2,096 yards on the ground.
This year, they’re currently 18th and are averaging just 3.9 yards per attempt. They’re hopeful that getting Zach Charbonnet back from a torn ACL suffered in January will give them a boost, but CBS Sports’ Carter Bahns thinks the problem goes beyond that.
Bahns believes their decision not to re-sign Kenneth Walker has been the problem on offense. He referred to him as the missing piece and says the best way to fill that hole is to make a blockbuster trade with the Philadelphia Eagles for Saquon Barkley.
“He is very much the missing piece, and they will rely on Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price to fill that gap when they return from injured reserve. Neither is an established No. 1 running back, though, so Seattle would benefit from admitting it needs a high-caliber starter, then placing Charbonnet back in his more natural secondary role and allowing Price to develop as a rookie third option,” Bahns wrote.
“They would have to pay a hefty price to pry Saquon Barkley away from Philadelphia because of his immense value and his giant cap hit, but with the Eagles poised to watch this season wither away in the wake of countless personnel losses, they should be willing to at least field calls on their superstar running back. Seattle is in as much of a win-now mode as any team in the league and thus is in a position to give up premium draft capital for a player who can help it return to the Super Bowl.”
Barkley signed a two-year, $41.5 million extension ahead of the 2025 season, which has him under contract through 2028. His cap hit each year is manageable ($9.88 million in 2026, $13 million in 2027, and $17.364 million in 2028), but he has four void years on his deal. That means he will be on the books until 2032.
Philly has shown no sign it plans to move on from Barkley, but with Jalen Hurts possibly missing the entire season, there’s a chance they could look to unload salary and stockpile picks. If so, the Seahawks would be foolish not to consider bringing in Barkley.
He’s an explosive player who can do damage as a runner and receiver. It would also keep Seattle from needing to rely too heavily on Charbonnet or Price, while also taking pressure off the shoulders of Sam Darnold.

title: Week 7 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Seahawks Remain Top 10 Despite Loss to Broncos
full_text:
This hasn’t been the start the Seattle Seahawks envisioned . The defending champs suffered an overtime loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 6 and are now 3-3 on the year.
There’s still plenty of time to turn things around and make a run at the playoffs, but it’s safe to say their first six weeks have been a disappointment.
Even so, they’re still a team that’s highly regarded around the league and among media outlets. That’s evident in our Week 7 NFL power rankings roundup, which still has Seattle as a fixture in the top 10.
Connor Orr dropped the Seahawks just one spot. He believes they could see some change on offense with the return of Zach Charbonnet , which is anticipated to happen very soon.
"Zach Charbonnet is (likely) back. With a completely new offensive coordinator and similar run philosophy, we’ll see if it makes the kind of difference we expect it to," Orr wrote.
ESPN kept Seattle at No. 6, although Brady Henderson also believes the run game needs help. He also says the pass protection and ball security need to improve as well. The good news is that all of this is fixable.
"The Seahawks' run game has been underwhelming and their pass protection has been problematic, but no issue is holding first-year coordinator Brian Fleury's unit back like turnovers. It has committed 12 of them, third most of any offense so far," Henderson wrote.
Bleacher Report had a similar drop from six to nine for Seattle, and Kristopher Knox is pointing at the ground game and Sam Darnold’s interceptions as the primary reasons for concern.
"Backfield injuries have prevented the Seahawks from running the ball effectively. As a team, Seattle has averaged just 3.9 yards per carry. This has allowed opposing defenses to focus on pressuring quarterback Sam Darnold, who has been the team's other issue," Knox wrote. "With seven interceptions in less than five full games, Darnold has actively cost Seattle wins."
Ranking: 10 | Last week: 6
The Athletic is also focused on the ground game, saying their offense will struggle as long as Emanuel Wilson is the lead back. They also gave the Seahawks the lowest spot out of all these rankings, putting them at No. 10 overall.
"Why are the defending champions struggling? Because a former undrafted free agent in his fourth year of a journeyman career is their top-scoring running back (9.4 ppg). While Kenneth Walker III is carrying the Chiefs, Seattle first-round pick Jadarian Price has struggled with injuries and fumbles and is 58th in the league in rushing (119 yards) while he rehabs a chest injury on injured reserve," Josh Kendall and Chad Graff wrote.
Nate Davis dropped Seattle three spots and accurately says you can’t have Sam Darnold throw 51 times per game and expect to win.
"Can't have QB Sam Darnold throwing a career-high 51 times − and getting beaten to a pulp in the process − and expect to win. Sure would help to get injured RBs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back," Davis wrote.
The Seahawks are a team that wins with defense and a strong run game. Even though they haven’t been elite to start the 2026 season, their defense has been good enough and their ground game can become vastly improved once healthy. That’s why they’re still seen as one of the biggest threats in the NFL.

title: Seahawks Urged to Target Eagles Tight End Ahead of Trade Deadline
full_text:
This season hasn’t gotten off to an ideal start for the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Their Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football left them with a record of 3-3.
That has them in second place as the NFC West isn’t as competitive as it was a year ago, but they’re still far behind the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. They’re also entering a tough stretch with the Kansas City Chiefs and Chicago Bears as their next two opponents.
These games will be huge for the Seahawks, who need to start putting wins together. For that to happen, their offense has to improve. Seahawks On SI’s Michael Hanich believes getting tight end A.J. Barner involved in the offense would help, but they could also look for an upgrade at that position ahead of the trade deadline.
One player who may be available is Dallas Goedert, who Matt Verderame of SI says would be a fit in Seattle . Verderame admits Goedert hasn’t been the same player he once was, but that could allow Seattle to bring in an experienced veteran without surrendering a premium pick.
“Rumors have suggested the Eagles might move off Goedert as he’s aged and dealt with injuries, missing at least three games in four of the past five years. Yet, Goedert has held on, and now might be the time for Philadelphia to cut ties. Goedert is 31 years old and hasn’t had 600 yards since the 2022 season,” Verderame wrote. “He won’t bring a premium, but Goedert is a useful player with a ton of postseason experience.”
Goedert is a big target at 6-foot-5 and 256 pounds and would offer nine years of experience. This season, he has 17 receptions for 180 yards and two touchdowns. That’s more receptions, yardage, and touchdown catches than anyone on Seattle’s roster outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and he accomplished that on a struggling offense in just four games.
With Jalen Hurts potentially out for the season, the Eagles could be sellers at the deadline. That’s why Verderame also mentioned guard Landon Dickerson as a player the Seahawks should target. Dickerson would be an upgrade at right guard, and could help Sam Darnold feel more comfortable in the pocket.
Whether it’s an offensive lineman, a running back , or a pass-catcher, the Seahawks need to make a move at the deadline. If not, they’ll have a hard time catching up in their division.

title: 5 Realistic Trade Targets for the 49ers Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are expected to be buyers at the NFL trade deadline. With defensive tackle being one of their most glaring needs, who are the most likely trade options for the 49ers?
The 49ers just saw Payne up close and personal to decide if he is worth acquiring in a trade. Payne is in the last year of his deal with Washington, and they are sitting at 1-4-1. Getting something back would make sense . The former first-round pick would instantly be the 49ers' best run defender.
Sieler might cost more to acquire than Payne. He is two years older, but he is signed through the 2029 season. Getting that type of team control will require more draft capital. Sieler only had five sacks last year, but had 20 in the two years combined before that.
The 0-5 Dolphins are looking to rebuild, and the current GM and head coach did not draft Sieler. They could try to trade him while his value is still high.
The 49ers were linked to Vita Vea earlier in the offseason when he had contract issues. While Tampa Bay extended Vea, they did not add too much in guarantees to the point that he is now untradable. Tampa Bay is sitting at 1-5, and they might be firing their head coach soon.
Vea is still one of the best run defenders in the NFL and he has won a Super Bowl. That type of impact and experience would be valuable. The 49ers could try to re-open trade talks.
If the 49ers cannot pry Vea away from the Bucs, Robinson is a great consolation prize. Robinson has been as good, if not better than Vea as a run defender this year. He is a leader in the locker room. Robinson has 11 years of NFL experience. However, this veteran being on a one-year deal should make him easier to obtain in a trade.
The Colts trading for DeForest Buckner when they could have taken a quarterback with that first-round pick might end up being the reason Buckner heads back to the 49ers years later. The Colts fired the GM who made the Buckner trade. Now, the All-Pro defensive tackle is not happy with the organization and is a free agent at the end of the year. The Colts could let him leave for nothing, or they could trade him for something now.

title: 49ers Defensive End Mykel Williams Suffers Another Knee Injury
full_text:
Mykel Williams seems to have re-injured his surgically repaired knee during the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Washington Commanders.
Williams seemed fine after the game. But today, head coach Kyle Shanahan mentioned that Williams has a knee injury and listed him among the players who would not participate in Wednesday's practice. When asked if Williams' surgically repaired knee "flared up" on Monday night during the game, Shanahan said, "Just knee," meaning that's all the information he was required to divulge.
It sounds like Williams did indeed re-aggravate his knee during the game on Monday night. If Shanahan could have provided some reassuring nugget of information, he probably would have, but he didn't. He allowed us to use our imaginations, which usually is a bad sign.
Williams tore his ACL on Nov. 2 last year. He missed all of training camp and the first four games of this season as he recovered as quickly as possible. As soon as he was eligible to be activated from the Physically Unable to Perform List, the 49ers activated him. That was two weeks ago.
Since then, Williams has come off the bench as a rotational defensive lineman and played fewer than 50 percent of the time. Clearly, he was not quite ready to play, even though he recorded his second career sack on Monday against the Commanders. The 49ers were trying to manage him prudently.
And Williams still re-injured his knee. That's disconcerting.
In hindsight, the 49ers once again allowed a player to play before he should have. I'm guessing the 49ers asked Williams if he felt ready to go, and he said yes, as almost any professional football player would say. They're programmed to want to play no matter what.
That's why teams have to protect players from themselves. You've heard that cliché a million times because it's true. Teams must prevent players from making shortsighted decisions. Teams have to be the ones who consider the big picture and worry about the long haul.
The 49ers don't do a good enough job of protecting players from themselves. Just last week, the 49ers let Mike Evans play through Achilles tendinitis, and he made it worse. Earlier in the season, they let Nick Bosa return from his third ACL tear before he had completed a full practice, and he wound up injuring his calf.
When players come back too early, they often reinjure themselves. If anyone should understand that by now, it's the 49ers.
When will they realize that they have to be more careful?

title: 9 49ers Miss First Week 7 Practice Against Falcons
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers were missing nine players in their first Week 7 practice against the Atlanta Falcons. It wouldn't be a normal practice report without multiple players out for the 49ers.
Many of the players who were held out were the usual suspects. Nick Bosa (calf) is still out, but Kyle Shanahan did leave the door open for him to practice on Thursday.
Although, at this point, it's best for the 49ers to hold him out through the Bye, since it comes after this week. They might as well give Bosa all the rest he can get for the second-half push.
Mike Evans (Achilles) isn't participating, which was to be expected after he exited the game on Monday night. He's dealing with Achilles tendinitis, so the 49ers need to be extra careful with him.
Evans should never have played against the Washington Commanders. He didn't participate in a single practice for that game because of his Achilles.
Yet the 49ers thought it was okay to trot him out there. Achilles injuries should always be treated with extreme caution. It's malpractice by the 49ers, especially since they dealt with this two years ago with Christian McCaffrey.
They should know better. Now, they will most likely play without Evans against the Falcons. I wouldn't expect him to be ready for Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders either.
Without Evans, the 49ers will rely on Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, and veteran Brandin Cooks. Brock Purdy is going to need to turn nothing into something with these receivers .
As for the rest of the players who missed practice: Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Luke Gifford (groin), Garrett Wallow (hamstring), Siran Neal (knee), Marques Sigle (ankle), Upton Stout (shoulder), and Mykel Williams (knee).
Samuel, Gifford, Wallow, and Sigle aren't a surprise. Neither is Stout. He left the game on Monday night because of his injury.
Williams, however, is a surprise for missing practice. The 49ers held him out because of a knee issue, but you have to wonder if it's soreness from back-to-back intense weeks.
Remember, Bosa dealt with knee soreness in training camp after intensifying his workload. The same could be happening to Williams
In any case, this is worth monitoring throughout the week, along with Stout's shoulder injury. So long as both players practice on Friday, they'll be good to go against the Falcons.

title: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey Hits New Rushing TD Milestone After Week 6 Win
full_text:
After six weeks, the San Francisco 49ers' touchdown leader is running back Christian McCaffrey.
Is it a surprise? Not really.
Despite seeing his workload reduced , McCaffrey has recorded seven rushing touchdowns, leading the franchise. Most, if not all, have come from short-range situations, typically between two and five yards out.
Let's be honest, keeping him fresh for those crucial goal-line carries is a smart move, especially given his ability to power through multiple defenders and find the end zone.
Against the Washington Commanders in Week 6 , McCaffrey recorded two as the 49ers won 23-17. It was a closer game than they wanted after an impressive start, but a win is a win.
At the time of writing, this week is especially significant for McCaffrey as he was traded by San Francisco four years ago. In that time, he's secured 55 touchdowns in total, from 54 games, which puts him in ninth on the franchise's all-time list.
But after two rushing touchdowns in Week 6, he's on 37 for the franchise, which places him fifth all time.
5. Christian McCaffrey (37 - Tied with J.D. Smith and Steve Young)
It would come as little surprise if McCaffrey overtakes Roger Craig before he retires, given his continued importance to San Francisco's offense. Despite a slight drop-off in explosiveness, he remains a key figure in the 49ers' running game.
His impact extends far beyond the end zone, though. With 34 games in which he's recorded at least 100 yards from scrimmage as a 49er, he ranks fourth in franchise history, behind Jerry Rice (70), Gore (66) and Craig (50).
His all-around ability was also on display after recording 64 rushing yards and 53 receiving yards, marking the 39th game of his career with at least 50 yards in both categories. That puts him second in NFL history, just two games behind Marshall Faulk’s record of 41. He's also two games behind Craig to equal the franchise record.
It is increasingly difficult to imagine McCaffrey's career ending without a place in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. His versatility as both a runner and receiver sets him apart. But to be so high up in franchise history just four years after joining is even more incredible.

title: One Trade Deadline Move the 49ers Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are expected to be buyers at the trade deadline. While trading for Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle A’Shawn Robinson is not the flashiest move the team can make, it is the smartest.
To start, the 49ers could use a wide receiver and an edge rusher. However, while both positions are thin, they are both expected to get significant starters back. Christian Kirk, Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel, and De’Zhaun Stribling could all be back in the lineup four weeks from now.
On the edge, they already got Mykel Williams back from injury, and Nick Bosa is expected to be back any week. However, they are not going to get Alfred Collins back this year, and run defense was already a weakness.
The 49ers currently rank 29th in success rate allowed on the ground. Because they lead in games and teams have to throw, it has not cost them. However, in tight playoff games, this flaw is big enough to end their season .
They have to make a move, and Robinson makes the most sense. Most fans will want DeForest Buckner or Daron Payne. Those are big names, but they come with big price tags. Both are free agents after the year as well.
So, the 49ers can trade a notable draft pick and pay a decent chunk of their salary for a run at the playoffs. However, Robinson might bring exactly what the 49ers need, and he can do it a fraction of the cost.
Gracen Halton and Osa Odighizuwa are great pass rushers. They both struggle against the run. They do not need Buckner or Payne to replace one of them. They need a complementary run defender to take them off the field when they are not needed.
Buckner or Payne would limit the progress of Halton. Robinson would put Halton in better positions to succeed while maintaining a high snap count.
This season, Payne has eight run stops and a 7.8% stop rate. Buckner has seven run stops and a 6.7% stop rate. Robinson has seven run stops and a 9.7% stop rate. The difference is that Buckner has 19 pressures, Payne has 17, and Robinson has seven.
If San Francisco needed a game-changing starter or impact pass rusher, those options make a lot of sense. Their biggest issue is depth and run defense. When it comes to cost, fit, and need, Robinson checks every box.

title: Why a Wide Receiver Trade Won’t Significantly Help the 49ers
full_text:
If the San Francisco 49ers showed up to a doctor's office, most of their wide receivers would be in the waiting room.
It’s been gnarly to see the injury stockpile at the position. It’s only gotten worse in the last two weeks, with Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Mike Evans (Achilles) joining the waiting room.
With their top two receivers out, it’s driven 49ers fans to further demand for a wide receiver trade . It was already being advocated beforehand, but now it’s been exacerbated.
The 49ers will rely on Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, and Brandin Cooks, who just signed the other week, in Week 7. It doesn’t get more desperate than that.
However, a wide receiver trade won’t significantly help the 49ers.
For starters, Samuel and Demarcus Robinson, who have played key roles, will most likely return in the next few weeks. One of those weeks will be spent on their Bye, so it doesn’t make much sense to trade for a wideout when they’ll be fully fit soon.
But let’s say the 49ers could really use an addition to boost them. It sounds great in theory until you realize there aren’t any big-time receivers available to trade for.
Who on earth are the 49ers going to bring in? Jerry Jeudy is one player who’s been suggested as a target, but he just led the Cleveland Browns in receiving this week.
I doubt he’s going anywhere, especially after the Browns just beat the Baltimore Ravens. Trading for Jauan Jennings would be helpful since the 49ers know he’s a fit and won’t take long to adapt.
But he’s not going to significantly change the 49ers’ offense. That leaves Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. He is the only one with the potential to significantly help, but the last time he was impactful was two years ago.
If the Jaguars thought he was sweet, they’d use him more. The fact that they don’t is telling. And with the few chances he’s gotten, he’s wasted them.
Maybe he’ll suddenly pick it up and be the impactful, promising player from his rookie season. But that’s a stretch. This is probably the real version of him.
In any case, he’s a top receiver in the trade market. Multiple teams will be interested in him, like the Las Vegas Raiders, Pittsburgh Steelers, and the Kansas City Chiefs, which means the cost to trade for him will increase.
Will the 49ers be willing to get into a bidding war for Thomas? Better yet, should they? I don’t think so. I doubt anyone will look back and say, “If only the 49ers had Brian Thomas Jr.”
Passing on him will not be a regretful move. Passing on any wide receiver will not be a regretful move. This isn't 2019 where the 49ers can pluck a sweet veteran like Emannuel Sanders again.
The wide receiver market isn't robust. They won't find anyone who can significantly help them, but there are options that can give them a bit of a boost.
It's a reality everyone must accept.

title: 4 Trades the 49ers Must Consider Before the Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than three weeks away.
That means the San Francisco 49ers need to lay out any possible trades that they could make, and I have some ideas that will work. Here are the four trades the 49ers must consider before the deadline.
I’ve been pounding the table for the 49ers to go save Khalil Mack from the Los Angeles Chargers for weeks. And now that the Chargers are still winless on their Bye, it makes for the perfect time to try.
Adding an edge rusher is the best move the 49ers can make at any other position. Even with Nick Bosa returning, they can’t bank on him to remain healthy for the rest of the season.
And if he is, it’ll make adding Mack much sweeter. They’ll have Bosa and Mack complementing each other and can rotate rookie Romello Height to keep them fresh. This trade makes too much sense for them to attempt.
If an edge rusher isn’t available, then the 49ers should pivot to the interior, paving the way for them to reunite with DeForest Buckner . The Indianapolis Colts are in a free fall after firing General Manager Chris Ballard.
They’re likely headed for a fire sale, especially after Buckner’s postgame comments in Week 6. Reuniting with Buckner would be a perfect story with the 49ers trending towards a Super Bowl appearance.
Buckner will allow the 49ers to be a destructive defensive front from the inside and out. They will create a lethal trio of Buckner, Osa Odighizuwa, and rookie Gracen Halton. That alone is enticing to make a reality.
Adding a player on the defensive line shouldn’t be the only trade the 49ers should consider. Given the shakiness of the wide receiver position with all of the injuries, the 49ers should consider bringing Jauan Jennings back.
He could be on the way out of Minnesota after he was visibly upset on the sidelines in Week 5. The Vikings have been looking to add receivers, which means Jennings is the odd man out.
He’s not going to significantly boost the offense, but he’ll provide a sizable impact and dependability that they don’t have right now. Plus, it won’t take him long to acclimate to the offense, and he should come at a low cost.
If the 49ers aren’t interested in another reunification, then they should look at Brian Thomas Jr. He’s been completely phased out from the Jacksonville Jaguars, with this last week being the exclamation point.
Thomas and the Jaguars need a split. He hasn’t been anywhere close to his impact from his rookie season. Perhaps the 49ers can bring that back out of him. Thomas has solid route-running ability to fit.
The main concern would be his mentality. Is he tough enough to be a fit for the 49ers? If he is and comes at a reasonable cost, then the 49ers should take a flyer on him and see if he can significantly boost them this year and become part of their future core.

title: The Biggest Overreaction From 49ers Week 6 Win vs. Commanders
full_text:
It wasn't pretty by any means, but the San Francisco 49ers got the job done against the Washington Commanders on Monday night, 23-17.
One reason the game got out of hand was that the 49ers were missing Mike Evans . He left the game with roughly two minutes left in the first half after hurting his Achilles on his third catch.
The 49ers wisely kept him out of the rest of the game. Evans dealt with Achilles soreness all week. That's why he didn't participate in any of the practices leading up to this game.
Evans will most likely miss Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons, rendering the 49ers desperate at wide receiver. His injury has led 49ers fans to further advocate for a blockbuster wide receiver trade.
While I understand the sentiment, it's a complete overreaction to the situation after their Week 6 win. Yes, things have certainly changed a bit with Evans' Achilles injury.
The wide receiver position is in a desolate spot, causing a knee-jerk reaction from fans to advocate for the 49ers to make a trade.
However, as I explained in a previous article, the 49ers don't need a blockbuster wide receiver trade . All of the players who are currently hurt are not lost for the season.
If that were the case, then by all means, make a trade. It would be malpractice for the 49ers not to make something happen with a couple more receivers out for the year.
But they're getting all of these players back in a few weeks. What's the point of making a trade for a wide receiver now?
Let's say the 49ers executed a trade at this very moment. That receiver will need time to acclimate to the 49ers' offense, which isn't easy.
How long will that take? At least a few games, probably, right? By that time, the 49ers will have Samuel and Robinson back. Evans might be fully fit by then, too.
So, this idea of needing a receiver isn't sound. At that point, it's basically saying the 49ers never had adequate talent at the position outside of Evans.
Meaning, the 49ers didn't do a great job addressing the position in the offseason. You can point to injuries and even mention Ricky Pearsall.
But Pearsall has always been an injury risk, so his absence isn't a surprise or detrimental. Even Evans' injury is expected, given his age and the mileage on his body.
This is the risk the 49ers took and were willing to take. For the most part, it's been working out perfectly fine. They have more than enough to continue to soar on offense.

title: 10 Winners and Losers From 49ers Week 6 Win vs. Commanders
full_text:
Defeating the Washington Commanders was a lot tougher than it should've been for the San Francisco 49ers . But they got it done nonetheless.
Some 49ers will love their performance in this game, while others will want to forget it. That said, here are the 10 winners and losers from the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Commanders.
What a performance from Malik Mustapha . He was the hero of this game, making back-to-back stops in the second-to-last series with the game on the line.
Mustapha could've folded under the pressure of those moments, but he met it head-on. He's been a wrecking ball ever since he started receiving playing time.
If Dre Greenlaw is the enforcer, then Mustapha is his second in command. It's safe to say he's cemented himself as the starter for the rest of the season.
Brock Purdy delivers another excellent performance. This time, he does it in primetime with the entire nation watching him. The bright lights never scare Purdy.
If anything, he thrived on it when he was lighting up the Commanders like a Christmas tree in the first half. Purdy simmered down in the second half, but he was balling nonetheless.
A major reason why Purdy was balling is that the offensive line kept him clean. Purdy was sacked twice but was only pressured six times on 34 dropbacks. That's nuts.
One of the sacks was a missed assignment, not an outright lost matchup. They also blocked really well in the run game. This group is the best one on the 49ers, and it isn't even close. They're elite.
The 49ers had done a great job in limiting Christian McCaffrey's workload this season, but against the Commanders, his heavy usage was required.
McCaffrey took 16 carries and nine receptions, which was desperately needed. The 49ers were lacking receivers, especially once Mike Evans exited the game.
A performance is a reminder that McCaffrey still has it. He's not the super explosive player he once was, but when the 49ers need him, he can carry a bulk of the offense.
Evans was off to an amazing start in this game with three catches for 94 yards. Unfortunately, he injured his Achilles on his final catch, which had been an issue for him all week.
Thankfully, Evans didn't suffer an Achilles tear. That's why he's a "winner." It could've been much worse. He'll most likely miss Week 7, but if that's all, it feels like the 49ers scored a win.
The first-half game plan for the 49ers was sensational. Everything Kyle Shanahan called was working perfectly. Yet for some reason, he didn't change it up in the second half when Evans left the game.
Shanahan got incredibly pass-happy in the second half. On the 49ers' second and third drives of that half, Shanahan called six straight passes. That's insane.
The running game was working well, and they needed to drain the clock with a two-score lead. His play calling allowed the Commanders to make it a close game. He must be better.
This was by far the worst performance of the season for Renardo Green. He can afford it since the 49ers won, and he's been phenomenal in every game before this.
But man, did he struggle. From busting coverages to committing a penalty, he looked like his 2025 version. Hopefully, this was just a one-off, and he bounces back next week.
With Mustapha playing lights out, he's making it impossible for Marques Sigle to get his starting job back. There's no telling if he'll see the field again, barring an injury to another player.
It's brutal for Sigle, as he was playing really well before his high ankle sprain. Unfortunately, this is part of the game. You miss time, another player shines in your place, and you're never seen again.
It feels like every game there is at least one blunder from Jacob Cowing. Against the Commanders, he did it as a punt returner when he decided to field punts around the five-yard line.
The 49ers have told Cowing he needs to let the ball hit the ground so it can bounce into the end zone. He's clearly not listening, which means it's only a matter of time before he loses his spot.
Another player who could lose his spot soon is kicker Eddy Pineiro. He has the yips, which is only fitting for a 49ers kicker.
I don't know if Pineiro caught lightning in a bottle last year and this is who he really is, but the 49ers can't continue like this. He's going to cost them a game if this doesn't get corrected soon.

title: How the 49ers Feel About Their 6-0 Start to the Season
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers sit atop the NFC standings after securing their sixth consecutive win of the season against the Washington Commanders.
Despite dealing with injuries, the 49ers have remained undefeated and hold the best record in the conference. They are 3-0 in the NFC West, having secured wins over the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, and the Los Angeles Rams, who went into this season as the Super Bowl favorites.
It's been a hugely successful start to the season for San Francisco. The 49ers have shown plenty of strengths despite dealing with a string of injuries , overcoming concerns so far that their injury-hit roster could derail their season.
Despite the challenges, the 49ers have continued to deliver results and exceed expectations through the opening weeks of the season. Their impressive start has drawn reactions from coaches and players, who have shared their thoughts on the 100% win record.
"I feel good that we just won a game. I mean, 6-0 is better than any other options in your record, but definitely, I feel good when the year's over and you're the last team to win the last game of the year. So, I'll wait until that moment," shared Kyle Shanahan.
"Yeah. A win is a win. You know, they're hard to come by and no game is given to you," added Trent Williams. "We had a lot of guys go down. They did as well. So it's not an excuse, but I think we were just a hair off a couple of plays where we could have kept the drive alive. And ultimately we could have probably ended the game on our terms."
“Of course, 6-0, fantastic,” stated Fred Warner. “We’re gonna still continue to chase progression. You don’t want to just be a 6-0, you want to be a team that’s on the rise.”
It's the r ight mentality to have . The 49ers have often appeared focused on the ultimate goal of reaching the Super Bowl, but last season brought a shift in mindset. Rather than looking too far ahead, the focus turned to taking each game as it came and ensuring every player fulfilled their responsibilities to the best of their ability.
Of course, the ultimate goal has to be winning the Super Bowl. The 49ers are one of the biggest franchises in the league for a reason, so expectations will always be high. However, the key is to focus on performing at their best, winning each game, and taking it one step at a time until they achieve their ultimate goal.
