title: Buccaneers Hit With Multiple Surprise Injuries
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have shown some fight over the past couple of weeks, but ultimately are still struggling as they sit 1-5 on the season.
Despite their struggles, the Bucs can still make up for it, considering they haven't reached division play. That starts this week when they head to Carolina to take on the Panthers.
It will undoubtedly be an uphill battle for them, and things might be a bit tougher than usual as they had numerous players show up on the injury report midweek.
Per the Bucs' official injury report , the Bucs saw multiple key players miss Wednesday's practice, including wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), Bucky Irving (illness), Zyon McCollum (illness), Luke Goedeke (calf) and Christian Rozeboom (finger).
The Bucs are dealing with injuries, but it also appears that some kind of sickness has made its rounds through the locker room. Outside of Irving and McCollum, Riley Dixon Calijah Kancey, and Chase McLaughlin all had illness designations but participated in some sort of fashion.
The hope is that the illness is able to subside as the week progresses towards game time, but the more serious concern is undoubtedly that of Egbuka and Goedeke's respective injuries.
The Tampa Bay offense has already been suspect to begin the season, and losing one of your top wideouts and starting right tackle would be detrimental to them trying to keep pace with the Panthers' offense, which has shown that they can put up points.
On a positive note, however, Baker Mayfield appears ready to return from his dislocated thumb, and the likes of Sean Tucker and Benjamin Morrison have returned from their injuries that kept them out against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Antoine Winfield Jr. also logged a limited practice as he recovers from his rib injury.
It would be hard-pressed to say that Winfield Jr. would make his return even if he logs limited practices the rest of the week. However, I would fully expect to see Tucker and Morrison back in the fold for their respective sides of the ball.
The real question will come down to whether or not the Bucs and Mayfield are on the same page on him returning after logging his first full practice back. If Mayfield is able to continue logging full practices through the rest of the week, one would imagine he would be behind center come Sunday. If not, or if the medical staff doesn't give the full clearance, then we could see Jalon Daniels make his fourth consecutive start.

title: How Baker Mayfield Looked Throwing at Buccaneers Practice Today
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have played backup quarterback Jalon Daniels for the last three weeks. They've been without incumbent starter Baker Mayfield since he dislocated his thumb against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3, but they likely won't be without him for much longer.
Mayfield returned to practice on Wednesday, marking his first one since Sept. 25. He arrived after the team stretched and started doing drills with the other quarterbacks — but how did he look in his first practice back?
BucsGameday was live at One Buccaneer Place to watch practice. Here's what we saw during our limited window:
Mayfield participated in practice with a white glove on his throwing hand. He did handoff drills first, opting to hand off with his left hand as opposed to his injured right hand, but he quickly started throwing during the latter half of the practice window.
There did not seem to be anything noticeably off about the way Mayfield threw the football. He was working with wideouts and tight ends like Chris Godwin and Bauer Sharp during this throwing period, and he didn't appear to struggle with accuracy or velocity during the practice window.
Baker Mayfield is back at practice today for the Bucs! He was wearing a white glove on his injured hand, but he was practicing and throwing today. #Buccaneers #GoBucs pic.twitter.com/bxSZuAt9SO
Mayfield also participated in ball security drills while holding the ball during practice. Mayfield has already struggled with that so far this season, fumbling the football three times in Week 1, but his injured hand could make it even more difficult to hold the football if he does end up playing on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers.
It's unclear if Mayfield will go on Sunday, but if he can, the Bucs will really want him to. Tampa Bay is playing the Panthers, who lead the division at the moment with a 3-2 record. Tampa Bay is 2.5 games back from Carolina — a win keeps the Bucs alive in the division and a playoff berth, while a loss would put them 3.5 games out from Carolina and see them fading fast.
The Bucs have not determined who is starting yet against the Panthers. That should become clearer on Thursday, when either Mayfield or Daniels will speak to the media ahead of Sunday's NFC South matchup.

title: Buccaneers' Wednesday Practice Brings Huge Update for Baker Mayfield
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers took a loss last Sunday to the Pittsburgh Steelers, which put the team at 1-5. That loss happened without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, but it looks like the Bucs won't be without Mayfield for long.
The Buccaneers held practice on Wednesday as they prepare to face the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, and Mayfield officially returned to practice. It's his first appearance at Bucs practice since Week 3, but that doesn't necessarily mean he'll play football on Sunday.
Mayfield returned to practice on Wednesday. His participation was likely limited, but he was seen out on the practice field as he continues to figure out how well he can grip the football after dislocating his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. He was wearing a white glove on his throwing hand.
Baker Mayfield is back at practice today for the Bucs! He was wearing a white glove on his injured hand, but he was practicing and throwing today. #Buccaneers #GoBucs pic.twitter.com/bxSZuAt9SO
Quarterback Jalon Daniels has subbed in for Mayfield while Mayfield has been out. Daniels, a rookie UDFA out of Kansas, has played admirably while deputizing Mayfield, throwing for 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions (one of which was a hail-mary pick at the end of that Vikings game).
That being said, the Bucs signed Mayfield to a three-year extension worth around $55 million this offseason, so he's the quarterback the Bucs expect to lead them into the future. Before getting hurt in Week 3, Mayfield had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions.
Daniels started against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and head coach Todd Bowles told the media on Monday that the team would initially prepare as if Daniels were starting. This is a very likely game for Mayfield to come back for, however, and it will be arguably the team's most important game of the year against an NFC South leader they're currently 2.5 games back on. With that in mind, the Bucs will have to make a decision between a healthy Daniels and a recovering Mayfield.
Mayfield rarely misses football games. The last NFL game he missed to injury before he got hurt against the Vikings was in 2022, when he missed two games with a high-ankle sprain while playing for the Carolina Panthers. If he can get healthy quickly, he may not miss much more time in Tampa Bay.
The Bucs will face the Panthers at 1 p.m. on Oct. 25 in Charlotte in hopes of moving to 2-5 and keeping their already-struggling season alive.

title: Why a Buccaneers Loss Against the Panthers Would End Their Playoff Hopes
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers haven't played very good football this season. They've started 1-5, and although the defense is slowly getting better, the offense hasn't caught up. The Bucs haven't won a game at home and currently hold the worst record in the NFC.
Because of all that, the team has arguably the most important game on its schedule already. The Bucs are set to play the division rival Carolina Panthers, and while all NFC South games are important, this game could be the game that sets Tampa Bay back on the path to contention — or so far down the depths that they cannot climb back up.
Here's why a Tampa Bay loss to Carolina could end their season just eight weeks into the year:
The math isn't in favor for Tampa Bay with a loss against Carolina in multiple respects.
The first? Their record would be 1-6 were they to fall to the Carolina Panthers, and history would bury them. No NFL team has ever made the playoffs after a 1-6 start, with only four teams at 1-5 ever moving on to the postseason. The Buccaneers could be the first, of course, but the chance that they make the playoffs would become nigh impossible.
The NFC South is an easy division, though, so Tampa Bay does have that on its side — unless it loses. The Bucs are playing the Panthers on Sunday, and the Panthers lead the NFC South with a 3-2 record. The Bucs are 2.5 games out of first place, but naturally, a Panthers win puts them 3.5 games out of first place. That wouldn't be absolutely impossible to overcome, but it put Carolina at a massive advantage heading into the rest of the year.
No season is truly over just seven games in. But Tampa Bay has struggled tremendously ever since the season began, and there hasn't been much hope outside of the Dallas Cowboys game the Bucs won that they'll get anything going anytime soon.
The Bucs play the Panthers at 1 p.m. in Charlotte, North Carolina on Oct. 25. A win keeps them in the fight — a loss may see the season slip away for good.

title: Could Baker Mayfield Miss Another Buccaneers Game?
full_text:
The NFL season is a roller coaster.
The Bucs had high expectations coming into the 2026 season. Those expectations quickly went by the wayside when starting quarterback Baker Mayfield — fresh off signing a massive new contract just before the season began — looked as bad as we've ever seen him in Tampa. His turnovers, poor timing and inaccuracy downfield played a big role in the team's disastrous 0-4 start.
Mayfield dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand on the final play of the team's Week 4 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and things appeared to be going from bad to worse.
That was until undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels surprised everyone by taking two quality teams to the wire in two consecutive weeks, highlighted by a standout performance in the Bucs' first win of the season against the Cowboys in Dallas on Thursday Night Football.
But just when some optimism began to creep back into the minds of the Buccaneers' faithful following that elusive victory, Daniels came back down to earth in a big way vs. the Steelers this past Sunday.
Despite a solid first half, he completely fell apart in the second half, going 8-for-20 passing while also throwing two interceptions. That ultimately allowed the Steelers to erase a 13-point fourth-quarter deficit to win the game.
So now, as the roller coaster that has been the Buccaneers' season takes yet another turn, it seems as though at this point, most people would prefer to see Mayfield back under center as soon as possible.
But when will that happen?
This weekend, the Buccaneers will face off against the Carolina Panthers, their first NFC South matchup of the year. The fact that the Bucs have six divisional games remaining means that, as unlikely as it may seem, there is still technically a chance that Tampa Bay could turn its season around.
On Monday, Todd Bowles was asked about what he needs to see from Mayfield, who continues to work his way back from his thumb injury, before he declares him ready to resume his role as the Bucs' starting quarterback.
"He's supposed to practice Wednesday," Bowles said. "We're going to take a good look at him there and then we'll kind of evaluate him during the week and see how he does."
Bowles was then asked if the team will be preparing as if Daniels will start.
"I think you have to," Bowles said. "Both will be in the meetings…Obviously, both will be in the meetings. We'll see how the week goes before we decide who it is."
Bowles was extremely vague about Mayfield's status heading into this game, so unfortunately, we don't have any clear information to work from. That being said, it wouldn't be advantageous to his football team in any way to disclose whether or not Mayfield will be available so early in the week.
Based on Bowles' comments this week, it does seem as though there is a legitimate chance that Mayfield will not be ready in time for this game against the Panthers, but no one outside of the building really knows. And if Mayfield does end up playing, then it's probably a good thing that his opponent isn't sure yet, either.

title: Buccaneers NFC South Update: How Far Back is Tampa Bay After Week 6?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 1-5 on Sunday after a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, and with just six games played, they're already right on the edge of a lost season.
Only four teams have ever made the playoffs on a 1-5 start in NFL history. Tampa Bay started the season 0-4, and only one team in NFL history has ever made the playoffs off that — their win against the Dallas Cowboys helped a bit, but another loss could plunge them too far down to make it up.
The Bucs face a weak division in the NFC South, though, which could be keeping their playoff hopes alive. What does the competition look like in the division? Are the Bucs close enough to claw their way back to the top, even at 1-5?
Here's what the NFC South looks like six weeks in:
As it stands, the Buccaneers are the worst team in the NFC — the Washington Commanders also have one win, but they have a tie as well, putting them ahead of Tampa Bay. The Bucs drop to 1-5 on the year after losing to the Steelers and, unbelievably, are one of three NFC South teams that have not won at home. The Bucs are still just two and a half games back from the Panthers, so they have time to string some wins together.
The Carolina Panthers remain at the head of the division after a win over the Philadelphia Eagles. The Panthers are the only team in the NFC South with a winning record, and they've played one less game than everyone else in the division because they've already had their bye week. They're the only NFC South team with a positive point differential and the only NFC South team that has won a game at home this season.
The Falcons were at one point 2-2 on a two-game win streak, but they've since developed a two-game losing streak and just fell to the Chicago Bears. The Falcons remain second in the division because they have an NFC South win over the New Orleans Saints already this year.
The Saints are third in the division behind Tampa Bay. They got a win on Sunday, defeating the New York Giants, so they're back in the win column and moved up in the standings after falling below Tampa Bay last week. The Falcons and Saints have the same record, but New Orleans falls behind because they've lost to the Falcons this year in a divisional matchup.
The Bucs and Panthers play each other next Sunday for Tampa Bay's first divisional matchup. The Falcons play the red-hot San Francisco 49ers, while the Saints will play the Steelers in Paris.

title: The Buccaneers’ Sack Leader Is On The Bench, And That Has To Stop
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 1-5 on Sunday with a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, giving them sole possession of the worst record in the NFC. There have been a few reasons why Tampa Bay has fallen behind this season, and the pass rush is certainly one of them.
The Buccaneers rank 31st in pressure rate and 23rd in sack rate, per Sumersports. Their pass rush has been considerably lacking once again, despite bringing in two edge rushers in first-round pick Rueben Bain Jr. and free agent Al-Quadin Muhammad.
There's one edge rusher the Bucs have on the roster that has been shining, though. He's been getting an increased number of snaps every week because of his play — but should he be getting even more snaps than he is?
The Buccaneers drafted David Walker in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. He tore his ACL that year in training camp and did not play, so this year is his first bit of NFL action. And boy, is he making the most of it.
Walker has indisputably been Tampa Bay's best pass rusher this year so far. He has a 28% pressure rate on 50 snaps, with the next highest player on the team being linebacker Alex Anzalone at 10.4% — the next highest defensive lineman is Calijah Kancey at 10.1%, and the next highest edge rusher is Anthony Nelson at 7.1%.
Walker's snaps have been steadily increasing each game, and he had the third-most snaps of the team's edge rushers against the Pittsburgh Steelers. But there's a very good argument he should be starting for the Buccaneers, as the team's two starters, Bain and Yaya Diaby, both have a pressure rate of just 6.6% and have just one sack between the two of them.
Head coach Todd Bowles isn't quite ready to commit to Walker starting, though. When asked about Walker on Monday, he said that the amount of snaps Walker can get from game to game are gameplan dependent.
"Yeah, game plan-wise, we ramp it up every week – he's been playing that well," Bowles said. "We give him the plays we can give him, but it's been ramped up every week. Depending on the game plan and what the other team does and personnel-wise, you want to see him get more reps in there. We intend to do that, but sometimes it doesn't work out that way depending on the game."
The Bucs are 1-5 and are already on the brink of oblivion (if they aren't there already). A solid pass rush can be the difference-maker when it comes to beating teams, and Walker gives the Bucs the best chance to have one so far this season. He's been playing more and more every week, but at this point, with how much better he's been playing than anyone else in the edge room, he should be starting.
The Bucs will face off against the Carolina Panthers in a crucial division game next Sunday. When they do, it will be interesting to see how much participation Walker has in the game, especially after his performance against the Steelers in Week 6.

title: Mike Evans Explains Why He Left Buccaneers for 49ers in Free Agency
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 1-5 this season after dropping their most recent game to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. It's the first season they've played in 12 years without wide receiver Mike Evans, who became a franchise legend with the Bucs throughout his tenure in Tampa Bay.
Evans, though? He joined up with the San Francisco 49ers in free agency this offseason, and the move has certainly paid off so far. The 49ers are undefeated at 5-0 and Evans is producing, with 24 receptions for 326 yards and three touchdowns so far this year.
Evans recently spoke on the reason why he made his move to the 49ers, and while his comments about the Bucs aren't outwardly said, he certainly seemed to imply a few things about Tampa Bay and where it's at as an organization.
Evans said in an interview with KNBR that he feels "rejuvenated" by his time in San Francisco, but there are a few other things of note he talked about that are interesting.
“This team rejuvenated me and probably added a few more years to my career," Evans said, per the Tampa Bay Times' Rick Stroud. "They had everything I needed and checked every box. They’re trying to win now. The quarterback, great skill players, great defense, great coaching staff, and lastly, a great organization.”
The Bucs are not directly mentioned here. However, he says that the 49ers "had everything he needed and checked every box", and that San Francisco is "trying to win now" — it isn't hard to assume that Evans could be implying that Tampa Bay did not have those things at the time that he left the organization in the offseason.
There are plenty of reasons Evans could have left Tampa Bay. He was likely set to get a decreased target share with players like Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan on the roster. The 49ers had certainly been more successful over the long term than the Bucs were, and he'd simply played for the Bucs for a very long time and could have been looking for a change at the tail end of his career.
There certainly seemed to be a few things left unsaid in how he described the 49ers in this interview. But whatever the reason, Evans is not a Buccaneers player anymore. In his absence, Tampa Bay has failed to establish a true No. 1 wide receiver, and while the offense has a multitude of problems, they certainly have suffered for it.
The Bucs won't play the 49ers this season unless both teams make it to the playoffs. That's looking almost impossible for Tampa Bay right now, and they desperately need to win their upcoming Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers next Sunday to stay alive in the NFC South.
Evans and the 49ers will play an NFC South team of their own when they face the Atlanta Falcons on the road at 1 p.m. in Week 7.

title: Aaron Rodgers Calls Out Raymond James Stadium After Beating Buccaneers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to the Pittsburgh Steelers 26-19 on Sunday, moving down to 1-5 on the year. The Bucs held the edge throughout the half, but the Steelers turned it around and gave Tampa Bay another close loss, this time in overtime.
The Steelers were led by quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who will go down as one of the best to ever play the game. Rodgers has played in Raymond James Stadium a few times over the years, and while this will almost certainly be the last time, he had a parting shot for the stadium in his post-game press conference.
Rodgers may have gotten the win, but he made his displeasure known about a certain aspect of playing football in Tampa Bay.
Rodgers told Steelers media after the game that he thought the playing surface at Raymond James Stadium is one of the worst in the NFL.
"It's gotta be one of the worst surfaces in the league," Rodgers said Sunday. "We're talking about player safety. I'm very thankful to not get hurt — I've gotten hurt twice on this field, in my opinion, because of this turf. I know USF plays here, I believe. That surface, you know, I don't think it's very safe."
#Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers calls out Raymond James Stadium for being “one of the worst surfaces in the league.” pic.twitter.com/Rc2eaJOGR3
The evidence from the last NFLPA report card backs up Rodgers' claim. In the anonymous survey, the Buccaneers' field was ranked F-, tied for worst in the NFL. Five teams earned an F- — three of them were turf, and the only other grass field was, ironically, the Steelers' Acrisure Stadium.
As Rodgers mentioned, USF playing its home games at the stadium the day before probably contributes in a big way to this problem. The turf also often hosts bowl games, too, so it gets a lot of use from teams that are not the Buccaneers.
Rodgers has played on that field at Raymond James Stadium seven times against the Buccaneers. He's 3-4 after his win on Sunday, and it will likely be the last time he ever plays in the stadium.
The Bucs won't be playing on that field next Sunday, as they'll play their first NFC South rivalry game of the year when they face off against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte.

title: The Best and Worst Position Groups in the Bucs' 26-19 Steelers Loss
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost another matchup, this time in overtime against the Pittsburgh Steelers. There was a lot of good and bad in this one, with certain groups doing much better than others.
Let's go over the grades for the Bucs' Week 6 loss:
It was a very rough game for Jalon Daniels. The Steelers knew how to rattle the rookie, and Daniels finished 22 of 43 passing for 164 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.
Daniels also had 39 rushing yards on the day and was sacked five times. One thing that won't show up on the stat sheets is the bad missed passes late in the game to open players like Emeka Egbuka and Bucky Irving.
After a great game against the Dallas Cowboys, Bucky Irving came back to earth in this game. Irving finished with 21 touches for 49 yards and zero touchdowns.
Kenny Gainwell didn't do much better with three touches for 24 yards, and we saw no opportunities for second-year back Josh Williams.
Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin combined for 24 targets today for 11 receptions, 85 yards and a single touchdown from Egbuka.
Ted Hurst also finished with three receptions for 40 yards as well. However, there were a couple of drops in this game with Egbuka, Godwin and Tez Johnson all having at least a single drop in this game.
The Bucs offensive line continues to struggle to protect the quarterback. That's not fully their fault, as the Steelers blitzed a ton that day. However, the team was not able to run block either in this matchup.
David Walker was an absolute star in this matchup and finished with seven total tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss and three quarterback hits.
We also saw A'Shawn Robinson get his second interception this season, which is absolutely insane. Rueben Bain Jr. got his first sack of the season and had the deflection on the pass that Robinson intercepted. Finally, you had other big contributions from guys like Yaya Diaby and Al-Quadin Muhammad.
Josiah Trotter looked good in this game, leading the defense with 12 total tackles and one pass deflection that should've been a pick-six for him.
Christian Rozeboom also had a great pass deflection in this game as well and has earned more playing time. Alex Anzalone, however, still missed multiple tackles in this game and was a bit of a liability towards the end of the game.
Zyon McCollum led the way for this group with 11 total tackles and one pass deflection. However, the star of the group was Keionte Scott, who had eight tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss and a quarterback hit.
Jacob Parrish was yet again solid with six tackles, one tackle for loss and two passes deflected.
The positive is that kicker Chase McLaughlin was awesome, making all of his kicks and keeping the Bucs alive going into overtime. The negative was that Riley Dixon was really bad in this game, and the team still needs to look at a new punter going forward. Yes, the game was windy, but it was not an issue for McLaughlin in this game, so I see it as no excuse for Dixon.

title: Titans Finally Make a Move Up in NFL Power Rankings After Comeback Road Win vs. Colts
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans have had a rough start to the 2026 season, but head coach Robert Saleh's group gained momentum this past Sunday with a road win over the Indianapolis Colts to tally their first victory of the year.
Saleh's team trailed by double digits at halftime and looked like the same lifeless squad we've watched all year. However, the Titans stepped up in the second half and made crucial plays in all three phases to escape Indianapolis with a win.
At 1-5, Tennessee is still fairly low in the latest NFL power rankings , but it is making progress toward being a competent and functional team.
Words from the author Nick Shook: The Titans are no longer winless! I felt as though the Colts presented Tennessee’s best opportunity to finally win a game, and thanks to strong special teams play, a slight revival of the ground game and some timely catches by rookie receiver Carnell Tate, the Titans finally notched a victory. Cam Ward and the offense still look like an awkward-at-best operation, but this week, they can spend a bit of time savoring a triumph.
Words from the author Connor Orr: Losing to the Titans will absolutely break you as a person. DeForrest Buckner is proof.
Words from the author Turron Davenport: The Titans' passing game is severely inconsistent and last in the league at 153.3 passing yards per game. Although QB Cam Ward has had accuracy issues and failed to see open receivers on occasion, it's not all on him. Ward's pass catchers have dropped passes, and no one has emerged as the second option to rookie receiver Carnell Tate. Second-year wideout Elic Ayomanor had an outstanding training camp but hasn't had much of an impact (seven catches over six games). The tight end group has also been nonexistent, totaling 14 receptions for 90 yards.
Words from the author Mike Florio: Can they build on their unlikely win in Indy?
The Titans are still among the bottom-feeders in the NFL, but the win against the Colts has a few analysts wondering whether Tennessee can build off the victory and string together a solid finish to the season in the next 12 weeks.
It's clear that the Titans' offense has a lot of work to do, as the unit was completely dysfunctional for most of the day last week despite quarterback Cam Ward connecting with rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate for the game-tying touchdown. However, if the defense continues to play well and the special teams make timely plays, such as the blocked punt returned for a touchdown by Femi Oladejo that ended up being a key score in the Week 6 win, Tennessee will have a chance in most contests.
A home matchup against the 4-2 Cleveland Browns is next for the Titans, who will look to win back-to-back games for the first time since November 2022.
Dharya Sharma is a sportswriter from Nebraska who has been covering the Tennessee Titans through his website, SharmSports, since 2023. He is also an NFL and NBA writer for The Sporting News and had a previous stop with Sportsnaut. Follow him on X @SharmSports

title: How Titans Can Break an Embarrassing, Multi-Year Streak With Week 7 Win vs. Browns
full_text:
A matchup with the Cleveland Browns doesn't mean what it used to. Todd Monken has come in as a first-year head coach and turned the franchise around, leading the Browns to a 4-2 record and the top spot in the AFC North. On the southern end of the conference, Robert Saleh and the Tennessee Titans are 1-5.
Not every rebuild is the same, and it's necessary to point out that Saleh came into one of the worst ongoing catastrophes in the NFL. Don't believe me? One streak tells the entire story - one streak that Saleh and the Titans have a chance to break in Week 7.
The Titans haven't won back-to-back football games since November of 2022. That's coming up on four years without two straight victories. That's an embarrassing figure that stretches back into the Mike Vrabel era, signifying that this franchise was long out of order before his departure.
Saleh may be 1-5, but putting a stopper in that negative history in year one is the best possible way he can set himself apart.
Nabbing a divisional win last week already went a long way for Saleh. Brian Callahan, in a season that saw him be let go six games in, failed to lead the Titans to a victory in the AFC South. Sure, that issue continued after he left, but it was Callahan's product.
Saleh has taken that product and ensured that the issue didn't become a streak with a win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. Breaking one that stretches over three head coaches feels like the next step.
In the Browns, Tennessee will be tasked with stopping a surprisingly efficient, youth-fueled offense to do just that. If Saleh's defense can replicate their winning performance last week, we'd be in for another box checked.
The Browns haven't broken 13 points in two weeks, but the same offense hung 27 points on the Pittsburgh Steelers in a shot-for-shot win prior to that drought. Even scoring only 13, Cleveland took down the Baltimore Ravens last Sunday at home.
This is a well-rounded group with a high ceiling. But it's also a group that relies on rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion to make plays. The Titans shut down an objectively better offense (ESPN metrics have the Colts' offense seven spots ahead of Cleveland) last week in Indy, and they'll have to apply the same pressure to find a win this week,
If Saleh's defensive line can come up with another six sacks, I can't imagine the result isn't close to, if not exactly the same. 2-5 isn't all that exciting, but back-to-back wins, as well as what would be the first home win of the season, is.
A rebuilding team takes what they can get, even if the rebuild is going on a half-decade now.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: 3 Pivotal Matchups that Will Decide Titans' Game vs. Browns: Defense Will Determine the Result
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are looking to extend their winning streak over the Cleveland Browns to two games in Week 7. Last season, one of the Titans' three wins came in Cleveland, when Tennessee narrowly came out on top in a thrilling 31-29 brawl.
However, this Browns team looks a little different. Last year's squad finished 5-12, and at the bottom of their division. This season, Cleveland sits in a three-way tie at the top of the AFC North, boasting a 4-2 record.
It'll be no easy feat for the Titans to win again. If Robert Saleh is to put another notch in his victory column, here are three pivotal matchups that Tennessee needs to go their way.
The Titans' defensive line are coming hot off their best performance of the season in Week 6. Tennessee leveled six sacks against the Indianapolis Colts and Daniel Jones, with DT Jeffery Simmons forcing a fumble in the process.
Tennessee had three total takeaways on the day. With Deshaun Watson's mobility posing a threat in the pocket and his multiple receiving options working to get open downfield, the Titans' d-line will be once again tasked with limiting an offense with high-scoring potential.
PFF has the Browns' o-line slotted in at 26th in the NFL. Per TeamRankings, Deshaun Watson taking 24 sacks through six games poses him as the most-sacked QB in the NFL this season.
Saleh's defense appears to have an advantage here, and the Titans will need to make the most of it to pull off the victory.
The worse Cam Ward looks, the more crucial his matchups become. The Titans beat the Colts on the back of those aforementioned three takeaways last Sunday. Even if that unit buckles down again, we shouldn't expect numbers like those to be repeated.
As a result, it may take Ward meeting them in the middle for Tennessee to come out on top. With star CB Denzel Ward and Pro-Bowl S Grant Delpit holding down the Browns' secondary, it'll be no easy feat for the second-year QB.
Where the previous matchup appeared favorable for Tennessee, Cleveland looks to have the upper hand in shutting down an inconsistent Ward before he even gets started.
Ward doesn't have to play flashy to play well. Running back something like his 222-yard, one-touchdown outing against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4 would be the epitome of "good enough" if Tennessee's defense shows out again.
The Titans need Ward to limit his mistakes in Week 7. A few deep completions or a first-half score certainly wouldn't hurt along the way.
S Amani Hooker just posted a career-high 13 tackles, as well as one interception, vs. the Colts. In the absence of CB Alontae Taylor, Hooker more than took it upon himself to handle Indy's functional WR1, in Josh Downs.
Facing off against rising rookie WR Denzel Boston in Week 7, the same efficiency will be expected of Hooker if Taylor can't go. Circling back to PFF, Hooker is graded at 81.1 overall, which situates him all the way up at number seven among 98 players at his position.
Boston already has three scores on 17 receptions this season. He's quickly emerged as a primary target for Watson, running efficient routes and even emerging as an early possibility for Offensive Rookie of the Year. The tape doesn't lie.
It's shaping up to be rookie vs. veteran with Hooker and Boston in Week 7. Lock Boston up, and Watson could be forced into making the same mistakes that Jones did with the Colts. That's a path to victory.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: News Recap: Details Emerge on Incident That Led to Titans Cutting DT Jordan Elliott
full_text:
On Tuesday, the Tennessee Titans announced the releasing of DT Jordan Elliott .
Further details emerged from Aaron Wilson on Wednesday: it was reported that Elliott had a heated practice with OT JC Latham, which resulted in Elliott storming out of the Titans' training facility to retrieve a firearm from his car, likely to confront Latham. Titans' DT John Franklin-Myers was able to calm Elliott down before tensions escalated any further.
The Titans' official statement, per Easton Freeze :
“On Thursday, October 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott. Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no further comment on the matter."
Head coach Robert Saleh told the media that Elliott was inactive for practice due to personal matters the day after the incident. Elliott didn't travel with the team for Tennessee's first win of the season over the Colts in Indianapolis.
Prior to the season, the 28-year-old Elliott signed a two-year deal with Tennessee worth up to $8.5 million. He previously played two seasons with the San Francisco 49ers under Saleh as defensive coordinator.
Elliott made five appearances for the Titans this season, collecting 11 tackles.
In Elliott's place, Tennessee elevated DT Timmy Horne, who played against the Colts on Sunday. It was Horne's first NFL appearance since 2023, when he was a member of the Atlanta Falcons.

title: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
full_text:
I'm all about celebrating a win, but the Tennessee Titans are coming up on a must-win game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory?
Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens.
In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction.
Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air.
If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing.
PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee.
Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going.
Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result.
Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit.
I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville.
However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win.
This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it.
Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee.
I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. I predict a narrow Titans win over the Browns.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: The Biggest Decision Robert Saleh Got Right Against Colts And What it Means Moving Forward
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans picked up their first win of the 2026 NFL season on the road, defeating the Indianapolis Colts 26-20 on Sunday.
Despite trailing by double digits at halftime , the Titans continued to fight and made timely plays in all three phases to finally break a seven-game losing streak dating back to Week 17 of the 2025 season.
One unit that deserves a ton of credit for Tennessee's victory over the weekend is the defense, especially the secondary. Though the group has had its struggles this year, they completely shut down the Colts' passing attack in the second half and also picked off two passes, one from safety Amani Hooker and the other from cornerback Cor'Dale Flott.
The secondary showed promise in Week 6, and one major coaching decision by head coach Robert Saleh may have been the difference-maker.
When the Titans announced the inactives for the Week 6 contest, starting cornerback Alontae Taylor was one of the names mentioned . Taylor was one of Tennessee's marquee free-agent additions, and just five weeks into the year, he was a healthy scratch.
Instead of playing Taylor, Tennessee gave the start to Joshua Williams, who made his season debut against the Colts after missing the first five games with a pectoral injury . Williams had 12 games of starting experience under his belt entering Sunday's game, and the Titans were hoping for solid play out of him to help the secondary.
Williams turned in an adequate day of work against Indianapolis in Tennessee's victory. The former Kansas City Chief played every defensive snap (83) and held his own in coverage, allowing two completions on five targets, 16 receiving yards, and a 48.8 passer rating, though Williams did commit a penalty.
Regardless, Williams proved to be an upgrade over Taylor in the back end for the Titans, validating Saleh's decision to hold the prized free-agent signing out. Saleh hasn't confirmed that Taylor was benched, calling it a coaches' decision, but based on his play, it's safe to say Taylor was benched for performance.
We'll see whether Taylor returns to the lineup in Week 7 as the Titans host the Cleveland Browns. Based on how Week 6 transpired, it wouldn't be a surprise if Williams receives his second straight start and Taylor sits on the sideline.

title: Titans Suddenly Cutting Veteran DT is Latest Sign of Team's Dysfunction
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans made waves throughout the NFL when three front-office executives were suddenly fired. Senior VP and chief revenue officer Adam Nuse, VP of creative Charles Jensen, and senior VP of brand marketing Erin Swartz were all let go in the midst of changes to the "business side" of the organization, per the team's official statement.
Tennessee's front office turnover has become a normal happening under President and CEO Burke Nihill. Somehow, blame continues to shift for everything going wrong for the football team in Nashville. New names come in and yield little improvement, and the cycle repeats.
Now, the team's general dysfunction has extended down to the roster. The Titans have officially released veteran DL Jordan Elliot due to an "incident" at the team facility.
Statement from the @Titans on DL Jordan Elliott. pic.twitter.com/blH9LdpFrt
Elliott missed Week 6 due to "personal reasons." Saleh specifically addressed Elliott's designation last Friday, saying: "He’s dealing with some personal stuff." Now, it appears the Titans have shone a public light on his recent absence, outright cutting the lineman for undisclosed reasons.
Between CB Alontae Taylor being deemed a healthy scratch vs. the Colts and Elliott being cut due to an incident behind the scenes, Tennessee's win from this past week is marred by questions about individuals such as these. The operation doesn't appear clean from the outside looking in.
Turron Davenport reported that the Taylor and Elliott situations are completely separate deals. That saves a little face, but still, that's two unexplained hiccups on the defensive side of the ball just within the last week.
Elliott hasn't been a crucial piece of the puzzle by any means for Tennessee. His activity in the run game with 1.5 STFs this season is about the only serious impact he's managed in Saleh's defense. Still, the vet represented a plug-in asset that the Titans made use of consistently.
Now, he's been removed, and the Titans "will have no further comment on the matter."
Fans can expect DT Nazir Stackhouse to get extended rotational looks in Elliott's absence. Stackhouse found his way into the gaps this past Sunday and had a noticeable impact in the run game. Tennessee may have a solution to losing Elliott, but the franchise frustratingly remains without an answer for why he was cut in the first place.
Perhaps the energy around news like that would be different if the Titans weren't 7-33 in their last 40 football games. That's not the world we're living in, however, which means the spotlight on the people making these decisions is hotter than ever.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Titans Rookie Power Rankings: Carnell Tate Runs Away With Top Spot After Week 6
full_text:
Things are slowly starting to come together for this Tennessee Titans team. You can say that it's already too late, or that one win doesn't mean much after five losses, but I'm just happy to see Robert Saleh get one under his belt.
There's a new air of confidence around this franchise, even if it's mild. With an AFC South victory over the Indianapolis Colts on the resume now, the Titans are pushing for a mid-season resurgence.
That possibility hinges, to some extent, on the team's play-making rookies in crucial roles. Here are our rookie power rankings after Week 6.
RG Fernando Carmona will be left off the list until he returns to the lineup. Let's jump in.
Carnell Tate has become comfortable at the top of our rookie rankings. He's proven his worth as a worthy fourth overall pick up to this point, and while Anthony Hill Jr. may be the more consistent rookie, Tate's offensive explosions are too hard to ignore.
Against the Colts in Week 6, Tate came down with six of his seven targets for 70 yards receiving. The pass-catcher also hauled in his first NFL touchdown in the fourth quarter, which helped spark what eventually became a Titans comeback win.
Tate already looks like WR1 next to Wan'Dale Robinson. Even as Cam Ward struggles to produce, Tate's efficiency hasn't taken any real hit. It's only up for the rookie receiver.
Hill remains top five in the NFL in tackles through six weeks, with 56. The rookie LB has taken no time at all to make an argument as the best player at his position for Tennessee, and he sits just below Tate on this list as a knockout pickup thus far.
Hill played all 78 of the Titans' defensive snaps facing Indy. Fellow LBs Cody Barton and Cedric Gray split their shares at 42 and 37, respectively. The rookie finished with nine total tackles, including one for a loss and one pass defended.
It's not even a question at this point who Tennessee's most impactful LB is, although Hill keeps finding ways to surprise on a weekly basis. Saleh plugged him into the defense from day one, and Hill has yet to slip in his role as a pivotal piece.
Keldric Faulk logged just one QB pressure vs. the Colts in Week 6. The rookie EDGE has slowly come down the runway in Saleh's defense this season, and he's yet to fully take control of the role that Tennessee traded up to draft him for.
Some of Faulk's adjustments have been clouded by the rest of the defensive line's solid performances up to this point. He's got time to develop under Saleh, and has plenty of potential to do so in time. Right now, however, he simply isn't there.
Per PFF, Faulk played just 29 snaps in Week 6. You could say his underwhelming season through six games has to do with opportunity, but that road goes both ways.
Until Faulk breaks out and adds to his current one-sack total, his position here is unlikely to change.
Of course, Nick Singleton was inactive in Week 6. Given his healthy state and on-off appearances in the backfield, I'm still including Singleton on this list.
Like Faulk, the rookie RB just hasn't shown enough flash yet to see the field consistently. Buried behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears on the ground, Singleton's role is set to remain limited until something shifts.
Pollard being moved before next month's trade deadline is the most likely scenario in which Singleton could see an uptick in production. However, if Pollard rides out the last year of his contract, we may have to wait until Singleton's second season to see what he's made of in an expanded role.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Grading Every Titans Position Group After Win vs. Colts: 1 Defensive Unit is Miles Ahead
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans finally got in the win column last Sunday, beating the Indianapolis Colts 26-20 in an AFC South showdown between two struggling teams.
The Colts got out to a 13-0 lead that honestly felt insurmountable at the half, but credit to HC Robert Saleh for keeping his guys locked in as they scored 26 points over the final two quarters to pull off the upset.
There was a lot of things to like in this game, along with plenty of reason to be concerned going forward. With that said, let’s take a look at this week’s positional grades.
QB Cam Ward made a handful of plays when the team needed him to, so that’ll keep him from getting an F. But the Titans simply need more from Ward than just 102 passing yards where 50% of his passes thrown short of the sticks, while also ignoring the middle of the field almost completely .
Tennessee desperately needs Ward to start being more aggressive with the ball if they realistically want any chance of turning this season around. Maybe the play calling is ultimately what’s holding him back, or maybe it’s a lack of trust in Ward to push the ball downfield.
Whatever the case may be, the Titans need to see better overall performances out of Ward going forward, or the skepticism and doubt surrounding his long-term future will only get louder with each passing week.
RB Tony Pollard led the way, running the ball 19 times for 76 yards, while RB Tyjae Spears only added one yard on one carry. As far as the former goes, Pollard had a solid outing overall.
It wasn’t anything to write home about, but he was able to help the Titans stay ahead of the chains and pick up first downs when the opportunity presented itself. Unfortunately, Tennessee finished the game with a negative rushing EPA of -0.17, per Pro Football Focus .
Therefore, I think a C is more than fair following a slightly above average (at best) performance from the Titans’ top ball carrier.
Rookie WR Carnell Tate is doing a ton of the heavy lifting on this grade. He made the most of the limited opportunities this passing attack allows, catching six of his eight targets for 70 yards, along with his first career touchdown.
The former Buckeye continues to flash signs of a budding star on the horizon. He finished the game with an overall grade of 87.2 , which was the highest offensive grade for either team.
Aside from the rookie, the rest of the receiver room accounted for just 25 yards combined. Partially due to Ward’s inconsistent play, but also due to self inflicted mistakes (drops, bad routes, not reaching landmarks on time, etc.)
The quarterback play undoubtedly needs to be better, but so do the guys around Tate, because right now, this offense is operating with only one consistent weapon at its disposal.
The tight end room continues to be non-existent, especially in the passing game. Neither of the Titans’ four tight ends caught a single pass yesterday.
Again, there weren’t a lot of passes to go around yesterday, and they did occasionally contribute to a couple of nice runs as well, but this group has to start contributing more than they are. Otherwise, it’s a safe bet that Tennessee will be looking to upgrade this position come springtime.
We gotta give this group some credit. They followed up an absolutely horrendous performance a week ago with an all-around strong outing last Sunday. The group upfront created lanes for Pollard to work with throughout the game.
More importantly, they didn’t allow a single sack over 23 pass blocking snaps. LG Peter Skoronski had one of his better games of the year, earning a grade of 74.2 after allowing a pressure rate of just 4.3%.
LT Dan Moore Jr. caught a lot of heat last week, most of it warranted, but that didn’t seem to faze him on Sunday. Moore pitched a shutout over his 23 pass-blocking snaps, allowing zero sacks, hits, pressures, or hurries.
If the Titans can continue to perform like they have most of this season, then this offense will have a puncher’s chance to right the ship as the season unfolds.
The Titans’ pass rush completely took this game over in the second half. In total, the group combined for a whopping 24 pressures, with DT Jeffery Simmons (eight), DL John Franklin-Myers (five), Jermaine Johnson (three), and Jacob Martin (two), accounting for 18 of them.
Simmons, in particular, was dominant once again, as evident by his team leading overall grade of 88.7. On top of his eight pressures, the All-Pro defensive tackle recorded six tackles, three run stops, two sacks, two tackles for loss, two QB hits, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery.
Simply put: Simmons is playing at a completely different level than the rest of his peers at the moment. As long as that continues, you can expect these grades to continue being rather high.
Rookie LB Anthony Hill Jr. continues to flash serious potential. The Texas product totaled nine tackles, three pressures, one tackle for loss, one pass breakup, one run stop, one
LB Cedric Gray also saw an increased workload, playing a total of 38 snaps while LB Cody Barton was on the field for 44 snaps. The trio of Hill, Barton and Gray are an intriguing group that should only get better with the more reps they get together.
The team decided to make CB Alontae Taylor a healthy scratch , and that bold decision certainly paid off.
The trio of CB Cor’Dale Flott (zero yards allowed), Joshua Williams (16 yards allowed), and Marcus Harris (25 yards allowed), combined for just 41 passing yards allowed between the three of them. Flott graded out as the Titans’ second-best defender, earning a grade of 84.7 after his solid performance that saw him reel in an interception.
Let’s start by giving S Tony Adams some credit. He stepped in for the absent Kevin Winston Jr. and played admirably, totaling 12 tackles, one QB hit, one tackle for loss, and one pass breakup.
However, S Amani Hooker was the star of this group. The former Hawkeye had a phenomenal outing on Sunday, recording 13 tackles, one pass deflection, and one beautiful interception in the red zone that directly took points off the Colts’ scoreboard.
Hooker nearly had a second interception late in the game that practically mirrored his pick from earlier in the game, but he wasn’t able to get both feet down the second time around.
The Titans’ veteran safety continues to make his presence felt along the backend, and if the pass rush continues to wreak havoc like they did against Indy, then there could be a lot more splash plays in Hooker’s near future.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: So Crazy it Just Might Work: How Titans Would Benefit From Trading CB Alontae Taylor
full_text:
If you’d have asked me heading into this season who was on the trade block for the Tennessee Titans , a few obvious names come to mind. In fact, those names are still in play.
Veterans like RB Tony Pollard and LB Cody Barton remain in the conversation, even given the former's current hold on Tennessee's backfield production. Seeing either of those names move would check an expected box for a Titans team that just secured their first win of the season.
However, with the November 10 deadline approaching, one surprise name may be in trade contention. There’s a case to be made for trading CB Alontae Taylor.
Crazy, I know, but it makes sense for Tennessee in the present moment.
For the folks about to point out that Taylor was signed to a $58 million, three-year deal this offseason: That was my first thought as well. It’d essentially be moving off of an experienced piece and admitting fault in the investment.
But would it be better to hold on to a player that just isn’t taking to the system in the hopes that he eventually pans out?
The ongoing Calvin Ridley experiment in Nashville says no.
Saleh on whether Alontae Taylor is a one-week inactive, and if he's now week to week: We'll discuss it as a staff and make a decision that is best moving forward @Titans
If Robert Saleh’s decision to sit Taylor in Week 6 vs. the Indianapolis Colts is any indication of Taylor’s standing with the team, it may be better for the Titans to squeeze any potential-based trade value out of him right now.
Coach Saleh has talked about the complication of his zone-structure defensive system numerous times. He’s even touched on the learning curve that comes with that; see Cedric Gray’s sudden drop in snaps for a prime example.
It hasn’t been confirmed that Taylor’s issue is with the system. However, he’s struggled to make any significant difference in the Titans’ secondary through five games.
What’s worse, Saleh sitting him yesterday resulted in what was perhaps the unit’s best performance of the year. Two interceptions in the first game without Taylor suggests a loud issue with his involvement.
The Titans wouldn’t get a king’s ransom for Taylor. You’d likely be looking at a mid-to-late draft pick or another waning defensive playmaker. But if the defense is better off without Taylor already, what does Tennessee have to lose there?
It’s not even a one-game sample size that I’m judging this on. PFF has Taylor ranked 100th among just 102 eligible CBs in the NFL. It isn’t a coincidence that the team looked better without him on the field.
Maybe there’s a team out there that believes in Taylor’s progression. Maybe that team has more time to allow him to come to grips with a change. If such a team exists, the Titans couldn’t be blamed for embracing the quick-draw nature of that decision and making a call.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Commanders Have Three Problems to Fix Before Their Season Slips Away
full_text:
It's been about a month since the Washington Commanders won a game. They currently stand at 1-4-1 entering Week 7 of the NFL regular season, with winnable matchups slipping away in the final seconds and key contributors continuing to go down with serious injuries, with no clear replacements to match their high-end production. This is about as bleak as the fan base has felt since the Jayden Daniels era commenced two and a half years ago.
Luckily, the Commanders' bye week spares fans from watching the team fall even further from the greatness they hoped to regain following their miracle run to 2024's NFC Championship Game. That gives them time to tend to their underperforming, still-talented team as they prepare to kick off November with a rematch with the Philadelphia Eagles .
Terry McLaurin, the beloved longtime Commanders receiver who's stuck it out through one of the league's most active quarterback carousels, won't join Washington on the field for the remainder of the 2026 season. For all we know, he may have played his last snaps with the team after suffering a torn patellar tendon in San Francisco last weekend.
Commanders WR Terry McLaurin was carted off the field with an apparent knee injury. pic.twitter.com/ohVT3BY6JG
That non-contact knee injury spelled doom the moment McLaurin went down, leaving a receiver room that'll have to replace Daniels' favorite downfield threat on the fly. He had more chemistry with the quarterback than any supplementary wideouts, and it showed on the field between Daniels' love for the go ball and McLaurin's unparalleled tracking skills.
It's up to the coaches and the players to begin focusing even harder on Daniels' connections with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams , and Treylon Burks, as those look like the best functional receivers of the bunch. Diggs and Williams, as the veteran slot target and sure-handed rookie, respectively, should see an uptick in targets as remaining starters who'll each move up a peg on the scoring depth chart.
If there's one thing that outsiders get on thankless linemen for, it's blocking. They're easy targets to point to in most vague instances, despite all of the moving parts that go into putting together a consistent attack, but in Washington's case, they've really been liable to error.
Five, count them, five penalties from Monday's 49ers loss could be traced directly to a few choice blockers, with holding calls, a false start, and an offensive facemask all contributing to the problem. If they're not going to make Daniels' life easier as a united front, they may as well avoid hampering the offense by repeatedly giving up yards on second- or third-and-longs.
They seem to have settled on Lucas Patrick at center for the time being following Nick Allegretti's demotion, so the coaching staff can at least narrow down the linemen pool to those most likely to see significant burn from here on out. This position group needs discipline as much as any on the Commanders' depth chart if anyone's dreaming about a miracle divisional seizure, which they should be, in the interest of holding their jobs and making the most of the sad state of the NFC East.
The Commanders looked ready to go home halfway through that performance in San Francisco, allowing the 49ers' Brock Purdy-Mike Evans connection to open the flat up for a dink-and-dunk game that Washington never seemed to adjust to during the first half.
Evans' early injury let the Commanders look much more energetic in the second half, when they rushed Purdy into a few three-and-outs while their own offense finally surged. While the game's momentum surely played a role in the flip, an uptick in aggression up front would be appreciated.
Who are these Commanders? Christian McCaffrey made easy work of the once-vaunted run defense by repeatedly slipping through first-half holes, while the secondary's blitzing attack was nowhere to be found in blowing up the short-field passing style that they feasted on to start the season. The bye week can give these guys a week off to develop more of their identity, since, like most other broad Commanders positions, there's clear talent here.
Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu down the gut. Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson on the edge. Nick Cross and Jeremy Reaves man the safety position. Amik Robertson and Rasul Douglas outside, with Trey Amos recently back in the fold. That's no shortage of starters who've produced highlights over six weeks, and first-year defensive coordinator Daronte Jones has already offered glimpses into that aggression everyone wants more of. A little more steadiness could go a long way in ensuring that fewer of these tight losses slip away from the Commanders. title: Commanders Power Rankings Take an Unexpected Turn After 49ers Loss
full_text:
Each week during the regular season, we'll look at what the national media is saying about the Washington Commanders via various publications' NFL Power Polls. With it being Week 7, things are starting to get clearer for several teams. The Washington Commanders entered their bye week at 1-4-1 after another frustrating loss , this time against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Oddly enough, that loss didn't hurt Washington's standing with everyone in the national media. In fact, a few publications actually moved the Commanders up in their latest power rankings, despite the team having just one win through six games. * Side note: Many have asked whether these polls are helpful, which is a fair question. One way to look at them is as a way to broaden your perspective on what others believe. Not to mention, sometimes it's fun to see the national media guys bump around in the dark, chasing their tails, clueless.
Commanders Power Rankings - Week 6 (Average of 27)
Commanders Power Rankings - Week 7 (Average of 26)

Sports Illustrated - No. 26
Note : The table above links each poll to the corresponding publication name. Last week’s Power Ranking Index : No. 27 HIGHEST Ranking: No. 20 LOWEST Ranking: No. 30 Last week’s result : lost to the San Francisco 49ers 23-17 This week : bye week ESPN had this to say (29th): Of the Commanders' 81 third downs, 48 have been for 7 yards or longer. So the Commanders are ranked 31st in third-down conversions at 30.9%. And when facing a third-and-7 or longer, they have picked up a first down only 10 times. It's not just a matter of running the ball better on early downs because Washington averages 4.1 yards per carry on first down. The big culprit is 16 offensive penalties on second down. Only one team (Chargers) has had more. -- John Keim
CBS Sports had this to say (28th) They did a nice job battling back against the 49ers, but another loss keeps them in last in their division. The heat is on Dan Quinn. — Pete Prisco NFL.com had this to say (23rd) Washington’s latest loss will undoubtedly disappoint its ardent fan base, but the mettle it showed in the second half in the unfriendly confines of Levi’s Stadium told me this team is more than its 1-4-1 record. Jayden Daniels’ return has opened more avenues for the Commanders to choose in their pursuit of victory, and even after Terry McLaurin was carted off with a knee injury, the quarterback managed to find success by turning to the lesser-known members of his team and using his legs when necessary. Yes, it has only one win, but this team has fight in it. Now, it needs to rely on the likes of Daniels, Treylon Burks, Antonio Williams and Stefon Diggs to try to dig out of this hole. — Nick Shook
Fox Sports had this to say (27th): Jayden Daniels looks closer to his old, magical self, but it all came too late to pull off the upset in San Francisco Monday night, and it might be too late to save the season in Washington. It might be too late for Dan Quinn too, since, for the second week in a row, his game management skills were exposed as … well, something. This time he was caught on camera seemingly surprised that the Commanders’ last play was a fourth-down play, as he tried to send the field goal unit on. Add that to last week’s clock disaster and Washington’s 1-4-1 record, and Quinn might not still be the Commanders coach anymore when they return from their bye. — Ralph Vacchiano Sports Illustrated had this to say (26th): Dan Quinn had one directive for the remainder of this season: Do not follow up one of the most egregious instances of clock mismanagement ever with another high-profile standalone game gaffe that shows an inability to handle game management.  — Conor Orr
Yahoo Sports had this to say (25th): Jayden Daniels throwing the ball away even though it was fourth down and Dan Quinn seemingly not knowing it was fourth down at all says everything that needs to be said about the 2026 Commanders. If that wasn't enough on Monday night, after last week's game-management debacle at the end of overtime against the Giants, the Commanders had to use a timeout with the clock stopped with 3:01 left in the game before a fourth down play. That ended up costing Washington a valuable 40 seconds, as it ran out of time on a comeback attempt in a 23-17 loss to the 49ers. Washington has a bye coming up next, and whatever answers Quinn gives to why he seemingly didn't know it was fourth down will be a big discussion point, not just among fans and media, but also within the organization. It seems like a team in desperate need of a reset.  — Frank Schwab Pro Football Talk had this to say (30th) Dan Quinn’s time is up. And the end result likely won’t be a tie. — Mike Florio The Athletic had this to say (27th) The Commanders quarterback hasn’t had much help this year, and things got worse Monday night after Terry McLaurin suffered what looked like a bad knee injury. Still, it has been a disappointing season for Daniels that has included another elbow injury, an inexplicable breakdown a week ago and a rally that came up short Monday night. He is 18th among quarterbacks in total fantasy points (85.7). — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Walter Football had this to say (20th) Another week, another coaching gaffe by Dan Quinn , who yelled for this team to go for a field goal after Jayden Daniels foolishly threw the ball away on fourth down. Daniels, meanwhile, looked like he pissed his pants at the prospect of scrambling into a Fred Warner-led linebacker group. The giant wuss ran for only 10 yards in a loss. Pathetic!
Put it all together, and the Commanders land at an average ranking of No. 26.1, a slight improvement from last week's 26.6. That's probably not much consolation for a team sitting at 1-4-1, but it does show just how differently the national media views Washington heading into its bye week. Some apparently saw enough against San Francisco to move the Commanders up, while others weren't nearly as impressed. We'll revisit these each week and see where the national pulse moves next. title: Commanders Quietly Added Former NFL Head Coach to Help Struggling Defense
full_text:
According to NFL Insiders Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport, the Washington Commanders hired Steve Wilks to help the defensive staff ahead of the game against the 49ers. The decision to hire Wilks was made back in September, but he didn't start working with the team until last week. Wilks will assist with game planning and will work under Quinn and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones; he will not be with the team on game days. Wilks has plenty of NFL experience, including two Super Bowl trips. He served as Carolina's assistant head coach and defensive backs coach in 2015, when the Panthers reached Super Bowl 50; as the head coach of the Arizona Cardinals in 2018; and the Carolina Panthers interim head coach in 2022. He returned to the Super Bowl as the San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator in 2023, when the defense ranked third in scoring at 17.5 points allowed and went to the Super Bowl. Most recently, Wilks served as the Jets' defensive coordinator in 2025 before being fired in December.
This hiring is not in response to anything that happened in recent weeks or an indictment on Daronte Jones as DC. This has been in the works since before the start of the season, but he officially started last week. https://t.co/mCNisEhzQB
Washington has been a running example of defensive inconsistency and entered the bye week at 1-4-1 after a game in which they surrendered 303 total yards and 17 first downs in the first half, and then rebounded to give up only 72 in the second. The defense currently gives up 28.7 points per game, which ranks 29th in the league through six matchups. They don't lack scheming ideas; they're just struggling to execute them consistently on the field. Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic notes that Wilks "comes in on Sundays and leaves after Wednesday practice." Essentially, the move adds another defensive perspective to the room, not another game-day decision-maker. Wilks is filled with knowledge that can be helpful for Jones, a first-time NFL coordinator. It's important to stress that Wilks has no playcalling duties and is there to make the staff's job easier. The real gauge will come after the bye, when everyone will see whether any consistency changes are visible, as adding another football mind doesn't guarantee anything changes on the field. That's still up to Quinn, Jones, and the rest of the staff who will still be around Wednesday afternoons after Wilks leaves. title: With Terry McLaurin Out, Washington Must Change How It Uses Antonio Williams
full_text:
With Washington Commanders receiver Terry McLaurin out for the rest of the season after tearing the patellar tendon in his left knee, the team is faced with the task of replacing the face of the franchise. The good news is the roster is in a position to fill his role with several players, but one stands out as the guy they need to use most: Antonio Williams. Williams has already spent the entire offseason program and the first six weeks of the regular season developing a connection with Daniels . But the reason they need to give him more looks is clear: he creates separation like no one else on the roster, and even though his snap share has stayed steady (hovering in the high 60s of late, even in London when McLaurin was out nursing a hamstring), he's criminally underused in David Blough's system. Against San Francisco, Williams ran 35 routes but had only four targets, catching three for 50 yards. All four targets came on third down in the fourth quarter, and his three catches accounted for Washington’s only successful third-down conversions of the night. In an offense looking for answers, why ignore one?
Watching Jayden Daniels tape back. I'm only seven throws in. So far he's been clinically good. Made the right read and was accurate on almost every throw. But on this short toss to Bates he misses a wide open Antonio Williams for a 21-yard TD. pic.twitter.com/PRWQMQbSSo
Daniels has a part in this, too. Those opportunities only help if he finds Williams when they’re there. This is something that was going on long before the 49ers game. Pro Football Focus credits Williams with 12 catches on 12 short targets for 85 yards and five catches on eight intermediate targets for 87 yards. That's 17 catches on 20 targets for 172 yards, one touchdown and no drops through six games; his PFF receiving grade is 75.2.
Against San Francisco, Washington was using McLaurin and Treylon Burks in two-receiver/two-tight-end personnel before the injury Monday night. McLaurin, Williams, and Diggs formed the three-receiver group. After McLaurin left the game , Burks, Williams, and Diggs became Washington’s primary three-receiver group. Williams further supports his case with a fair amount of snaps in the slot and outside. Quinn has already hinted at multiple players being in line for Terry's snaps: "So we do have a deep crew at that position, and we’ll lean in, you know, on a number of the guys to find some of the unique roles that Terry does," Quinn said Tuesday . Against San Francisco, Diggs caught six passes for 44 yards and a touchdown; Burks caught four for 66, including a 30-yard gain; Chig Okonkwo added seven receptions for 69 yards from the tight end spot. Quinn also pointed to McLaurin’s contested catches as one of his biggest strengths. Williams has already given Washington a productive option between the numbers, catching all 10 short and intermediate-range targets in that area for 104 yards. That’s where I’d start after the bye: more first- and second-down opportunities for Williams across the middle, with McLaurin’s downfield and contested-catch work spread across the group. It's maddening to see an offense in need of playmakers fail to use the ones they have. A glance over Williams' numbers above makes a major case for him to be involved earlier and more often, including plays where he's the intended first read. PFF credits him with 69 run-blocking snaps and a 51.5 run-blocking grade, leaving room for improvement if Washington expands his role in two-receiver formations. The bye gives Blough time to make Williams a bigger part of the plan from the opening drive. Give him designed opportunities on first and second down. Washington has a lot of production to replace with McLaurin out, and Williams has already shown he can handle more of that work. It’s time to give him the chance.
